abortion-infertility-myth-base-rate.en:
The warning usually comes from an aunt, a neighbour or a forwarded message: "Get it done and you will never have a child." Years later, when a woman who once had an abortion struggles to get pregnant, the same voices say they knew it all along. To the family it looks like proof. It is a statistical illusion: two very common events landing in the same life, and only one of them taking the blame.

## Where the 'barren after abortion' fear comes from

Abortion in India is common and almost always kept quiet. An estimated 15.6 million abortions took place in 2015, yet the Health Ministry recorded only 701,415 in 2014-15 [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Very few are ever spoken about, and most are never counted; we traced that silence in our story on India's invisible abortion count.

Secrecy decides which stories travel. Consider two women. One had an abortion at 22 and two easy pregnancies at 28, and she never mentions the first, so her story vanishes. The other struggles to conceive and gets questioned about her past. If an abortion turns up, the family has its explanation.

The fear also holds a grain of truth, placed in the wrong spot. When the World Health Organization lists causes of infertility in women, it names blocked fallopian tubes caused by untreated sexually transmitted infections or by complications of unsafe abortion [[who-infertility]]. The myth takes a danger that belongs to unsafe methods and pins it on abortion itself.

## The base-rate trap: two common events, one false link

Start with how ordinary both events are. India had an estimated 48.1 million pregnancies in 2015, and one third of them ended in induced abortion [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Worldwide, WHO puts the share at 29% of all pregnancies [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Infertility is common too: about 17.5% of adults, roughly 1 in 6, experience it at some point in their lives, with similar rates in rich countries (17.8%) and poorer ones (16.5%) [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. That estimate is global, not Indian, but it shows the scale.

When two things are this common, they will often happen to the same person purely by chance. Some women who face infertility will have had an abortion earlier, simply because so many women do. Many of them will also have changed jobs or moved to a new city. Nobody blames the new city. The abortion gets blamed because it is the event wrapped in guilt.

Statisticians call this ignoring the base rate. The honest question is not "Did she have an abortion before she struggled?" but "Do women who had safe abortions struggle more often than women who never had one?" Family memory cannot answer that, because it keeps the cases that fit and forgets the rest. The same coincidence gets the pill and the Copper-T blamed, as our story on contraception myths showed; abortion carries extra shame, so the blame sticks harder.

## What a safe abortion does and does not do to the body

Most abortions reported in NFHS-5 (2019-21) used medicines [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The government-approved combination of mifepristone and misoprostol can be used up to nine weeks (63 days) of pregnancy and succeeds in 95-99% of early abortions, according to the Health Ministry's 2023 guidelines [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. The medicines make the uterus empty itself, with cramps and bleeding that are usually heavier than a period. Nothing is scraped, and nothing is left "weak" or "dried up".

The safety record is stark. WHO says deaths from safe abortion are negligible, under 1 per 100,000 abortions [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Like any treatment it can occasionally go wrong, with an incomplete abortion or an infection, which is why a doctor's check before and a follow-up after matter [[who-abortion]].

The law, in general terms (this is information, not legal advice): up to 20 weeks, one registered doctor can end a pregnancy on the grounds the MTP Act lists, which include a risk to the woman's physical or mental health. Since 2021 the contraceptive-failure ground covers "any woman or her partner", so unmarried women can rely on it too [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. An adult woman's own consent is the only consent needed [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

## The real danger: unsafe methods and delayed care

The harm the myth warns about is real, but it lives in unsafe abortion. Where unsafe abortion is common, WHO counts more than 200 deaths per 100,000 abortions [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. In India, unsafe abortion is the third leading cause of maternal deaths, and close to eight women die every day from causes related to it, by UNFPA's estimate [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. In a 2015 survey of six states, 4-16% of women receiving care after an abortion were being treated for serious complications such as infection of the uterus, perforation, sepsis and shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Infections like these are how an abortion can damage the tubes, and fertility with them [[who-infertility]].

The myth feeds exactly this risk. A woman who believes any abortion will leave her barren has every reason to delay, to hide, and to avoid the clinic where someone might see her. Many abortions already happen outside a clinic: in NFHS-5 (2019-21), 26.9% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion said they had done it themselves [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Pills taken with correct information can be safe. But without a doctor confirming how far along the pregnancy is and that it is inside the uterus, the same pills can lead to heavy bleeding, an incomplete abortion or an infection that nobody treats in time [[who-abortion]].

## Trying to conceive after an abortion

If you had a safe abortion and want a baby later, the evidence is on your side: a safe abortion does not normally affect future pregnancies [[who-abortion]]. The body can be ready to conceive again soon, so if you do not want another pregnancy yet, ask about contraception at the same visit.

If a year of regular unprotected sex brings no pregnancy, WHO calls that infertility [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]], and it is time for both partners to see a doctor. Infertility can come from the man or the woman [[who-infertility]]. Blaming an old abortion often means the husband is never tested at all.

Then look for the causes that matter. Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), which WHO calls a leading cause of infertility, affects an estimated 10-13% of women of reproductive age, and up to 70% of women with it do not know they have it [[who-pcos-factsheet-2026]]. Endometriosis, which can also affect fertility, touches about 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide, and diagnosis takes 4 to 12 years on average [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]]. Many of these causes can be found and treated, but only if the doctor is looking at a woman's body rather than at her past.
abortion-infertility-myth-base-rate.hg:
Warning aksar kisi chachi, padosan ya forwarded message se aati hai: "Karwa liya toh kabhi baccha nahi hoga." Saalon baad, jab ek aurat jisne kabhi abortion karwaya tha pregnant hone ke liye struggle karti hai, toh wahi aawazein kehti hain ki unhe toh pehle se pata tha. Family ko yeh saboot lagta hai. Asal mein yeh ek statistical illusion hai: do bahut common events ek hi zindagi mein aa girte hain, aur ilzaam sirf ek par aata hai.

## 'Abortion ke baad baanjh' wala darr kahan se aata hai

India mein abortion common hai aur lagbhag hamesha chhupaya jaata hai. 2015 mein estimated 15.6 million abortions hue, lekin Health Ministry ne 2014-15 mein sirf 701,415 record kiye [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Unmein se bahut kam ke baare mein kabhi baat hoti hai, aur zyada tar kabhi gine hi nahi jaate; us chuppi ko humne India ki invisible abortion count wali story mein trace kiya tha.

Kaunsi kahani aage chalegi, yeh secrecy tay karti hai. Do aurton ko socho. Ek ne 22 ki umar mein abortion karwaya aur 28 mein do aasaan pregnancies hui; woh pehli baat ka zikr kabhi nahi karti, toh uski kahani gayab ho jaati hai. Doosri conceive karne mein struggle karti hai aur usse uske past ke baare mein sawaal hote hain. Agar koi abortion nikal aaye, toh family ko apna explanation mil jaata hai.

Is darr mein sach ka ek daana bhi hai, bas galat jagah rakha hua. World Health Organization jab aurton mein infertility ki wajahein ginata hai, toh blocked fallopian tubes ka naam leta hai, jo bina ilaaj ke chhode gaye sexually transmitted infections se ya unsafe abortion ki complications se hoti hain [[who-infertility]]. Myth ek aisa khatra uthata hai jo unsafe tareekon ka hai, aur use abortion par hi chipka deta hai.

## Base-rate trap: do common events, ek jhootha link

Pehle yeh dekho ki dono events kitne aam hain. 2015 mein India mein estimated 48.1 million pregnancies hui, aur unmein se one third, yaani ek-tihaai, induced abortion par khatam hui [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Duniya bhar ke liye WHO yeh hissa saari pregnancies ka 29% batata hai [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Infertility bhi common hai: lagbhag 17.5% adults, yaani roughly 1 in 6, zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi ise jhelte hain, aur rate ameer deshon (17.8%) aur gareeb deshon (16.5%) mein lagbhag ek jaisa hai [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. Yeh estimate global hai, Indian nahi, lekin scale dikha deta hai.

Jab do cheezein itni common hon, toh woh aksar ek hi insaan ke saath sirf ittefaq se hongi. Infertility jhelne wali kuch aurton ne pehle abortion karwaya hoga, sirf isliye ki itni saari aurtein karwati hain. Unmein se kai ne job bhi badli hogi ya naye sheher mein shift hui hongi. Naye sheher ko koi blame nahi karta. Abortion blame hota hai kyunki wahi woh event hai jo guilt mein lipta hua hai.

Statisticians ise base rate ko ignore karna kehte hain. Imaandaar sawaal yeh nahi hai ki "Kya struggle se pehle usne abortion karwaya tha?" balki yeh ki "Kya safe abortion karwane wali aurtein un aurton se zyada struggle karti hain jinhone kabhi nahi karwaya?" Family ki yaaddaasht iska jawaab nahi de sakti, kyunki woh fit hone wale cases yaad rakhti hai aur baaki bhool jaati hai. Isi ittefaq ki wajah se pill aur Copper-T par bhi ilzaam aata hai, jaisa contraception myths par hamari story ne dikhaya; abortion par sharam zyada hai, toh ilzaam aur zor se chipakta hai.

## Safe abortion body ke saath kya karta hai aur kya nahi

NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein report hue zyada tar abortions dawaiyon se hue the [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Government-approved mifepristone aur misoprostol ka combination nau hafte (63 din) tak ki pregnancy mein use ho sakta hai, aur Health Ministry ki 2023 ki guidelines ke mutabik 95-99% early abortions mein kaamyaab hota hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Dawaiyan uterus ko khud khaali hone par majboor karti hain, cramps aur bleeding ke saath, jo aam taur par period se zyada heavy hoti hai. Kuch khurcha nahi jaata, aur kuch "kamzor" ya "sookha" nahi reh jaata.

Safety record bilkul saaf hai. WHO kehta hai ki safe abortion se maut na ke barabar hai, har 100,000 abortions par 1 se kam [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Kisi bhi ilaaj ki tarah yeh kabhi-kabhi galat ja sakta hai, incomplete abortion ya infection ke saath, isiliye pehle doctor ka check aur baad mein follow-up maayne rakhta hai [[who-abortion]].

Kanoon, general taur par (yeh jaankari hai, legal advice nahi): 20 hafte tak ek registered doctor MTP Act mein likhe grounds par pregnancy khatam kar sakta hai, jinmein aurat ki physical ya mental health ko khatra bhi shaamil hai. 2021 se contraceptive-failure wala ground "any woman or her partner" par laagu hota hai, yaani unmarried aurtein bhi iska sahara le sakti hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Adult aurat ki apni consent hi woh akeli consent hai jo chahiye [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

## Asli khatra: unsafe tareeke aur der se mili care

Myth jis nuksaan se darata hai woh asli hai, lekin woh unsafe abortion mein rehta hai. Jahan unsafe abortion common hai, wahan WHO har 100,000 abortions par 200 se zyada maut ginta hai [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. India mein unsafe abortion maternal deaths ki teesri sabse badi wajah hai, aur UNFPA ke estimate ke mutabik isse judi wajahon se har din lagbhag aath aurton ki maut hoti hai [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. 2015 mein chhe states ke ek survey mein, abortion ke baad care le rahi 4-16% aurton ka ilaaj serious complications ke liye ho raha tha, jaise uterus ka infection, perforation, sepsis aur shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Aise hi infections ke zariye abortion tubes ko nuksaan pahuncha sakta hai, aur unke saath fertility ko [[who-infertility]].

Myth theek isi risk ko badhata hai. Jo aurat maanti hai ki koi bhi abortion use "baanjh" kar dega, uske paas der karne, chhupane aur us clinic se bachne ki har wajah hai jahan koi use dekh sakta hai. Kai abortions pehle se clinic ke bahar hote hain: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein, jin aurton ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 26.9% ne kaha ki unhone yeh khud kiya tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sahi jaankari ke saath li gayi pills safe ho sakti hain. Lekin jab koi doctor confirm nahi karta ki pregnancy kitne hafte ki hai aur uterus ke andar hai, tab wahi pills heavy bleeding, incomplete abortion ya aise infection tak le ja sakti hain jiska waqt par koi ilaaj nahi karta [[who-abortion]].

## Abortion ke baad conceive karne ki koshish

Agar tumne safe abortion karwaya tha aur baad mein baby chahti ho, toh evidence tumhari taraf hai: safe abortion aam taur par aage ki pregnancies par asar nahi daalta [[who-abortion]]. Body jaldi hi dobara conceive karne ke liye taiyaar ho sakti hai, toh agar abhi doosri pregnancy nahi chahiye, usi visit par contraception ke baare mein poocho.

Agar ek saal regular unprotected sex ke baad bhi pregnancy na ho, toh WHO use infertility kehta hai [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]], aur tab dono partners ko doctor ke paas jaana chahiye. Infertility mard ki taraf se bhi ho sakti hai aur aurat ki taraf se bhi [[who-infertility]]. Purane abortion ko blame karne ka matlab aksar yeh hota hai ki pati ka test kabhi hota hi nahi.

Phir un wajahon ko dhundho jo sach mein maayne rakhti hain. Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), jise WHO infertility ki ek leading wajah kehta hai, reproductive age ki estimated 10-13% aurton ko hota hai, aur PCOS wali up to 70% aurtein jaanti hi nahi ki unhe yeh hai [[who-pcos-factsheet-2026]]. Endometriosis, jo fertility par bhi asar daal sakta hai, duniya bhar mein reproductive age ki lagbhag 10% aurton ko hota hai, aur diagnosis mein average 4 se 12 saal lag jaate hain [[who-endometriosis-factsheet-2025]]. Inmein se kai wajahein pakdi aur theek ki ja sakti hain, lekin tabhi jab doctor aurat ki body ko dekh raha ho, uske past ko nahi.

abuse-not-poor-family-problem.en:
Imagine a Class 9 student in a South Delhi school who tells her mother that an uncle with a senior government job makes her uncomfortable. In many homes the first answer is disbelief: he is educated, respected, from a good family. That reflex rests on an unspoken myth. Sexual abuse, like son preference, is supposed to belong to other people: the poor, the rural, the uneducated.

## The comfortable myth of 'other people'

The surveys do show a class gradient, and hiding it would be dishonest. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 43% of women married to men with no schooling reported physical, sexual or emotional violence by their husband, against 22% of women married to men with 12 or more years of schooling [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Schooling halves the risk. It does not end it: more than one in five women married to the most-schooled men still reported violence. In NFHS-6, 17.5% of ever-married women in cities reported physical or sexual violence by a husband, against 24.4% in rural areas [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Money and status change the odds. They also change something no survey measures: how long abuse stays hidden, and who decides whether it is investigated. Four records from places Indian families admire show how.

## Cinema: a power group and no complaints committee

Kerala set up the Justice K. Hema Committee in 2017, after an actor was abducted and sexually assaulted, to study harassment in Malayalam cinema [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]]. It found an all-male 'power group' of 10 to 15 directors, producers and actors who decide who stays in the industry and can ban even prominent figures; the committee was told that a prominent actor had called this lobby a 'mafia' [[tnm-hema-mafia-bans-2024]]. Junior artists were promised roles if they complied with demands for sex; women who agreed were code-named 'cooperating artists' [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

The report reached the state government in December 2019. It was made public on 19 August 2024, nearly five years later, after 63 pages of the 295-page draft were removed to protect identities [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]]. In September 2024 the Kerala High Court asked why the government had been 'inactive or silent' since 31 December 2019, when the state police chief had held a copy since February 2021 [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]].

The industry lacked even basic safeguards. The Women in Cinema Collective went to the Kerala High Court in 2018 because the actors' association, AMMA, had no Internal Complaints Committee; in 2022 the collective said it still had none [[livelaw-kwc-wcc-pil-2022]]. Cinema is not an outlier: in 2023 an Indian Express investigation found 16 of India's 30 national sports federations failing the POSH Act, five of them, including wrestling, with no complaints committee at all [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]].

## Medicine: a hospital that could not keep its own doctor safe

On 9 August 2024 a trainee doctor was raped and murdered at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata, her own workplace. On 20 August the Supreme Court took up the case on its own and set up a National Task Force on the safety of medical professionals [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Its order warned: 'The nation cannot await a rape or murder for real changes on the ground.'

Her degree and profession did not protect her. Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud's words explain why: 'If women cannot go to a place of work and feel safe, we are denying them equal opportunity.' On 20 January 2025 a Sealdah court sentenced the convicted man to life imprisonment for the rest of his natural life [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. Our RG Kar case file follows the trial. The point here is simpler: a teaching hospital full of educated people was not a safe workplace.

## Power on trial: the Unnao conviction

In 2017 a minor girl was raped in Unnao, Uttar Pradesh, by a man who was then an MLA. The Supreme Court moved all the Unnao trials from Lucknow to Delhi. On 20 December 2019 a Delhi court sentenced former MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar to imprisonment for the remainder of his life and a Rs 25 lakh fine [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]].

Conviction did not end the contest. In December 2025 the Delhi High Court suspended his life sentence pending appeal, reasoning at that interim stage that an MLA was not a 'public servant' for the aggravated POCSO offence, and that he had already served more than seven years [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]]. The Supreme Court stayed that order on 29 December 2025. On 15 May 2026 it set the suspension aside and sent the matter back, asking the High Court either to decide his main appeal quickly or to pass a fresh order on suspension [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]]. We found no decision on the appeal as of 20 November 2026.

Look at what it took: a trial moved out of the state, then two rounds in the Supreme Court over suspending a life sentence. Power did not prevent a conviction, but his former office sat at the centre of the reasoning that briefly suspended it.

## Missing daughters in the capital

Son preference gets filed under the same myth. The Sample Registration System says otherwise. In 2021-23 India recorded 917 girls born per 1,000 boys; urban India, at 925, did only slightly better than rural India, at 914 [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. Delhi, the national capital, recorded 872, second-lowest among the bigger states after Uttarakhand (868) [[srs-statistical-report-2023]].

Choosing a son before birth is not a village superstition. It is an illegal medical service: it needs a scan, a clinic and a doctor willing to break the law. That is why the PC-PNDT Act threatens such doctors with up to three years in prison and loss of their registration [[indiacode-pcpndt-1994]]. UNFPA estimated that about 460,000 girls went 'missing' at birth in India every year between 2013 and 2017 [[unfpa-swop-2020]].

The myth fails twice. It sends prevention to the wrong address, and it tells survivors in respectable places that nobody will believe them. The test of a family, a film set, a hospital or a legislature is not its reputation. It is whether a complaint against its most powerful member gets heard.
abuse-not-poor-family-problem.hg:
Imagine kijiye, South Delhi ke ek school mein Class 9 ki ek student apni mummy ko batati hai ki ek uncle ki harkaton se use ajeeb lagta hai. Uncle ki badi sarkari naukri hai. Bahut se gharon mein pehla jawab yahi hota hai: "Aisa kaise ho sakta hai? Woh padhe-likhe hain, respected hain, achhe ghar se hain." Is reflex ke peeche ek myth hai jo koi zor se nahi bolta. Myth yeh hai ki sexual abuse, aur beta chahne ki soch bhi, "doosre logon" ki baat hai: gareebon ki, gaon walon ki, anpadh logon ki.

## "Doosre log" wala comfortable myth

Surveys mein class ka farak dikhta hai, aur use chhupana dishonest hoga. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein jin aurton ke pati kabhi school nahi gaye the, unmein se 43% ne husband ki physical, sexual ya emotional violence report ki. Jinke pati 12 ya usse zyada saal padhe the, unmein yeh 22% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yaani padhai risk ko aadha kar deti hai. Par khatam nahi karti: sabse zyada padhe patiyon ki wives mein bhi har paanch mein se ek se zyada ne violence report ki. NFHS-6 mein shehron ki 17.5% married women ne husband ki physical ya sexual violence report ki, aur rural areas mein 24.4% ne [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Paisa aur status odds badalte hain. Woh ek aur cheez bhi badalte hain jo koi survey nahi naapta: abuse kitni der chhupa rehta hai, aur kaun decide karta hai ki investigation hogi ya nahi. Neeche chaar records hain, aisi jagahon se jinhe Indian families bahut izzat se dekhti hain.

## Cinema: ek power group, aur complaint sunne wali koi committee nahi

2017 mein Kerala mein ek actor ko abduct karke un par sexual assault hua. Iske baad Kerala government ne Justice K. Hema Committee banayi, taaki Malayalam cinema mein harassment ki jaanch ho sake [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]]. Committee ko 10 se 15 directors, producers aur actors ka ek all-male "power group" mila, jo decide karta tha ki industry mein kaun tikega aur bade naamon par bhi ban laga sakta tha. Committee ko bataya gaya ki ek jaane-maane actor ne is lobby ko "mafia" kaha tha [[tnm-hema-mafia-bans-2024]]. Junior artists se kaha jaata tha ki sex ki demand maan lo toh films mein chance milega. Jo aurtein maan jaati thi, unka code name tha "cooperating artists" [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

Report December 2019 mein hi state government ke paas pahunch gayi thi. Public hui 19 August 2024 ko, yaani lagbhag paanch saal baad. Woh bhi 295 pages ke draft se 63 pages hata kar, taaki logon ki identity chhupi rahe [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]]. September 2024 mein Kerala High Court ne seedha poocha: government 31 December 2019 se "inactive ya silent" kyun baithi rahi? Jabki state ke police chief ke paas February 2021 se report ki copy thi [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]].

Industry ne sabse basic safeguard bhi nahi banaya tha. Women in Cinema Collective 2018 mein Kerala High Court gaya, kyunki actors ki association AMMA mein Internal Complaints Committee hi nahi thi. 2022 mein bhi collective ne kaha ki committee ab tak nahi bani [[livelaw-kwc-wcc-pil-2022]]. Yeh sirf cinema ki kahani nahi hai. 2023 mein Indian Express ki ek investigation mein pata chala ki India ki 30 national sports federations mein se 16 POSH Act ko follow nahi kar rahi thi. Wrestling samet paanch mein toh complaints committee thi hi nahi [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]].

## Medicine: ek hospital jo apni hi doctor ko safe nahi rakh saka

9 August 2024 ko Kolkata ke RG Kar Medical College and Hospital mein ek trainee doctor ka rape aur murder hua. Yeh unki apni workplace thi. 20 August ko Supreme Court ne khud yeh case uthaya aur medical professionals ki safety par ek National Task Force banayi [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Order mein likha tha: "The nation cannot await a rape or murder for real changes on the ground", yaani desh zameen par asli badlav ke liye kisi rape ya murder ka intezaar nahi kar sakta.

Unki degree aur profession unhe bacha nahi paaye. Kyun? Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ki baat mein jawab hai: "Agar aurtein kaam ki jagah jaakar safe feel nahi kar sakti, toh hum unse barabari ka mauka chheen rahe hain." 20 January 2025 ko Sealdah court ne convict ko baaki poori zindagi ke liye umrqaid di [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. Trial ki poori kahani hamari RG Kar case file mein hai. Yahan point simple hai: padhe-likhe logon se bhara ek teaching hospital bhi kaam ke liye safe jagah nahi tha.

## Power on trial: Unnao ka faisla

2017 mein Uttar Pradesh ke Unnao mein ek minor ladki ka rape hua. Jis aadmi ko iske liye convict kiya gaya, woh us waqt MLA tha. Supreme Court ne Unnao ke saare trials Lucknow se Delhi shift kar diye. 20 December 2019 ko Delhi ki ek court ne former MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar ko baaki poori zindagi jail aur Rs 25 lakh fine ki saza di [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]].

Conviction ke baad bhi ladai khatam nahi hui. December 2025 mein Delhi High Court ne appeal pending rehte uski umrqaid suspend kar di. Us shuruati stage par High Court ne do baatein kahi. Pehli, aggravated POCSO offence ke liye MLA "public servant" nahi maana jaata. Doosri, woh saat saal se zyada jail kaat chuka hai [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]]. 29 December 2025 ko Supreme Court ne us order par rok laga di. Phir 15 May 2026 ko use set aside karke matter High Court ko wapas bhej diya, aur kaha ki High Court ya toh main appeal par jaldi faisla kare ya suspension par naya order de [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]]. 20 November 2026 tak appeal par koi faisla hamein nahi mila.

Sochiye, ismein kya-kya laga: trial ko state se bahar le jaana pada, phir umrqaid suspend ho ya nahi, is par do baar Supreme Court ko aage aana pada. Power conviction ko rok nahi paayi. Par jis reasoning se uski saza thode samay ke liye suspend hui, uske centre mein uska MLA wala pad hi tha.

## Capital mein gayab betiyan

Beta chahne ki soch ko bhi isi myth ke khaate mein daal diya jaata hai, jaise yeh sirf gaon ki problem ho. Sample Registration System (SRS) kuch aur kehta hai. 2021-23 mein India mein har 1,000 ladkon par 917 ladkiyan paida hui. Shehron mein yeh 925 tha aur gaon mein 914, yaani shehar bas thoda sa aage the [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. Desh ki capital Delhi mein yeh number 872 tha. Bade states mein isse neeche sirf Uttarakhand (868) tha [[srs-statistical-report-2023]].

Paida hone se pehle beta chunna koi gaon ka andhvishwas nahi hai. Yeh ek illegal medical service hai: iske liye scan chahiye, clinic chahiye, aur law todne ko taiyaar doctor chahiye. Isiliye PC-PNDT Act mein aise doctors ke liye teen saal tak ki jail hai, aur unka medical registration bhi ja sakta hai [[indiacode-pcpndt-1994]]. UNFPA ka estimate hai ki 2013 se 2017 ke beech India mein har saal lagbhag 460,000 ladkiyan birth ke time "missing" hui [[unfpa-swop-2020]].

Yeh myth do tarah se fail hota hai. Ek, bachav ki koshish galat address par jaati hai. Do, "respectable" jagahon ke survivors ko lagta hai ki koi unki baat nahi maanega. Kisi family, film set, hospital ya assembly ki asli pehchaan uski reputation nahi hai. Asli test yeh hai ki jab complaint wahan ke sabse powerful aadmi ke khilaf ho, toh woh suni jaati hai ya nahi.

abusers-dont-look-like-monsters.en:
When a man is accused of sexual abuse, the first witness for the defence is usually his reputation. He is a good husband. He has taught at that school for twenty years. "He's not the type," people say, and they mean it. In their minds an abuser is a stranger with a frightening face, and the man they know looks nothing like that.

The records show that picture is wrong. The mistake has a cost: it is the trusted man's best protection.

## The monster we expect

Films, crime bulletins and school safety talks have taught one image of a sexual offender: unknown, visibly dangerous, waiting somewhere dark. The Supreme Court's 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes lists the belief that rapists are usually strangers as a false stereotype. Its correction: "Very often men sexually assault or rape a woman known to them in some capacity" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

The monster image does two jobs. It tells families where to look: outside, at strangers. And it hands every accused man who is polite, married, devout or generous a ready defence: he does not match the picture.

## Who the records actually name

In 2024 police in India registered 29,536 rape cases. In 28,597 of them, 96.8%, the offender was known to the victim [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Family members were named in 2,134 cases, and a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person in 12,584. The other 13,879 known-offender cases named friends, online friends, live-in partners or separated husbands. In only 939 was the offender unknown or unidentified [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The pattern holds for children. Of 44,126 cases of penetrative sexual assault registered under the POCSO Act in 2024, the offender was a family member in 3,658 and a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person in 16,668. In only 1,492 was the offender unknown or unidentified [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The victims in those cases included 892 boys, a number that reflects how rarely abuse of boys is reported, not how rarely it happens [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

None of this is new. The government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse found that 50% of abusers were persons known to the child or in a position of trust and responsibility, and that most children told no one [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Police figures count registered cases only, and sexual violence is heavily under-reported. What goes unreported is, by definition, uncounted. The cases that are counted point overwhelmingly to people the victim knows.

## Trust as the abuser's tool

A good reputation is not evidence against abuse. Often it is the means. Trust is what gets a man time alone with a child, a key to the house, authority over a student or an employee, and the benefit of the doubt when someone finally speaks.

Darkness to Light, a child-protection group, describes grooming as a deliberate process by which offenders gradually build a secret sexual relationship with a child. Its red flags include special attention to one child, gifts, touching or hugging, sympathetic listening and offers to help the family [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Every item on that list is also something a kind uncle does. The difference lies in secrecy, in the focus on one child, and in what happens when the child says no.

Consider a 12-year-old in Indore. The man is her father's oldest friend. He drove her mother to hospital, he helps with her brother's fees, he is "like family". When she says she does not want to sit near him, she is told not to be rude. Nobody in that house is hiding a monster. They are defending a man they love, using the only picture of an abuser they have.

Indian law understands this better than Indian drawing rooms do. Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) lists 13 aggravated forms of rape that can carry imprisonment for the rest of the offender's natural life. They include rape by police, public servants and hospital staff, and by "a relative, guardian or teacher of, or a person in a position of trust or authority towards the woman" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In those prosecutions, once intercourse is proved and the woman tells the court she did not consent, the court must presume she did not [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. The law treats trust as something that makes the crime worse, never as proof of innocence. This is general information, not legal advice.

## When the abuser runs the institution

A social audit by the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, done for the Bihar government and submitted in April 2018, flagged sexual abuse at several institutions, including a state-funded shelter home for girls in Muzaffarpur [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. The audit revealed the sexual abuse of 34 minor girls there [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. On 20 January 2020 a POCSO court at Saket, Delhi, convicted 19 of the 20 accused [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. On 11 February 2020 it sentenced the man who ran the home to life imprisonment for the remainder of his life [[livelaw-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

He was not an outsider who slipped past a guard. He was the person the state funded and trusted to keep those girls safe, and it took an outside audit to expose him.

POCSO makes reporting child sexual abuse mandatory, and the head of an institution who fails to report abuse by a subordinate faces up to one year in prison [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. When the head himself is the abuser, that safeguard fails from the top. Only outside eyes can catch it: inspections, audits, and a way for children to complain to someone the institution does not employ.

## Judging behaviour, not reputation

None of this makes every kind man a suspect. It means kindness and status tell you nothing either way. Behaviour does: an adult who arranges time alone with one child, who attaches secrecy to gifts, who ignores a child's "no", who turns angry when questioned.

When a child or a woman names a respected man, the first response decides what follows. "He would never" ends the conversation. "Tell me what happened" keeps it open. Listening is not a verdict; courts decide guilt. But a child who is disbelieved once may not speak again, and most never speak at all.

If a child tells you, believe them and call the Child Helpline on 1098. A reputation is what a person shows the world, and abuse happens where the world is not looking. The question is never "is he the type?" It is "what did he do?"
abusers-dont-look-like-monsters.hg:
Jab kisi aadmi par sexual abuse ka aarop lagta hai, toh uski taraf se sabse pehla gawah aksar uski reputation hoti hai. Woh achha pati hai. Woh us school mein bees saal se padha raha hai. Log kehte hain, "Woh aisa aadmi nahi hai," aur dil se kehte hain. Unke dimaag mein abuser ek daravne chehre wala ajnabi hota hai, aur jis aadmi ko woh jaante hain, woh waisa bilkul nahi dikhta.

Records dikhate hain ki yeh tasveer galat hai. Is galti ki ek keemat hai: bharosemand aadmi ki sabse badi hifazat yahi tasveer hai.

## Woh monster jiski hum ummeed karte hain

Films, crime bulletins aur school ke safety talks ne sexual offender ki ek hi image sikhayi hai: anjaan, dekhne mein hi khatarnaak, kisi andheri jagah par intezaar karta hua. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes is soch ko ek galat stereotype maanti hai ki rapists aksar ajnabi hote hain. Handbook ka jawaab hai: "Very often men sexually assault or rape a woman known to them in some capacity", yaani aksar aadmi usi aurat ka sexual assault ya rape karte hain jise woh kisi na kisi tarah jaante hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Monster wali image do kaam karti hai. Yeh families ko batati hai ki dekhna kahan hai: bahar, ajnabiyon ki taraf. Aur yeh har us accused aadmi ko ek ready defence de deti hai jo tameezdaar, shaadi-shuda, dharmik ya dildaar hai: woh us tasveer se match hi nahi karta.

## Records asal mein kiska naam lete hain

2024 mein India mein police ne 29,536 rape cases register kiye. Inmein se 28,597 mein, yaani 96.8% mein, offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2,134 cases mein family members ka naam tha, aur 12,584 mein family friend, padosi, employer ya kisi aur jaan-pehchaan wale ka. Jaan-pehchaan wale baaki 13,879 cases mein friends, online friends, live-in partners ya separated husbands the. Sirf 939 cases mein offender anjaan tha ya uski pehchaan nahi ho payi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Bachchon ke cases mein bhi pattern yahi hai. 2024 mein POCSO Act ke under penetrative sexual assault ke 44,126 cases register hue. Inmein se 3,658 mein offender family member tha, aur 16,668 mein family friend, padosi, employer ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala. Sirf 1,492 cases mein offender anjaan tha ya uski pehchaan nahi ho payi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In cases ke victims mein 892 ladke bhi the. Yeh number dikhata hai ki ladkon ke saath hua abuse kitna kam report hota hai, yeh nahi ki woh kitna kam hota hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh koi nayi baat nahi hai. Government ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein paaya gaya ki 50% abusers bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale the ya position of trust and responsibility mein the, aur zyada tar bachchon ne kisi ko kuch nahi bataya [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Police ke figures sirf registered cases ginte hain, aur sexual violence bahut kam report hoti hai. Jo report hi nahi hua, woh gina bhi nahi gaya. Par jo cases gine gaye hain, woh saaf taur par victim ke jaan-pehchaan walon ki taraf ishaara karte hain.

## Bharosa: abuser ka auzaar

Achhi reputation abuse ke khilaf koi saboot nahi hai. Aksar wahi zariya hoti hai. Bharosa hi kisi aadmi ko bachche ke saath akela waqt deta hai, ghar ki chaabi deta hai, student ya employee par authority deta hai, aur jab koi aakhirkaar bolta hai, toh benefit of the doubt bhi usi ko milta hai.

Child-protection group Darkness to Light ke mutabik grooming ek sochi-samjhi process hai, jismein offender dheere-dheere bachche ke saath ek secret sexual relationship banata hai. Iske red flags mein yeh shaamil hain: ek hi bachche par special attention, gifts, chhoona ya hug karna, hamdardi se uski baatein sunna, aur family ki madad ke offers [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Is list ki har cheez woh bhi hai jo ek achha chacha ya mama karta hai. Farq secrecy mein hai, ek hi bachche par focus mein hai, aur is mein ki jab bachcha "na" kehta hai tab kya hota hai.

Indore ki ek 12 saal ki bachchi ke baare mein sochiye. Woh aadmi uske papa ka sabse purana dost hai. Usi ne uski mummy ko hospital pahunchaya tha, wahi uske bhai ki fees mein madad karta hai, woh "ghar jaisa" hai. Jab bachchi kehti hai ki use uske paas nahi baithna, toh use kaha jaata hai ki badtameezi mat karo. Us ghar mein koi kisi monster ko nahi chhupa raha. Woh log ek aise aadmi ko defend kar rahe hain jisse woh pyaar karte hain, aur unke paas abuser ki bas wahi ek tasveer hai.

Indian law yeh baat Indian drawing rooms se behtar samajhta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 64 rape ke 13 aggravated forms ginata hai, jinmein offender ko uski baaki natural life tak ki qaid ho sakti hai. Inmein police, public servants aur hospital staff ke haathon rape shaamil hai, aur us aadmi ke haathon bhi jo "a relative, guardian or teacher of, or a person in a position of trust or authority towards the woman" ho, yaani rishtedaar, guardian, teacher, ya woh jis par aurat ka bharosa ho ya jiski us par authority ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aise prosecutions mein jab intercourse saabit ho jaaye aur aurat court mein kahe ki usne consent nahi diya tha, toh court ko yahi maanna hoga ki consent nahi tha [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Law bharose ko crime ko aur gambhir banane wali cheez maanta hai, begunahi ka saboot kabhi nahi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Jab abuser hi institution chalata ho

Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) ne Bihar government ke liye ek social audit kiya, jo April 2018 mein submit hua. Usne kai institutions mein sexual abuse flag kiya, jinmein Muzaffarpur ka ek state-funded girls' shelter home bhi tha [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. Audit se wahan 34 minor ladkiyon ka sexual abuse saamne aaya [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. 20 January 2020 ko Delhi ke Saket ki POCSO court ne 20 mein se 19 accused ko convict kiya [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. 11 February 2020 ko usi court ne us aadmi ko, jo yeh home chalata tha, uski baaki zindagi tak ki umrqaid sunayi [[livelaw-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

Woh koi bahar wala nahi tha jo guard ki nazar bacha kar andar ghus aaya ho. Woh wahi aadmi tha jise state ne paisa diya tha aur jis par un bachchiyon ko safe rakhne ka bharosa kiya tha. Use expose karne ke liye ek bahar ke audit ki zaroorat padi.

POCSO child sexual abuse ki reporting ko mandatory banata hai, aur jis institution ka head apne subordinate ke abuse ko report nahi karta, use ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Par jab head khud abuser ho, toh yeh safeguard upar se hi fail ho jaata hai. Tab sirf bahar ki nazar ise pakad sakti hai: inspections, audits, aur bachchon ke liye kisi aise insaan se complaint karne ka raasta jo us institution ka employee na ho.

## Reputation nahi, behaviour dekhiye

Iska matlab yeh nahi ki har achha aadmi suspect hai. Matlab yeh hai ki achhai aur status, dono taraf se kuch saabit nahi karte. Behaviour batata hai: woh adult jo ek hi bachche ke saath akele rehne ke mauke banata hai, jo gifts ke saath secret jod deta hai, jo bachche ki "na" ko ignore karta hai, jo sawaal poochne par gussa ho jaata hai.

Jab koi bachcha ya aurat kisi respected aadmi ka naam leti hai, toh pehla response tay karta hai ki aage kya hoga. "Woh aisa kabhi nahi karega" baat wahin khatam kar deta hai. "Batao kya hua tha" baat ko khula rakhta hai. Sunna faisla sunana nahi hai; guilt court tay karti hai. Par jis bachche ki baat ek baar nahi maani gayi, woh shayad dobara na bole, aur zyada tar bachche toh kabhi bolte hi nahi.

Agar koi bachcha aapko bataye, toh uski baat par yakeen kijiye aur Child Helpline 1098 par call kijiye. Reputation woh hai jo insaan duniya ko dikhata hai, aur abuse wahan hota hai jahan duniya dekh nahi rahi hoti. Sawaal kabhi yeh nahi hai ki "kya woh aisa aadmi hai?" Sawaal yeh hai ki "usne kiya kya?"

adult-women-rape-conviction-gap.en:
"A grown woman could have stopped him." The sentence gets said in living rooms and at police stations, and in 2023 the Supreme Court published a handbook to help judges stop reasoning from stereotypes about women [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. The 2024 court data show a gap exactly where that belief would bite. In rape trials completed in 2024, courts convicted in 31.4% of cases when the victim was a girl under 18, and in 23.7% when she was an adult woman [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Two conviction rates, one law

Both rates are for the same offence: rape, charged under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code for older cases and under Sections 63 and 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for offences from 1 July 2024 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) splits the completed trials by the victim's age.

| Victim | Trials completed, 2024 | Convictions | Conviction rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Girls under 18 | 1,935 | 608 | 31.4% |
| Women aged 18 or over | 18,652 | 4,424 | 23.7% |
| All | 20,587 | 5,032 | 24.4% |

Nine in ten of these trials had an adult victim, so the women's rate is, in effect, India's rape conviction rate [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The girls' row is small because most child rape is charged under the POCSO Act and counted separately: 43,313 cases with girl victims in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The pattern holds there too. For penetrative sexual assault on children under POCSO, the conviction rate was 30.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Where the victim is a child, about three in ten trials end in conviction. Where she is an adult, fewer than one in four do.

## Who the victims are: women aged 18 to 30

Of the 29,742 victims recorded under the rape head in 2024, 28,950 were adults, and 19,489 of them were aged 18 to 30 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Only 792 were under 18, a figure that reflects the POCSO split, not the number of children raped.

That is the age of college, first jobs and first relationships. The accused is rarely a stranger: the offender was known to the victim in 96.8% of the rape cases registered in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The largest group, 13,879 cases, involved friends, online friends, live-in partners on the pretext of marriage, or separated husbands [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

When two people knew each other, the defence need not argue mistaken identity. It can argue that she agreed.

## When consent is the question: where myths enter

For a girl under 18, the law removes that argument. Section 63 says the act is rape "with or without her consent" [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and in a POCSO trial Section 29 makes the court presume that the accused committed the offence unless the contrary is proved [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The trial turns on two facts: did it happen, and how old was she.

For a woman, the prosecution must also prove that she did not consent, usually about a room with no witnesses. The law presumes no consent only in aggravated cases, such as rape by a police officer, public servant, relative, guardian or hospital staff [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Everyone else starts without it.

Consider a 24-year-old in Pune who reports a colleague five days after a party. In the witness box, the questions write themselves. Why did she go to his flat? Why did she not shout? Why are there no injuries? Why did she wait? None of these asks what he did. Each one measures her against an imagined "real" victim who fights, screams and runs straight to a police station.

How much of the gap is weak evidence and how much is belief? The data cannot say: the NCRB publishes verdicts, not reasons. Some of it will be evidence: a consent trial rests on one person's account of a private moment, and with 1,85,785 rape cases pending at the end of 2024, that account is often tested long afterwards [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. But the doubts those questions plant are the ones the law tells courts not to act on.

## What the law and the Supreme Court say

Section 63 defines consent as an "unequivocal voluntary agreement" to the specific act, communicated by words, gestures or any other form of communication. It adds that a woman who does not physically resist is not, for that reason alone, to be regarded as consenting [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. "She could have stopped him" is not a defence the statute recognises.

Her past is off limits too. Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, a survivor's character or previous sexual experience is irrelevant to consent, and in a rape trial she may not be cross-examined about her "general immoral character" or sexual history to prove consent [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

The Supreme Court's handbook rejects the beliefs that a woman who delays reporting is lying, that a "real" survivor cries incessantly, and that women are very likely to make false allegations [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

> "There is no 'correct' or 'appropriate' way in which a survivor or victim behaves." (Supreme Court handbook for judges, 2023)

These tables count only women and girls, because Section 63 defines rape as an act by a man against a woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Adult male and transgender survivors do not appear in them at all.

## Preparing for a trial that turns on consent

This is general information, not legal advice. But a survivor who knows where a trial will press can prepare.

Get medical care first. Every hospital, public or private, must give free treatment, and police must send a survivor for a medical examination within 24 hours of being informed, only with her consent [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Going early preserves evidence. Going late does not cancel the complaint.

Write down what happened, in order, while it is fresh. Keep every message, call log and photo, including friendly ones from before or after. Context is not consent, and your lawyer should see all of it.

A magistrate, as far as practicable a woman, records the survivor's statement, and the trial is held in camera [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. If the defence asks about her sexual history to suggest consent, the prosecutor can object, because the law bars it.

The verdict is not the only outcome. An acquittal means the court was not sure beyond reasonable doubt, not that she lied. Compensation through the Legal Services Authority is available even after an acquittal [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. For support at any stage, call the Women Helpline.
adult-women-rape-conviction-gap.hg:
"Badi aurat thi, rok sakti thi." Yeh line drawing rooms mein boli jaati hai aur police stations mein bhi, aur 2023 mein Supreme Court ne ek handbook nikaali taaki judges women ke baare mein stereotypes ke sahaare reasoning karna band karein [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. 2024 ka court data theek usi jagah gap dikhata hai jahan yeh soch asar karti. 2024 mein poore hue rape trials mein, jab victim 18 se kam ki girl thi toh courts ne 31.4% cases mein conviction di, aur jab woh adult woman thi toh 23.7% mein [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Do conviction rates, ek hi law

Dono rates ek hi offence ke hain: rape, jo purane cases mein Indian Penal Code ke Section 376 ke tahat charge hota tha aur 1 July 2024 se hue offences mein Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Sections 63 aur 64 ke tahat [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) poore hue trials ko victim ki umar ke hisaab se alag dikhata hai.

| Victim | Poore hue trials, 2024 | Convictions | Conviction rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18 se kam ki girls | 1,935 | 608 | 31.4% |
| 18 ya usse upar ki women | 18,652 | 4,424 | 23.7% |
| Sab | 20,587 | 5,032 | 24.4% |

In trials mein se das mein se nau mein victim adult thi, isliye women wala rate hi asal mein India ka rape conviction rate hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Girls wali row chhoti isliye hai ki child rape ke zyadatar cases POCSO Act ke tahat charge hote hain aur alag gine jaate hain: 2024 mein girl victims wale 43,313 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Pattern wahan bhi yahi hai. POCSO ke tahat bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke cases mein conviction rate 30.2% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jahan victim bachchi hai, wahan das mein se kareeb teen trials conviction par khatm hote hain. Jahan woh adult hai, wahan chaar mein se ek se bhi kam.

## Victims kaun hain: 18 se 30 saal ki women

2024 mein rape head ke tahat record hui 29,742 victims mein se 28,950 adult thi, aur inmein se 19,489 ki umar 18 se 30 saal thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sirf 792 victims 18 se kam ki thi. Yeh number POCSO wale alag hisaab ki wajah se chhota hai; isse yeh nahi pata chalta ki kitne bachchon ka rape hua.

Yeh college, pehli job aur pehle relationships ki umar hai. Accused shayad hi koi stranger hota hai: 2024 mein darj rape cases mein se 96.8% mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sabse bada group, 13,879 cases, friends, online friends, shaadi ke bahaane wale live-in partners ya separated husbands ka tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Jab dono ek doosre ko jaante the, toh defence ko yeh kehne ki zaroorat nahi padti ki pehchaan mein galti hui. Woh keh sakta hai ki usne haan kaha tha.

## Jab sawaal consent ka ho: myths yahin se andar aate hain

18 se kam ki girl ke case mein law yeh argument hi khatm kar deta hai. Section 63 kehta hai ki act rape hai "with or without her consent", yaani uski consent ho ya na ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur POCSO trial mein Section 29 ke tahat court ko yeh maan kar chalna hota hai ki accused ne offence kiya, jab tak ulta saabit na ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Trial do facts par tikta hai: act hua ya nahi, aur uski umar kya thi.

Woman ke case mein prosecution ko yeh bhi saabit karna hota hai ki usne consent nahi di, aur aksar baat aise kamre ki hoti hai jahan koi gawah nahi tha. Law sirf aggravated cases mein yeh presume karta hai ki consent nahi thi, jaise police officer, public servant, relative, guardian ya hospital staff ke haathon rape [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Baaki sabke paas yeh sahara nahi hota.

Sochiye, Pune ki ek 24 saal ki woman ek party ke paanch din baad apne colleague ke khilaf report karti hai. Witness box mein sawaal apne aap ban jaate hain. Woh uske flat par kyun gayi? Chillayi kyun nahi? Injuries kyun nahi hain? Itne din kyun ruki? Inmein se ek bhi sawaal yeh nahi poochhta ki us aadmi ne kya kiya. Har sawaal use ek kalpanik 'asli' victim se naapta hai, jo ladti hai, cheekhti hai aur seedhe police station bhaagti hai.

Is gap mein kitna hissa kamzor evidence ka hai aur kitna soch ka? Data yeh nahi bata sakta: NCRB verdicts chhaapta hai, unki wajah nahi. Kuch hissa evidence ka zaroor hoga: consent wala trial ek insaan ke us bayaan par tikta hai jo ek private pal ke baare mein hai, aur 2024 ke end mein 1,85,785 rape cases pending the, isliye us bayaan ki jaanch aksar bahut baad mein hoti hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin woh sawaal jo shaq paida karte hain, wahi shaq hain jin par law courts ko chalne se mana karta hai.

## Law aur Supreme Court kya kehte hain

Section 63 consent ko us specific act ke liye "unequivocal voluntary agreement" batata hai, jo words, gestures ya kisi bhi aur tarah ke communication se zaahir ki jaaye. Saath hi yeh kehta hai ki agar woman physically resist nahi karti, toh sirf is wajah se use consenting nahi maana jaayega [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. "Woh rok sakti thi" aisa koi defence statute mein nahi hai.

Uska past bhi sawaalon se bahar hai. Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam ke tahat survivor ka character ya previous sexual experience consent ke sawaal ke liye irrelevant hai, aur rape trial mein consent saabit karne ke liye usse cross-examination mein uske "general immoral character" ya sexual history ke baare mein nahi poochha ja sakta [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Supreme Court ki handbook in beliefs ko reject karti hai ki der se report karne wali woman jhooth bol rahi hai, ki 'asli' survivor lagataar roti rehti hai, aur ki women ke jhoothe allegations lagane ke chances bahut zyada hote hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

> "There is no 'correct' or 'appropriate' way in which a survivor or victim behaves." (Supreme Court ki judges ke liye handbook, 2023)

Yeh tables sirf women aur girls ko ginti hain, kyunki Section 63 rape ko aisa act batata hai jo ek man ek woman ke khilaf karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Adult male aur transgender survivors inmein kahin nahi dikhte.

## Aise trial ki taiyaari jo consent par tika ho

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Lekin jis survivor ko pata ho ki trial mein dabaav kahan padega, woh taiyaari kar sakti hai.

Sabse pehle medical care lijiye. Har hospital ko, public ho ya private, free treatment dena hota hai, aur police ko jaankari milne ke 24 ghante ke andar survivor ko medical examination ke liye bhejna hota hai, sirf uski consent se [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jaldi jaane se evidence bachta hai. Der se jaane se complaint khatm nahi ho jaati.

Jo hua use sequence mein likh lijiye, jab tak yaad taaza hai. Har message, call log aur photo sambhaal kar rakhiye, pehle ya baad ke friendly messages bhi. Context consent nahi hota, aur aapke lawyer ko sab kuch dekhna chahiye.

Survivor ka statement magistrate record karta hai, jahan tak ho sake woman magistrate, aur trial in camera, yaani band kamre mein hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar defence consent dikhane ke liye uski sexual history ke baare mein poochhe, toh prosecutor object kar sakta hai, kyunki law ise rokta hai.

Verdict hi akela nateeja nahi hai. Acquittal ka matlab hai ki court ko reasonable doubt se pare yakeen nahi hua, yeh nahi ki usne jhooth bola. Legal Services Authority ke zariye compensation acquittal ke baad bhi mil sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Kisi bhi stage par support ke liye Women Helpline par call kijiye.

being-gay-not-illness-medicine-law.en:
Imagine a 22-year-old in Kanpur who tells his mother he is gay. Within a fortnight the family has three plans. An uncle knows a psychiatrist. A neighbour swears by a course of "hormone" tablets. An aunt has a rishta from Lucknow, because marriage "settles" boys. All three plans rest on one belief: that what he told them is a symptom. Over the past decade India's courts and its medical regulator have refused to treat it as one, and Parliament has barred mental health care from discriminating over it.

## The 'illness' families still believe in

The belief usually arrives as concern. "It is a phase." "It is the hormones." "One good doctor will sort it out." The words change, but the model underneath is the same: an illness, with a cause to find and a cure to buy.

It survives partly because it is the gentlest explanation a frightened family can reach for. A sick child can be treated, and nobody has to be blamed. It also survives because, for most of living memory, the state said something harsher: that gay relationships were a crime. We found no national data on how many Indian families look for a "cure".

## From 'against the order of nature' to Navtej, 2018

Section 377 of the colonial-era Indian Penal Code punished "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" with up to life imprisonment [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]], and for most of its life it covered consensual sex between adults of the same sex. A law that calls an act "against the order of nature" does more than threaten jail. What the statute called unnatural, the family learnt to call abnormal.

The label did not fall in one move. On 2 July 2009 the Delhi High Court decriminalised consensual gay sex. On 11 December 2013 the Supreme Court reversed that verdict, and gay sex was a crime again for nearly five years [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. On 6 September 2018, a five-judge Supreme Court bench in *Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India* unanimously read down Section 377, decriminalising consensual sex between adults of the same sex while keeping non-consensual acts and bestiality as crimes [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Consider the 2013 reversal from inside a home. A son who came out in 2010 was, by the end of 2013, once again living under a law that made his relationships a crime. A myth lives comfortably on that kind of signal. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024, has no Section 377 at all. Nothing replaced it, which has left sexual assault of adult men and transgender people without a specific offence [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## What Indian medicine and law now say

The World Health Organization does not classify being gay, lesbian or bisexual as a mental disorder [[who-sexual-health]]. Older medical books treated it as a problem, and the idea has outlived them. Indian law has moved the same way on three fronts.

**Parliament.** Section 21 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 says there shall be no discrimination in mental health care "on any basis including gender, sex, sexual orientation, religion, culture, caste, social or political beliefs, class or disability" [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. Sexual orientation sits in that list beside religion and caste, as a fact about a patient that must not change the care they get. Parliament wrote that in 2017, while the 2013 ruling still made gay sex a crime.

**The courts.** In June 2021 the Madras High Court, hearing a petition from a lesbian couple, directed that any attempt to medically "cure" or change the sexual orientation or gender identity of LGBTQIA+ people be prohibited, with action against the professionals involved, up to withdrawal of their licence [[livelaw-madras-hc-sushma-2021]].

**The regulator.** After that court directed it to act, the National Medical Commission wrote to all state medical councils on 25 August 2022, declaring that conducting "conversion therapy" on LGBTQIA+ persons is professional misconduct [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]]. For the psychiatrist the uncle knows, the "treatment" the family wants is now a reason to be reported to his medical council.

The limits are real: this is a rule of professional conduct for registered medical practitioners, so it does not reach faith healers or unregistered "counsellors".

## What 'conversion' attempts do to people

Being gay is not an illness, so there is nothing for these attempts to cure. What they produce is harm. WHO lists stigma, discrimination and exclusion among the things that put adolescents at greater risk of mental health conditions, and names those from sexual minority backgrounds among the groups at risk [[who-adolescent-mh]]. A "cure" delivers all three, from the people a young person depends on most.

Each session, tablet or ritual tells the person that their family's acceptance depends on changing something that will not change. When the attempt fails, the failure is treated as theirs. The treatment ends; the shame stays.

Marriage is offered as a "cure" too, and it harms two people. It changes nobody's orientation. It can tie a second person, who may be told nothing, into a marriage built on a secret.

## Support instead of a cure

For parents, the fear is real: of relatives, of a child growing old alone, of what the neighbours will say. A counsellor can help a family with that fear, and a young person with anxiety or depression if they have it. That is the legitimate work here. Before the first session, ask whether the professional tries to change orientation. If the answer is yes, leave.

For the young person: you are not sick. This is general information, not legal advice, but if a registered doctor offers a "cure", a written complaint can go to the state medical council, citing the NMC letter of 25 August 2022. If you are being confined, threatened or forced, call 112, or the Child Helpline on 1098 if you are under 18. If any of this has left you with thoughts of ending your life, call Tele-MANAS on 14416; it is free and open round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

The diagnosis was always wrong. Indian law took from 2009 to 2018 to stop treating gay relationships as a crime, and the medical regulator now treats the "cure" as the misconduct. A family can get there faster.
being-gay-not-illness-medicine-law.hg:
Socho, Kanpur ka ek 22 saal ka ladka apni mummy ko batata hai ki woh gay hai. Do hafte ke andar family ke paas teen plans ready hain. Ek uncle kisi psychiatrist ko jaante hain. Ek padosi "hormone" ki goliyon ke course ki kasam khaata hai. Aur ek bua ke paas Lucknow ka rishta hai, kyunki shaadi ladkon ko "settle" kar deti hai. Teeno plans ek hi belief par tike hain: ki usne jo bataya, woh ek symptom hai. Pichhle das saal mein India ke courts aur medical regulator ne ise symptom maanne se inkaar kiya hai, aur Parliament ne mental health care mein iski wajah se discrimination ko mana kiya hai.

## Woh 'bimari' jisme families aaj bhi yakeen karti hain

Yeh belief aksar fikar ban kar aata hai. "Yeh ek phase hai." "Hormones ki wajah se hai." "Ek achha doctor sab theek kar dega." Shabd badalte rehte hain, par neeche ka model wahi rehta hai: ek bimari, jiska cause dhoondhna hai aur cure kharidna hai.

Yeh belief kuch had tak isliye tika hai kyunki ek dari hui family ke liye yeh sabse naram explanation hai. Bimaar bachche ka ilaaj ho sakta hai, aur kisi ko dosh nahi dena padta. Yeh isliye bhi tika hai kyunki zyadatar logon ki yaad mein state isse bhi sakht baat kehta raha: ki gay relationships crime hain. Kitni Indian families "cure" dhoondhti hain, is par humein koi national data nahi mila.

## 'Against the order of nature' se Navtej, 2018 tak

Colonial daur ke Indian Penal Code ka Section 377 "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" ke liye umar qaid tak ki saza deta tha [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]], aur apni zyadatar zindagi mein yeh same-sex adults ke beech consensual sex ko bhi cover karta raha. Jo law kisi act ko "against the order of nature" kehta hai, woh sirf jail ki dhamki nahi deta. Jise law ne unnatural kaha, use family ne abnormal kehna seekh liya.

Yeh label ek jhatke mein nahi gira. 2 July 2009 ko Delhi High Court ne consensual gay sex ko decriminalise kiya. 11 December 2013 ko Supreme Court ne woh faisla palat diya, aur gay sex lagbhag paanch saal ke liye phir se crime ban gaya [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. 6 September 2018 ko Supreme Court ki paanch-judge bench ne *Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India* mein unanimously Section 377 ko read down kiya: same-sex adults ke beech consensual sex decriminalise hua, jabki non-consensual acts aur bestiality crime bane rahe [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

2013 ke us palatne ko ek ghar ke andar se dekho. Jis bete ne 2010 mein come out kiya tha, woh 2013 ke end tak phir se ek aise law ke neeche jee raha tha jo uske relationships ko crime maanta tha. Aise signal par myth aaraam se zinda rehta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, jisne 1 July 2024 ko IPC ki jagah li, usme Section 377 hai hi nahi. Uski jagah kuch nahi aaya, jiski wajah se adult men aur transgender logon par sexual assault ke liye koi specific offence nahi bacha [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Indian medicine aur law ab kya kehte hain

World Health Organization gay, lesbian ya bisexual hone ko mental disorder nahi maanta [[who-sexual-health]]. Purani medical kitaabein ise problem ki tarah dekhti thin, aur yeh idea un kitaabon se zyada lamba jee gaya. Indian law teen moorchon par isi disha mein badha hai.

**Parliament.** Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 ka Section 21 kehta hai ki mental health care mein "on any basis including gender, sex, sexual orientation, religion, culture, caste, social or political beliefs, class or disability" koi discrimination nahi hoga [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. Is list mein sexual orientation religion aur caste ke saath baithi hai, yaani patient ke baare mein ek aisa fact jiski wajah se uski care nahi badalni chahiye. Parliament ne yeh 2017 mein likha, jab 2013 wala faisla gay sex ko abhi bhi crime maan raha tha.

**Courts.** June 2021 mein Madras High Court ne ek lesbian couple ki petition sunte hue direction di ki LGBTQIA+ logon ki sexual orientation ya gender identity ko medically "cure" karne ya badalne ki har koshish prohibit ki jaaye, aur isme shaamil professionals par action ho, jo licence withdraw hone tak ja sakta hai [[livelaw-madras-hc-sushma-2021]].

**Regulator.** Usi court ke kehne ke baad National Medical Commission ne 25 August 2022 ko saari state medical councils ko letter likha ki LGBTQIA+ persons par "conversion therapy" karna professional misconduct hai [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]]. Uncle jis psychiatrist ko jaante hain, uske liye woh "treatment" jo family chahti hai, ab apni medical council mein report hone ki wajah hai.

Limits bhi asli hain: yeh registered medical practitioners ke professional conduct ka rule hai, isliye faith healers ya unregistered "counsellors" tak nahi pahunchta.

## 'Conversion' ki koshishein logon ke saath kya karti hain

Gay hona bimari nahi hai, isliye in koshishon ke paas 'theek' karne ko kuch hai hi nahi. Inse jo milta hai woh nuksaan hai. WHO ke mutabik stigma, discrimination aur exclusion un cheezon mein hain jo adolescents mein mental health conditions ka risk badhati hain, aur jin groups ko woh zyada risk mein ginta hai unmein sexual minority backgrounds ke adolescents bhi hain [[who-adolescent-mh]]. Ek "cure" yeh teeno cheezein ek saath deta hai, aur unhi logon ke haathon jin par ek young insaan sabse zyada depend karta hai.

Har session, har goli ya har ritual us insaan se yahi kehta hai ki family ka acceptance ek aisi cheez badalne par tika hai jo badlegi nahi. Jab koshish fail hoti hai, toh failure usi ke sar daal diya jaata hai. Treatment khatam ho jaata hai; sharam reh jaati hai.

Shaadi ko bhi "cure" ki tarah offer kiya jaata hai, aur isse do logon ka nuksaan hota hai. Isse kisi ki orientation nahi badalti. Yeh ek doosre insaan ko, jise shaayad kuch bataya hi na jaaye, ek secret par khadi shaadi mein baandh sakti hai.

## Cure ki jagah support

Parents ka darr asli hai: rishtedaaron ka, bachche ke akele boodhe hone ka, padosi kya kahenge iska. Counsellor is darr mein family ki madad kar sakta hai, aur agar young insaan ko anxiety ya depression hai toh usme uski. Yahan yahi jaayaz kaam hai. Pehle session se pehle poocho ki kya professional orientation badalne ki koshish karta hai. Jawab haan ho, toh wahan se nikal jao.

Aur young insaan ke liye: tum bimaar nahi ho. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi, par agar koi registered doctor "cure" offer kare, toh NMC ke 25 August 2022 wale letter ka hawala dete hue state medical council ko written complaint di ja sakti hai. Agar tumhe band kiya ja raha hai, dhamkaya ja raha hai ya zabardasti ki ja rahi hai, toh 112 par call karo, aur 18 se kam ho toh Child Helpline 1098 par. Agar in sab ki wajah se apni zindagi khatam karne ke khayal aa rahe hain, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 par call karo; yeh free hai aur chaubees ghante khula rehta hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Diagnosis hamesha se galat tha. Indian law ko gay relationships ko crime maanna band karne mein 2009 se 2018 tak ka time laga, aur medical regulator ab "cure" ko hi misconduct maanta hai. Ek family wahan isse kaafi jaldi pahunch sakti hai.

boys-dont-cry-costs-of-silence.en:
Imagine a seven-year-old in Indore who falls off his cycle and walks home with a bleeding knee. Before anyone cleans the wound, an uncle tells him to stop crying: "Ladki hai kya?" Are you a girl? Nobody in the room thinks of this as teaching. But the boy has just been taught a rule he will hear for the next fifteen years, from fathers, coaches, seniors and films: fear and tears are for girls.

The rule sounds harmless. Its cost shows up in three sets of Indian data that are rarely read together: boys who are sexually abused, men who die by suicide, and men who are violent at home.

## The lesson every boy learns

The rule is rarely stated in full. It arrives as "mard ko dard nahi hota", as "be a man", or as laughter when a boy flinches. What it teaches is not courage. It teaches that pain must be hidden, that asking for help is failure, and that anger is the one feeling a man may show.

Researchers have measured how far such ideas travel. In 2014 the International Center for Research on Women (ICRW) and UNFPA surveyed 9,205 men and 3,158 women in seven Indian states. They classified 32% of the men as holding 'rigid' masculinity, 45% as moderate and only 23% as gender-equitable [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. About one man in three sat at the hard end of that scale.

## Hurt and silent: boys who are abused

The first cost is paid by boys who are hurt. In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, boys were 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse and girls 47.06%; 9 of the 13 states surveyed found a higher share among boys [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The study was not a random sample and included many working and street children, who are disproportionately boys, so it is not a national rate. It does show that boys are abused in large numbers.

Police records show almost none of them. Of the 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault recorded under the POCSO Act in 2024, 43,675 were girls and 892 were boys [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is about 2 boys in every 100 victims.

The law is not the barrier. POCSO protects every child under 18, boy or girl [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The barrier is what a boy must admit in order to use it: that someone overpowered him, that he was afraid, that he could not handle it alone. Every part of that admission breaks the rule he was raised on. In the 2007 study, 72.1% of children who had been sexually assaulted told no one, and only 3.4% went to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. A boy carries an added fear: being laughed at, or being asked why he did not fight back.

After 18, the law itself repeats the lesson. Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines rape as an act by a man against a woman, so an adult man cannot legally be a victim of rape in India [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Men who do not ask for help

The second cost comes later. Men made up 71.8% of India's suicide victims in 2022, according to the National Crime Records Bureau, and about 68% of those men were married [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]].

Suicide never has a single cause, and a police record cannot say what any one man was carrying. What the figure does show is who reaches that point without help. The same silence shows in how rarely men's distress reaches treatment. In the National Mental Health Survey 2015-16, alcohol use disorder affected 9% of men against 0.5% of women, and the treatment gap for alcohol use disorders was 86% [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. A family sees a man who drinks every night as a man with a bad habit. It rarely sees a man in distress.

If you are struggling, or thinking about ending your life, call Tele-MANAS on 14416. It is the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock helpline [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. You do not have to explain why you waited.

## From silence to violence

The third cost is paid by women. In the ICRW-UNFPA survey, 60% of men said they had acted violently against a wife or partner at some point, a count that includes emotional and economic violence. Men who had frequently faced discrimination as children were four times more likely to be violent to a partner than men who never had [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

A boy who is hurt and forbidden to say so does not stop hurting. He is left with the one feeling the rule allows, and the people at home receive it. This explains a pattern; it excuses nothing. A hard childhood does not make violence inevitable, and the violence is never the woman's fault.

The same study found that the lesson can be taught differently. Men raised in families where fathers did household chores were two times more likely to hold gender-equitable attitudes [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

## What to say to a boy instead

Change the sentence, not the boy. When he cries, say "that hurt, tell me what happened" instead of "stop crying". When he is scared, tell him that brave people are scared too.

Tell boys, as plainly as girls are told, that nobody may touch them in ways that feel wrong, that this happens to boys too, and that it is never their fault, even if they did not fight back.

If a boy tells you he was abused, believe him, and do not ask why he did not resist. Do not promise to keep it secret: under Sections 19 and 21 of POCSO, anyone who knows of a sexual offence against a child must report it, and failing to report can mean up to 6 months in prison or a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Promise instead that you will stay with him through what comes next. (This is general information, not legal advice.)

With a friend who has gone quiet or is drinking more, ask directly how he is, and listen without fixing or joking. Fathers can do the most with the least: cook a meal, apologise when wrong, and say "I was scared" where a son can hear it.
boys-dont-cry-costs-of-silence.hg:
Imagine kijiye Indore ka ek saat saal ka ladka. Woh cycle se girta hai aur chhile hue, khoon behte ghutne ke saath ghar aata hai. Koi chot saaf kare, usse pehle ek uncle keh dete hain: "Ro mat. Ladki hai kya?" Kamre mein kisi ko nahi lagta ki yeh koi sabak hai. Par ladke ne abhi-abhi ek rule seekh liya hai, jo woh agle pandrah saal papa, coach, seniors aur filmon se sunta rahega: darr aur aansu ladkiyon ke liye hote hain.

Rule sunne mein harmless lagta hai. Iski keemat India ke teen alag data sets mein dikhti hai, jinhe shayad hi kabhi saath padha jaata hai: ladke jinka sexual abuse hota hai, men jo suicide se marte hain, aur men jo ghar mein violence karte hain.

## Woh sabak jo har ladka seekhta hai

Yeh rule poora shayad hi kabhi bola jaata hai. Yeh "mard ko dard nahi hota" ban kar aata hai, "mard ban" ban kar, ya us hansi ki shakal mein jo ladke ke sehem jaane par sunai deti hai. Yeh himmat nahi sikhata. Yeh sikhata hai ki dard chhupana hai, help maangna haar hai, aur gussa hi woh ek feeling hai jo mard dikha sakta hai.

Researchers ne naapa hai ki aisi soch kitni door tak jaati hai. 2014 mein International Center for Research on Women (ICRW) aur UNFPA ne saat Indian states mein 9,205 men aur 3,158 women ka survey kiya. Unhone 32% men ko 'rigid' masculinity wala, 45% ko moderate aur sirf 23% ko gender-equitable maana [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. Yaani lagbhag har teen mein se ek aadmi us scale ke sabse sakht sire par tha.

## Chot khaye aur chup: ladke jinka abuse hota hai

Pehli keemat woh ladke chukate hain jinhe chot pahunchti hai. Government ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein jin bachchon ne sexual abuse report kiya, unmein 52.94% ladke the aur 47.06% ladkiyan; survey hue 13 states mein se 9 mein ladkon ka share zyada tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Yeh study random sample nahi thi aur ismein kaam karne wale aur sadak par rehne wale bahut bachche shamil the, jinmein ladkon ki sankhya kaafi zyada hoti hai, isliye yeh national rate nahi hai. Par itna zaroor dikhata hai ki ladkon ka abuse badi sankhya mein hota hai.

Police records mein yeh ladke lagbhag dikhte hi nahi. 2024 mein POCSO Act ke under penetrative sexual assault ke 44,567 child victims record hue; inmein 43,675 ladkiyan thi aur 892 ladke [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani har 100 victims mein lagbhag 2 ladke.

Rukawat law nahi hai. POCSO 18 saal se kam ke har bachche ko protect karta hai, ladka ho ya ladki [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Rukawat woh hai jo ladke ko law tak pahunchne ke liye kabool karna padta hai: ki kisi ne us par zor chalaya, ki woh darr gaya tha, ki woh akele sambhal nahi paaya. Is kabool karne ka har hissa us rule ko todta hai jis par woh bada hua hai. 2007 ki study mein jin bachchon ka sexual assault hua tha, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya aur sirf 3.4% police tak pahunche [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Ladke ke saath ek darr aur juda hota hai: log hansenge, ya poochenge ki tune muqabla kyun nahi kiya.

18 ke baad law khud wahi sabak dohrata hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 63 rape ko aise define karta hai ki yeh ek man karta hai aur ek woman ke saath hota hai. Isliye India mein ek adult aadmi legally rape ka victim ho hi nahi sakta [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Men jo help nahi maangte

Doosri keemat baad mein saamne aati hai. National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ke mutabik 2022 mein India ke suicide victims mein 71.8% men the, aur in men mein se lagbhag 68% shaadi-shuda the [[ncrb-adsi-2022-hindi-snapshots]].

Suicide ki kabhi koi ek wajah nahi hoti, aur police record yeh nahi bata sakta ki koi ek aadmi andar kya dho raha tha. Yeh figure itna zaroor dikhata hai ki us mod tak bina help ke kaun pahunchta hai. Yahi chuppi is baat mein bhi dikhti hai ki men ki takleef kitni kam baar treatment tak pahunchti hai. National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 mein alcohol use disorder 9% men mein tha, jabki women mein 0.5%; aur alcohol use disorders ka treatment gap 86% tha [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Family ko har raat peene wala aadmi 'buri aadat wala aadmi' dikhta hai. Takleef mein dooba aadmi use shayad hi dikhta hai.

Agar aap struggle kar rahe hain, ya apni zindagi khatam karne ke khayal aa rahe hain, toh Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call kijiye. Yeh Health Ministry ki free helpline hai aur chaubees ghante chalti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Aapko yeh samjhana nahi padega ki aapne itni der kyun ki.

## Chuppi se violence tak

Teesri keemat aurtein chukati hain. ICRW-UNFPA survey mein 60% men ne kaha ki unhone kabhi na kabhi apni wife ya partner ke saath violence ki hai; is ginti mein emotional aur economic violence bhi shamil hai.
