Jin men ne bachpan mein baar-baar discrimination jhela tha, unke partner par violence karne ka chance un men se chaar guna zyada tha jinhone yeh kabhi nahi jhela [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

Jis ladke ko chot lagi ho aur use bolne ki ijaazat na ho, uska dard ruk nahi jaata. Uske paas wahi ek feeling bachti hai jiski rule ijaazat deta hai, aur woh ghar ke logon par utarti hai. Yeh ek pattern ko samjhata hai; kisi cheez ko maaf nahi karta. Mushkil bachpan violence ko tay nahi kar deta, aur violence kabhi aurat ki galti nahi hoti.

Usi study mein yeh bhi mila ki sabak alag tarah se sikhaya ja sakta hai. Jin families mein papa ghar ka kaam karte the, wahan pale men mein gender-equitable soch hone ka chance do guna tha [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

## Ladke se iski jagah kya kahein

Ladke ko nahi, apna sentence badliye. Jab woh roye, toh "rona band kar" ki jagah kahiye "chot lagi na, bata kya hua". Jab woh dare, toh use bataiye ki bahadur log bhi darte hain.

Ladkon ko utne hi saaf shabdon mein bataiye jitna ladkiyon ko bataya jaata hai: koi bhi unhe aise touch nahi kar sakta jo galat lage, yeh ladkon ke saath bhi hota hai, aur yeh kabhi unki galti nahi hoti, chahe unhone muqabla na kiya ho.

Agar koi ladka bataye ki uske saath abuse hua hai, toh uski baat par yakeen kijiye, aur yeh mat poochiye ki usne roka kyun nahi. Yeh promise mat kijiye ki baat secret rahegi: POCSO ke Sections 19 aur 21 ke under, jise bhi bachche ke khilaf sexual offence ka pata ho, use report karna zaroori hai, aur report na karne par 6 mahine tak ki jail ya fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Iski jagah yeh promise kijiye ki aage jo bhi hoga, aap uske saath rahenge. (Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.)

Jo dost chup-chup rehne laga hai ya zyada peene laga hai, usse seedha poochiye ki woh kaisa hai, aur bina solution thope, bina mazaak udaye suniye. Papa sabse kam mein sabse zyada kar sakte hain: khana banaiye, galti ho toh sorry boliye, aur "main darr gaya tha" wahan kahiye jahan beta sun sake.

crimes-against-women-fall-2024-misread.en:
When the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) released Crime in India 2024 on 6 May 2026 [[theprint-ncrb-cii-2024-release-2026]], one line was ready-made for a headline. Police had registered 4,41,534 crimes against women in 2024, 1.5% fewer than the 4,48,211 of 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. The rate fell too, from 66.2 to 64.6 cases per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Read quickly, it sounds as if Indian women became a little safer. Read slowly, the dip says almost nothing about safety, and a great deal about police stations.

## The headline: a 1.5% fall

Every one of those 4,41,534 cases is an FIR: a complaint that a woman, or someone on her behalf, managed to get registered. NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence. Violence that never reaches a police station is not in the count, and that is most of it. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 77% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone, and of those who did seek help, only 6% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

So the national figure mixes two things: how much violence there is, and how easily it gets written down. A 1.5% change can come from either, and the total cannot tell you which.

## A flat line for three years

Step back and the line barely moves. NCRB counted 4,45,256 crimes against women in 2022, 4,48,211 in 2023 and 4,41,534 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The big jump came earlier, from 3,71,503 in 2020 to 4,28,278 in 2021 [[ncrb-cii-2022]]. Since then registrations have sat on a plateau of about 4.4 to 4.5 lakh a year. A 1.5% wobble on a plateau is not a trend.

Look inside the wobble and it shrinks further. Rajasthan's registrations fell from 45,450 in 2023 to 36,563 in 2024, a drop of 19.6% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That one state's fall is bigger than India's entire fall: take Rajasthan out, and registrations in the rest of the country went up slightly. By category the pattern repeats. Cases of cruelty by husband or relatives fell from 1,33,676 in 2023 to 1,20,227 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], again more than the national drop, so the other categories together rose.

2024 was also a changeover year: offences before 1 July were registered under the Indian Penal Code and later ones under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, so NCRB's tables carry both [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]].

## Assam down, Bihar and Tamil Nadu up

Under the flat national line, states moved hard in opposite directions.

| State | 2023 | 2024 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rajasthan | 45,450 | 36,563 | −19.6% |
| Assam | 12,070 | 10,546 | down; 29,046 in 2021 |
| Bihar | 22,952 | 27,359 | +19.2% |
| Tamil Nadu | 8,943 | 11,363 | +27.1% |
| India | 4,48,211 | 4,41,534 | −1.5% |

Assam's registered crimes against women fell from 29,046 in 2021 to 14,148 in 2022, 12,070 in 2023 and 10,546 in 2024, a drop of almost two-thirds in three years [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Rajasthan's rate, even after its fall, was 91.3 per lakh women, still the fifth-highest in India [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Going the other way, Bihar's registrations rose 19.2% in a single year, though its rate of 44.1 per lakh women stayed below the national 64.6 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Tamil Nadu's jumped 27.1%, while its rate, 29.4, remained among the lowest in the country [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Did Assam become two-thirds safer while Tamil Nadu grew more dangerous? The national health survey points the other way. In NFHS-6 (2023-24), Bihar had the highest share of ever-married women reporting physical or sexual violence by a husband, 36.1%, and Tamil Nadu was joint third at 28.5% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Where many women describe violence to a surveyor but few reach a police station, more registrations may mean more women being heard. The tables cannot settle that for any one state, and our map of domestic-violence silence compares the two sources state by state.

## Registration is not crime: NCRB's own warning

NCRB says so itself. Its word of caution states that "rise in crime" and "increase in registration of crime by police" are "clearly two different things", and that higher numbers may follow citizen-centric steps such as e-FIR facilities or women's help desks [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Comparing states on these figures alone, it adds, "will be too simplistic and is best avoided".

Research on India backs the warning. After states reserved a third of local council seats for women, documented crimes against women rose 46%, driven mainly by more reporting rather than more crime [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]]. All-women police stations were associated with a 29% rise in police reports of crimes against women, with no change in killings of women [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]].

In this data, then, a rise can be good news and a fall can be bad news. By March 2025, India had set up 14,658 women help desks in police stations [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. If they make stations easier to walk into, registrations should rise. A falling total does not prove the desks failed, but it cannot be read as proof of safety either.

## Better ways to measure safety

Registration is where a case starts. The better questions follow it.

What happens after the FIR? Police filed charge-sheets in 77.2% of the crime-against-women cases they disposed of in 2024, from 54.1% in Rajasthan, the lowest of any State or UT, to 95.9% in Mizoram [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rajasthan police also closed 12,217 such cases as "false", a third of all such closures in India; that is a police label after investigation, not a court's finding [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Does anyone get convicted? Courts convicted in 25.7% of crime-against-women trials completed in 2024, and 24,32,527 cases, 92.1% of those before the courts, were still pending at year-end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Among large states, conviction rates ran from 76.6% in Uttar Pradesh to 1.6% in West Bengal; Assam, whose registrations fell so sharply, convicted in 8.1% of trials [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

What do women say when asked in private? NFHS-6 found 22.3% of ever-married women aged 18-49 reporting violence by a husband, down from 29.2% in NFHS-5 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Experts quoted by Deccan Herald doubted that fall, saying women may not disclose abuse to a surveyor in front of family members [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]]. Even the better measure needs privacy to work.

Next time a headline says crimes against women fell, ask three things. Fell where? Registered by whom? And what happened to the cases that were registered?
crimes-against-women-fall-2024-misread.hg:
National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ne 6 May 2026 ko Crime in India 2024 release kiya [[theprint-ncrb-cii-2024-release-2026]], toh usmein ek line headline ke liye bani-banayi thi. Police ne 2024 mein crimes against women ke 4,41,534 cases register kiye, jo 2023 ke 4,48,211 se 1.5% kam the [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Rate bhi gira, har ek lakh women par 66.2 se 64.6 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Jaldi mein padhiye toh lagta hai ki Indian women thodi zyada safe ho gayi hain. Dhyan se padhiye toh yeh giravat safety ke baare mein lagbhag kuch nahi batati, aur police stations ke baare mein bahut kuch batati hai.

## Headline: 1.5% ki giravat

In 4,41,534 cases mein se har ek case ek FIR hai: ek complaint, jise koi woman, ya uski taraf se koi aur, register karwa paya. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke neeche. Jo violence police station tak pahunchti hi nahi, woh is count mein nahi hai, aur zyada tar violence wahi hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 77% women ne na kabhi madad maangi thi, na kisi ko bataya tha, aur jinhone madad maangi, unmein se sirf 6% police ke paas gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Isliye national figure mein do cheezein mili hui hain: violence kitni hai, aur woh kitni aasani se likhi jaati hai. 1.5% ka badlaav dono mein se kisi se bhi aa sakta hai, aur total yeh nahi bata sakta ki kis se aaya.

## Teen saal se ek seedhi line

Thoda peechhe hat kar dekhiye toh line mushkil se hilti hai. NCRB ne crimes against women 2022 mein 4,45,256, 2023 mein 4,48,211 aur 2024 mein 4,41,534 gine [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bada jump isse pehle aaya tha, 2020 ke 3,71,503 se 2021 ke 4,28,278 tak [[ncrb-cii-2022]]. Tab se registrations saal ke lagbhag 4.4 se 4.5 lakh ke plateau par tike hain. Plateau par 1.5% ka hilna koi trend nahi hai.

Is hilne ke andar jhaankiye toh yeh aur chhota ho jaata hai. Rajasthan ke registrations 2023 ke 45,450 se girkar 2024 mein 36,563 reh gaye, yaani 19.6% ki giravat [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Akele is ek state ki giravat India ki poori giravat se badi hai: Rajasthan ko hata dijiye, toh baaki desh mein registrations thode badhe hain. Category ke hisaab se bhi yahi pattern dikhta hai. Pati ya rishtedaaron ki cruelty ke cases 2023 ke 1,33,676 se girkar 2024 mein 1,20,227 reh gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh bhi national drop se zyada hai, yaani baaki categories milakar badhi hain.

2024 badlaav ka saal bhi tha: 1 July se pehle ke offences Indian Penal Code ke under register hue aur uske baad ke Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke under, isliye NCRB ki tables mein dono hain [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]].

## Assam neeche, Bihar aur Tamil Nadu upar

Seedhi national line ke neeche states zor se ulti dishaon mein hile.

| State | 2023 | 2024 | Badlaav |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rajasthan | 45,450 | 36,563 | −19.6% |
| Assam | 12,070 | 10,546 | neeche; 2021 mein 29,046 |
| Bihar | 22,952 | 27,359 | +19.2% |
| Tamil Nadu | 8,943 | 11,363 | +27.1% |
| India | 4,48,211 | 4,41,534 | −1.5% |

Assam mein registered crimes against women 2021 ke 29,046 se girkar 2022 mein 14,148, 2023 mein 12,070 aur 2024 mein 10,546 reh gaye, yaani teen saal mein lagbhag do-tihai ki giravat [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Rajasthan ka rate, giravat ke baad bhi, har ek lakh women par 91.3 tha, India mein ab bhi paanchva sabse zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Doosri taraf, Bihar ke registrations ek hi saal mein 19.2% badhe, halaanki uska rate, har ek lakh women par 44.1, national 64.6 se neeche raha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Tamil Nadu ke registrations 27.1% uchhle, jabki uska rate, 29.4, desh ke sabse kam rates mein bana raha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Toh kya Assam do-tihai zyada safe ho gaya aur Tamil Nadu zyada khatarnaak? National health survey ulti taraf ishaara karta hai. NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein pati ki physical ya sexual violence batane wali ever-married women ka sabse bada hissa Bihar mein tha, 36.1%, aur Tamil Nadu 28.5% ke saath joint third tha [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Jahan bahut si women surveyor ko violence ke baare mein batati hain par police station tak kam hi pahunchti hain, wahan zyada registrations ka matlab yeh ho sakta hai ki zyada women ki baat suni ja rahi hai. Tables kisi ek state ke liye yeh faisla nahi kar sakti. Domestic violence ki khamoshi wala hamara map in dono sources ko state-by-state compare karta hai.

## Registration crime nahi hai: NCRB ki apni warning

NCRB khud yahi kehta hai. Uska "word of caution" kehta hai ki "rise in crime" aur "increase in registration of crime by police" "clearly two different things" hain, aur zyada numbers e-FIR facility ya women help desks jaise citizen-centric kadmon ka nateeja ho sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Woh yeh bhi jodta hai ki sirf in figures par states ko compare karna "will be too simplistic and is best avoided".

India par hui research bhi is warning ke saath khadi hai. Jab states ne local councils ki ek-tihai seats women ke liye reserve ki, toh documented crimes against women 46% badhe, aur iski badi wajah zyada crime nahi, zyada reporting thi [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]]. All-women police stations ke saath crimes against women ki police reports mein 29% ki badhat judi mili, jabki women ki hatya ke cases mein koi badlaav nahi aaya [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]].

Yaani is data mein badhat achhi khabar ho sakti hai aur giravat buri khabar. March 2025 tak India ne police stations mein 14,658 women help desks bana liye the [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Agar inse station ke andar jaana aasaan hota hai, toh registrations badhne chahiye. Girta hua total yeh saabit nahi karta ki desks fail hue, par use safety ka saboot bhi nahi maana ja sakta.

## Safety naapne ke behtar tareeke

Registration se case sirf shuru hota hai. Behtar sawaal uske baad ke hain.

FIR ke baad kya hota hai? 2024 mein police ne crimes against women ke jitne cases nipataye, unmein se 77.2% mein charge-sheet file ki. Yeh rate Rajasthan mein 54.1% tha, jo kisi bhi State ya UT mein sabse kam hai, aur Mizoram mein 95.9% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rajasthan police ne aise 12,217 cases "false" bata kar band bhi kiye, jo India ke aise saare closures ka ek-tihai hai; yeh investigation ke baad police ka lagaya hua label hai, court ka faisla nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Kya kisi ko saza hoti hai? 2024 mein poore hue crimes-against-women trials mein se 25.7% mein courts ne convict kiya, aur 24,32,527 cases, yaani courts ke saamne ke cases ka 92.1%, saal ke end mein bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bade states mein conviction rate Uttar Pradesh ke 76.6% se West Bengal ke 1.6% tak gaya; Assam, jiske registrations itni tezi se gire, wahan 8.1% trials mein conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Jab women se akele mein poochha jaata hai, toh woh kya kehti hain? NFHS-6 mein 18-49 saal ki 22.3% ever-married women ne pati ki violence batayi, jo NFHS-5 ke 29.2% se kam hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Deccan Herald se baat karne wale experts ne is giravat par shak jataya; unka kehna tha ki family members ke saamne women shayad surveyor ko abuse ke baare mein na batayein [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]]. Behtar paimaane ko bhi kaam karne ke liye privacy chahiye.

Agli baar koi headline kahe ki crimes against women kam hue, toh teen sawaal poochhiye. Kahan kam hue? Register kisne kiye? Aur jo cases register hue, unka kya hua?

crimes-against-women-not-just-rape.en:
Ask ten people what "crime against women" means and most will describe one scene: a stranger, an empty road, a rape. India's police register describes something else. In 2024, police registered 4,41,534 crimes against women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rape accounted for 29,536 of them, or 6.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. This is not an argument that rape matters less. It is a look at the rest of the register, the part that rarely becomes a headline.

## What we picture when we hear 'crime against women'

The picture is wrong twice. It is wrong about rape itself: in 96.8% of the rape cases registered in 2024, the accused was someone the woman knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And it is wrong about scale: rape was roughly one registered case in every fifteen.

The picture also decides where the effort goes. Families set curfews for daughters, cities put cameras on main roads, and public anger peaks after one terrible case and then fades. A register filled mostly by marriages, girls under 18 and everyday harassment needs a different response.

## The 2024 count, category by category

NCRB's snapshot names the four largest headings. Rape comes after all of them [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]].

| NCRB heading | In plain words | Cases | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cruelty by husband or relatives | Violence or harassment inside a marriage | 1,20,227 | 27.2% |
| Kidnapping and abduction of women | A woman or girl taken away unlawfully | 67,829 | 15.4% |
| POCSO, girl victims | Sexual offences against girls under 18 | 67,809 | 15.4% |
| Assault to outrage modesty | Sexual assault short of rape, often called molestation | 48,303 | 10.9% |
| Rape | Rape registered under the IPC or the BNS | 29,536 | 6.7% |

The four largest headings add up to more than two-thirds of everything registered. The kidnapping line needs care. It bundles very different situations under one heading, and the headline figure does not separate them.

## Cruelty at home: the biggest column

Cruelty by a husband or his relatives produced 1,20,227 cases, about four times the rape count. Sections 85 and 86 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) define it as wilful conduct likely to drive a woman to suicide or cause her grave injury, or harassment to force her or her family to meet unlawful demands for property. The punishment is up to three years in prison and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Imagine a 26-year-old in Kanpur, two years into her marriage. Her in-laws want a car. She is slapped, locked out for a night and told she is a burden. Her mother tells her to adjust. None of this will trend. In law it is cruelty, and if she reaches a police station she becomes one of the 1,20,227.

Most women in her position never get there. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 32% of women aged 18-49 said they had faced physical or sexual violence. Of those women, 77.2% had never sought help or told anyone, and only 14.1% had sought help. Among those who did, just 6% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A household survey and a police register cannot be matched number for number, but they point the same way: towards home.

When cruelty ends in a death, the case moves to another line. Police registered 5,737 dowry-death cases in 2024, with 5,811 victims, about 16 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Girls and everyday harassment

The POCSO line, 67,809 cases with girl victims, is more than twice the rape head [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. It covers sexual harassment and non-penetrative assault as well as rape. Of these cases, 43,313 were penetrative sexual assault on girls, which is child rape filed under a different heading [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. So the 6.7% understates rape itself.

POCSO treats everyone under 18 as a child and protects boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. A boy who is abused is covered by the same Act, but his case sits in the crimes-against-children tables, outside this total.

Then come the offences many families still tell girls to ignore: the hand on the bus, the man who follows her home from tuition, the photo taken without asking. Beyond the 48,303 assault cases, police registered 15,609 cases of sexual harassment, 9,865 of stalking, 8,409 of assault with intent to disrobe and 1,722 of voyeurism [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Together these five offences were registered 83,908 times, roughly 230 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## What one FIR, one offence leaves out

NCRB counts each FIR once, under its gravest charge. Its disclaimer explains that when one FIR lists several offences, only the one carrying the maximum punishment is counted, so the real count under each heading may be different [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A rape that ends in murder appears only as murder with rape. By the same rule, an FIR alleging both cruelty and a dowry death is counted only as a dowry death [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]].

So every share in the table is a share of FIRs sorted by their heaviest charge, not a count of everything done to women. And each FIR needs a woman who reached a police station and an officer who wrote her complaint down.

> The register shows what police record, not everything that happens. Even so, it points away from the empty road and towards the house.

Prevention has to start where the numbers are: inside marriages, with children, and with harassment that gets waved away. If any of this is happening to you, call 112 if you are in danger, or the Child Helpline on 1098 if you are under 18. If you are struggling to cope or having thoughts of suicide, Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free and open round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. This is general information, not legal advice.
crimes-against-women-not-just-rape.hg:
Das logon se poochhiye ki "women ke khilaaf crime" ka matlab kya hai, toh zyada tar ek hi scene bataenge: ek stranger, sunsaan sadak, rape. India ka police register kuch aur dikhata hai. 2024 mein police ne women ke khilaaf 4,41,534 crimes register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inmein rape ke 29,536 cases the, yaani 6.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki rape kam serious hai. Yeh story register ke baaki hisse ko dekhti hai, jo shayad hi kabhi headline banta hai.

## 'Women ke khilaaf crime' sunte hi hum kya imagine karte hain

Yeh picture do jagah galat hai. Pehle toh rape ke baare mein hi: 2024 mein register hue rape cases mein se 96.8% mein accused koi aisa tha jise aurat jaanti thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur scale ke baare mein bhi: rape register hue lagbhag har pandrah cases mein se ek tha.

Yahi picture tay karti hai ki mehnat kahan lagegi. Parivaar betiyon par curfew lagate hain, shehar main roads par camera lagate hain, aur public ka gussa kisi ek bhayanak case ke baad chadhta hai aur phir thanda pad jaata hai. Lekin jis register ka zyada tar hissa shaadiyon, 18 se kam umr ki ladkiyon aur roz ke harassment se bhara ho, use alag jawab chahiye.

## 2024 ki ginti, category dar category

NCRB ka snapshot chaar sabse badi headings batata hai. Rape in sabke baad aata hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]].

| NCRB heading | Seedhe shabdon mein | Cases | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pati ya relatives ki cruelty | Shaadi ke andar violence ya harassment | 1,20,227 | 27.2% |
| Women ka kidnapping aur abduction | Kisi aurat ya ladki ko gair-kaanooni tareeke se le jaana | 67,829 | 15.4% |
| POCSO, girl victims | 18 se kam umr ki ladkiyon ke khilaaf sexual offences | 67,809 | 15.4% |
| Modesty bhang karne ke iraade se assault | Rape se neeche ka sexual assault, jise aksar molestation kaha jaata hai | 48,303 | 10.9% |
| Rape | IPC ya BNS ke under register hua rape | 29,536 | 6.7% |

Chaar sabse badi headings milkar kul registered crimes ka do-tihai se zyada hain. Kidnapping wali line ko dhyan se padhna zaroori hai. Ismein bahut alag-alag situations ek hi heading ke neeche aa jaati hain, aur headline figure inhe alag karke nahi dikhata.

## Ghar ke andar ki cruelty: sabse bada column

Pati ya uske relatives ki cruelty ke 1,20,227 cases register hue, rape ki ginti se lagbhag chaar guna. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 85 aur 86 ke hisaab se cruelty ka matlab hai jaan-boojhkar aisa behaviour jo aurat ko suicide ki taraf dhakel sakta ho ya use gambhir chot pahuncha sakta ho, ya use ya uske parivaar ko property ki gair-kaanooni maang poori karne ke liye harass karna. Saza teen saal tak ki jail aur fine hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Imagine kijiye Kanpur ki ek 26 saal ki aurat, jiski shaadi ko do saal hue hain. Sasural walon ko car chahiye. Use thappad maara jaata hai, ek raat ghar se bahar rakha jaata hai aur kaha jaata hai ki woh bojh hai. Uski maa kehti hai adjust kar lo. Ismein se kuch bhi trend nahi karega. Law ki nazar mein yeh cruelty hai, aur agar woh police station tak pahunch jaaye toh un 1,20,227 mein se ek ban jaati hai.

Uski jaisi situation mein zyada tar women wahan tak pahunchti hi nahi. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 18-49 saal ki 32% women ne kaha ki unhone physical ya sexual violence jheli hai. Inmein se 77.2% ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya, aur sirf 14.1% ne help maangi. Jinhone help maangi, unmein se bhi sirf 6% police ke paas gayin [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Ghar-ghar jaakar kiya gaya survey aur police register number-se-number match nahi kiye ja sakte, par dono ek hi taraf ishaara karte hain: ghar ki taraf.

Jab cruelty maut par khatm hoti hai, toh case doosri line mein chala jaata hai. 2024 mein police ne dowry death ke 5,737 cases register kiye, jinmein 5,811 victims the, yaani roz lagbhag 16 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Ladkiyaan aur roz ka harassment

POCSO wali line, yaani girl victims wale 67,809 cases, rape head ke double se bhi zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ismein rape ke saath sexual harassment aur non-penetrative assault bhi aate hain. In cases mein se 43,313 ladkiyon par penetrative sexual assault ke the, yaani child rape, jo ek alag heading mein darj hota hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isliye 6.7% khud rape ko bhi kam karke dikhata hai.

POCSO 18 se kam umr ke har insaan ko child maanta hai aur ladke-ladkiyon dono ko protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Jis ladke ke saath abuse hota hai, woh bhi isi Act mein cover hai, lekin uska case crimes-against-children wali tables mein jaata hai, is total se bahar.

Phir aate hain woh offences jinhe aaj bhi kai parivaar ladkiyon se ignore karne ko kehte hain: bus mein lagaya gaya haath, tuition se ghar tak peechha karne wala aadmi, bina poochhe li gayi photo. 48,303 assault cases ke alaawa police ne sexual harassment ke 15,609, stalking ke 9,865, disrobe karne ke iraade se assault ke 8,409 aur voyeurism ke 1,722 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh paanchon offences milkar 83,908 baar register hue, yaani roz lagbhag 230 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Ek FIR, ek offence: is rule se kya chhoot jaata hai

NCRB har FIR ko sirf ek baar ginta hai, uske sabse bhaari charge ke naam par. Uska disclaimer batata hai ki jab ek FIR mein kai offences hon, toh sirf woh gina jaata hai jiski saza sabse zyada hai, isliye har heading ki asli ginti alag ho sakti hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo rape murder par khatm hota hai, woh sirf murder with rape mein dikhta hai. Isi rule se, jis FIR mein cruelty aur dowry death dono ka allegation ho, woh sirf dowry death mein gini jaati hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]].

Toh table ka har share FIRs ka share hai, jinhe unke sabse bhaari charge ke hisaab se sort kiya gaya hai. Yeh women ke saath hui har cheez ki ginti nahi hai. Aur har FIR ke peechhe ek aurat chahiye jo police station tak pahunchi, aur ek officer jisne uski complaint likhi.

> Register woh dikhata hai jo police darj karti hai, woh sab nahi jo hota hai. Phir bhi yeh sunsaan sadak se hatkar ghar ki taraf ishaara karta hai.

Prevention wahin se shuru honi chahiye jahan numbers hain: shaadi ke andar, bachchon ke saath, aur us harassment se jise hans kar taal diya jaata hai. Agar aapke saath aisa kuch ho raha hai aur aap khatre mein hain, toh 112 par call kijiye. Agar aap 18 se kam umr ke hain, toh Child Helpline 1098 par call kar sakte hain. Agar sab sambhaalna mushkil lag raha hai ya suicide ke khayal aa rahe hain, toh Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call kijiye; yeh free hai aur din-raat khula hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

death-penalty-for-rape-already-law.en:
After every case that shakes the country, the same demand rises from streets, TV studios and legislatures: hang rapists. It is made as if Indian law had no such punishment. It does. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) allows a death sentence in four kinds of rape cases [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and the POCSO Act in a fifth [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. What a statute cannot do is convict. Of the rape trials that courts completed in 2024, 24.4% ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## The demand after every outrage

After the 2012 Delhi gang rape case, Parliament passed the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013. It allowed death for rape that kills a woman or leaves her in a persistent vegetative state, and for repeat offenders [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. In 2018 Parliament added death for the rape of a girl under 12 [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. In 2019 it amended POCSO to allow death for aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

The demand did not stop. A doctor was raped and murdered at RG Kar Medical College in Kolkata on 9 August 2024 [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Less than a month later, on 3 September, the West Bengal Assembly unanimously passed a Bill making death mandatory for rape where the victim dies or is left in a vegetative state [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]]. Central law already allowed a death sentence in exactly that situation.

## Where Indian law already allows death

| Situation | Provision | Sentence the court may give |
|---|---|---|
| Rape of a girl under 12 | BNS Section 65 | 20 years to the rest of natural life, or death |
| Rape that causes death or a persistent vegetative state | BNS Section 66 | 20 years to the rest of natural life, or death |
| Gang rape of a girl under 18 | BNS Section 70 | Rest of natural life, or death |
| Second conviction for rape | BNS Section 71 | Rest of natural life, or death |
| Aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child | POCSO Section 6 | 20 years to the rest of natural life, or death |

Three things are worth noticing. Death is the maximum in each row, not the rule: the judge chooses within the range. The net has widened over time: the 2018 law allowed death for the gang rape of a girl under 12 [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]], and the BNS, in force since 1 July 2024 [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]], draws that line at 18 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. And POCSO protects boys and girls alike, so its death provision covers the worst assaults on boys as well [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Rape outside these rows still carries at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment, and up to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## What the numbers did next

Police registered 31,516 rape cases in 2022, 29,670 in 2023 and 29,536 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These are complaints that became FIRs, not a measure of how much rape happens, so a small fall proves little either way. Three years of figures cannot prove whether a law deters anyone, and these show no sharp change either way.

The courtroom figures are clearer. In 2024 courts completed 20,587 rape trials. They convicted in 5,032 cases and acquitted in 13,980, a conviction rate of 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In 2012, before any of these amendments, the rate was about 24% [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]]. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were still pending trial, 89.8% of all those before the courts that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Death sentences themselves move slowly and can be undone on appeal. The four adult convicts in the December 2012 Delhi case were hanged on 20 March 2020, more than seven years after the crime [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. The first death sentences under the 2013 repeat-offender section came in Mumbai's Shakti Mills cases on 4 April 2014 [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. On 25 November 2021 the Bombay High Court commuted them to life imprisonment, holding that a constitutional court cannot award punishment based on public opinion [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

## What the Verma Committee warned

None of this would have surprised the committee set up in December 2012, after the Delhi case. Justice J.S. Verma, Justice Leila Seth and Gopal Subramanium submitted their report on 23 January 2013. They advised against the death penalty for rape, noting that it "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament wrote it into the law anyway.

A punishment deters only if a person expects to face it. On the 2024 figures, roughly three in four completed rape trials ended without a conviction. A threat that rarely arrives is a weak threat, however severe it looks on paper.

Who the accused are matters too. In 96.8% of rape cases registered in 2024, he was someone the woman knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. When the accused is a relative, a neighbour or a family friend, a family deciding whether to report is weighing what happens to someone it knows. A harsher maximum sentence does nothing to make that decision easier.

> A death sentence reaches only the cases that end in conviction. In 2024 that was about one completed rape trial in four.

## Certainty, not severity

Imagine two systems. In the first, the maximum punishment is death, and about one completed trial in four ends in conviction. In the second, the maximum is lower, but a complaint reliably becomes an FIR, a charge-sheet, a prompt trial and a verdict. The second is the one an offender has reason to fear.

On paper, India has already promised the second system. A police officer who fails to record an FIR for rape faces six months to two years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police must complete a rape investigation within two months, and the trial must end within two months of the charge-sheet, but the law sets no consequence for missing either deadline [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

So when the demand goes up again, ask for the less dramatic numbers: how many complaints in your state become FIRs on the first visit, how long trials take, and how many end in conviction. Those figures, more than the top line of a punishment clause, decide whether the law protects anyone. This is general information, not legal advice.
death-penalty-for-rape-already-law.hg:
Jab bhi koi case desh ko hila deta hai, sadkon, TV studios aur assemblies se ek hi maang uthti hai: rapists ko phaansi do. Maang aise ki jaati hai jaise Indian law mein aisi koi saza ho hi nahi. Saza hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) chaar tarah ke rape cases mein death sentence ki ijaazat deta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur POCSO Act paanchvi tarah ke case mein [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Jo kaam koi law khud nahi kar sakta, woh hai convict karna. 2024 mein courts ne jitne rape trials poore kiye, unmein se 24.4% conviction par khatm hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Har outrage ke baad wahi maang

2012 ke Delhi gang rape case ke baad Parliament ne Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 paas kiya. Isne us rape ke liye death ki ijaazat di jisse aurat ki maut ho jaaye ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaaye, aur repeat offenders ke liye bhi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. 2018 mein Parliament ne 12 se kam umr ki ladki ke rape ke liye death jodi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. 2019 mein POCSO ko amend karke child par aggravated penetrative sexual assault ke liye death ki ijaazat di gayi [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Maang phir bhi nahi ruki. 9 August 2024 ko Kolkata ke RG Kar Medical College mein ek doctor ka rape aur murder hua [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Ek mahine se bhi kam mein, 3 September ko, West Bengal Assembly ne sabki sehmati se ek Bill paas kiya, jo us rape ke liye death ko mandatory banata hai jismein victim ki maut ho jaaye ya woh vegetative state mein chali jaaye [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]]. Central law theek isi situation mein death sentence ki ijaazat pehle se deta tha.

## Indian law kahan pehle se death ki ijaazat deta hai

| Situation | Provision | Court kya saza de sakti hai |
|---|---|---|
| 12 se kam umr ki ladki ka rape | BNS Section 65 | 20 saal se lekar baaki poori natural life tak, ya death |
| Rape jisse maut ho ya persistent vegetative state | BNS Section 66 | 20 saal se lekar baaki poori natural life tak, ya death |
| 18 se kam umr ki ladki ka gang rape | BNS Section 70 | Baaki poori natural life, ya death |
| Rape ke liye doosri baar conviction | BNS Section 71 | Baaki poori natural life, ya death |
| Child par aggravated penetrative sexual assault | POCSO Section 6 | 20 saal se lekar baaki poori natural life tak, ya death |

Teen baatein dhyan dene layak hain. Har row mein death maximum hai, rule nahi: judge is range ke andar saza chunta hai. Yeh daayra waqt ke saath phaila hai: 2018 ka law 12 se kam umr ki ladki ke gang rape mein death ki ijaazat deta tha [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]], aur BNS, jo 1 July 2024 se laagu hai [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]], yeh line 18 par kheenchta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aur POCSO ladke-ladkiyon dono ko protect karta hai, isliye uska death provision ladkon par hue sabse gambhir assaults ko bhi cover karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Jo rape in rows se bahar hai, usmein bhi kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, jo life tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Uske baad numbers ne kya kiya

Police ne 2022 mein 31,516, 2023 mein 29,670 aur 2024 mein 29,536 rape cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh woh complaints hain jo FIR bani, yeh is baat ka naap nahi ki rape kitna hota hai, isliye thodi si girawat kisi bhi taraf kuch saabit nahi karti. Teen saal ke figures yeh saabit nahi kar sakte ki koi law logon ko rokta hai ya nahi, aur in figures mein kisi bhi taraf koi tez badlaav nahi dikhta.

Courtroom ke figures zyada saaf hain. 2024 mein courts ne 20,587 rape trials poore kiye. 5,032 cases mein conviction hua aur 13,980 mein acquittal, yaani conviction rate 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2012 mein, in sab amendments se pehle, yeh rate lagbhag 24% tha [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]]. 2024 ke end mein 1,85,785 rape cases ka trial abhi pending tha, yaani us saal courts ke saamne maujood sab rape cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Death sentences khud bhi dheere chalte hain aur appeal mein palat sakte hain. December 2012 ke Delhi case ke chaar adult convicts ko 20 March 2020 ko phaansi di gayi, crime ke saat saal se bhi zyada baad [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. 2013 ke repeat-offender section ke under pehle death sentences 4 April 2014 ko Mumbai ke Shakti Mills cases mein sunaye gaye [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. 25 November 2021 ko Bombay High Court ne inhe life imprisonment mein badal diya, yeh kehte hue ki ek constitutional court public opinion ke aadhaar par saza nahi de sakti [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

## Verma Committee ne kya warn kiya tha

Is sab se us committee ko koi hairaani nahi hoti jo December 2012 mein, Delhi case ke baad, banayi gayi thi. Justice J.S. Verma, Justice Leila Seth aur Gopal Subramanium ne apni report 23 January 2013 ko di. Unhone rape ke liye death penalty ke khilaaf salaah di, aur note kiya ki yeh "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament ne phir bhi ise law mein likh diya.

Saza tabhi rokti hai jab insaan ko lage ki woh sach mein milegi. 2024 ke figures ke hisaab se poore hue rape trials mein se lagbhag har chaar mein se teen bina conviction ke khatm hue. Jo dhamki shayad hi kabhi poori ho, woh kamzor dhamki hai, chahe kaagaz par kitni bhi sakht dikhe.

Accused kaun hai, yeh bhi maayne rakhta hai. 2024 mein register hue rape cases mein se 96.8% mein woh koi aisa tha jise aurat jaanti thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab accused koi relative, padosi ya family friend ho, toh report karne ka faisla lene wala parivaar yeh bhi tol raha hota hai ki uske jaan-pehchaan wale insaan ka kya hoga. Maximum saza ko aur sakht karne se yeh faisla zara bhi aasaan nahi hota.

> Death sentence sirf un cases tak pahunchta hai jo conviction par khatm hote hain. 2024 mein yeh poore hue rape trials mein lagbhag har chaar mein se ek tha.

## Certainty, severity nahi

Do systems imagine kijiye. Pehle mein maximum saza death hai, aur poore hue lagbhag har chaar trials mein se ek conviction par khatm hota hai. Doosre mein maximum saza kam hai, lekin complaint bharose ke saath FIR banti hai, phir charge-sheet, jaldi trial aur verdict. Offender ke paas darne ki wajah doosre system mein hai.

Kaagaz par India doosre system ka vaada pehle hi kar chuka hai. Jo police officer rape ki FIR darj nahi karta, use chhe mahine se do saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police ko rape ki investigation do mahine mein poori karni hoti hai, aur trial charge-sheet ke do mahine ke andar khatm hona chahiye, lekin dono mein se koi bhi deadline miss hone par law koi nateeja tay nahi karta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Toh agli baar jab yeh maang uthe, toh kam dramatic numbers maangiye: aapke state mein kitni complaints pehli hi visit par FIR banti hain, trials kitna time lete hain, aur kitne conviction par khatm hote hain. Punishment clause ki sabse upar wali line se zyada, yahi figures tay karte hain ki law kisi ko protect karta hai ya nahi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

dhat-semen-loss-anxiety-myth.en:
Imagine a 21-year-old in Patna, a year into preparing for a competitive exam. He has had nightfall twice in a week, his semen looks thinner than he thinks it should, and he is too tired to hold a page in his head. A hostel senior gives it a name: dhat. Your strength is leaking out, he says, and a clinic near the station can fix it. The clinic sells him a "course". Nobody there asks how he has been sleeping, or what he is afraid of.

## What 'dhat' means to the men who fear it

"Dhat" is the everyday word for the belief that semen is escaping the body, in sleep, through masturbation or mixed into urine, and taking strength with it. The idea is old and was held in good faith, long before anyone knew which glands make semen: semen as the body's most refined essence, with many drops of blood said to go into a single drop.

The loss gets blamed for weakness, a thin body, poor memory, failure on the wedding night and childlessness. Doctors in South Asia hear this cluster so often that they have a name for it, dhat syndrome. The name can mislead. It does not describe a leak. It describes the fear of one, and what that fear does to a man.

## Semen, strength and fertility: the biology

Semen is not made from blood. Most of it is fluid from glands, mainly the seminal vesicles and the prostate: water, sugars and proteins, with sperm from the testes forming a small part. The body makes it continuously and replaces what leaves. Releasing it, in a wet dream, by masturbating or during sex, does not drain strength or harm the body [[who-sexual-health]].

"Thin" semen is not a warning sign either. Semen varies in thickness, colour and amount from day to day, and fertility cannot be judged by looking; only a laboratory semen analysis ordered by a doctor can assess it. Infertility has medical causes that can be tested for, and nightfall and masturbation are not among them [[who-infertility]].

A wet dream is a normal body event that nobody can control. The Hindi word for it, swapnadosh, calls it a fault. There is no fault.

## Anxiety dressed up as a disease

Why, then, does he feel weak? Because fear has a body. A young man convinced he is draining away sleeps badly, checks his urine, avoids his friends and wakes up guilty. Poor sleep and constant worry produce the very tiredness, aches and poor concentration he then blames on semen. The symptoms are real. The cause he has been handed is wrong.

Distress like this rarely reaches anyone trained to treat it. India's National Mental Health Survey of 2015-16 found overall mental morbidity higher in men (13.9%) than in women (7.5%) [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. That is not because men were recorded as more anxious: depression and anxiety disorders were higher in women, while alcohol use disorder affected 9% of men against 0.5% of women [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. And the treatment gap, the share of people with a disorder who were getting no treatment, ran from 28% to 83% for mental disorders [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]].

The survey did not count dhat. It does describe the silence dhat grows in. A man who would never say "I am anxious" can say "I have a weakness problem", because a body that leaks is easier to admit to than a mind that is frightened. So the complaint goes to a clinic that sells tonics, not to one that treats anxiety.

A qualified doctor works differently. They ask about sleep, mood and worry, and test only when something points to a physical problem, such as burning while passing urine or a discharge, which can signal an infection [[who-sti]]. Then they explain how semen is made and treat the worry itself, through counselling and, where anxiety or depression is present, psychiatric care. A capsule cannot do that, because nothing is leaking.

## The 'sex power' ads a 1954 law already bans

Much of the trade in this fear is already illegal. Section 3 of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 bans advertising any drug for "the maintenance or improvement of the capacity of human beings for sexual pleasure" [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Advertising a drug for conditions in the Act's Schedule, which include sexual impotence, is a crime: up to six months in jail, a fine or both on a first conviction, and up to one year on a repeat [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

The law has stayed on paper. On 26 March 2025, in Indian Medical Association v. Union of India, the Supreme Court said that although the Act was more than 70 years old, "there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit". It ordered states to appoint enforcement officers within one month and to give the public a way to complain, such as a toll-free number or email, within two months [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

A wall that promises a guaranteed cure for "dhat, swapnadosh, kamzori" tells every teenager who walks past that a normal body event is a disease. It creates the patient before it sells the cure. And a man with a real, treatable problem, such as an infection, can lose months to powders.

## Where to get real help

- **For the worry itself.** Call Tele-MANAS on 14416 [[tele-manas]]. The Health Ministry's helpline has offered free counselling round the clock since October 2022 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
- **For teenagers.** Adolescent Friendly Health Centres offer counselling and clinical care at primary and community health centres, district hospitals and medical colleges [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].
- **For the body.** See a qualified doctor for burning while passing urine, a sore or discharge, blood in semen, or a lump, swelling or pain in a testicle.

The 21-year-old in Patna is not losing his strength in his sleep. He is losing it to fear, at a clinic that needs him to stay afraid. What he needs is one accurate explanation, and someone qualified to treat the worry.
dhat-semen-loss-anxiety-myth.hg:
Socho, Patna ka ek 21 saal ka ladka, jo ek saal se competitive exam ki taiyari kar raha hai. Ek hafte mein use do baar nightfall hua hai, use apna semen pehle se patla lagta hai, aur thakaan itni hai ki ek page bhi dimaag mein nahi tikta. Hostel ka ek senior is sab ko ek naam de deta hai: dhat. Woh kehta hai ki teri taakat beh rahi hai, aur station ke paas wala clinic ise theek kar dega. Clinic use ek "course" bech deta hai. Wahan koi nahi poochhta ki woh so kaisa raha hai, ya use darr kis baat ka hai.

## Jo men isse darte hain, unke liye 'dhat' ka matlab

"Dhat" us belief ka aam naam hai ki semen body se nikal raha hai, neend mein, masturbation se ya urine mein mil kar, aur apne saath taakat le ja raha hai. Yeh soch purani hai aur nek-niyati se maani jaati rahi, us waqt se jab kisi ko pata nahi tha ki semen kaun si glands banati hain: semen yaani body ka sabse keemti saar, jiski ek boond mein blood ki kai boondein lagti hain.

Is "loss" par kamzori, dubli body, kamzor memory, shaadi ki pehli raat par nakaami aur aulaad na hone ka ilzaam lagta hai. South Asia ke doctors yeh shikayatein itni baar sunte hain ki unhone iska ek naam rakh diya hai: dhat syndrome. Naam se dhokha ho sakta hai. Yeh kisi leak ka naam nahi hai. Yeh leak ke darr ka naam hai, aur us haalat ka jo yeh darr ek aadmi ki kar deta hai.

## Semen, taakat aur fertility: biology kya kehti hai

Semen blood se nahi banta. Iska zyada tar hissa glands ka fluid hai, khaas kar seminal vesicles aur prostate ka: paani, sugars aur proteins, jismein testes se aaye sperm ka hissa chhota sa hota hai. Body ise lagataar banati rehti hai aur jo nikal jaata hai use replace kar deti hai. Wet dream mein, masturbation se ya sex ke dauraan semen nikalne se na taakat ghatti hai, na body ko koi nuksaan hota hai [[who-sexual-health]].

"Patla" semen bhi koi warning sign nahi hai. Semen ka gaadhapan, rang aur matra din-ba-din badalti rehti hai, aur dekh kar fertility ka andaaza nahi lagaya ja sakta; yeh sirf doctor ka likha hua laboratory semen analysis bata sakta hai. Infertility ki medical wajahein hoti hain jinka test ho sakta hai, aur nightfall aur masturbation unmein nahi aate [[who-infertility]].

Wet dream body ka ek normal event hai jise koi control nahi kar sakta. Hindi mein ise swapnadosh kehte hain, yaani ek "dosh". Ismein koi dosh nahi hai.

## Bimari ke bhes mein anxiety

Toh phir use kamzori kyun lagti hai? Kyunki darr body mein utar aata hai. Jis ladke ko yakeen ho gaya hai ki woh andar se khaali ho raha hai, woh theek se sota nahi, baar-baar apna urine check karta hai, doston se katne lagta hai aur har subah guilt ke saath uthta hai. Kharab neend aur lagataar chinta wahi thakaan, dard aur dhyan na lagna paida karti hai, jiska ilzaam woh phir semen par daalta hai. Symptoms asli hain. Jo wajah use batayi gayi hai, woh galat hai.

Aisi takleef kam hi kisi aise insaan tak pahunchti hai jo iska ilaaj karna jaanta ho. India ke National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 mein overall mental morbidity men mein (13.9%) women (7.5%) se zyada mili [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki men zyada anxious record hue: depression aur anxiety disorders women mein zyada the, jabki alcohol use disorder 9% men mein tha aur 0.5% women mein [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Aur treatment gap, yaani disorder wale un logon ka hissa jinhe koi treatment nahi mil raha tha, mental disorders ke liye 28% se 83% tak tha [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]].

Survey ne dhat ko nahi gina. Par woh us khamoshi ko zaroor dikhata hai jismein dhat panapta hai. Jo aadmi kabhi nahi kahega ki "mujhe anxiety hai", woh yeh keh sakta hai ki "mujhe kamzori ki problem hai", kyunki body ka "leak" maanna, dare hue mann ko maanne se aasaan hai. Isliye shikayat us clinic par pahunchti hai jo tonic bechta hai, us clinic par nahi jo anxiety ka ilaaj karta hai.

Qualified doctor alag tareeke se kaam karta hai. Woh neend, mood aur chinta ke baare mein poochhta hai, aur test tabhi karwata hai jab kuch kisi physical problem ki taraf ishaara kare, jaise urine mein jalan ya discharge, jo infection ka sign ho sakta hai [[who-sti]]. Phir woh samjhata hai ki semen banta kaise hai, aur asli chinta ka ilaaj karta hai: counselling se, aur jahan anxiety ya depression ho, wahan psychiatric care se. Capsule yeh nahi kar sakta, kyunki kuch leak ho hi nahi raha.

## 'Sex power' ke ads, jin par 1954 ka kanoon pehle se ban lagata hai

Is darr ka zyada tar dhandha pehle se hi gair-kanooni hai. Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 ka Section 3 kisi bhi aisi drug ke ad par ban lagata hai jo "the maintenance or improvement of the capacity of human beings for sexual pleasure" ke liye ho [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Act ke Schedule mein di gayi conditions, jinmein sexual impotence shaamil hai, ki dawa ka ad dena crime hai: pehli conviction par chhah mahine tak ki jail, fine ya dono, aur dobara conviction par ek saal tak [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Kanoon kaagaz par hi reh gaya hai. 26 March 2025 ko Indian Medical Association v. Union of India mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki Act 70 saal se zyada purana hone ke bawajood "there is no implementation of the 1954 Act in its true letter and spirit". Court ne states ko order diya ki ek mahine ke andar enforcement officers appoint karein aur do mahine ke andar public ke liye complaint ka raasta banayein, jaise toll-free number ya email [[sc-ima-order-mar-2025]].

Jis deewar par "dhat, swapnadosh, kamzori" ke guaranteed ilaaj ka vaada likha hai, woh paas se guzarte har teenager ko batati hai ki body ka ek normal event bimari hai. Woh pehle mareez banati hai, phir ilaaj bechti hai. Aur jis aadmi ko sach mein koi aisi problem hai jiska ilaaj ho sakta hai, jaise infection, uske mahine powders mein nikal jaate hain.

## Asli madad kahan milegi

- **Chinta ke liye.** Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call karo [[tele-manas]]. Health Ministry ki yeh helpline October 2022 se chaubees ghante free counselling de rahi hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
- **Teenagers ke liye.** Adolescent Friendly Health Centres primary aur community health centres, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein counselling aur clinical care dete hain [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].
- **Body ke liye.** Urine mein jalan, ghaav ya discharge, semen mein blood, ya testicle mein gaanth, soojan ya dard ho, toh qualified doctor ko dikhao.

Patna ka woh 21 saal ka ladka neend mein apni taakat nahi kho raha. Woh use darr mein kho raha hai, ek aise clinic par jise uska dara rehna hi chahiye. Use chahiye bas ek sahi jaankari, aur koi qualified insaan jo uski chinta ka ilaaj kare.

emergency-pill-shame-myths.en:
Imagine a 20-year-old student in Indore on a Sunday morning. The condom broke the night before. There is a chemist at the end of her lane, and she walks past it three times: the man at the counter knows her mother, and there are other customers. When she finally buys the pill, from a shop two neighbourhoods away, it is Tuesday evening. Nothing medical delayed her by almost three days. What delayed her was what she believed the pill would say about her.

## The pill with a deadline

Emergency contraception (EC) is the one contraceptive used after sex, and it comes with a deadline. EC pills can be taken up to five days (120 hours) after unprotected sex, and they work better the sooner they are taken. They work mainly by delaying ovulation, the release of an egg, so that sperm find nothing to fertilise. A copper IUD fitted by a trained provider within the same five days is the most effective emergency method of all [[who-ec]].

That is why hesitation is costly. The longer she waits, the greater the chance that the egg has already been released, and a pill that works by delaying its release then has little left to do. The hours lost between needing this pill and buying it are hard to measure. But the beliefs behind the delay can be named, and each of them is wrong.

## Myth one: it is an abortion

It is not. An EC pill cannot end a pregnancy that is already established, and if a woman is already pregnant it will simply not work [[who-ec]]. EC stops a pregnancy from starting. An abortion ends one that has started. They are different medicines doing opposite jobs.

The confusion matters at the counter. A young woman who thinks she is asking for "a small abortion" feels she is confessing to something, so she delays, or does not go. An estimated 15.6 million abortions took place in India in 2015, and nearly half of all pregnancies that year were unintended [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Abortion is legal health care and no cause for shame either. But the pill people whisper about is one of the few things that can prevent the need for it after sex has already happened.

## Myth two: it harms future fertility

The warning usually comes from a friend, a cousin or a reel: take it once and you will struggle to conceive later. WHO's evidence says the opposite. Emergency contraceptive pills do not harm future fertility, and there is no delay in the return of fertility after taking them [[who-ec]].

Side effects are uncommon and mild, such as nausea, tiredness and some irregular bleeding, and the next period may arrive a few days early or late [[who-ec]]. That late period is probably where the myth starts. In a hostel corridor, "her period was a week late after the pill" quickly becomes "it damaged something inside her".

The real limits on repeat use are practical. EC is less reliable than a regular method, it covers only the sex that has already happened, and it gives no protection against sexually transmitted infections [[who-ec]]. Needing it twice is a reason to ask a doctor about a regular method. It is not evidence of harm.

## Myth three: only 'loose' girls need it

This belief does the most damage, and it can be measured. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 19.6% of Indian men aged 15-49 agreed that women who use contraception may become promiscuous. In the same survey, 35.1% of men agreed that contraception is women's business and a man should not have to worry about it [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

> Contraception is called her job, and then she is judged for doing it.

The judgment decides what girls are allowed to know. Only 54.4% of young women aged 15-24 knew where to get a condom, against 87.3% of young men [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. (The male figure is slightly inflated: any man who had used a condom in the past year was counted as knowing a source.) A girl who is not supposed to know where condoms are sold will not find it easy to ask a chemist for the pill taken afterwards.

Needing EC says nothing about character. Condoms split in marriages as well as in first relationships. Daily pills are forgotten. And sex is sometimes forced, by a stranger, a boyfriend or a husband; EC is meant for that situation too [[who-ec]]. Nor does knowing about contraception make young people reckless. UNESCO's 2018 guidance found that curriculum-based sexuality education contributes to delayed first sex, fewer sexual partners, reduced risk-taking and increased use of condoms and contraception [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

## Buying it without shame

A chemist or a doctor can provide EC. Ask for an emergency contraceptive pill and pay for it; you do not owe the person at the counter a story, a wedding ring or an apology. If you cannot face it, the man you had sex with can buy it. Two people created the risk, and nothing about the pill requires the woman to be the one standing in the shop.

If you are under 18, the law works differently. Sexual activity with anyone under 18 is an offence under the POCSO Act whatever the "consent", and anyone who knows of it, a doctor included, is required to report it, so no doctor can promise complete secrecy [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. You are still entitled to care. Tell an adult you trust, or call the Child Helpline on 1098.

If the sex was forced, at any age, go to a hospital as soon as you can. The same five-day clock applies, and doctors can also assess the risk of HIV, where the preventive medicine has to start within 72 hours [[who-pep]].

Afterwards, if your period is more than a week late, take a pregnancy test and see a doctor. Taking this pill in time is not a confession of anything. It is a medicine with a deadline, and the deadline does not care what the neighbours think.
emergency-pill-shame-myths.hg:
Socho, Indore ki ek 20 saal ki student hai aur Sunday ki subah hai. Kal raat condom phat gaya tha. Gali ke kone par chemist hai, aur woh uske saamne se teen baar nikal jaati hai: counter wala uncle uski mummy ko jaanta hai, aur dukaan par doosre customers bhi khade hain. Aakhir mein jab woh do mohalle door ki ek dukaan se pill kharidti hai, tab tak Tuesday ki shaam ho chuki hoti hai. Lagbhag teen din ki is deri ke peeche koi medical wajah nahi thi. Wajah yeh thi ki uske hisaab se yeh pill uske baare mein kya keh degi.

## Deadline wali pill

Emergency contraception (EC) woh akela contraceptive hai jo sex ke baad use hota hai, aur iske saath ek deadline aati hai. EC pills unprotected sex ke paanch din (120 ghante) baad tak li ja sakti hain, aur jitni jaldi li jaayein utna achha kaam karti hain. Yeh mainly ovulation ko, yaani egg ke release ko, delay karti hain, taaki sperm ko fertilise karne ke liye kuch mile hi nahi. Unhi paanch dinon ke andar trained provider se lagwaya gaya copper IUD sabse effective emergency method hai [[who-ec]].

Isiliye hichkichahat mehengi padti hai. Woh jitna wait karegi, utna chance badhega ki egg pehle hi release ho chuka ho, aur jo pill release ko delay karke kaam karti hai, uske paas phir karne ko zyada kuch nahi bachta. Is pill ki zaroorat padne aur ise kharidne ke beech kitne ghante barbaad hote hain, yeh naapna mushkil hai. Par deri ke peeche ke beliefs ka naam liya ja sakta hai, aur unmein se har ek galat hai.

## Pehla myth: yeh abortion hai

Nahi hai. EC pill us pregnancy ko end nahi kar sakti jo pehle se established ho, aur agar woman already pregnant hai toh yeh bas kaam nahi karegi [[who-ec]]. EC pregnancy ko shuru hone se rokti hai. Abortion us pregnancy ko end karta hai jo shuru ho chuki hai. Dono alag medicines hain aur dono ka kaam ek doosre se ulta hai.

Yeh confusion counter par asar dikhata hai. Jis young woman ko lagta hai ki woh "chhota abortion" maang rahi hai, use lagta hai ki woh kuch confess kar rahi hai, isliye woh der karti hai, ya jaati hi nahi. 2015 mein India mein estimated 15.6 million abortions hue, aur us saal ki lagbhag aadhi pregnancies unintended thin [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Abortion legal health care hai aur usme bhi sharam ki koi baat nahi. Lekin jis pill ke baare mein log phusphusa kar baat karte hain, woh un gini-chuni cheezon mein se hai jo sex ho jaane ke baad bhi abortion ki zaroorat ko rok sakti hain.

## Doosra myth: isse future fertility kharab hoti hai

Yeh warning aksar kisi dost, cousin ya reel se aati hai: ek baar le li toh baad mein conceive karne mein dikkat hogi. WHO ka evidence iska ulta kehta hai. Emergency contraceptive pills future fertility ko nuksaan nahi pahunchati, aur inhe lene ke baad fertility wapas aane mein koi deri nahi hoti [[who-ec]].

Side effects kam logon ko hote hain aur halke hote hain, jaise nausea, thakaan aur thodi irregular bleeding, aur agla period kuch din pehle ya kuch din late aa sakta hai [[who-ec]]. Shayad myth wahin se shuru hota hai, us late period se. Hostel ke corridor mein "pill ke baad uska period ek hafta late aaya" bahut jaldi "pill ne andar kuch kharab kar diya" ban jaata hai.

Baar-baar use karne ki asli limits practical hain. EC regular method se kam reliable hai, sirf us sex ko cover karti hai jo ho chuka hai, aur sexually transmitted infections se koi protection nahi deti [[who-ec]]. Do baar zaroorat padna doctor se regular method ke baare mein poochne ki wajah hai. Yeh nuksaan ka saboot nahi hai.

## Teesra myth: iski zaroorat sirf 'loose' ladkiyon ko padti hai

Sabse zyada nuksaan yahi belief karta hai, aur ise naapa ja sakta hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 15-49 saal ke 19.6% Indian men ne maana ki contraception use karne wali women promiscuous ho sakti hain. Usi survey mein 35.1% men ne maana ki contraception women ka kaam hai aur man ko iski chinta nahi karni chahiye [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

> Contraception ko uski zimmedari bataya jaata hai, aur phir zimmedari nibhane par usi ko judge kiya jaata hai.

Yahi judgment tay karta hai ki ladkiyon ko kya jaanne ki ijaazat hai. 15-24 saal ki sirf 54.4% young women ko pata tha ki condom kahan milta hai, jabki young men mein yeh 87.3% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. (Men ka figure thoda badha hua hai: jis bhi man ne pichhle ek saal mein condom use kiya tha, use source jaanne wala gin liya gaya.) Jis ladki se umeed hi yeh hai ki use pata na ho ki condom kahan bikta hai, uske liye chemist se baad mein li jaane wali pill maangna aasaan nahi hoga.

EC ki zaroorat padna character ke baare mein kuch nahi batata. Condom shaadi mein bhi phat-te hain aur pehle relationship mein bhi. Roz ki pills bhool jaati hain. Aur kabhi-kabhi sex zabardasti hota hai, kisi stranger, boyfriend ya husband ke haathon; EC us situation ke liye bhi hai [[who-ec]]. Contraception ke baare mein jaanna young logon ko laparwah bhi nahi banata. UNESCO ki 2018 ki guidance ne paaya ki curriculum-based sexuality education se pehla sex der se hota hai, sexual partners kam hote hain, risk lena ghat-ta hai aur condom aur contraception ka use badhta hai [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

## Bina sharam ke kharidna

EC chemist ya doctor se mil sakti hai. Emergency contraceptive pill maango aur paise do; counter par khade insaan ko na koi kahani sunani hai, na shaadi ki ring dikhani hai, na maafi maangni hai. Agar tumse nahi ho pa raha, toh jis man ke saath sex hua tha, woh kharid sakta hai. Risk do logon ne banaya tha, aur pill mein aisa kuch nahi hai jiske liye dukaan par woman ko hi khada hona pade.

Agar tum 18 se kam ho, toh law alag tarah se kaam karta hai. 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath sexual activity POCSO Act ke under offence hai, "consent" ho ya na ho, aur jise bhi iska pata chale, doctor samet, use report karna zaroori hai, isliye koi doctor poori secrecy ka promise nahi kar sakta [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Care par tumhara haq phir bhi hai. Kisi bharose wale adult ko batao, ya Child Helpline 1098 par call karo.

Agar sex zabardasti hua tha, umar koi bhi ho, jitni jaldi ho sake hospital jao. Wahi paanch din wali clock wahan bhi chalti hai, aur doctors HIV ka risk bhi assess kar sakte hain, jiski preventive medicine 72 ghante ke andar shuru karni hoti hai [[who-pep]].

Uske baad, agar period ek hafte se zyada late ho, toh pregnancy test karo aur doctor ko dikhao. Yeh pill time par lena kisi cheez ka confession nahi hai. Yeh deadline wali medicine hai, aur deadline ko is baat se koi matlab nahi ki padosi kya sochenge.

false-promise-marriage-section-69-myth.en:
Picture a familiar scene. A relationship ends, an FIR names the ex-boyfriend, and the family WhatsApp group splits in two. One side says the law has gone mad: any relationship that ends after sex can now become a rape case. The other shrugs: he lied, but lying is not a crime, and she should have known better. Both sides are wrong, and the law that proves it has been in force since 1 July 2024 [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]].

## Two myths about a broken promise

The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which replaced the Indian Penal Code that day, answers both myths with one section. Section 69 makes it a separate offence to get sex by "deceitful means", or by a promise of marriage made with no intention of keeping it. The maximum punishment is 10 years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

So the second myth falls first: lying to get sex can be a crime. But the same section says this sex is "not amounting to the offence of rape" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Ten years is the most a court can give under Section 69, and the least it must give for rape under Section 64 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A false promise is its own wrong, and the law treats it as a smaller one. That breaks the first myth too.

## What Section 69 says, word by word

Every phrase in the section does a job.

- **"Deceitful means."** The law lists examples: a false promise of a job or a promotion, or marrying a woman while hiding one's identity [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A manager who dangles a promotion is covered, not only a boyfriend.
- **"Without any intention of fulfilling the same."** The test is the intention when the promise was made, not how the relationship ended.
- **"Not amounting to the offence of rape."** If the facts show rape, the case belongs under the rape law, not here.
- **"A woman."** The rape section defines the crime as one by a man against a woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and Section 69 also speaks only of a woman. A man or a transgender person deceived the same way is not covered.

The old code had no such offence; NCRB's tables show no IPC equivalent and no earlier years [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Broken later or never meant: the line the law draws

Consider two hypothetical couples. In the first, two people in Indore date for three years. He promises marriage and means it. His parents refuse, he gives in, and it ends badly. The promise was broken, but it was not made "without any intention" of keeping it.

In the second, a man meets a woman on a dating app. He says he is single, promises marriage within months and keeps postponing, while his own wedding is already fixed elsewhere. Here the facts point to a promise that was hollow from the start.

The difference is not how hurt anyone is at the end. It is what can be shown about the beginning: messages, what he told others, a false name, a marriage already arranged. Courts weigh that evidence case by case. This is general information, not legal advice.

Two more lines matter. The BNS defines consent as an "unequivocal voluntary agreement" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. And Section 63 treats sex as rape when consent was obtained through fear of death or hurt, or by a man posing as the woman's husband; other deceit falls under the lesser Section 69 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. If a "relationship" involved threats or force, it is not a broken-promise case, and calling it one shrinks the crime.

## What the first 1,325 cases tell us

Between July and December 2024, police registered 1,325 cases under Section 69 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In the same months, 9,853 rape cases were registered under the BNS, while rapes committed before 1 July were still filed under the IPC [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The new offence is real, and far smaller than the first myth imagines.

The deceit is not only face to face. NCRB's cyber crime tables count 99 Section 69 cases in 2024, in which a phone or computer was part of the offence [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Read the 1,325 with three cautions. NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence, so a complaint that also alleges rape sits in the rape column [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Promise-of-marriage complaints filed as rape stay hidden: the largest group of known accused in the 2024 rape table, 13,879 cases, lumps friends, online friends, live-in partners "on pretext of marriage" and separated husbands together, and NCRB cannot separate them [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Our explainer on the first BNS crime data shows how this new row may pull cases out of the rape count. And the number has no past and no outcome yet; it says nothing about convictions.

One gap deserves attention. The new procedure code, the BNSS, tells police to finish rape investigations within two months, and courts to finish rape trials within two months of the chargesheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Section 69 is on neither list [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A woman who files under it gets no such deadline.

## Before a relationship becomes a complaint

If you make promises, make only the ones you mean. A promise of marriage, a job or a promotion used to get sex is not romance or ambition. It can be a crime.

If you feel deceived, write down dates, keep the messages and note exactly what was promised. For cognizable offences, any police station must record your complaint wherever the offence happened (a Zero FIR), and you are entitled to a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. If there were threats or force, say so: that is rape, not a broken promise.

If anyone involved is under 18, none of this applies. Sex with a girl under 18 is rape whatever she says [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The same NCRB column of friends, online friends and live-in partners "on pretext of marriage" turns up in child cases too: in 2024 it held 22,308 POCSO penetrative assault cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

If families push a "settlement", remember that the Supreme Court has said courts must not suggest compromise or marriage in sexual offence cases [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. A wedding arranged to bury a complaint protects reputations, not people.
false-promise-marriage-section-69-myth.hg:
Ek familiar scene socho. Ek relationship khatam hota hai, ek FIR mein ex-boyfriend ka naam aata hai, aur family ka WhatsApp group do hisson mein bant jaata hai. Ek side kehti hai ki law pagal ho gaya hai: ab sex ke baad khatam hua har relationship rape case ban sakta hai. Doosri side kandhe uchka deti hai: usne jhooth bola, par jhooth bolna crime nahi hai, ladki ko samajhna chahiye tha. Dono galat hain, aur yeh saabit karne wala law 1 July 2024 se laagu hai [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]].

## Toote promise ke baare mein do myths

Usi din Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne Indian Penal Code (IPC) ki jagah li. Yeh naya law dono myths ka jawab ek hi section mein deta hai: Section 69. Iske hisaab se "deceitful means" yaani dhoke se sex haasil karna ek alag offence hai, aur shaadi ka aisa promise karke bhi, jise nibhane ka koi intention hi na ho. Maximum saza 10 saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Toh doosra myth pehle girta hai: sex ke liye jhooth bolna crime ho sakta hai. Lekin yahi section saaf likhta hai ki aisa sex "rape ke offence tak nahi pahunchta" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Dhyan do: Section 69 mein court zyada se zyada 10 saal de sakta hai, aur Section 64 mein rape ke liye use kam se kam 10 saal dene hi padte hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Jhootha promise apne aap mein galat hai, par law ise rape se halka maanta hai. Isse pehla myth bhi toot jaata hai.

## Section 69 kya kehta hai, word by word

Is section ka har phrase kuch kaam karta hai.

- **"Deceitful means."** Law khud examples deta hai: naukri ya promotion ka jhootha promise, ya apni identity chhupakar kisi woman se shaadi karna [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yaani promotion ka laalach dene wala manager bhi isme aata hai, sirf boyfriend nahi.
- **"Nibhane ka koi intention na ho."** Sawaal yeh hai ki promise karte waqt intention kya tha, yeh nahi ki relationship kaise khatam hua.
- **"Rape ke offence tak nahi."** Agar facts rape dikhate hain, toh case rape wale law mein jaayega, yahan nahi.
- **"Ek woman."** Rape wala section ise ek man ka ek woman ke khilaaf crime batata hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur Section 69 bhi sirf woman ki baat karta hai. Agar kisi man ya transgender person ke saath aisa hi dhoka ho, toh yeh section unhe cover nahi karta.

Purane law mein aisa koi offence tha hi nahi: NCRB ki tables mein Section 69 ka na koi IPC equivalent hai, na pichhle saalon ka data [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Baad mein toota, ya kabhi nibhana hi nahi tha: law ki line

Do hypothetical couples socho. Pehle mein, Indore ke do log teen saal se date kar rahe hain. Ladka shaadi ka promise karta hai aur sach mein karna chahta hai. Uske parents mana kar dete hain, woh jhuk jaata hai, aur relationship bure tareeke se khatam hota hai. Promise toota, lekin woh "bina intention" ke nahi kiya gaya tha.

Doosre mein, ek aadmi dating app pe ek woman se milta hai. Kehta hai ki woh single hai, kuch mahino mein shaadi ka promise karta hai aur baar-baar taalta rehta hai, jabki uski apni shaadi kahin aur pehle se fixed hai. Yahan facts batate hain ki promise shuru se khokhla tha.

Farq isse nahi padta ki end mein kaun kitna hurt hai. Farq isse padta hai ki shuruaat ke baare mein kya dikhaya ja sakta hai: messages, usne doosron se kya kaha, jhootha naam, pehle se tay shaadi. Court har case mein yeh evidence alag se tolta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Do baatein aur zaroori hain. BNS consent ko "unequivocal voluntary agreement" maanta hai, yaani saaf aur apni marzi se di gayi haan [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aur Section 63 ke hisaab se, agar consent maut ya chot ka darr dikhakar li gayi, ya aadmi ne khud ko woman ka pati batakar li, toh woh rape hai; baaki tarah ka dhoka halke Section 69 mein aata hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Agar kisi "relationship" mein dhamki ya zabardasti thi, toh woh toote promise ka case hai hi nahi, aur use aisa kehna crime ko chhota kar deta hai.

## Pehle 1,325 cases kya batate hain

July se December 2024 ke beech police ne Section 69 mein 1,325 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Unhi mahino mein BNS ke under rape ke 9,853 cases register hue, jabki 1 July se pehle hue rapes ke cases tab bhi IPC mein darj ho rahe the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Naya offence real hai, lekin pehla myth jitna bada sochta hai, usse kaafi chhota hai.

Dhoka sirf aamne-saamne nahi hota. NCRB ki cyber crime tables mein 2024 mein Section 69 ke 99 cases hain, jinme phone ya computer offence ka hissa tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

1,325 ko teen cautions ke saath padho. Pehla, NCRB har FIR ko sirf ek baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke naam pe, toh jis complaint mein rape ka aarop bhi hai, woh rape wale column mein jaati hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Doosra, shaadi ke promise wale jo complaints rape ke roop mein darj hue, woh chhupe rehte hain. 2024 ki rape table mein jaan-pehchaan wale accused ka sabse bada group, 13,879 cases, dost, online dost, "pretext of marriage" wale live-in partners aur alag reh rahe pati, sabko ek saath ginta hai, aur NCRB inhe alag nahi kar sakta [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. BNS ke pehle crime data pe hamara explainer batata hai ki yeh nayi row dheere-dheere rape count se cases kaise kheench sakti hai. Teesra, is number ka na koi past hai, na abhi koi outcome; conviction ke baare mein yeh kuch nahi batata.

Ek gap pe dhyan dena zaroori hai. Naya procedure law, BNSS, kehta hai ki police rape ki investigation do mahine mein poori kare, aur court chargesheet ke do mahine ke andar rape ka trial khatam kare [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Section 69 in dono mein se kisi list mein nahi hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yaani is section mein complaint karne wali woman ke liye aisi koi deadline nahi hai.

## Relationship complaint bane, usse pehle

Agar tum promise karte ho, toh wahi karo jo sach mein nibhana hai. Sex ke liye kiya gaya shaadi, naukri ya promotion ka promise na romance hai, na ambition. Yeh crime ho sakta hai.

Agar tumhe lagta hai ki tumhare saath dhoka hua, toh dates likh lo, messages sambhaal ke rakho aur exactly likho ki kya promise kiya gaya tha. Jin offences mein police seedha FIR darj karti hai (cognizable offences), unme koi bhi police station tumhari complaint darj karega, chahe offence kahin bhi hua ho. Ise Zero FIR kehte hain, aur FIR ki copy tumhe free milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar dhamki ya zabardasti hui thi, toh zaroor batao: woh rape hai, toota promise nahi.

Agar involved koi bhi insaan 18 se kam umar ka hai, toh upar ki koi baat laagu nahi hoti. 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex rape hai, chahe woh kuch bhi kahe [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. NCRB ka yahi column, yaani dost, online dost aur "pretext of marriage" wale live-in partners, bachchon ke cases mein bhi dikhta hai: 2024 mein POCSO ke 22,308 penetrative assault cases isi column mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Aur agar family "settlement" ka pressure daale, toh yaad rakho: Supreme Court keh chuka hai ki sexual offence cases mein courts compromise ya shaadi ka suggestion tak na dein [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Complaint dabane ke liye karaayi gayi shaadi izzat bachati hai, insaan nahi.

false-rape-case-myth-cost-of-complaint.en:
Every few weeks a post goes viral about a man "ruined" by a false rape complaint. It arrives with a verdict already attached: women lie for money, women lie for revenge. The rest of the record never travels with it, and that record points the other way. In India, reporting a rape costs a woman years of her life, offers at most a few lakh rupees in compensation, which she can claim without naming anyone, and ends in a conviction in only 24.4% of completed trials. Most women never report at all.
