## Why the myth spreads so fast online

One dramatic case is easy to share. A trial that drags on for years never trends.

The myth also does a job for the people around the accused. In 96.8% of rape cases registered in India in 2024, the offender was someone the victim knew: 28,597 of 29,536 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. When the accused is a cousin, a neighbour, a boss or an ex, "she is lying" is the easiest story for a family, a mohalla or an office.

Some of these posts also name or show the woman. Publishing anything that could identify a rape survivor is a crime under Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yet police registered just 11 such cases from July to December 2024, the first six months of the new code [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The Supreme Court has already rejected this belief. Its 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes says: "It is therefore untrue that women are very likely to make false allegations." [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]] It adds that a delay in reporting is not a sign of lying: fear of repercussions or a lack of family support can make a survivor wait.

## Years in the queue: what a complaint sets in motion

Consider a 22-year-old in Kanpur who tells the police that a relative raped her. A magistrate, a woman wherever practicable, must record her statement [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A doctor examines her. Then the investigation begins. In 2024 police filed charge-sheets in 24,614 rape cases, a charge-sheeting rate of 81.3%, and 8,905 cases were still under investigation at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

On paper, her trial should finish within two months of the charge-sheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. In reality, of the 2,06,777 rape cases before Indian courts in 2024, 1,85,785 were still pending at the end of the year: 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Even the courts built for speed are jammed. About 2,45,579 rape and POCSO cases were pending before Fast Track Special Courts on 31 December 2025 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]].

Meanwhile she may live in the same lane as the accused, under steady pressure to "settle". In March 2021 the Supreme Court had to strike down a High Court bail condition that told a man accused of sexual assault to ask the complainant to tie a rakhi on him. It ruled that courts must not suggest compromise or marriage [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

And the money? Under NALSA's 2018 scheme, a rape survivor is entitled to Rs 4-7 lakh [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]], though actual payouts depend on state and district legal services authorities. It comes through a state-run scheme, and a survivor can apply even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Naming a particular man is not a condition for it. At work, the POSH Act bars any money settlement as the basis of conciliation [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## What 'false' means in police files, and what it does not

In 2024 police disposed of 30,272 rape cases. They closed 3,776 with a final report calling the case "false", 714 as a mistake of fact or law or a civil dispute, and 1,044 as true but with insufficient evidence or the accused untraced [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

That "false" is a police label given at the investigation stage, not a finding by any court. It cannot tell a complaint that was invented from one that a survivor withdrew under pressure from her own family. And the same police forces that wrote "false" on 3,776 files filed charge-sheets in 24,614.

> "False" in a police file is an investigator's opinion. It is not a court's finding that a woman lied.

## An acquittal is not a verdict on honesty

Courts completed 20,587 rape trials in 2024. They convicted in 5,032 cases and acquitted in 13,980: a conviction rate of 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Myth-sellers read 13,980 acquittals as 13,980 lies. That is not what an acquittal means. A criminal court convicts only when guilt is proved beyond reasonable doubt. When a trial runs for years, memories fade, witnesses move away or are pressured, and evidence weakens. A case can fail without anyone finding that the complaint was false.

The law says this plainly in another setting. The POSH Act states that "a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant"; malicious intent has to be established through an inquiry [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Failing to prove is not the same as lying.

## The silent majority who never report

The real distortion in India's rape numbers is not false complaints. It is silence. A 2022 peer-reviewed study noted estimates that only about 1% of victims of sexual violence in India report it to the authorities [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. Our stories on why the police count is not the rape count, and on why surveys and police records disagree, break down the arithmetic of that silence.

Silence even makes India look safer than it is. WHO's 2023 estimates put lifetime sexual violence by a non-partner at 4.1% for Indian women aged 15-49, against 39.8% in Sweden. WHO cautions that such gaps reflect differences in disclosure, stigma and survey methods as well as real differences in violence [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Where stigma is high, services are few and reporting carries serious repercussions, it adds, real levels are likely much higher than the estimates show [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

That is the cost this story has counted: years, pressure, suspicion. Every viral "false case" post raises it for the next woman, and lowers the risk for the next offender.

This is general information, not legal advice.
false-rape-case-myth-cost-of-complaint.hg:
Har kuch hafton mein ek post viral hoti hai: ek aadmi jiski zindagi ek jhoothi rape complaint ne "barbaad" kar di. Post ke saath verdict bhi chipka hota hai: aurtein paise ke liye jhooth bolti hain, badla lene ke liye jhooth bolti hain. Baaki record kabhi is post ke saath travel nahi karta, aur woh record bilkul ulti kahani batata hai. India mein rape report karne mein ek aurat ki zindagi ke kai saal chale jaate hain, compensation zyada se zyada kuch lakh rupaye ka hota hai, jiske liye kisi ka naam lena zaroori bhi nahi, aur jin trials ka faisla aata hai unmein se sirf 24.4% mein conviction hota hai. Zyada tar aurtein toh report hi nahi karti.

## Yeh myth online itni tezi se kyun failta hai

Ek dramatic case share karna aasaan hai. Saalon tak ghisatne wala trial kabhi trend nahi karta.

Yeh myth accused ke aas-paas walon ke bhi bade kaam aata hai. 2024 mein India mein register hue 96.8% rape cases mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha: 29,536 mein se 28,597 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab accused cousin ho, padosi ho, boss ho ya ex ho, toh family, mohalle ya office ke liye sabse aasaan kahani yahi hai: "ladki jhooth bol rahi hai."

Aisi kuch posts mein aurat ka naam ya photo bhi daal diya jaata hai. Rape survivor ki pehchaan khol de, aisa kuch bhi publish karna Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 72 ke under crime hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Phir bhi naye code ke pehle chhe mahino mein, July se December 2024 tak, police ne aise sirf 11 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Supreme Court is soch ko pehle hi reject kar chuka hai. Uski 2023 ki Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes kehti hai: "It is therefore untrue that women are very likely to make false allegations." [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]] Yaani yeh sach nahi ki aurtein aksar jhoothe aarop lagati hain. Handbook yeh bhi kehti hai ki der se report karna jhooth ki nishaani nahi hai: aage kya hoga iska darr, ya family ka saath na milna, survivor ko rok sakta hai.

## Line mein saal: ek complaint ke baad kya-kya hota hai

Sochiye, Kanpur ki ek 22 saal ki ladki police ko batati hai ki ek rishtedaar ne uska rape kiya. Ab ek magistrate uska statement record karega, jahan tak ho sake ek mahila magistrate [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Doctor uska examination karega. Phir investigation shuru hogi. 2024 mein police ne 24,614 rape cases mein charge-sheet file ki, yaani charge-sheeting rate 81.3% raha, aur saal ke end tak 8,905 cases ki investigation abhi bhi chal rahi thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Kaagaz par, charge-sheet ke do mahine ke andar trial khatam ho jaana chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Asliyat mein, 2024 mein courts ke saamne 2,06,777 rape cases the, aur saal ke end mein inmein se 1,85,785 abhi bhi pending the: 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo courts speed ke liye bane the, wahan bhi jam laga hai. 31 December 2025 ko Fast Track Special Courts mein lagbhag 2,45,579 rape aur POCSO cases pending the [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]].

Is beech woh shayad usi gali mein rehti hai jahan accused rehta hai, aur "settle" karne ka pressure lagataar bana rehta hai. March 2021 mein Supreme Court ko ek High Court ki bail condition cancel karni padi, jismein sexual assault ke accused se kaha gaya tha ki woh complainant se rakhi bandhwaye. Court ne kaha ki courts compromise ya shaadi suggest nahi kar sakte [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

Aur paisa? NALSA ki 2018 scheme ke under rape survivor Rs 4-7 lakh compensation ki haqdaar hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]], lekin asal mein kitna milega yeh state aur district legal services authorities decide karti hain. Yeh paisa ek state scheme se aata hai, aur survivor tab bhi apply kar sakti hai jab offender ka pata hi na chale aur koi trial na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Matlab kisi khaas aadmi ka naam lena iski shart hi nahi hai. Aur kaam ki jagah ki complaints mein POSH Act paise ke badle conciliation ki permission hi nahi deta [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Police file mein 'false' ka matlab kya hai, aur kya nahi

2024 mein police ne 30,272 rape cases dispose kiye. Inmein se 3,776 ko final report mein "false" bolkar band kiya, 714 ko "mistake of fact ya law" ya "civil dispute" bolkar, aur 1,044 ko sach maana gaya par saboot kam the ya accused ka pata nahi chala [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh "false" police ka label hai jo investigation ke stage par lagta hai, kisi court ka faisla nahi. Yeh label nahi bata sakta ki complaint sach mein gadhi gayi thi, ya survivor ne apni hi family ke pressure mein case wapas le liya. Aur dhyan dijiye: jis police ne 3,776 files par "false" likha, usi ne 24,614 cases mein charge-sheet bhi file ki.

> Police file mein "false" ek investigating officer ki raay hai. Yeh court ka faisla nahi ki aurat ne jhooth bola.

## Acquittal ka matlab yeh nahi ki usne jhooth bola

2024 mein courts ne 20,587 rape trials poore kiye. 5,032 cases mein conviction hua aur 13,980 mein accused bari ho gaye: conviction rate 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Myth failane wale in 13,980 acquittals ko 13,980 jhooth ki tarah dikhate hain. Par acquittal ka yeh matlab nahi hota. Criminal court tabhi saza deta hai jab guilt "beyond reasonable doubt" saabit ho. Jab trial saalon chalta hai, yaadein dhundhli ho jaati hain, gawah kahin aur chale jaate hain ya un par pressure daala jaata hai, aur saboot kamzor pad jaate hain. Case gir sakta hai bina kisi ke yeh paaye ki complaint jhoothi thi.

Indian law ek aur jagah yeh baat saaf kehta hai. POSH Act ke hisaab se, "a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant" [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Yaani sirf complaint saabit na kar paane se complainant par action nahi banta, aur malicious intent ho toh woh alag se inquiry mein saabit karna padta hai. Saabit na kar paana aur jhooth bolna, do alag cheezein hain.

## Woh khamosh majority jo kabhi report nahi karti

India ke rape numbers mein asli gadbad false complaints nahi hain. Asli gadbad hai chuppi. 2022 ki ek peer-reviewed study ne estimates note kiye ki India mein sexual violence ke sirf lagbhag 1% victims hi authorities tak report karte hain [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. Is chuppi ka poora hisaab hamari do stories mein hai: ek batati hai ki police ka count rape ka asli count kyun nahi hai, aur doosri ki surveys aur police records alag-alag kyun bolte hain.

Yeh chuppi India ko kaagaz par zyada safe bhi dikhati hai. WHO ke 2023 estimates ke hisaab se India mein 15-49 saal ki 4.1% aurton ne zindagi mein kabhi kisi non-partner ki sexual violence jheli, jabki Sweden mein yeh 39.8% hai. WHO khud warn karta hai ki aise gaps mein sirf violence ka fark nahi hota: log kitna khulkar batate hain, kitna stigma hai aur survey kaise hua, in sab ka bhi asar hota hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. WHO kehta hai ki jahan stigma zyada hai, services kam hain aur report karne ke serious nateeje bhugatne padte hain, wahan asli level shayad estimates se kahin zyada hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Yahi woh keemat hai jiska hisaab is story ne lagaya: saal, pressure aur shak. Har viral "false case" post yeh keemat agli aurat ke liye badha deti hai, aur agle offender ka risk ghata deti hai.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

fast-track-courts-not-fast-myth.en:
After a crime that shocks the country, the announcements follow a pattern: a special team, a promise of the harshest punishment, and a "fast-track court". The phrase does a lot of work. It suggests that this case, at least, will be decided in weeks, and that the system has a quick lane for the worst crimes. The government's own figures describe a lane that is jammed, and getting slower.

## The promise in the headline

India does have a fast-track system for sexual violence. In November 2026 it counted 779 Fast Track Special Courts in 29 states and union territories, 399 of them only for POCSO cases [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Since the scheme began on 2 October 2019, these courts have disposed of 4,02,457 rape and POCSO cases [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. That is real work, and real survivors got verdicts from it.

On 4 November 2026 the Union Cabinet extended the scheme to 31 March 2031, with an outlay of Rs 3,788.04 crore and room for up to 850 courts [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. So the promise will keep being made. The question is what it actually delivers.

## What a Fast Track Special Court actually is

A Fast Track Special Court is a court funded under a centrally sponsored scheme to hear rape and POCSO cases. The Centre's share comes from the Nirbhaya Fund [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]], which had released Rs 1,234.55 crore for these courts by July 2026 [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

What the label does not bring is a deadline of its own. The two-month limit for finishing a rape trial applies to every court that hears one, fast-track or not [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. For children, the POCSO Act already asks every designated Special Court to record the child's evidence within 30 days and to finish the trial, as far as possible, within a year [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. A fast-track court is a dedicated courtroom with a dedicated list, not a faster law.

It is not even permanent everywhere. Jharkhand left the scheme in July 2025 [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]].

## The two-month rule and the real queue

On paper, a rape trial must end within two months of the chargesheet, and an appeal against the sentence within six months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The law sets no consequence when a court misses that deadline.

Now look at the queue. About 2,45,579 rape and POCSO cases were pending before fast-track courts on 31 December 2025 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. That means hundreds of cases waiting before each court. A judge cannot give every one of them a two-month trial. The rule describes a single case; the queue describes the system.

And the fast-track courts carry only part of the load. At the end of 2024, NCRB counted 1,85,785 rape cases and 2,86,903 POCSO cases pending trial in Indian courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The fast-track courts held 2,04,122 cases at the same point [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. The two counts come from different systems, but the gap is plain: many survivors' cases never reach a fast-track court at all.

## Disposals falling, cases waiting

The courts built for speed are deciding fewer cases. They disposed of 76,319 rape and POCSO cases in 2023 and 85,595 in 2024, then only 66,500 in 2025, a fall of 22% [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]].

In the same year, more cases arrived than before: 1,43,936 new cases reached these courts in 2025 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. More than twice as many cases came in as went out. The backlog had barely moved from 2,02,175 at the end of 2023 to 2,04,122 at the end of 2024; then it jumped to 2,45,579 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. By our arithmetic, at the 2025 pace these courts would need more than three years to clear that backlog even if not a single new case arrived.

A disposal is also not a conviction. It counts every case that leaves the list, whatever the result. Across all Indian courts in 2024, trials ended in conviction in 24.4% of rape cases and 32.3% of POCSO cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Speed matters to survivors, but a quick acquittal after a weak investigation is not the justice the headline promised.

## What a survivor can realistically expect

Consider a 16-year-old in Patna whose case is sent to a POCSO fast-track court. Inside the courtroom, the law protects her in ways that do not depend on the queue. Lawyers must put their questions through the judge. The court must not allow aggressive questioning or call her to testify again and again. She must not have to face the accused while testifying, and the trial must be held in camera with a parent or trusted person present [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Adult survivors also have the right to an in-camera trial, as far as practicable before a woman judge [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Ask for these protections by name.

What the queue changes is time. On the government's own numbers, plan for months or years, not weeks. Use the rights that do not wait for a verdict. A victim is entitled to an update on the investigation within 90 days and, if she has a lawyer, to free copies of the police report, FIR and statements [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Compensation can be claimed from the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

More courts can help, and the extension allows up to 850 [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. But a courtroom with hundreds of cases on its list is fast only in name. When the next leader promises a fast-track court, ask the follow-up question: how many cases are already waiting in the ones we have?
fast-track-courts-not-fast-myth.hg:
Desh ko hila dene wale kisi crime ke baad announcements ka pattern same hota hai: ek special team, sabse sakht saza ka promise, aur ek "fast-track court". Yeh phrase bahut kaam karta hai. Lagta hai ki kam se kam is case ka verdict toh kuch hafton mein aa jaayega, aur sabse bure crimes ke liye system mein ek fast lane hai. Sarkar ke apne figures batate hain ki yeh lane jam hai, aur aur bhi slow hoti ja rahi hai.

## Headline wala promise

India mein sexual violence ke liye fast-track system sach mein hai. November 2026 mein 29 states aur union territories mein 779 Fast Track Special Courts chal rahe the, jinme se 399 sirf POCSO cases sunte hain [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Scheme 2 October 2019 ko shuru hui thi, aur tab se in courts ne rape aur POCSO ke 4,02,457 cases dispose kiye hain [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Yeh real kaam hai, aur real survivors ko isse verdict mile hain.

4 November 2026 ko Union Cabinet ne scheme ko 31 March 2031 tak extend kiya, Rs 3,788.04 crore ke outlay ke saath aur 850 tak courts ki gunjaish ke saath [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Toh yeh promise aage bhi hota rahega. Sawaal yeh hai ki isse asal mein milta kya hai.

## Fast Track Special Court asal mein hai kya

Fast Track Special Court ek aisa court hai jo ek centrally sponsored scheme ke paise se chalta hai aur rape aur POCSO cases sunta hai. Centre ka share Nirbhaya Fund se aata hai [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]], jisne July 2026 tak in courts ke liye Rs 1,234.55 crore release kiye the [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

Lekin "fast-track" label ke saath koi alag deadline nahi aati. Rape trial do mahine mein khatam karne ka rule har us court pe laagu hai jo aisa case sunta hai, chahe woh fast-track ho ya nahi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Bachchon ke cases mein POCSO Act pehle se har designated Special Court se kehta hai ki bachche ka bayaan 30 din mein record ho, aur jahan tak ho sake, trial ek saal mein poora ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yaani fast-track court ek dedicated courtroom hai apni dedicated list ke saath, koi faster law nahi.

Yeh har jagah permanent bhi nahi hai. Jharkhand July 2025 mein scheme se bahar ho gaya [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]].

## Do mahine ka rule aur asli queue

Kaagaz pe rape trial chargesheet ke do mahine ke andar khatam hona chahiye, aur saza ke khilaaf appeal chhe mahine mein [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Lekin agar court yeh deadline miss kare, toh law mein koi consequence tay nahi hai.

Ab queue dekho. 31 December 2025 ko fast-track courts mein rape aur POCSO ke lagbhag 2,45,579 cases pending the [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. Matlab har court ke saamne sainkdon cases wait kar rahe hain. Koi judge un sabko do-do mahine ka trial nahi de sakta. Rule ek case ki baat karta hai; queue poore system ki haalat batati hai.

Aur fast-track courts poore load ka sirf ek hissa uthate hain. 2024 ke end mein NCRB ke hisaab se Indian courts mein rape ke 1,85,785 aur POCSO ke 2,86,903 cases mein trial baaki tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi time fast-track courts mein 2,04,122 cases the [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. Dono counts alag systems se aate hain, par gap saaf hai: bahut se survivors ka case kabhi fast-track court tak pahunchta hi nahi.

## Disposals gire, cases wait karte rahe

Jo courts speed ke liye bane the, woh ab pehle se kam cases decide kar rahe hain. Unhone 2023 mein rape aur POCSO ke 76,319 cases dispose kiye aur 2024 mein 85,595, phir 2025 mein sirf 66,500, yaani 22% ki girawat [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]].

Usi saal pehle se kahin zyada cases aaye: 2025 mein in courts mein 1,43,936 naye cases pahunche [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. Jitne cases nikle, usse double se bhi zyada naye aa gaye. Backlog 2023 ke end mein 2,02,175 tha aur 2024 ke end mein 2,04,122, yaani lagbhag utna hi; phir woh uchhalkar 2,45,579 ho gaya [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. Hamare hisaab se, 2025 ki speed pe in courts ko yeh backlog clear karne mein teen saal se zyada lagenge, woh bhi tab jab ek bhi naya case na aaye.

Aur disposal ka matlab conviction nahi hai. Isme har woh case gina jaata hai jo list se hata, result chahe jo ho. 2024 mein India ki saari courts mein jin cases ka trial poora hua, unme rape ke 24.4% aur POCSO ke 32.3% cases mein conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Survivors ke liye speed matter karti hai, lekin weak investigation ke baad jaldi mila acquittal woh justice nahi hai jiska promise headline mein hua tha.

## Survivor asal mein kya expect kare

Socho, Patna ki ek 16 saal ki ladki ka case POCSO fast-track court mein bheja gaya hai. Courtroom ke andar law use kai protections deta hai jo queue pe depend nahi karte. Lawyers apne sawaal judge ke through poochenge. Court aggressive questioning allow nahi karega, aur use baar-baar gawahi ke liye nahi bulayega. Gawahi dete waqt use accused ka saamna nahi karna padega, aur trial in camera, yaani band kamre mein, hoga, jahan uske parent ya koi bharosemand insaan saath rahega [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Adult survivors ko bhi in-camera trial ka haq hai, jahan tak ho sake woman judge ke saamne [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. In protections ko naam lekar maango.

Queue jo badalti hai, woh hai time. Sarkar ke apne numbers dekhkar hafton ki nahi, mahino ya saalon ki planning rakho. Jo rights verdict ka wait nahi karte, unka use karo. Victim ko 90 din ke andar investigation ka update paane ka haq hai, aur agar uska lawyer hai, toh police report, FIR aur statements ki free copies ka bhi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Compensation State ya District Legal Services Authority se maanga ja sakta hai, chahe offender kabhi trace na ho aur trial ho hi na [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Zyada courts se madad mil sakti hai, aur extension 850 tak courts allow karta hai [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Lekin jis courtroom ki list mein sainkdon cases hon, woh sirf naam ka fast hai. Agli baar jab koi neta fast-track court ka promise kare, toh follow-up sawaal poocho: jo courts pehle se hain, unme kitne cases wait kar rahe hain?

ghar-ki-baat-privacy-myth-crimes.en:
Consider this situation. In a housing society in Pune, the neighbours hear a man shouting and a woman crying through one wall every few nights. In the lift the next morning, nobody mentions it. Asked, someone will say "unke ghar ka mamla hai": it is their family's matter. Inside the flat, the woman has heard the same rule from her own mother. "Ghar ki baat ghar mein rehni chahiye." What happens at home stays at home.

The rule is presented as dignity and privacy. The data shows what it actually keeps inside.

## The rule nobody wrote down

No law sets out the rule, but nearly everyone can recite it. A wife does not complain about her husband to outsiders. A child does not speak against an uncle. A neighbour does not interfere. The penalty for breaking it is shame, summed up in three words: "log kya kahenge".

It is obeyed. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 77.2% of women aged 18-49 who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone, and only 14.1% had ever sought help [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Even "telling" mostly stays indoors: of the women who did seek help, 60.9% turned to their own family and only 6.3% went to the police.

## What hides behind it: three crimes at home

**Wife-beating.** In NFHS-5, 29.3% of ever-married women reported physical or sexual violence by a husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Police registered 1,20,227 cases of cruelty by a husband or his relatives in 2024, the single largest category of crimes against women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Those are only the cases that left the house.

**Sexual violence in marriage.** Among ever-married women who had faced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband and 14% a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The rule holds tightest while the marriage lasts: only 11.3% of women who faced violence solely from their current husband ever sought help, against 23.6% of those who faced it only from a former husband.

**Child sexual abuse.** In 2024 police recorded 3,658 cases of penetrative sexual assault on a child in which the accused was a family member, 8.3% of the 44,126 such cases under the POCSO Act [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Among never-married women in NFHS-5 who had faced sexual violence, the person named most often was a relative other than a father or brother (39%). Only 5% named a stranger, though that estimate rests on a small group of women [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Whose privacy is being protected?

Privacy is a real right, and in Indian law it belongs to a person. The Supreme Court's nine-judge privacy ruling of 2017 tied a woman's right to an abortion to her own reproductive choices under Article 21 [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. The law also guards a survivor's identity: publishing the name, or anything that could identify, a rape survivor is a crime under Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), punishable with up to 2 years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Both protections are hers: her body, her choices, her name. 'Ghar ki baat' reverses this. It hands the privacy to the household's reputation, and takes from the woman or child the one thing privacy is for, the power to decide who knows.

Ask who gains from the silence. Not the person being hurt, for whom silence means it continues. The gain goes to the person doing the hurting, and to relatives who would rather not know.

> Privacy lets a person decide who knows. 'Ghar ki baat' decides for her that nobody will.

## What the law says about the home

The law stopped treating the home as a closed room long ago. Cruelty to a woman by her husband or his relatives is a crime under Sections 85 and 86 of the BNS, punishable with up to 3 years in prison and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 counts sexual abuse as domestic violence [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

For children, silence is itself an offence. Under Sections 19 and 21 of POCSO, anyone who knows of child sexual abuse must report it, and failing to report can mean up to 6 months in prison or a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

In one place the law still agrees with the myth. Exception 2 to Section 63 of the BNS says sex by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. As of 19 November 2026 the Supreme Court had not ruled on the challenge to it, and said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

Cases that leave the home are often pulled back in. In 2024, 16,396 cruelty cases in court ended in compromise or compounding, more than the 10,689 that ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The data cannot say how many of those compromises were freely chosen. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Breaking the rule safely

Breaking the rule does not mean a scene on the staircase. A confrontation can make the next night worse for her.

If you hear someone in immediate danger, call 112. Otherwise, find a moment when she is alone and say: "I have heard it. I am here. Tell me what you need." Then let her lead. An adult woman decides whether and when to go to the police. Your job is to make sure she is not alone when she does.

If she is your daughter or sister, retire the sentence "adjust kar lo". Tell her the door of her parents' home is open, and mean it. She can call the Women Helpline or walk into a One Stop Centre; 985 were operational across India as of July 2026 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

With a child there is no waiting. Believe what you are told, do not promise secrecy, and report to the Child Helpline 1098 or the police [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Teachers and doctors are bound by the same duty.

The rule survives because each person who obeys it assumes everyone else will too. It takes one neighbour, one aunt or one teacher to show a woman or a child that someone outside the door already knows, and is on their side.
ghar-ki-baat-privacy-myth-crimes.hg:
Is situation ko sochiye. Pune ki ek housing society mein padosiyon ko har kuch raaton mein ek deewar ke us paar se ek aadmi ke chillane aur ek aurat ke rone ki awaaz aati hai. Agli subah lift mein koi iska zikr nahi karta. Poochne par koi keh dega, "Unke ghar ka mamla hai." Flat ke andar us aurat ne yahi rule apni maa se bhi suna hai: "Ghar ki baat ghar mein rehni chahiye."

Is rule ko izzat aur privacy ka naam diya jaata hai. Data dikhata hai ki yeh asal mein andar kya band rakhta hai.

## Woh rule jo kisi ne likha nahi

Yeh rule kisi law mein nahi likha, par lagbhag har kisi ko zubaani yaad hai. Biwi bahar walon se pati ki shikayat nahi karti. Bachcha chacha ya mama ke khilaf nahi bolta. Padosi beech mein nahi padta. Rule todne ki saza hai sharm, jo teen shabdon mein simat jaati hai: "log kya kahenge".

Aur yeh rule maana jaata hai. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein 18-49 saal ki jin women ne physical ya sexual violence jheli thi, unmein se 77.2% ne kabhi help nahi maangi aur kisi ko bataya bhi nahi; sirf 14.1% ne kabhi help maangi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. "Batana" bhi zyada tar ghar ke andar hi rehta hai: jin women ne help maangi, unmein se 60.9% apni hi family ke paas gayi aur sirf 6.3% police ke paas.

## Iske peeche kya chhupa hai: ghar ke teen crimes

**Wife-beating.** NFHS-5 mein 29.3% ever-married women ne bataya ki pati ne un par physical ya sexual violence ki [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. 2024 mein police ne pati ya uske relatives ki cruelty ke 1,20,227 cases register kiye; yeh crimes against women ki sabse badi single category hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur yeh sirf woh cases hain jo ghar se bahar nikal paaye.

**Shaadi ke andar sexual violence.** Jin ever-married women ne sexual violence jheli thi, unmein se 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya aur 14% ne former husband ka [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Rule sabse kas kar tab tak laagu rehta hai jab tak shaadi chal rahi hai: jin women ne sirf current husband ki violence jheli, unmein se sirf 11.3% ne kabhi help maangi, jabki jinhone sirf former husband ki violence jheli, unmein 23.6% ne.

**Child sexual abuse.** 2024 mein police ne bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke 3,658 aise cases record kiye jinmein accused family member tha; yeh POCSO Act ke aise 44,126 cases ka 8.3% hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NFHS-5 mein jin never-married women ne sexual violence jheli thi, unhone sabse zyada kisi aise relative ka naam liya jo papa ya bhai nahi tha (39%). Sirf 5% ne kisi stranger ka naam liya, halanki yeh estimate women ke ek chhote group par tika hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Privacy kiski bachayi ja rahi hai?

Privacy ek asli haq hai, aur Indian law mein yeh insaan ka haq hai. Supreme Court ke nau judges ke 2017 ke privacy faisle ne aurat ke abortion ke haq ko Article 21 ke under uske apne reproductive choices se joda [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Law survivor ki pehchaan ki bhi hifazat karta hai: rape survivor ka naam ya uski pehchaan khol sakne wali koi bhi detail publish karna Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 72 ke under crime hai, jismein 2 saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yeh dono protections uski hain: uski body, uske choices, uska naam. 'Ghar ki baat' ise ulat deti hai. Yeh privacy ghar ki izzat ko de deti hai, aur aurat ya bachche se wahi cheez chheen leti hai jiske liye privacy bani hai: yeh tay karne ki taaqat ki kise pata chale.

Poochiye ki chuppi se fayda kise hota hai. Us insaan ko nahi jise chot pahunch rahi hai; uske liye chuppi ka matlab hai ki yeh chalta rahega. Fayda use hota hai jo chot pahuncha raha hai, aur un relatives ko jo jaanna hi nahi chahte.

> Privacy insaan ko tay karne deti hai ki kise pata chale. 'Ghar ki baat' uski jagah tay kar deti hai ki kisi ko pata nahi chalega.

## Ghar ke baare mein law kya kehta hai

Law ne ghar ko band kamra maanna bahut pehle chhod diya tha. Pati ya uske relatives ka aurat ke saath cruelty karna BNS ke Sections 85 aur 86 ke under crime hai, jismein 3 saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 sexual abuse ko domestic violence maanta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Bachchon ke maamle mein chuppi khud ek offence hai. POCSO ke Sections 19 aur 21 ke under, jise bhi child sexual abuse ka pata ho, use report karna zaroori hai, aur report na karne par 6 mahine tak ki jail ya fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Ek jagah law abhi bhi myth ke saath khada hai. BNS ke Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar biwi 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh pati ka uske saath sex rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 19 November 2026 tak Supreme Court ne is exception ke challenge par faisla nahi diya tha, aur kaha tha ki final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko rakhi jayegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

Jo cases ghar se bahar nikalte hain, unhe aksar wapas andar kheench liya jaata hai. 2024 mein court mein cruelty ke 16,396 cases compromise ya compounding par khatam hue, jo conviction par khatam hue 10,689 cases se zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Data yeh nahi bata sakta ki inmein se kitne compromise apni marzi se hue. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Rule ko safely kaise todein

Rule todne ka matlab seedhiyon par tamasha karna nahi hai. Aamna-saamna karne se uski agli raat aur buri ho sakti hai.

Agar aapko lage ki koi abhi khatre mein hai, toh 112 par call kijiye. Warna aisa mauka dhoondhiye jab woh akeli ho, aur kahiye: "Maine suna hai. Main yahan hoon. Batao tumhe kya chahiye." Phir use lead karne dijiye. Police ke paas jaana hai ya nahi, aur kab, yeh ek adult aurat khud tay karti hai. Aapka kaam yeh pakka karna hai ki jab woh jaaye toh akeli na ho.

Agar woh aapki beti ya behen hai, toh "adjust kar lo" wala sentence retire kar dijiye. Use bataiye ki maayke ka darwaza khula hai, aur sach mein khula rakhiye. Woh Women Helpline par call kar sakti hai ya One Stop Centre ja sakti hai; July 2026 tak India bhar mein 985 One Stop Centres chal rahe the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

Bachche ke maamle mein intezaar nahi hota. Jo bataya jaaye us par yakeen kijiye, secret rakhne ka promise mat kijiye, aur Child Helpline 1098 ya police ko report kijiye [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Teachers aur doctors par bhi yahi duty hai.

Yeh rule isliye chalta hai kyunki ise maanne wala har insaan maan leta hai ki baaki sab bhi maanenge. Ek padosi, ek mausi ya ek teacher kaafi hai kisi aurat ya bachche ko yeh dikhane ke liye ki darwaze ke bahar koi pehle se jaanta hai, aur uski taraf hai.

good-girls-are-safe-respectability-myth.en:
Imagine the rules a 15-year-old in Kanpur could recite without thinking. Dupatta in place. Home before the streetlights come on. No boys, no arguing, no phone calls after dinner. Behind the list sits a bargain her family believes in: follow the rules and you will be safe. The bargain has a second half that is rarely said aloud. A girl who breaks the rules, and any woman who never followed them, has given up part of her claim to protection, and to being believed.

Both halves fail against the evidence.

## The bargain families offer their daughters

The bargain does not end at the wedding; it is rewritten for wives. In the fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 45% of women and 44% of men said a husband is justified in beating his wife in at least one of seven situations [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The reason accepted most often was not cruelty or crime. It was 'disrespect' to her in-laws, accepted by 32% of women and 31% of men.

That is the bargain in plain numbers. Obedience is the price of safety, and any lapse becomes the excuse. Our state map of wife-beating excuses shows where this belief runs deepest. The point here is what it teaches a girl long before her marriage: that violence is something a woman earns.

## Who is actually assaulted: wives and children in 'safe' places

If modesty, obedience and staying home protected women, the most respectable role of all, the wife at home, would be the safest. It is not. Among ever-married women in NFHS-5 who had faced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband and 14% a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Children in the most protected places are not safe either. In a social audit of Bihar's children's homes, done for the state government and submitted in April 2018, the Tata Institute of Social Sciences flagged sexual abuse at several institutions, including a state-funded girls' shelter home in Muzaffarpur [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. The audit exposed the sexual abuse of 34 minor girls there [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. These were girls the state had taken into its own care. On 20 January 2020 a POCSO court in Saket, Delhi, convicted 19 of the 20 accused; 11 were later sentenced to life imprisonment [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

Obedience does not shield children from this kind of abuse; it can help hide it. The government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse found that half of abusers were people known to the child or in a position of trust and responsibility, and that most children told no one [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. A child trained never to question an adult is the easiest child to silence.

## 'She has a past': what the law says about character

The second half of the bargain says some women cannot really be raped: the girlfriend, the divorcee, the woman who drinks, the sex worker. Indian law rejected that idea in 2013, when Parliament made a survivor's character or previous sexual experience irrelevant to the question of consent [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. In 2022 the Supreme Court called it patriarchal and sexist to doubt a rape complaint because a woman is sexually active [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]].

Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines rape by the absence of real consent: acts done against a woman's will or without her consent, with consent obtained through fear of death or hurt, with consent given while she was intoxicated or of unsound mind, or when she cannot communicate consent [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Nothing in it depends on her clothes, her job, her past or her reputation. A sex worker is covered as fully as anyone else.

There is one hole, and it sits exactly where the bargain says women are safest. Exception 2 to Section 63 says sex by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. As of 19 November 2026 the Supreme Court had not ruled on the challenge to that exception, and said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The words the Supreme Court told judges to drop

Respectability needs a vocabulary, and Indian courtrooms had one. In August 2023 the Supreme Court issued a Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes for judges [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Its glossary takes 'chaste woman', 'fallen woman', 'harlot', 'whore', 'slut', 'seductress' and 'woman of easy virtue' and replaces every one of them with a single word: 'woman'. 'Prostitute' becomes 'sex worker'. 'Unwed mother' becomes 'mother'. 'Child prostitute' becomes 'child who has been trafficked'.

Each old label sorted women into those who deserve protection and those who do not. The handbook also rejects the idea of a 'proper' survivor who keeps to the bargain even after the crime: 'There is no "correct" or "appropriate" way in which a survivor or victim behaves.' Our story on the 'she asked for it' myth covers what the handbook says about clothes. The point here is that the court has refused to rank women at all.

## Raising children without the bargain

Children learn the bargain at home, and they can unlearn it there. Women whose fathers beat their mothers were more than twice as likely to face violence from their own husbands: 58% against 25% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Men raised in homes where fathers did household chores were twice as likely to hold gender-equal attitudes, a 2014 ICRW-UNFPA study across seven states found [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

In 2024 the Supreme Court recommended comprehensive sex education that gives young people a clear understanding of consent [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. At home, that means replacing 'be a good girl' with things a daughter can actually use: the correct names for her body, the right to refuse any adult, relatives included, and a promise that she will be believed whatever rule she broke. It also means telling sons the rule the bargain never states: no woman's clothes, past, job or marriage gives anyone permission.
good-girls-are-safe-respectability-myth.hg:
Imagine kijiye Kanpur ki ek 15 saal ki ladki ko. Use kuch rules bina soche yaad hain. Dupatta theek rakho. Street lights jalne se pehle ghar aa jao. Ladkon se baat nahi, behas nahi, dinner ke baad phone nahi. Is list ke peeche ek deal hai jis par uski family bharosa karti hai: rules maanogi toh safe rahogi. Is deal ka ek doosra hissa bhi hai jo zor se nahi bola jaata. Jo ladki rules todti hai, aur jo aurat kabhi in rules par chali hi nahi, woh protection ka haq kuch had tak kho deti hai. Log uski baat maanna bhi band kar dete hain.

Evidence ke saamne yeh dono hisse fail ho jaate hain.

## Woh deal jo families betiyon ke saamne rakhti hain

Yeh deal shaadi par khatam nahi hoti; biwi ke liye ise naye sire se likha jaata hai. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein 45% women aur 44% men ne kaha ki saat mein se kam se kam ek situation mein pati ka biwi ko peetna justified hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sabse zyada maana gaya reason koi crime ya zulm nahi tha. Reason tha in-laws ki "disrespect", jise 32% women aur 31% men ne sahi maana.

Numbers mein yahi deal hai. Safety ki keemat hai kehna maanna, aur zara si chook violence ka bahana ban jaati hai. Yeh soch kin states mein sabse gehri hai, woh hamari wife-beating ke bahanon wali state map story mein hai. Yahan point yeh hai ki yeh soch ek ladki ko shaadi se bahut pehle kya sikhati hai: ki violence kuch aisa hai jo aurat khud "kamaati" hai.

## Asli mein assault kiska hota hai: 'safe' jagahon par wives aur bachche

Agar modesty, kehna maanna aur ghar par rehna aurton ko bachate, toh sabse respectable role, yaani ghar par rehne wali wife, sabse safe hoti. Aisa nahi hai. NFHS-5 mein jin married women ne sexual violence jheli thi, unmein se 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya aur 14% ne former husband ka [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Sabse protected jagahon par rehne wale bachche bhi safe nahi hain. Bihar government ke liye kiye gaye aur April 2018 mein submit hue ek social audit mein Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) ne kai institutions mein sexual abuse flag kiya. Inmein Muzaffarpur ka ek state-funded girls' shelter home bhi tha [[newslaundry-tiss-audit-bihar-2018]]. Audit se wahan 34 minor ladkiyon ka sexual abuse saamne aaya [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. Yeh woh bachchiyan thi jinki care ki zimmedari state ne khud li thi. 20 January 2020 ko Delhi ke Saket ki POCSO court ne 20 mein se 19 accused ko convict kiya; baad mein 11 ko umrqaid ki saza hui [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

Kehna maanna bachchon ko aise abuse se nahi bachata; ulta yeh abuse ko chhupane mein madad kar sakta hai. Government ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein pata chala ki aadhe abusers bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale the, ya aise log the jin par bachche ki zimmedari thi aur jin par bachcha bharosa karta tha. Zyada tar bachchon ne kisi ko kuch nahi bataya [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Jis bachche ko sikhaya gaya ho ki badon se kabhi sawaal mat karo, use chup karana sabse aasaan hai.

## 'Uska toh past hai': character ke baare mein law kya kehta hai

Deal ka doosra hissa kehta hai ki kuch aurton ka asli mein rape ho hi nahi sakta: girlfriend, divorcee, drink karne wali aurat, sex worker. Indian law ne yeh soch 2013 mein hi reject kar di thi, jab Parliament ne tay kiya ki consent ke sawaal par survivor ka character ya pehle ka sexual experience relevant nahi hai [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki kisi aurat ki rape complaint par sirf isliye shak karna ki woh sexually active hai, patriarchal aur sexist soch hai [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]].

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 63 rape ko asli consent ke na hone se define karta hai: aurat ki marzi ke khilaf ya uske consent ke bina, maut ya chot ka darr dikha kar li gayi "haan", nashe mein ya dimaagi haalat theek na hone par di gayi "haan", ya jab woh consent bata hi na sake [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Ismein kahin nahi likha ki uske kapde kaise the, woh kya kaam karti hai, uska past kya hai ya log uske baare mein kya kehte hain. Ek sex worker ko bhi yeh law utna hi protect karta hai jitna kisi aur ko.

Par ismein ek chhed hai, aur woh theek wahin hai jahan deal kehti hai ki aurat sabse safe hai. Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar biwi 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh pati ka uske saath sex rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 19 November 2026 tak Supreme Court ne is exception ke challenge par faisla nahi diya tha, aur kaha ki final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko rakhi jayegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Woh shabd jinhe chhodne ko Supreme Court ne judges se kaha

Respectability ko apni vocabulary chahiye, aur courtrooms mein woh chalti thi. August 2023 mein Supreme Court ne judges ke liye "Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes" jaari ki [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Iski glossary 'chaste woman', 'fallen woman', 'harlot', 'whore', 'slut', 'seductress' aur 'woman of easy virtue' jaise labels leti hai, aur har ek ki jagah sirf ek shabd rakhti hai: 'woman'. 'Prostitute' ban jaata hai 'sex worker'. 'Unwed mother' ban jaati hai sirf 'mother'. Aur 'child prostitute' ban jaata hai 'child who has been trafficked', yaani trafficking ka shikaar hua bachcha.

Har purana label aurton ko do hisson mein baant-ta tha: jo protection ki haqdaar hain, aur jo nahi. Handbook us soch ko bhi reject karti hai ki crime ke baad bhi survivor ko 'theek' tarah behave karna chahiye. Usmein likha hai: "There is no 'correct' or 'appropriate' way in which a survivor or victim behaves", yaani survivor ke behave karne ka koi 'sahi' tareeka nahi hota. Kapdon par handbook kya kehti hai, woh hamari 'she asked for it' myth wali story mein hai. Yahan point yeh hai ki court ne aurton ko upar-neeche rank karne se hi mana kar diya hai.

## Bachchon ko is deal ke bina bada karna

Bachche yeh deal ghar mein seekhte hain, aur ghar mein hi ise bhool bhi sakte hain. Jin aurton ke papa unki mummy ko maarte the, unke saath unke apne husband ki violence ka chance do guna se bhi zyada tha: 58%, jabki baaki aurton mein 25% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. 2014 mein saat states mein hui ICRW-UNFPA study ke mutabik, jin gharon mein papa ghar ka kaam karte the, wahan pale ladkon mein gender-equal soch hone ka chance do guna tha [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

2024 mein Supreme Court ne recommend kiya ki bachchon ko comprehensive sex education mile, jo consent ki clear samajh de [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Ghar par iska matlab hai 'achhi ladki bano' ki jagah beti ko aisi cheezein dena jo sach mein kaam aayein: body parts ke sahi naam, kisi bhi bade ko mana karne ka haq, relatives ko bhi, aur yeh promise ki usne koi bhi rule toda ho, uski baat maani jayegi. Iska matlab beton ko woh rule batana bhi hai jo yeh deal kabhi nahi batati: kisi aurat ke kapde, uska past, uska kaam ya uski shaadi, kisi ko bhi permission nahi dete.

hiv-contact-myths-discrimination.en:
Imagine a housing society in Nagpur. A man on the second floor has started going to the government hospital every month, and someone who has seen him there mentions why. By evening the society's WhatsApp group knows. Within a week the landlord has asked whether the family "might be more comfortable elsewhere", a parent has asked the school to seat his daughter on a separate bench, and the neighbour who used to share tiffin with his wife has stopped. None of this protects anyone from HIV. Some of it is what Indian law now forbids.

## Hugs, plates, mosquitoes: what people still believe

The beliefs that drive a week like that are not fringe. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), only 54% of women and 64% of men aged 15-49 knew that HIV cannot be transmitted by mosquito bites. Only 45% of women and 59% of men knew it cannot spread by sharing food with a person who has AIDS [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Turn those numbers around. Nearly half of Indian women, 46%, did not know a mosquito cannot give them HIV, and 55% could not rule out a shared meal; those shares include wrong answers and "don't know". In the same survey, only 22% of women and 31% of men had what it calls comprehensive knowledge of HIV/AIDS [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. When a neighbourhood learns that a family has HIV in it, most of the adults deciding how to behave are guessing.

## How HIV actually spreads

HIV is carried in specific body fluids, including blood, semen, vaginal fluids and breast milk. It passes on through sex without a condom, shared needles and syringes, unscreened blood, and from a parent to a baby during pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding when there is no treatment. It does not spread through ordinary day-to-day contact: hugging, kissing, shaking hands, or sharing food, water, plates and other personal objects [[who-hiv]]. A mosquito cannot pass it on either; the national survey treats that belief as a misconception [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

India's own records agree. Among 1,63,306 people newly diagnosed with HIV in 2024-25, these were the routes they reported [[naco-sankalak-2025]]:

| Reported route | Share of new diagnoses, 2024-25 |
|---|---|
| Heterosexual sex | nearly 74% |
| Shared needles or syringes | 11.5% |
| Homosexual or bisexual sex | 5.4% |
| Mother-to-child | 3.5% |
| Blood | 1.2% |
| No route given | 4.7% |

There is no row for plates, hugs or mosquitoes. The routes are self-reported, and stigma pushes people to under-report sex between men and drug use. Inside the heterosexual share, 32.1% of all newly diagnosed people reported sex with a casual partner, 15.1% with a commercial partner and 26.5% with a regular partner [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. More than one in four named a regular partner. "It only happens to other kinds of people" is a myth as well.

## From fear to exclusion

If you believe a plate can infect you, keeping a separate plate feels like caution, not cruelty. That is how a wrong fact turns into a social rule: the steel glass kept aside, the child moved to the last bench, the tenant asked to leave, the employee told to resign "for everyone's comfort". We found no national count of how often this happens. The clearest record is the law, which had to list these acts one by one in order to ban them.

The exclusion also works against everyone's health. An estimated 25.61 lakh people were living with HIV in India in 2024, and in 2024-25 only 83.9% of them knew their status [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Someone who has watched a neighbour lose a home over a test result has a reason never to take the test. Meanwhile the people being shunned pose no risk in daily life, and with regular treatment a person whose virus is undetectable does not pass HIV on through sex either [[who-hiv]].

## What the HIV Act, 2017 forbids

This is general information, not legal advice. The HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act was enacted in April 2017 and came into force on 10 September 2018 [[mohfw-hiv-act-commencement-2018]].

Section 3 bars discrimination against people living with HIV, and against those who live with them, in employment, health care, education, housing and public or private office. It forbids isolating or segregating them, and it forbids demanding an HIV test as a condition for a job, health care or education [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. In the Nagpur example, the wife and daughter are protected too. A landlord who pushes the family out, or a school that agrees to the separate bench, is doing what the section lists.

The Act also reaches speech. Under Sections 4 and 37, anyone who publishes, propagates or advocates hatred against people living with HIV can be punished with imprisonment of three months to two years, a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh, or both. It guards the information too: no HIV test without informed consent, and no one can be compelled to disclose their status except by a court order [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Every state must appoint an Ombudsman to hear complaints [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. By March 2025, 34 States/UTs had an Ombudsman, 33 had designated Complaints Officers and 29 had notified rules under the Act [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. What is missing is the outcome: we found no national data on how many complaints were filed, how they ended, or whether anyone has been prosecuted for spreading hatred.

## If you see someone being shut out

Start with the ordinary thing: sit down and eat with them. Shared meals, classrooms, bathrooms and hugs carry no risk [[who-hiv]], and one person behaving normally in front of others does more than an argument. When the myth is spoken aloud, answer with the real routes. Do not pass on anyone's status, and do not ask anyone to prove theirs.

If a school, employer, hospital or landlord is doing the excluding, the person can complain in writing to the institution's Complaints Officer or the state's HIV Ombudsman. Help them write it, and keep copies. For questions you cannot ask anyone you know, the national AIDS helpline 1097 is toll-free and gives confidential counselling round the clock in 16 languages [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

The virus has a short list of routes. Everything else on the list was added by fear.
hiv-contact-myths-discrimination.hg:
Socho, Nagpur ki ek housing society hai. Second floor par rehne wala ek aadmi har mahine government hospital jaane laga hai, aur kisi ne use wahan dekha hai aur wajah bhi bata di hai. Shaam tak society ke WhatsApp group ko pata chal chuka hota hai. Ek hafte ke andar landlord pooch leta hai ki family "kahin aur zyada comfortable toh nahi rahegi", ek parent school se keh deta hai ki uski beti ko alag bench par bithaya jaaye, aur jo padosan uski wife ke saath tiffin share karti thi, usne band kar diya. Inmein se koi bhi cheez kisi ko HIV se nahi bachati. Inmein se kuch cheezein wahi hain jinhe Indian law ab mana karta hai.

## Hug, plate, machhar: log aaj bhi kya maante hain

Aise hafte ke peeche jo beliefs hain, woh kisi chhote se group ke nahi hain. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 15-49 saal ki sirf 54% women aur 64% men ko pata tha ki HIV machhar ke kaatne se transmit nahi ho sakta. Sirf 45% women aur 59% men ko pata tha ki AIDS wale insaan ke saath khana share karne se yeh nahi failta [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Ab in numbers ko ulta karke dekho. Lagbhag aadhi Indian women, 46%, ko pata nahi tha ki machhar se unhe HIV nahi ho sakta, aur 55% yeh nahi keh sakti thin ki saath khane se nahi failta; in shares mein galat jawab bhi hain aur "pata nahi" wale jawab bhi. Usi survey mein sirf 22% women aur 31% men ke paas woh tha jise survey HIV/AIDS ki comprehensive knowledge kehta hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jab kisi mohalle ko pata chalta hai ki kisi family mein HIV hai, toh kaise behave karna hai yeh tay karne wale zyadatar adults bas andaaza laga rahe hote hain.

## HIV asal mein kaise failta hai

HIV kuch specific body fluids mein hota hai, jinmein blood, semen, vaginal fluids aur breast milk shaamil hain. Yeh bina condom ke sex se, shared needles aur syringes se, unscreened blood se, aur treatment na ho toh pregnancy, birth ya breastfeeding ke dauraan parent se baby mein pass hota hai. Yeh roz ke aam contact se nahi failta: hug karne, kiss karne, haath milane, ya khana, paani, plate aur doosri personal cheezein share karne se nahi [[who-hiv]]. Machhar bhi ise pass nahi kar sakta; national survey is belief ko misconception maanta hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

India ke apne records bhi yahi kehte hain. 2024-25 mein jin 1,63,306 logon mein HIV naya diagnose hua, unhone yeh routes bataye [[naco-sankalak-2025]]:

| Bataya gaya route | 2024-25 ke naye diagnoses mein share |
|---|---|
| Heterosexual sex | lagbhag 74% |
| Shared needles ya syringes | 11.5% |
| Homosexual ya bisexual sex | 5.4% |
| Mother-to-child | 3.5% |
| Blood | 1.2% |
| Koi route nahi bataya | 4.7% |

Is table mein plate, hug ya machhar ki koi row nahi hai. Routes logon ne khud bataye hain, aur stigma ki wajah se men ke beech sex aur drug use kam report hote hain. Heterosexual share ke andar, saare naye diagnose hue logon mein se 32.1% ne casual partner ke saath sex bataya, 15.1% ne commercial partner ke saath aur 26.5% ne regular partner ke saath [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Yaani har chaar mein se ek se zyada ne regular partner ka naam liya. "Yeh toh sirf doosri tarah ke logon ko hota hai" bhi ek myth hi hai.

## Darr se exclusion tak

Agar tum maante ho ki plate se infection lag sakta hai, toh alag plate rakhna tumhe cruelty nahi, savdhaani lagti hai. Isi tarah ek galat fact social rule ban jaata hai: steel ka glass alag rakh diya gaya, bachche ko last bench par bhej diya gaya, tenant se kaha gaya ki ghar khaali kar do, employee se kaha gaya ki "sabke comfort ke liye" resign kar do. Yeh kitni baar hota hai, iski koi national ginti humein nahi mili. Sabse saaf record khud law hai, jise in harkaton ko ban karne ke liye ek-ek karke likhna pada.

Yeh exclusion sabki health ke khilaaf bhi kaam karta hai. 2024 mein India mein estimated 25.61 lakh log HIV ke saath jee rahe the, aur 2024-25 mein unmein se sirf 83.9% ko apna status pata tha [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Jisne apne padosi ko ek test result ki wajah se ghar khote dekha hai, uske paas test kabhi na karwane ki wajah hai. Udhar jin logon se sab door bhaag rahe hain, unse roz ki zindagi mein koi risk hai hi nahi, aur regular treatment se jis insaan ka virus undetectable ho jaata hai, usse sex ke through bhi HIV pass nahi hota [[who-hiv]].

## HIV Act, 2017 kya mana karta hai

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act April 2017 mein bana aur 10 September 2018 ko lagu hua [[mohfw-hiv-act-commencement-2018]].

Section 3 HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ke khilaaf, aur unke saath rehne walon ke khilaaf, employment, health care, education, housing aur public ya private office mein discrimination ko mana karta hai. Yeh unhe isolate ya segregate karne se rokta hai, aur job, health care ya education ke liye HIV test ki shart rakhne se bhi [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. Nagpur wale example mein wife aur beti bhi protected hain. Jo landlord family ko nikalne par majboor kare, ya jo school alag bench wali baat maan le, woh wahi kar raha hai jo is section mein likha hai.

Yeh Act bolne-likhne tak bhi pahunchta hai. Sections 4 aur 37 ke under, jo bhi HIV ke saath jee rahe logon ke khilaaf nafrat publish, propagate ya advocate kare, use teen mahine se do saal tak ki jail, Rs 1 lakh tak ka fine, ya dono ho sakte hain. Act jaankari ki bhi hifazat karta hai: informed consent ke bina HIV test nahi ho sakta, aur court order ke bina kisi ko apna status batane par majboor nahi kiya ja sakta [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Har state ko complaints sunne ke liye ek Ombudsman appoint karna hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. March 2025 tak 34 States/UTs mein Ombudsman tha, 33 mein designated Complaints Officers the aur 29 ne Act ke under rules notify kar diye the [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Jo cheez gaayab hai woh hai nateeja: kitni complaints file hui, unka kya hua, ya nafrat failane par kisi par case chala ya nahi, is par humein koi national data nahi mila.

## Agar tum kisi ko alag kiya jaata dekho

Sabse simple cheez se shuru karo: unke saath baithkar khana khao. Saath khane, saath class mein baithne, bathroom share karne aur hug karne mein koi risk nahi hai [[who-hiv]], aur sabke saamne ek insaan ka normal behave karna kisi bhi behes se zyada kaam karta hai. Jab koi myth zor se bola jaaye, toh asli routes batao. Kisi ka status aage mat badhao, aur kisi se apna status saabit karne ko mat kaho.

Agar alag karne wala koi school, employer, hospital ya landlord hai, toh woh insaan institution ke Complaints Officer ya state ke HIV Ombudsman ko written complaint de sakta hai. Complaint likhne mein unki madad karo, aur copies sambhal kar rakho. Jo sawaal tum kisi jaan-pehchaan wale se nahi pooch sakte, unke liye national AIDS helpline 1097 toll-free hai aur 16 languages mein chaubees ghante confidential counselling deti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

Virus ke routes ki list chhoti hai. Us list mein baaki sab kuch darr ne joda hai.

hpv-vaccine-promiscuity-myth.en:
Imagine a parents' WhatsApp group in Jaipur in March 2026. Someone forwards a message: the free "cancer injection" offered to 14-year-old girls is really a sex vaccine, and girls from good families do not need it. Some parents quietly keep their daughters at home. The forward is wrong about the vaccine and wrong about the disease. India began offering a single free dose of HPV vaccine to 14-year-old girls on 28 February 2026 [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Cervical cancer, which the vaccine helps prevent, killed an estimated 36,319 women in India in 2024, by the latest GLOBOCAN estimate [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

## The myth: a vaccine for 'that kind' of girl

The logic is simple, and wrong. HPV spreads through sex, so a vaccine against it must be for girls who are having sex, or soon will. From there it is a short step to treating cervical cancer as the price of a "loose" life, and a woman who has it as someone to whisper about.

India has heard this argument before. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 19.6% of Indian men agreed that women who use contraception may become promiscuous [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sex education faced the same charge. The UN's 2018 guidance on sexuality education, whose evidence rests mainly on two commissioned reviews, including a 2016 Oxford review of 22 systematic reviews and 77 randomised controlled trials, states that it does not increase sexual activity, sexual risk-taking or STI/HIV infection rates [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

A vaccine is further still from behaviour: it teaches the immune system to recognise a virus and carries no message about sex. A tetanus shot does not tell a child to go looking for rusty nails. We know of no survey that measures how widely the promiscuity story is believed. Each refusal, though, leaves a girl without a protection that is free today.

## What HPV is, and how common it is

Human papillomavirus is a very common infection passed on through sexual skin contact. Most sexually active people get it at some point in their lives, usually without symptoms, and the body clears most infections on its own [[who-cervical]]. When certain high-risk types persist for years, they can turn cells in the cervix, the opening of the uterus, cancerous. In India, types 16 and 18 account for more than 80% of cervical cancer cases, according to a government backgrounder [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]].

"Most sexually active people" includes wives who have only ever been with their husbands. A husband can pass on HPV he picked up years earlier without knowing it. Men also get genital warts and some cancers from the virus [[who-hpv]]. A diagnosis says a virus persisted; it says nothing about how many partners a woman has had, or about her character.

It is not a rare disease: the latest GLOBOCAN estimates put new cases in India at 79,360 in 2024, the second most common cancer among Indian women [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

## Why the dose comes at 14

The dose is Gardasil-4, a vaccine against four HPV types including 16 and 18, given free at government health facilities [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. The vaccine prevents infection but cannot treat one, so it works best before any exposure to the virus; that is why WHO's elimination target counts girls fully vaccinated by the age of 15 [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

A dose at 14 is not a guess about when a girl will start having sex. It puts protection in place long before she might, whether that is at 19, at 25 or never. For many Indian women the first possible exposure comes with marriage, and marriage sometimes comes early: in NFHS-6 (2023-24), 20.1% of women aged 20-24 had been married before 18 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. A girl vaccinated at 14 is protected before any wedding, wanted or not.

Vaccination is voluntary and a parent's consent is mandatory [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. That is right for a public programme, and it is exactly where a myth can cost a girl her dose.

## Uptake, screening and the cost of stigma

By 15 July 2026, 52,10,302 girls had received the vaccine, the health ministry told Parliament, about 43% of the target of 1.2 crore [[etvbharat-hpv-parliament-2026]]. By 11 September, more than 80 lakh doses had been given, and Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Mizoram reported 100% coverage of the girls they had identified [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]]. That is fast progress, but a large share of the yearly cohort of about 1.2 crore girls was still waiting.

Screening shows what silence about this part of the body already costs. A test can find changes in the cervix years before they turn into cancer [[who-cervical]], yet in 2019-21 only 1.2% of Indian women aged 15-49 had ever been screened for cervical cancer [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. WHO's elimination strategy, to which 194 countries committed, asks for 90% of girls fully vaccinated by 15 and 70% of women screened by 35 and again by 45, all by 2030 [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

A test that means talking about the cervix with a doctor, often with a relative in the room, competes with the fear of what people will say. When a disease is treated as a verdict on character, symptoms get hidden and check-ups get postponed. Women living with HIV, who carry a second stigma, are six times more likely to develop cervical cancer than women without HIV [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]].

## What parents and young women can do

Treat the HPV vaccine like every other vaccine on a child's card. If there is a 14-year-old girl in your family, ask at the nearest government facility; the dose is offered everywhere from Ayushman Arogya Mandir health centres to medical colleges [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. If a relative objects, the answer is short: it prevents a cancer, and it is given before any risk because that is when it works.

Older teenagers and young adults who missed it can still ask a doctor about catch-up vaccination [[who-hpv]]. Vaccinated or not, adult women still need cervical screening, because the vaccine does not cover every cancer-causing HPV type [[who-cervical]]. Bleeding between periods or after sex needs a doctor at any age.

And change the words. Say "cervical cancer is caused by a common virus", not "she must have done something". A girl's vaccination card records her health. It is not a certificate of her character.
hpv-vaccine-promiscuity-myth.hg:
Socho, March 2026 mein Jaipur ke parents ka ek WhatsApp group hai. Koi ek message forward karta hai: 14 saal ki ladkiyon ko jo free "cancer ka injection" diya ja raha hai, woh asal mein sex ki vaccine hai, aur achhe ghar ki ladkiyon ko iski zaroorat nahi. Kuch parents chupchaap beti ko ghar par hi rok lete hain. Yeh forward vaccine ke baare mein bhi galat hai aur bimari ke baare mein bhi. India ne 28 February 2026 se 14 saal ki ladkiyon ko HPV vaccine ki ek free dose dena shuru kiya [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Jis cervical cancer se bachane mein yeh vaccine madad karti hai, usse 2024 mein India mein estimated 36,319 auraton ki maut hui, GLOBOCAN ke latest estimate ke hisaab se [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

## Myth: 'aisi-waisi' ladkiyon ki vaccine

Logic kuch aisa chalta hai. HPV sex se failta hai, toh iski vaccine unhi ladkiyon ke liye hogi jo sex kar rahi hain, ya jaldi karengi. Wahan se agla step aasaan hai: cervical cancer ko 'bigdi hui' life ki saza maan lena, aur jis aurat ko yeh ho, uske baare mein gossip karna. Logic simple lagta hai, par galat hai.

India yeh argument pehle bhi sun chuka hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 19.6% Indian men ne maana ki contraception use karne wali auratein 'promiscuous' ho sakti hain, yaani kai logon se relation banane lagengi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sex education par bhi yahi ilzaam laga. UN ki 2018 ki sexuality education guidance ka evidence mainly do commissioned reviews par tika hai, jinme se ek Oxford ka 2016 ka review hai, jisme 22 systematic reviews aur 77 randomised controlled trials dekhe gaye the. Guidance saaf kehti hai ki sex education se na sexual activity badhti hai, na risky behaviour, na STI/HIV infection [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

Vaccine toh behaviour se aur bhi door ki cheez hai: yeh immune system ko ek virus pehchanna sikhati hai, aur isme sex ka koi message nahi hota. Tetanus ka injection kisi bachche se nahi kehta ki jao, zang lagi keelein dhoondo. Hamari jaankari mein aisa koi survey nahi hai jo measure kare ki 'promiscuity' wali yeh kahani kitne log maante hain. Par har refusal ka matlab hai ki ek ladki us protection se chook gayi jo aaj free mil raha hai.

## HPV kya hai, aur kitna common hai

Human papillomavirus, yaani HPV, ek bahut common infection hai jo sexual contact mein skin-to-skin chhoone se failta hai. Sex karne wale zyadatar logon ko zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi yeh hota hai, aksar bina kisi symptom ke, aur zyadatar infections body khud clear kar deti hai [[who-cervical]]. Lekin kuch high-risk types saalon tak tike rahein, toh cervix ke cells ko cancer mein badal sakte hain. Cervix yaani uterus ka muh. Government ke ek backgrounder ke mutabik India mein cervical cancer ke 80% se zyada cases HPV type 16 aur 18 se hote hain [[pib-hpv-backgrounder-2026]].

"Sex karne wale zyadatar log" mein woh wives bhi shaamil hain jinka kabhi apne husband ke alawa kisi se relation nahi raha. Ho sakta hai husband ko yeh virus saalon pehle laga ho, bina use pata chale, aur woh ise wife tak pahuncha de. Men ko bhi is virus se genital warts aur kuch cancers hote hain [[who-hpv]]. Diagnosis bas itna batata hai ki virus body mein tika raha. Yeh nahi batata ki aurat ke kitne partners rahe, aur uske character ke baare mein toh kuch bhi nahi.

Yeh koi rare bimari bhi nahi hai. GLOBOCAN ke latest estimate ke mutabik 2024 mein India mein cervical cancer ke 79,360 naye cases aaye, aur Indian women mein yeh doosra sabse common cancer hai [[iarc-globocan-india-factsheet-2024]].

## Dose 14 saal par hi kyun

Campaign mein Gardasil-4 vaccine lagti hai, jo HPV ke chaar types se bachati hai, jinmein 16 aur 18 bhi hain. Government health facilities par yeh free lagti hai [[pib-hpv-campaign-launch-2026]]. Vaccine infection se bachati hai, par ho chuke infection ka ilaaj nahi karti, isliye yeh virus se kisi bhi exposure se pehle sabse achha kaam karti hai. Isiliye WHO ka elimination target un ladkiyon ko ginta hai jinhe 15 saal ki umar tak poori vaccine lag chuki ho [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

14 saal par dose dene ka matlab yeh guess karna nahi hai ki ladki kab sex shuru karegi. Matlab hai usse bahut pehle protection ready kar dena, chahe woh din 19 ki umar mein aaye, 25 mein, ya kabhi na aaye. Bahut si Indian auraton ke liye virus se pehla possible exposure shaadi ke saath aata hai, aur shaadi kai baar jaldi ho jaati hai: NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein 20-24 saal ki 20.1% women ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho chuki thi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Jis ladki ko 14 saal par vaccine lag gayi, woh har shaadi se pehle protected hai, shaadi uski marzi se ho ya nahi.

Vaccination voluntary hai aur parents ka consent zaroori hai [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. Ek public programme ke liye yeh sahi rule hai, aur theek yahin ek myth kisi ladki se uski dose chheen sakta hai.

## Uptake, screening aur stigma ki keemat

Health ministry ne Parliament ko bataya ki 15 July 2026 tak 52,10,302 ladkiyon ko vaccine lag chuki thi, jo 1.2 crore target ka lagbhag 43% tha [[etvbharat-hpv-parliament-2026]]. 11 September tak 80 lakh se zyada doses lag chuki thin, aur Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh aur Mizoram ne apni identified ladkiyon mein 100% coverage report kiya [[pib-hpv-80-lakh-doses-2026]]. Speed achhi hai, lekin har saal ki lagbhag 1.2 crore ladkiyon mein se bada hissa abhi baaki tha.

Screening dikhati hai ki body ke is hisse par chuppi ki keemat pehle se kitni bhaari hai. Ek test cervix ke badlaav cancer banne se saalon pehle pakad sakta hai [[who-cervical]], phir bhi 2019-21 mein 15-49 saal ki sirf 1.2% Indian women ne kabhi cervical cancer screening karwayi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Is cancer ko khatam karne ki WHO strategy par 194 countries ne commit kiya hai. Target hai ki 2030 tak 90% ladkiyon ko 15 saal ki umar tak poori vaccine lag jaaye, aur 70% women ki 35 aur phir 45 ki umar tak screening ho jaaye [[who-cervical-elimination-launch-2020]].

Jis test ke liye doctor se cervix ke baare mein baat karni pade, aur aksar koi relative bhi room mein ho, wahan "log kya kahenge" ka darr bhaari padta hai. Jab kisi bimari ko character par verdict maan liya jaaye, toh symptoms chhupaye jaate hain aur check-ups talte rehte hain. HIV ke saath jee rahi women pehle se ek aur stigma jhelti hain, aur unhe cervical cancer hone ka chance HIV ke bina wali women se chhe guna zyada hai [[who-cervical-cancer-factsheet-2026]].

## Parents aur young women kya kar sakte hain

HPV vaccine ko bhi bachche ke card ki baaki vaccines jaisa hi treat karo. Agar tumhari family mein koi 14 saal ki ladki hai, toh nearest government facility par poocho. Ayushman Arogya Mandir health centres se lekar medical colleges tak, government centres par yeh dose milti hai [[pib-hpv-update-march-2026]]. Agar koi relative objection kare, toh jawab chhota hai: yeh cancer se bachati hai, aur kisi bhi risk se pehle isliye di jaati hai kyunki tabhi yeh sabse achha kaam karti hai.

Jin older teenagers aur young adults ki vaccine miss ho gayi, woh bhi doctor se catch-up vaccination ke baare mein pooch sakte hain [[who-hpv]]. Vaccine lagi ho ya nahi, adult women ko cervical screening phir bhi karwani chahiye, kyunki vaccine cancer karne wale har HPV type ko cover nahi karti [[who-cervical]]. Periods ke beech mein ya sex ke baad bleeding ho, toh kisi bhi umar mein doctor ko dikhao.

Aur apne words badlo. "Usne zaroor kuch kiya hoga" mat kaho. Kaho, "cervical cancer ek common virus se hota hai." Ek ladki ka vaccination card uski health ka record hai. Uske character ka certificate nahi.

india-myth-census-nfhs-beliefs.en:
A myth sounds like something you cannot count: a line from an uncle at a wedding, a forward in the family WhatsApp group. But India does count its myths: the National Family Health Survey asks adults what they believe. In its fifth round, NFHS-5 (2019-21), 44% of men aged 15-49 said a husband is justified in beating his wife in at least one of seven situations. So did 45% of women [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## How a survey measures a myth

The survey does not ask people whether they support violence in general. It names a situation and asks for a verdict. Is a husband justified in hitting or beating his wife if she shows disrespect to her in-laws? If she refuses to have sex with him? There are seven such situations, and anyone who says yes to even one is counted [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Imagine the interview. A 28-year-old man in a small town sits across from a stranger with a questionnaire and is taken through the list. Nobody checks how he lives. The survey records only what he is willing to say aloud.

That gives two cautions. These figures are attitudes, not counts of violence. And they are answers given to a stranger, so each one is better read as the share of people who will admit to a belief than as everyone who holds it.

## Marriage and violence: what men and women accept

| The question | Men | Women |
|---|---|---|
| Husband justified in beating his wife in at least one of seven situations | 44% | 45% |
| Justified if she shows disrespect to her in-laws | 31% | 32% |
| Justified if she refuses sex | 10% | 11% |
| Knows HIV cannot spread by sharing food | 59% | 45% |
| Very important to have at least one son (2014, seven states) | 76% | 81% |

Disrespect to in-laws was the reason most often accepted, and refusing sex the least [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Compare the two columns. On every row about marriage, women agree at least as often as men. This is not only a "male opinion". It is a norm that many women have absorbed too.

The map does not follow the usual stereotypes either. Among women, 84% in Andhra Pradesh and in Telangana, and 78% in Tamil Nadu, said wife-beating could be justified. Among men the figure reached 82% in Karnataka [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The trend splits by gender. Women's agreement fell from 52% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 45%. Men's rose, from 42% to 44% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Contraception and sex: the gendered gaps

Men were also asked what a husband has the right to do if his wife refuses sex. Nearly one in five, 19.2%, said he may get angry and reprimand her.
