The BNS has no counterpart, so non-consensual penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape, and no specific offence replaced it [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

What is left are general crimes such as hurt or wrongful confinement, depending on the facts. Voluntarily causing hurt carries at most one year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 10,000, or both [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Transgender survivors fare little better: sexual abuse of a transgender person is punishable with six months to two years, a range the 2026 amendment left unchanged [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

The count has gone too: 987 cases under Section 377 in 2022, 888 in 2023, never split by the victim's gender, and no row at all in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], as our explainer on the first crime data under the BNS shows.

## The warning Parliament ignored, and the courts since

This was foreseen. On 10 November 2023, Parliament's Standing Committee on Home Affairs warned that dropping Section 377 would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men, transgender persons and animals unpunished, and recommended keeping it. The government did not [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]].

Then people went to court. On 28 August 2024, the Delhi High Court asked the Centre to decide within six months on a demand to restore the offence, remarking that "there can't be a vacuum to an offence" [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. On 14 October 2024, a Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud refused to entertain a similar plea, saying it cannot direct Parliament to create an offence [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. In March 2026, after about a year and a half without a decision, the Delhi High Court revived the case, said "the decision is nowhere in sight", and gave the Centre four weeks to file an affidavit [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]].

One court has called it a vacuum. The highest court says only Parliament can fill it, and Parliament has not.

## What a male survivor can do today

This is general information, not legal advice. Start with your body. HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) must start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure, and is taken for 28 days [[who-pep]]. Get tested for other infections too, because many cause no symptoms [[who-sti]]. The law that makes hospitals treat survivors free of cost names rape, acid attack and POCSO offences [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], so an adult man is not expressly covered. Go anyway and ask for PEP by name; our explainer on the 72-hour PEP window has the details.

You can still go to the police. What they can charge depends on the facts, and free legal aid is available through legal services authorities [[nalsa]]. For a boy, POCSO protects every child below 18 [[pocso-act-2012]], and the Child Helpline is 1098.

Then comes the step the myth makes hardest: telling someone. Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock helpline, offers counselling to anyone on 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. What happened to you was real, it was not your fault, and a missing section in a penal code does not make it any less real.
men-cannot-be-raped-gender-neutral-bns.hg:
Hostel ke corridor mein ya office canteen mein yeh baat kahiye, koi na koi hans dega: men can't be raped. Myth kehta hai ki aadmi ya toh itna strong hota hai ki rok le, ya phir andar hi andar khush hota hai. 1 July 2024 se India ka main criminal law bhi is myth se behas nahi karta. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) rape ko "a man" ka "a woman" ke against kiya gaya act batati hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Usne purane Indian Penal Code ka Section 377 bhi hata diya, jo kisi bhi man, woman ya animal ke saath non-consensual "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" par life imprisonment tak ki saza deta tha, aur uski jagah kuch nahi rakha [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]].

## Myth: 'asli mard' par assault ho hi nahi sakta

Yeh myth do ideas par tika hai: ki taakat hi sab kuch decide karti hai, isliye jis aadmi par assault hua usne resist nahi kiya hoga, aur ki men hamesha sex chahte hain, isliye ek aadmi sach mein unwilling ho hi nahi sakta. Dono galat hain. Women ke case mein law pehla idea pehle hi reject kar chuka hai: Section 63 ke hisaab se, agar aurat ne physically resist nahi kiya, toh sirf is wajah se use consenting nahi maana jaayega [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Darr, dhamkiyan, ya aap par power rakhne wala koi insaan kisi ko bhi resist karne se rok sakta hai. Aur body ka reaction agreement nahi hota. Consent ek decision hai, reflex nahi.

Yeh myth bachpan se shuru hota hai. UNICEF ka estimate hai ki aaj zinda har 11 mein se kareeb 1 boy ya man bachpan mein rape ya sexual assault ka shikaar hua [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. India mein 2024 mein police ne POCSO ke tahat penetrative sexual assault ke child victims mein 892 ladke darj kiye, aur yeh number dikhata hai ki ladkon ke cases kitne kam report hote hain, yeh nahi ki unka abuse kitna kam hota hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yahi ladke bade hokar aise aadmi bante hain jinhe sikhaya gaya hai ki unke saath aisa ho hi nahi sakta.

## Home Ministry ke note mein 'gender-neutral' ka matlab kya tha

July 2024 mein naye laws par Home Ministry ke note mein likha tha ki "various offences against women and children have been made gender-neutral in BNS, covering all victims and perpetrators regardless of gender", aur ki gender ki definition "now includes transgender individuals" [[pib-new-criminal-laws-2024]].

Code khud padhiye toh yeh claim chhota pad jaata hai. BNS yeh zaroor kehti hai ki pronoun "he" kisi bhi insaan ke liye hai, "whether male, female or transgender". Lekin woh "man" ko male aur "woman" ko female define karti hai, jisse rape sirf ek man ke ek woman par assault tak limited reh jaata hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Jo bhi gender-neutral bana ho, rape nahi bana.

## 'A man' aur 'a woman': Section 63 simple shabdon mein

Section 63 shuru hota hai: "A man is said to commit 'rape' if he…", aur isme list kiya gaya har act ek woman ke saath kiya gaya act hai. Sirf man rape kar sakta hai aur sirf woman ka rape ho sakta hai; ek adult man legally rape victim ho hi nahi sakta [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Myth kehta hai ki mard ke saath aisa nahi ho sakta. Law ab ek tarah se kehta hai ki agar ho bhi jaaye, toh woh rape nahi hai.

Jab Supreme Court ne 2018 mein Navtej Singh Johar case mein do adults ke beech consensual same-sex relations ko decriminalise kiya, tab bhi non-consensual acts ke liye Section 377 bana raha [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Kisi doosre aadmi ke assault ka shikaar hua aadmi isi offence ka sahara le sakta tha. BNS mein iska koi counterpart nahi hai, isliye kisi adult man ya transgender insaan ke saath non-consensual penetrative sex rape nahi hai, aur iske liye koi specific offence nahi banaya gaya [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Ab bache hain general crimes, jaise hurt ya wrongful confinement, jo facts par depend karta hai. Voluntarily causing hurt ki saza zyada se zyada ek saal jail, Rs 10,000 tak fine, ya dono hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Transgender survivors ka haal bhi kuch behtar nahi: transgender insaan ke sexual abuse ki saza chhe mahine se do saal tak hai, aur 2026 ke amendment ne ise nahi badla [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

Ginti bhi chali gayi: Section 377 ke tahat 2022 mein 987 cases, 2023 mein 888, jinhe kabhi victim ke gender ke hisaab se alag nahi kiya gaya, aur 2024 mein yeh row hi nahi hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]], jaisa BNS ke pehle crime data par hamara explainer dikhata hai.

## Parliament ne warning ignore ki, phir courts

Yeh pehle se dikh raha tha. 10 November 2023 ko Parliament ki Standing Committee on Home Affairs ne warning di thi ki Section 377 hatane se men, transgender persons aur animals ke against non-consensual sexual offences ki koi saza nahi bachegi, aur ise rakhne ki recommendation di. Sarkar ne yeh nahi maana [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]].

Phir log court gaye. 28 August 2024 ko Delhi High Court ne Centre se kaha ki is offence ko wapas laane ki demand par chhe mahine mein decide kare, aur remark kiya ki "there can't be a vacuum to an offence" [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. 14 October 2024 ko Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ki lead wali Supreme Court bench ne aisi hi ek plea sunne se mana kar diya, yeh kehkar ki woh Parliament ko koi offence banane ka direction nahi de sakti [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. March 2026 mein, kareeb dedh saal tak koi decision na hone ke baad, Delhi High Court ne case phir khola, kaha ki "the decision is nowhere in sight", aur Centre ko affidavit file karne ke liye chaar hafte diye [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]].

Ek court ise vacuum keh chuka hai. Sabse badi court kehti hai ki ise sirf Parliament bhar sakti hai, aur Parliament ne ab tak nahi bhara.

## Ek male survivor aaj kya kar sakta hai

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Shuruaat apni body se kijiye. HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) jitni jaldi ho sake aur exposure ke 72 hours ke andar shuru honi chahiye, aur 28 din tak li jaati hai [[who-pep]]. Doosre infections ka test bhi karwaiye, kyunki kai mein koi symptoms nahi hote [[who-sti]]. Jo law hospitals ko survivors ka free treatment karne ko kehta hai, woh rape, acid attack aur POCSO offences ka naam leta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]], isliye ek adult man usme saaf taur par cover nahi hai. Phir bhi hospital jaiye aur naam lekar PEP maangiye; 72-hour PEP window par hamara explainer poori detail deta hai.

Aap phir bhi police ke paas ja sakte hain. Woh kaunsa charge lagayenge, yeh facts par depend karta hai, aur free legal aid legal services authorities se milti hai [[nalsa]]. Agar survivor ladka hai, toh POCSO 18 se kam umar ke har bachche ko protect karta hai [[pocso-act-2012]], aur Child Helpline 1098 hai.

Phir aata hai woh step jo yeh myth sabse mushkil bana deta hai: kisi ko batana. Tele-MANAS, Health Ministry ki free, 24x7 helpline, 14416 par kisi ko bhi counselling deti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Aapke saath jo hua woh real tha, usme aapki koi galti nahi thi, aur penal code mein ek section na hone se woh zara bhi kam real nahi ho jaata.

more-women-than-men-headline-myth.en:
In 2021 one line from a national survey went viral: India now has more women than men. The fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) had estimated 1,020 females for every 1,000 males [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]]. Many took it as the end of a long story about daughters who were never allowed to be born. The same survey carried a second number that travelled far less: among children born in the five years before it, 929 girls for every 1,000 boys [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]]. Both numbers are real. Only the second measures sex selection.

## The headline and why it spread

The 1,020 had everything a forward needs: one clean figure that sounded like progress and seemed to settle a decades-old argument. "Sex ratio" also means several different things, and few posts said which one they meant.

The official record never said the problem was over. When the government gave the Lok Sabha the NFHS-5 figures in December 2021, the 1,020 sat in the text and the 929 in an annexure table [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]]. The good news made the headlines. The warning stayed in the annexure.

## Two ratios, two different questions

The population sex ratio counts females per 1,000 males among people of every age in the homes a survey visits. It answers one question: who lives here today? That depends on who was born decades ago, who survived and who moved away. NFHS-5 is a sample survey of households, not a census: it counts only the people living in the homes it visits.

Consider a hypothetical village where many young men have gone to work in Surat, Delhi or the Gulf. Their mothers, wives, sisters and children stay. A surveyor there will count more women than men, even if fewer girls than boys were born in the village last year.

The sex ratio at birth asks something else: are girls born in the numbers nature would produce? Nature makes slightly more boys, about 105 for every 100 girls. India stood at about 111 boys per 100 girls in the 2011 census, about 109 in NFHS-4 and 108 in NFHS-5 [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. The population ratio is a family photo; the birth ratio is the maternity ward's register. Sex selection shows up only in the register.

## What the birth figures say

The official series is the Sample Registration System (SRS), which reports three-year averages. It put India's sex ratio at birth at 917 girls per 1,000 boys in 2021-23. The climb has been slow: 904 in 2017-19, then 907, 913, 914 and 917 [[srs-statistical-report-2023]], and 918 for 2022-24 in the report published in May 2026 [[srs-statistical-report-2024]]. That is progress, but slow, and still well short of nature's level.

Nor is it confined to villages or one region. Among bigger states in 2021-23 the lowest ratios were in Uttarakhand (868), Delhi (872), Haryana (884), Maharashtra (894) and Bihar (897); the highest were in Chhattisgarh (974) and Kerala (971) [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. The national capital and the state that is home to Mumbai are in the bottom five.

Revealing a foetus's sex has been a crime since 1 January 1996 [[mohfw-pndt-act-rules-2003]], a history our abortion-law timeline traces. Police records show only 31 cases under the PC-PNDT Act in 2024, 30 in 2023 and 57 in 2022 [[ncrb-crime-in-india-2024-vol1]]. That is not the full picture: courts can act on these offences only on a complaint, usually from district health officials, so many prosecutions never reach police data [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Abortion itself is not the crime: it is legal on one doctor's opinion up to 20 weeks, and later in specific cases [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Choosing by sex is.

## Missing women: the long count

How can a survey find more women than men while India is short of tens of millions? Because "missing" is measured against the population India would have had without discrimination. UNFPA counted 45.8 million "missing" females in India in 2020, out of 142.6 million worldwide, second only to China's 72.3 million [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. That count adds up two losses over decades: girls never born because of sex selection, and excess deaths of girls after birth.

About 460,000 girls in India went "missing" at birth every year between 2013 and 2017; of all India's missing girls, sex selection explains about two thirds and excess deaths after birth about one third [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Pew Research Center estimated in 2022 that at least 9.0 million female births went missing between 2000 and 2019 because of female-selective abortions, with the yearly number falling from about 480,000 in 2010 to 410,000 in 2019 [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]].

The yearly loss is shrinking. It has not stopped. The 1,020 counts who is in the house; the 45.8 million estimates who never arrived or did not survive. One cannot cancel the other.

## Reading the next viral statistic

There will be another sex-ratio headline. Before you forward it, ask four questions.

**Which ratio?** The whole population, young children or births. Only the last two can show sex selection.

**Which source?** SRS is the official annual series; NFHS is a separate survey with its own sampling error. Do not join their numbers into one trend.

**How big is the sample?** State figures swing. NFHS-5 put Uttarakhand's sex ratio at birth at 984 [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]]; SRS put it at 868 for 2021-23, the lowest among bigger states [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. A gap that wide is a warning about small samples, not proof of change.

**What does it leave out?** A ratio cannot tell you who was pressured into a scan, or how girls are treated once born.

If your family is pushing you towards a test to learn your baby's sex, the law starts on your side: unless proved otherwise, it presumes a pregnant woman was compelled by her husband or relatives, and it does not punish a woman who was forced [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Our story on who else decides a woman's abortion looks at that pressure. For advice, call the Women Helpline; in danger, call 112. This is general information, not legal advice.
more-women-than-men-headline-myth.hg:
2021 mein ek national survey ki ek line viral ho gayi: India mein ab mardon se zyada aurtein hain. Paanchve National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) ne har 1,000 mardon par 1,020 aurton ka estimate diya tha [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]]. Kai logon ne ise un betiyon ki lambi kahaani ka ant maan liya jinhe kabhi paida hi nahi hone diya gaya. Usi survey mein ek doosra number bhi tha, jo kahin kam door tak gaya: survey se pehle ke paanch saalon mein paida hue bachchon mein har 1,000 ladkon par 929 ladkiyan [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]]. Dono number sahi hain. Sex selection sirf doosra number naapta hai.

## Headline aur woh itni kyun phaili

1,020 mein woh sab tha jo ek forward ko chahiye: ek saaf-suthra figure jo progress jaisa lagta tha, aur kai dashakon purani bahas ko khatam karta dikhta tha. Upar se 'sex ratio' ke kai alag matlab hote hain, aur bahut kam posts ne bataya ki woh kaun se ratio ki baat kar rahi hain.

Official record ne kabhi nahi kaha ki problem khatam ho gayi. Jab sarkar ne December 2021 mein Lok Sabha ko NFHS-5 ke figures diye, toh 1,020 jawab ke text mein tha aur 929 ek annexure table mein [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]]. Achchi khabar headlines tak pahunchi. Warning annexure mein hi padi rahi.

## Do ratio, do alag sawaal

Population sex ratio survey ke visit kiye gharon mein har umar ke logon ko ginta hai: har 1,000 mardon par kitni aurtein. Yeh ek sawaal ka jawab deta hai: aaj yahan kaun rehta hai? Yeh is par depend karta hai ki dashakon pehle kaun paida hua, kaun bacha aur kaun kahin aur chala gaya. NFHS-5 households ka sample survey hai, census nahi: yeh sirf unhi logon ko ginta hai jo uske visit kiye gharon mein rehte hain.

Ek hypothetical gaon sochiye, jahan ke kai jawaan mard Surat, Delhi ya Gulf mein kaam karne chale gaye hain. Unki maa, patni, behnein aur bachche gaon mein hi rehte hain. Wahan surveyor mardon se zyada aurtein ginega, chahe pichhle saal gaon mein ladkon se kam ladkiyan paida hui hon.

Sex ratio at birth kuch aur poochta hai: kya ladkiyan utni sankhya mein paida ho rahi hain jitni nature paida karti? Nature thode zyada ladke banati hai, har 100 ladkiyon par lagbhag 105 ladke. 2011 census mein India mein har 100 ladkiyon par lagbhag 111 ladke the, NFHS-4 mein lagbhag 109 aur NFHS-5 mein 108 [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. Population ratio ek family photo hai; birth ratio maternity ward ka register. Sex selection sirf register mein dikhta hai.

## Janam ke figures kya kehte hain

Official series Sample Registration System (SRS) hai, jo teen-teen saal ka average deta hai. Isne 2021-23 mein India ka sex ratio at birth har 1,000 ladkon par 917 ladkiyan bataya. Sudhaar bahut dheere hua hai: 2017-19 mein 904, phir 907, 913, 914 aur 917 [[srs-statistical-report-2023]], aur May 2026 mein chhapi report mein 2022-24 ke liye 918 [[srs-statistical-report-2024]]. Yeh progress hai, par dheemi, aur nature ke level se abhi bhi kaafi neeche.

Yeh sirf gaon ya kisi ek region ki problem bhi nahi hai. 2021-23 mein bade states mein sabse kam ratio Uttarakhand (868), Delhi (872), Haryana (884), Maharashtra (894) aur Bihar (897) mein the; sabse zyada Chhattisgarh (974) aur Kerala (971) mein [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. Desh ki rajdhani aur Mumbai wala state, dono bottom five mein hain.

Foetus ka sex batana 1 January 1996 se crime hai [[mohfw-pndt-act-rules-2003]]; yeh history hamari abortion-law timeline mein hai. Police records mein PC-PNDT Act ke under 2024 mein sirf 31 cases dikhte hain, 2023 mein 30 aur 2022 mein 57 [[ncrb-crime-in-india-2024-vol1]]. Yeh poori tasveer nahi hai: courts in offences par sirf complaint milne par action le sakti hain, jo aam taur par district health officials karte hain, isliye kai prosecutions police data tak pahunchte hi nahi [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Abortion khud crime nahi hai: 20 hafte tak ek doctor ki opinion par yeh legal hai, aur uske baad kuch khaas cases mein [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Crime hai sex dekh kar chunna.

## Missing women: lambi ginti

Koi survey mardon se zyada aurtein kaise gin sakta hai, jab India mein karodon aurtein kam hain? Kyunki 'missing' us population ke muqable naapa jaata hai jo bina bhedbhav ke India mein hoti. UNFPA ne 2020 mein India mein 45.8 million 'missing' females gine, duniya ke 142.6 million mein se; India se aage sirf China tha, 72.3 million ke saath [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Yeh ginti dashakon ke do nuksaan jodti hai: woh ladkiyan jo sex selection ki wajah se kabhi paida nahi hui, aur woh jo janam ke baad normal se zyada sankhya mein mar gayi.

2013 se 2017 ke beech India mein har saal lagbhag 460,000 ladkiyan janam ke waqt 'missing' hui; India ki saari missing ladkiyon mein se lagbhag do-tihaai ki wajah sex selection hai, aur lagbhag ek-tihaai ki wajah janam ke baad hone wali yeh extra maut [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Pew Research Center ne 2022 mein estimate kiya ki 2000 se 2019 ke beech female-selective abortions ki wajah se kam se kam 9.0 million female births 'missing' hui, aur saalana sankhya 2010 mein lagbhag 480,000 se ghat kar 2019 mein 410,000 ho gayi [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]].

Saalana nuksaan ghat raha hai. Ruka nahi hai. 1,020 batata hai ki ghar mein kaun hai; 45.8 million estimate karta hai ki kaun kabhi aaya hi nahi, ya bach nahi paaya. Ek number doosre ko cancel nahi kar sakta.

## Agla viral statistic kaise padhein

Sex ratio ki ek aur headline aayegi. Forward karne se pehle chaar sawaal poochiye.

**Kaun sa ratio?** Poori population, chhote bachche ya janam. Sirf aakhri do hi sex selection dikha sakte hain.

**Kaun sa source?** SRS official saalana series hai; NFHS ek alag survey hai jiska apna sampling error hai. Dono ke numbers jod kar ek trend mat banaiye.

**Sample kitna bada hai?** State ke figures bahut upar-neeche hote hain. NFHS-5 ne Uttarakhand ka sex ratio at birth 984 bataya [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]]; SRS ne 2021-23 ke liye 868 bataya, jo bade states mein sabse kam tha [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. Itna bada gap chhote samples ki warning hai, badlaav ka saboot nahi.

**Isme kya chhoot gaya?** Koi ratio yeh nahi bata sakta ki kis aurat par scan ke liye pressure daala gaya, ya paida hone ke baad ladkiyon ke saath kaisa bartaav hota hai.

Agar aapki family aapko baby ka sex jaanne wale test ki taraf dhakel rahi hai, toh law shuru se aapki taraf hai: jab tak ulta saabit na ho, law maanta hai ki pregnant aurat ko uske pati ya rishtedaron ne majboor kiya, aur jis aurat ko majboor kiya gaya use saza nahi deta [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Aurat ke abortion ka faisla aur kaun-kaun karta hai, is par hamari story isi pressure ko dekhti hai. Salah ke liye Women Helpline par call kijiye; khatre mein ho toh 112 par. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

no-such-thing-as-child-prostitute.en:
Two words have long done abusers a quiet favour: "child prostitute". The phrase has turned up in court records, news reports and everyday talk. The Supreme Court's 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes, written to help judges stop using stereotyped language, lists it among the terms to replace. The replacement is plain: "child who has been trafficked" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. This is not about politeness. It puts the crime back on the adults who committed it.

## A phrase that blames the child

"Prostitute" names a trade, and a trade implies a deal: someone offered, someone agreed. Put "child" in front of it and the sentence quietly makes the child a party to that deal. The trafficker becomes an "agent". The man who pays becomes a "customer". Only the child is left carrying a label, and in many families and neighbourhoods that label follows her home, if she is allowed home at all.

Notice what the court did not write. For adult women, the handbook replaces "prostitute" with "sex worker" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. For children, it offers no "child sex worker". There is no work here that a child can agree to, only abuse done to a girl or a boy.

The Supreme Court made the same move in September 2024, when it told all courts to stop saying "child pornography" and to use "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" instead [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Its reasoning: such images are not merely pornographic; they are records of a child being abused. Words that describe a product hide the crime that made it.

## What the law says about a child's 'consent'

Indian law closes every door the phrase tries to open. The POCSO Act, 2012 defines a child as anyone under 18 and protects boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Under Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), sex with a girl under 18 is rape, whatever she says [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Under POCSO, penetrative sexual assault on any child carries 10 years to life, and the aggravated form 20 years to life or death [[prs-pocso-amendment-bill-2019]]. A man who pays to have sex with a child is not a customer. In law, he is committing rape or penetrative sexual assault.

Trafficking law says the same thing in its own words. Section 143 of the BNS punishes trafficking for exploitation, including sexual exploitation, and states that the victim's consent is immaterial. Trafficking a child carries at least 10 years; trafficking more than one child, at least 14; and a police officer or public servant involved faces imprisonment for the rest of his natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 144 reaches the buyer too: knowingly sexually exploiting a trafficked child carries 5 to 10 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

So the law leaves no room to treat a child as a willing "prostitute". It sees a child, and adults committing serious crimes against that child. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Who is trafficked: the 2024 numbers

In 2024 police recorded 6,018 people as trafficked in India. Of them, 2,297 were children, and 1,384 of those children were boys [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Of 5,839 trafficking victims rescued that year, some of them from earlier cases, 2,347, or 40%, had been trafficked for sexual exploitation [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Two cautions. NCRB does not split the purpose by age or sex, so these tables cannot say how many of the children were sexually exploited; our data story on trafficked children examines that gap. And the counts cover only the 2,135 cases reported by Anti-Human Trafficking Units [[ncrb-cii-2024]], so they are a floor.

"Child prostitute" almost always conjures a girl. Yet boys were six in ten trafficked children on record, and a sexually exploited boy has no place in that picture at all.

Consider a hypothetical. A 15-year-old from a poor district is offered a job at a beauty parlour in a big city by a woman her family knows. She goes, because her family needs the money. In the city her phone is taken, a "debt" appears, and she is sold for sex. If police find her two years later, the old language calls her a "child prostitute" who went willingly. The law calls her a trafficked child and a rape survivor. Which words the adults around her choose decides whether she is protected or judged.

## Traffickers, buyers and a 7.3% conviction rate

On paper, the law is severe. In court, it rarely holds. In 2024, trials were completed in 586 trafficking cases, and only 43 ended in conviction, a rate of 7.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. More than nine in ten ended in acquittal or discharge.

The tables do not say why. But a trafficking prosecution often depends on the victim, frequently a frightened child, being believed and protected long enough to testify. Each adult who sees a "prostitute" instead of a trafficked child makes that harder, from the officer who records her statement to the relative who asks what she did to end up there. The phrase also keeps the buyer out of the frame: in a news story, a "customer" is background; in law, he is an offender.

The police are bound too. An officer who fails to record information about trafficking faces six months to two years in prison under Section 199 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Words to use, and what to do if you suspect trafficking

| Instead of | Say |
|---|---|
| child prostitute | child who has been trafficked |
| child pornography | child sexual exploitation and abuse material |
| client, customer | offender, abuser |
| she went willingly | she was trafficked; in law her consent is immaterial |

The first replacement comes from the Supreme Court's 2023 handbook, the second from its 2024 judgment; the last two are ours. On "victim" or "survivor", the handbook says both terms apply and the person's own preference should be respected [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. A child named correctly is a child the system owes shelter, care and protection. A child called a "prostitute" is a child people feel free to judge.

If you suspect a child is being trafficked, watch for adults who move a child and cannot explain why, a child kept out of school or never allowed to speak alone, and online posts that offer young people for sex. Call the Child Helpline 1098, which is linked to the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. You do not need proof. Finding out is the job of the people you call.
no-such-thing-as-child-prostitute.hg:
Do shabdon ne lambe samay se abusers ka chupchaap bhala kiya hai: "child prostitute". Yeh shabd court records, news reports aur roz ki baat-cheet mein aata raha hai. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes, jo judges ko stereotype wali bhasha chhodne mein madad ke liye likhi gayi, ise un shabdon mein ginti hai jinhe badalna hai. Badle mein seedha sa shabd diya gaya hai: "child who has been trafficked", yaani aisa bachcha jise traffic kiya gaya [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Yeh tameez ka maamla nahi hai. Yeh crime ko wapas un adults par rakhta hai jinhone use kiya.

## Ek shabd jo bachche ko hi blame karta hai

"Prostitute" ek dhande ka naam hai, aur dhanda ek deal ki taraf ishaara karta hai: kisi ne offer kiya, kisi ne haan kahi. Iske aage "child" laga dijiye aur sentence chupchaap bachche ko us deal ka hissa bana deta hai. Trafficker "agent" ban jaata hai. Paise dene wala aadmi "customer" ban jaata hai. Label sirf bachche ke paas reh jaata hai, aur kai parivaron aur mohallon mein woh label uske saath ghar tak jaata hai, agar use ghar aane bhi diya jaaye.

Dhyaan dijiye court ne kya nahi likha. Adult aurton ke liye handbook "prostitute" ki jagah "sex worker" kehti hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Bachchon ke liye woh koi "child sex worker" nahi deti. Yahan aisa koi kaam hai hi nahi jiske liye bachcha haan keh sake. Sirf abuse hai, jo kisi ladki ya ladke ke saath kiya gaya.

September 2024 mein Supreme Court ne yahi qadam phir uthaya, jab usne saari courts se kaha ki "child pornography" kehna band karein aur uski jagah "child sexual exploitation and abuse material" kahein [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Court ka tark tha ki aisi tasveerein sirf pornography nahi hain; woh ek bachche ke abuse ka record hain. Jo shabd kisi cheez ko product ki tarah bataate hain, woh us crime ko chhupa dete hain jisse woh bani.

## Bachche ki 'consent' par law kya kehta hai

Indian law har woh darwaza band karta hai jo yeh shabd kholne ki koshish karta hai. POCSO Act, 2012 18 saal se kam umar ke har insaan ko child maanta hai aur ladkon aur ladkiyon ko barabar protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 63 ke tahat 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex rape hai, chahe woh kuch bhi kahe [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO ke tahat kisi bhi bachche par penetrative sexual assault ki saza 10 saal se umrqaid tak hai, aur aggravated form ki 20 saal se umrqaid ya maut tak [[prs-pocso-amendment-bill-2019]]. Bachche ke saath sex ke liye paise dene wala aadmi customer nahi hai. Law ki nazar mein woh rape ya penetrative sexual assault kar raha hai.

Trafficking law apne shabdon mein yahi baat kehta hai. BNS ki Section 143 exploitation ke liye trafficking ko saza deti hai, jismein sexual exploitation bhi shaamil hai, aur saaf kehti hai ki victim ki consent ka koi matlab nahi. Bachche ki trafficking par kam se kam 10 saal; ek se zyada bachchon ki trafficking par kam se kam 14 saal; aur agar koi police officer ya public servant shaamil ho, toh use baaki poori zindagi ki jail [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 144 kharidne wale tak bhi pahunchti hai: jaan-boojhkar kisi trafficked bachche ka sexual exploitation karne par 5 se 10 saal ki saza [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yaani law mein kisi bachche ko apni marzi wali "prostitute" maanne ki koi jagah nahi. Law ko ek bachcha dikhta hai, aur woh adults jo us bachche ke khilaaf gambhir crime kar rahe hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Kise traffic kiya jaata hai: 2024 ke numbers

2024 mein police ne India mein 6,018 logon ko trafficked darj kiya. Inmein 2,297 bachche the, aur in bachchon mein 1,384 ladke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Us saal rescue hue 5,839 trafficking victims mein se, jinmein kuch purane cases ke bhi the, 2,347, yaani 40%, ko sexual exploitation ke liye traffic kiya gaya tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Do baaton ka dhyaan rakhiye. NCRB trafficking ka maqsad umar ya sex ke hisaab se alag nahi karta, isliye yeh tables nahi bata sakti ki inmein se kitne bachchon ka sexual exploitation hua; trafficked bachchon par hamari data story isi gap ko dekhti hai. Aur yeh ginti sirf Anti-Human Trafficking Units ke report kiye 2,135 cases ki hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]], isliye yeh asli sankhya ka sirf nichla hissa hai.

"Child prostitute" sunte hi dimaag mein aksar ek ladki ki tasveer aati hai. Lekin record par trafficked bachchon mein har das mein se chhe ladke the, aur sexually exploit hue ladke ki us tasveer mein koi jagah hi nahi.

Ek hypothetical sochiye. Ek gareeb zile ki 15 saal ki ladki ko uske parivar ki jaan-pehchaan wali ek aurat bade shehar ke beauty parlour mein naukri ka offer deti hai. Woh chali jaati hai, kyunki ghar ko paison ki zaroorat hai. Shehar mein uska phone le liya jaata hai, ek "karz" khada kar diya jaata hai, aur use sex ke liye becha jaata hai. Agar do saal baad police use dhoondh nikaale, toh purani bhasha use "child prostitute" kahegi jo "apni marzi se gayi". Law use trafficked bachcha aur rape survivor kehta hai. Uske aas-paas ke adults kaun se shabd chunte hain, isi se tay hota hai ki use protection milegi ya judgement.

## Traffickers, kharidne wale aur 7.3% conviction rate

Kaagaz par law sakht hai. Court mein woh kam hi tikta hai. 2024 mein 586 trafficking cases ke trial poore hue, aur sirf 43 conviction par khatam hue, yaani 7.3% ka rate [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Das mein se nau se zyada cases acquittal ya discharge par khatam hue.

Tables yeh nahi bataati ki aisa kyun hua. Lekin trafficking case aksar is par tikta hai ki victim, jo kai baar ek dara hua bachcha hota hai, itni der tak bharosa aur protection paaye ki gawahi de sake. Har woh adult jo trafficked bachche ki jagah ek "prostitute" dekhta hai, yeh kaam aur mushkil kar deta hai: statement record karne wale officer se lekar us rishtedaar tak jo poochhta hai ki usne aisa kya kiya ki wahan pahunch gayi. Yeh shabd kharidne wale ko bhi tasveer se bahar rakhta hai: news story mein "customer" bas background hota hai; law mein woh offender hai.

Police bhi law se bandhi hai. Jo officer trafficking ki jaankari record nahi karta, use BNS ki Section 199 ke tahat chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Kaun se shabd use karein, aur trafficking ka shak ho toh kya karein

| Yeh mat kahiye | Yeh kahiye |
|---|---|
| child prostitute | child who has been trafficked (trafficked bachcha) |
| child pornography | child sexual exploitation and abuse material |
| client, customer | offender, abuser |
| woh apni marzi se gayi | use traffic kiya gaya; law mein uski consent ka koi matlab nahi |

Pehla badlaav Supreme Court ki 2023 handbook se aata hai, doosra uske 2024 ke judgment se; aakhri do hamare hain. "Victim" ya "survivor" par handbook kehti hai ki dono shabd sahi hain aur us insaan ki apni pasand ka samman hona chahiye [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Jis bachche ko sahi naam diya jaata hai, system par uske liye shelter, dekhbhaal aur protection ka farz banta hai. Jise "prostitute" kaha jaata hai, use log judge karna apna haq samajhne lagte hain.

Agar aapko shak ho ki kisi bachche ko traffic kiya ja raha hai, toh in baaton par nazar rakhiye: aise adults jo kisi bachche ko ek jagah se doosri jagah le ja rahe hain aur wajah nahi bata paate; school se door rakha gaya, ya kabhi akele baat na karne diya gaya bachcha; aur online posts jo young logon ko sex ke liye offer karti hain. Child Helpline 1098 par call kariye, jo 112 emergency system se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Aapko saboot ki zaroorat nahi. Pata lagana un logon ka kaam hai jinhe aap call karte hain.

period-blood-not-impure-myth.en:
"Ganda khoon nikal raha hai." Bad blood is coming out. For many Indian girls this is the first explanation anyone offers for a period, usually said kindly, by a mother or an aunt. Imagine a 12-year-old in Nagpur who finds a stain on her uniform in Class 7 and is handed that sentence, and with it a list: not the pickle jar, not the prayer corner, no temple until it stops. The sentence is the myth. The list follows from it. If the blood is dirty then so, for a few days every month, is she.

## What 'impure' is supposed to mean

The claim comes in two versions. The older one is religious: a menstruating woman is ritually impure, so she must keep away from worship, the kitchen and sometimes the family's plates. The newer one borrows the language of health: the body is "cleaning itself", pushing out stale or toxic blood that would make her ill if it stayed. The second sounds like science, so it survives in homes that have dropped the first.

Both end in the same instruction: keep away. A 2016 meta-analysis in BMJ Open, pooling studies of adolescent girls in India, found that 77% were kept from religious activities during their periods, such as visiting places of worship or praying, and that only one in eight faced no restriction at all [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. The studies vary in quality and most predate 2016, so read the figures as a broad picture, not a national survey.

The idea belongs to no single faith, and not to India alone. For most of history nobody could see inside the womb, and many cultures explained bleeding without a wound as cleansing. Whatever rest or privacy the old rules once gave women, the practical reasons faded. The word "impure" stayed.

## What menstrual blood actually is

Each month the lining of the womb, the uterus, thickens in case a pregnancy begins. When none does, the body has no use for that lining, so it breaks down and leaves through the vagina [[nhs-periods]]. That is all a period is: blood, tissue from the lining and ordinary vaginal fluid. Bleeding usually lasts 2 to 7 days, and the total is only a few tablespoons [[nhs-periods]].

Nothing in it is dirty. It is not stale blood, not a toxin and not waste that had to be purged. The body does not clean itself by bleeding; the kidneys and the liver do that work every day, in men as well as women. The lining a family calls dirty is the tissue that would have nourished a pregnancy. Everyone who repeats the rule once grew inside one.

Pickle spoils from moisture and microbes, not from whose hands open the jar. Like any blood, period blood calls for ordinary care: a pad changed every few hours, washed hands, a daily bath. That is hygiene, not purification.

Some trans men and non-binary people have periods too, and the biology is the same.

## Restricted at home, absent from school

The myth does not stay in the prayer room. In the same meta-analysis, about a quarter of girls (24%) missed school during their periods [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. The figure comes without reasons; missing toilets, water and pain all play a part. But a girl taught that her blood is filth has one more reason to stay home: a stain stops being an accident and becomes an exposure.

The health-flavoured version does its own damage. If bleeding is "cleansing", then heavy bleeding looks like a good clean-out and a late period looks like dirt trapped inside. Neither is true. Soaking through a pad every one to two hours, or bleeding for more than 7 days, is a reason to see a doctor, because months of heavy bleeding can cause anaemia [[nhs-periods]]. A late period has causes worth finding. It is not poison building up.

## Why the myth survives: girls told too late

A myth this easy to disprove lasts because the rules reach a girl before the biology does. Only about half of adolescent girls (48%) had been told about menstruation before their first period, in the meta-analysis's pooled estimate from the 88 of its 138 studies that reported on this [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Whoever speaks first, usually an older woman repeating what she was told, gets to define it.

School does not reliably fill the gap. India's National Education Policy 2020 does not use the words "menstruation" or "puberty" anywhere in its 66 pages [[nep-2020-full-text]]. The UN's guidance on sexuality education asks for the opposite: menstruation taught as a normal and natural part of growing up, without secrecy or stigma [[unesco-itgse]].

On 30 January 2026, in Dr Jaya Thakur v. Government of India, the Supreme Court held that menstrual health is part of the right to life under Article 21, and directed all schools to provide working, gender-segregated toilets with water, free sanitary napkins and safe disposal [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. It also asked for boys and male teachers to be sensitised [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. A court can order pads and toilets. It cannot change the sentence a girl hears at home.

## What changes when a family drops it

Dropping the myth costs nothing. It starts with words.

- Name it. Say "period" or "mahina", and say what it is: the lining of the womb, shed because there is no pregnancy. Retire "ganda khoon".
- Tell her before her first period, so that she does not have to learn it from fear.
- Tell the boys too. A brother who knows the biology does not treat a stain as a joke.
- Swap the rule for a question. "Don't touch that" becomes "Do you need rest, a pad, something for the pain?"
- Leave worship to her. Whether she prays during her period can be her own choice. Being called impure should not come with it.

The girl in Nagpur does not need purifying. She needs one adult to reach her before the list does, and to tell her the truth: nothing dirty is leaving her body.
period-blood-not-impure-myth.hg:
"Ganda khoon nikal raha hai." India ki bahut si ladkiyon ko period ke baare mein sabse pehle yahi samjhaya jaata hai, aur aksar pyaar se, maa ya mausi ke munh se. Socho, Nagpur ki ek 12 saal ki ladki, jise Class 7 mein apni uniform par daag dikhta hai. Use yahi ek line milti hai, aur uske saath ek list: achaar ka dabba nahi, pooja ka kona nahi, jab tak yeh ruke nahi tab tak mandir nahi. Yeh line hi myth hai. List usi se nikalti hai. Agar blood ganda hai, toh har mahine kuch dinon ke liye woh khud bhi gandi hai.

## 'Impure' ka matlab aakhir kya bataya jaata hai

Yeh claim do roop mein aata hai. Purana roop religious hai: periods mein aurat ritually impure hoti hai, isliye use pooja se, kitchen se aur kabhi-kabhi ghar ki thaaliyon se bhi door rehna chahiye. Naya roop health ki bhasha udhaar leta hai: body "apni safai kar rahi hai", purana ya zehreela khoon bahar nikaal rahi hai, jo andar rehta toh use bimaar kar deta. Doosra roop science jaisa sunai deta hai, isliye woh un gharon mein bhi bacha hua hai jinhone pehla chhod diya hai.

Dono ka nateeja ek hi hidayat hai: door raho. 2016 mein BMJ Open mein chhape ek meta-analysis ne India ki adolescent girls par hui studies ko jod kar dekha. Usne paaya ki 77% ladkiyon ko periods mein religious activities se roka jaata tha, jaise worship ki jagah jaana ya pray karna, aur har aath mein se sirf ek ladki par koi restriction nahi tha [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. In studies ki quality alag-alag hai aur zyada tar 2016 se pehle ki hain, isliye in numbers ko ek broad picture ki tarah padho, national survey ki tarah nahi.

Yeh soch kisi ek religion ki nahi hai, aur sirf India ki bhi nahi. Itihaas ke zyada tar hisse mein koi uterus ke andar dekh nahi sakta tha, aur kai cultures ne bina ghaav ki bleeding ko "safai" keh kar samjhaya. In purane rules se auraton ko kabhi jo bhi aaram ya privacy milti thi, woh practical wajahein peechhe chhoot gayi. "Impure" shabd reh gaya.

## Period ka blood asal mein kya hai

Har mahine uterus (bachchedaani) ki andar wali layer moti hoti hai, is taiyari mein ki shayad pregnancy shuru ho. Pregnancy nahi hoti, toh body ko us layer ki zaroorat nahi rehti; woh tootti hai aur vagina ke raaste bahar nikal jaati hai [[nhs-periods]]. Period bas itna hi hai: blood, layer ka tissue aur normal vaginal fluid. Bleeding aam taur par 2 se 7 din chalti hai, aur kul matra bas kuch tablespoons hoti hai [[nhs-periods]].

Ismein kuch bhi ganda nahi hai. Yeh na baasi khoon hai, na koi toxin, na aisi gandagi jise bahar phenkna zaroori tha. Body bleeding se apni safai nahi karti; yeh kaam kidneys aur liver roz karte hain, men mein bhi aur women mein bhi. Jis layer ko family gandi kehti hai, wahi tissue pregnancy ko poshan deta. Yeh rule dohrane wala har insaan kabhi aisi hi ek layer ke andar bada hua tha.

Achaar nami aur microbes se kharab hota hai, is baat se nahi ki dabba kiske haathon ne khola. Kisi bhi blood ki tarah period ke blood ke liye bhi bas aam dekhbhaal chahiye: har kuch ghante mein pad badalna, haath dhona, roz nahana. Yeh hygiene hai, shuddhikaran nahi.

Kuch trans men aur non-binary logon ko bhi periods hote hain, aur biology wahi hai.

## Ghar mein rok-tok, school se gair-haazir

Yeh myth pooja ke kamre tak nahi rukta. Usi meta-analysis mein lagbhag ek-chauthai ladkiyan (24%) periods ke dinon mein school miss karti thi [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Yeh figure wajah nahi batata; toilet na hona, paani na hona aur dard, sab ka haath hai. Par jis ladki ko sikhaya gaya hai ki uska blood gandagi hai, uske paas ghar rehne ki ek wajah aur hai: daag ab ek accident nahi rehta, uski pol khulne jaisa lagta hai.

Health wala roop apna alag nuksaan karta hai. Agar bleeding "safai" hai, toh heavy bleeding achhi safai lagti hai aur late period andar phansi gandagi. Dono baatein galat hain. Har ek-do ghante mein pad ka poora bheeg jaana, ya 7 din se zyada bleeding, doctor ko dikhane ki wajah hai, kyunki mahino ki heavy bleeding se anaemia ho sakta hai [[nhs-periods]]. Late period ki wajahein hoti hain jinhe dhoondhna chahiye. Woh andar jama hota zeher nahi hai.

## Myth kyun tika hai: ladkiyon ko bahut der se bataya jaata hai

Itni aasani se galat saabit hone wala myth isliye tika hai kyunki ladki tak biology se pehle rules pahunch jaate hain. Sirf lagbhag aadhi adolescent girls (48%) ko pehla period aane se pehle menstruation ke baare mein bataya gaya tha; yeh meta-analysis ka pooled estimate hai, uski 138 mein se un 88 studies se jinhone yeh baat report ki [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Jo sabse pehle bolta hai, aksar koi badi aurat jo wahi dohra rahi hoti hai jo use bataya gaya tha, wahi tay karta hai ki period ka matlab kya hai.

School bhi yeh kami bharose ke saath poori nahi karta. India ki National Education Policy 2020 apne 66 pages mein kahin bhi "menstruation" ya "puberty" shabd use nahi karti [[nep-2020-full-text]]. UN ki sexuality education guidance iska ulta maangti hai: menstruation ko bade hone ke ek normal aur natural hisse ki tarah padhaya jaaye, bina secrecy aur stigma ke [[unesco-itgse]].

30 January 2026 ko Dr Jaya Thakur v. Government of India mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki menstrual health Article 21 ke right to life ka hissa hai, aur sabhi schools ko order diya ki woh paani wale, chalu, gender-segregated toilets, free sanitary napkins aur safe disposal ka intezaam karein [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Court ne ladkon aur male teachers ko sensitise karne ko bhi kaha [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Court pads aur toilets ka order de sakta hai. Ghar mein ladki jo line sunti hai, use woh nahi badal sakta.

## Jab family yeh myth chhod deti hai, toh kya badalta hai

Myth chhodne mein kuch kharch nahi hota. Shuruaat shabdon se hoti hai.

- Sahi naam lo. "Period" ya "mahina" bolo, aur batao ki yeh hai kya: uterus ki andar wali layer, jo pregnancy na hone par nikal jaati hai. "Ganda khoon" ko retire kar do.
- Use pehle period se pehle hi bata do, taaki use yeh sab darr se na seekhna pade.
- Ladkon ko bhi batao. Jo bhai biology jaanta hai, woh daag ko mazaak nahi banata.
- Rule ki jagah sawaal rakho. "Ise mat chhuo" ki jagah "Tumhe aaram chahiye, pad chahiye, dard ke liye kuch chahiye?"
- Pooja ka faisla us par chhodo. Periods mein woh pray kare ya nahi, yeh uski apni choice ho sakti hai. Uske saath "impure" kehlana nahi aana chahiye.

Nagpur ki us ladki ko shuddh karne ki zaroorat nahi hai. Use bas ek aisa bada chahiye jo us list se pehle us tak pahunche aur use sach bataye: uski body se kuch bhi ganda nahi nikal raha.

pill-copper-t-infertility-myth.en:
In many Indian homes the warning arrives before the facts do. The pill "dries up the womb". The Copper-T "spoils the uterus". Take hormones for too long and "you will never have a baby". The lines come from older relatives, from neighbours, from WhatsApp forwards. None of them is true: reversible contraceptives do not cause infertility [[who-fp]]. Yet the way India actually prevents pregnancy looks like a country that believes them.

## 'It will dry up the womb': the fear

The fear is not foolish. It grows out of real experiences that nobody explained. The pill can change bleeding patterns, and a copper IUD can make periods heavier or more crampy, especially at first [[who-fp]]. If no one says so in advance, a normal side effect looks like damage.

Timing does the rest. A woman stops the pill because she wants a child. If the pregnancy takes a while, for reasons such as age or her partner's health, the pill gets the blame. Infertility is common everywhere: about 17.5% of adults worldwide, roughly 1 in 6, experience it in their lifetime, the WHO estimates [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. Some women who once took the pill were always going to be among them. The coincidence becomes a story, and the story travels.

Then there is shame. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 35.1% of Indian men agreed that "contraception is women's business and a man should not have to worry about it", and 19.6% agreed that women who use contraception may become promiscuous [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A young wife who asks for the pill can be judged twice: for risking the family's next child, and for wanting sex without one.

## How India's method mix reflects it

In NFHS-5, 66.7% of currently married women used some method of contraception and 56.4% a modern one [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Look at which methods:

| Method (currently married women, NFHS-5) | Share |
|---|---|
| Female sterilisation | 37.9% |
| Condom | 9.5% |
| Pill | 5.1% |
| IUD, including the Copper-T | 2.1% |
| Injectable | 0.6% |
| Male sterilisation | 0.3% |

Female sterilisation, a permanent operation, makes up about two thirds of all modern contraceptive use [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The pill, IUD, injectable and condom together reach fewer than one in five married women. And for every married woman whose husband has had a vasectomy, more than a hundred have had the operation themselves.

A survey cannot say how much of this is fear and how much is what clinics offer, what husbands allow or what women are told. But the pattern fits the myth: avoid the "risky" reversible methods, have the children, then choose the permanent one. Meanwhile 9.4% of married women had an unmet need for family planning: they wanted to delay or stop having children but were using nothing [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## What the pill and the IUD actually do

The combined pill works mainly by stopping ovulation, the monthly release of an egg [[who-fp]]. Nothing dries up. Stop taking it and its effect ends, and fertility comes back [[who-fp]].

A copper IUD contains no hormones. It sits inside the uterus and stops sperm from fertilising an egg [[who-ec]]. It can be removed whenever the woman wants, and fertility returns quickly afterwards [[who-fp]]. It is so reliable that, fitted within five days of unprotected sex, it is the most effective form of emergency contraception [[who-ec]].

In typical use, about 7 in 100 pill users and fewer than 1 in 100 IUD users get pregnant in a year [[who-fp]]. The exception to a quick return is the contraceptive injection: after it, fertility can take several months longer to come back, but it does come back [[who-fp]].

What can genuinely harm fertility is not a contraceptive but an untreated infection. Sexually transmitted infections that are never treated can damage fertility [[who-infertility]]. That is a reason to use condoms and get tested, not a reason to fear the pill.

## Married teenagers and the cost of fear

The fear costs most where women have the least say. Among currently married women aged 15 to 19, only 28.1% used any method, and 17.8% had an unmet need for family planning, nearly double the national figure [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Of all women aged 15 to 19, 6.8% had already begun childbearing, rising to 20.0% by age 19 [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Many of these wives should never have been married. A girl married before 18 is in a child marriage under the law [[indiacode-pcma-2006]], and since 2017 sex with a wife under 18 has been rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. The first answer is to stop child marriage. But for a young bride already living with her in-laws, expected to prove she can have a child, a rumour that the pill will make her barren is not a small thing. It can decide whether she gets a year or two to finish school, recover from a birth, or simply grow up.

## Choosing without fear

A reversible method is exactly that: reversible. A pill can be stopped in any month and an IUD taken out on any day. You do not need a "break" to clean the body before trying for a baby [[who-fp]].

Before choosing, ask a doctor or trained health worker three questions. How does this method work? Which side effects are common? What do I do if I want to stop? If one method does not suit you, switch to another rather than going without. Add condoms whenever an infection is possible. And if a year of trying brings no pregnancy, see a doctor together with your partner, because infertility affects men too [[who-infertility]].

The womb does not dry up. What dries up, when the myth wins, is a woman's choice.
pill-copper-t-infertility-myth.hg:
Kai Indian gharon mein facts se pehle warning pahunch jaati hai. Pill "bachchedani sukha deti hai". Copper-T "bachchedani kharab kar deta hai". Hormones zyada din tak liye toh "kabhi baby nahi hoga". Yeh baatein ghar ke bado se, padosiyon se, WhatsApp forwards se aati hain. Inmein se ek bhi sach nahi hai: reversible contraceptives se infertility nahi hoti [[who-fp]]. Phir bhi India asal mein jis tarah pregnancy rokta hai, woh ek aise desh jaisa dikhta hai jo in baaton par poora yakeen karta hai.

## 'Bachchedani sookh jaayegi': yeh darr

Yeh darr bewakoofi nahi hai. Yeh un asli experiences se nikalta hai jinhe kabhi kisi ne samjhaya hi nahi. Pill se bleeding ka pattern badal sakta hai, aur copper IUD se periods zyada heavy ho sakte hain ya cramps badh sakte hain, khaaskar shuruaat mein [[who-fp]]. Agar pehle se koi yeh na bataye, toh ek normal side effect nuksaan jaisa lagta hai.

Baaki kaam timing kar deti hai. Ek aurat pill isliye band karti hai kyunki use bachcha chahiye. Agar pregnancy mein thoda time lagta hai, umar ya partner ki health jaisi kisi wajah se, toh blame pill par aata hai. Infertility har jagah common hai: WHO ke estimate ke mutabik duniya ke lagbhag 17.5% adults, yaani roughly 6 mein se 1, zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi infertility face karte hain [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. Jin aurton ne kabhi pill li thi, unmein se kuch toh waise bhi isi group mein hoti. Coincidence kahaani ban jaata hai, aur kahaani door tak jaati hai.

Phir sharm ki baat aati hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 35.1% Indian mard is baat se sahmat the ki "contraception aurton ka kaam hai aur mard ko iski fikr nahi karni chahiye", aur 19.6% maante the ki contraception use karne wali aurtein promiscuous, yaani kai logon ke saath sambandh banane wali, ban sakti hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jo young wife pill maangti hai, use do baar judge kiya ja sakta hai: ek, family ke agle bachche ko risk mein daalne ke liye, aur do, bina bachche ke sex chahne ke liye.

## India ka method mix yahi darr dikhata hai

NFHS-5 mein 66.7% currently married aurtein koi na koi contraception method use kar rahi thi, aur 56.4% koi modern method [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Ab dekhiye, kaun se methods:

| Method (currently married aurtein, NFHS-5) | Share |
|---|---|
| Female sterilisation | 37.9% |
| Condom | 9.5% |
| Pill | 5.1% |
| IUD, Copper-T samet | 2.1% |
| Injectable | 0.6% |
| Male sterilisation (nasbandi) | 0.3% |

Female sterilisation, jo ek permanent operation hai, saare modern contraceptive use ka lagbhag do-tihaai hissa hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Pill, IUD, injectable aur condom milkar bhi paanch mein se ek shaadishuda aurat tak nahi pahunchte. Aur har us shaadishuda aurat ke muqable jiske pati ne vasectomy karwayi hai, sau se zyada aurtein khud operation karwa chuki hain.

Survey yeh nahi bata sakta ki isme kitna hissa darr ka hai, aur kitna is baat ka ki clinics kya offer karte hain, pati kya allow karte hain ya aurton ko kya bataya jaata hai. Lekin pattern myth se poora mel khaata hai: 'risky' reversible methods se bacho, bachche paida karo, phir permanent wala chuno. Saath hi 9.4% shaadishuda aurton ki family planning ki unmet need thi: woh agla bachcha der se chahti thi ya aur bachche nahi chahti thi, phir bhi kuch use nahi kar rahi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Pill aur IUD asal mein kya karte hain

Combined pill mainly ovulation rok kar kaam karti hai, yaani har mahine ovary se egg nikalne ka process [[who-fp]]. Kuch bhi sookhta nahi. Pill band kijiye toh uska asar khatam, aur fertility laut aati hai [[who-fp]].

Copper IUD mein koi hormone nahi hota. Yeh uterus ke andar rehta hai aur sperm ko egg fertilise karne se rokta hai [[who-ec]]. Aurat jab chahe ise nikalwa sakti hai, aur uske baad fertility jaldi laut aati hai [[who-fp]]. Yeh itna reliable hai ki unprotected sex ke paanch din ke andar lagwaya jaaye, toh yeh emergency contraception ka sabse effective tareeka hai [[who-ec]].

Typical use mein, ek saal mein pill use karne wali 100 mein se lagbhag 7 aurtein pregnant hoti hain, aur IUD use karne wali 100 mein se 1 se bhi kam [[who-fp]]. Jaldi wapsi ka ek exception contraceptive injection hai: iske baad fertility lautne mein kuch mahine zyada lag sakte hain, lekin woh lautti zaroor hai [[who-fp]].

Fertility ko asli nuksaan contraceptive se nahi, bina ilaaj wale infection se ho sakta hai. Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) ka agar kabhi ilaaj na ho, toh woh fertility ko nuksaan pahuncha sakte hain [[who-infertility]]. Yeh condom use karne aur test karwane ki wajah hai, pill se darne ki nahi.

## Shaadishuda teenagers aur is darr ki keemat

Is darr ki sabse badi keemat wahan chukaayi jaati hai jahan aurton ki sabse kam chalti hai. 15 se 19 saal ki currently married aurton mein sirf 28.1% koi method use kar rahi thi, aur 17.8% ki family planning ki unmet need thi, jo national figure se lagbhag double hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. 15 se 19 saal ki sabhi aurton mein 6.8% bachche paida karna shuru kar chuki thi, aur 19 saal ki umar tak yeh figure 20.0% ho jaata hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Inmein se kai wives ki shaadi honi hi nahi chahiye thi. 18 se pehle byaahi gayi ladki ki shaadi law ke hisaab se child marriage hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]], aur 2017 se 18 se kam umar ki biwi ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. Pehla jawab hai child marriage rokna. Lekin jo young dulhan pehle se sasural mein reh rahi hai, aur jisse ummeed ki jaati hai ki woh saabit kare ki bachcha paida kar sakti hai, uske liye yeh afwaah ki pill use baanjh bana degi, chhoti baat nahi hai. Isi se tay ho sakta hai ki use school poora karne, ek delivery se recover hone, ya bas thoda bada hone ke liye ek-do saal milenge ya nahi.

## Bina darr ke chunna

Reversible method ka matlab hi yahi hai: jise palta ja sake. Pill kisi bhi mahine band ki ja sakti hai aur IUD kisi bhi din nikalwaya ja sakta hai. Baby ke liye try karne se pehle body ko 'saaf' karne ke liye kisi 'break' ki zaroorat nahi hoti [[who-fp]].

Method chunne se pehle doctor ya trained health worker se teen sawaal poochiye. Yeh method kaise kaam karta hai? Iske kaun se side effects common hain? Agar band karna ho toh kya karna hoga? Agar ek method suit na kare, toh bina kuch use kiye rehne ke bajaye doosra method try kijiye. Jab bhi infection ka chance ho, condom bhi use kijiye. Aur agar ek saal koshish ke baad bhi pregnancy na ho, toh apne partner ke saath doctor se miliye, kyunki infertility mardon ko bhi hoti hai [[who-infertility]].

Bachchedani nahi sookhti. Jab myth jeet jaata hai, toh jo sookhta hai woh hai aurat ka choice.

porn-not-sex-education-consent.en:
Imagine a 15-year-old in Lucknow with a phone, a bedroom door that shuts and a question he cannot ask anyone at home. His parents have decided, lovingly, that he is too young for "that talk". His school skipped the chapter. So he types the question into a search bar, and within seconds a video answers it.

Nobody chose porn as his teacher. The adults around him chose silence, and porn took the job that silence left open.

## The silence that hands the job to porn

The belief behind the silence is simple: talk to teenagers about sex and they will go and do it. So families change the channel, and a school may leave the reproduction chapter for "self-study". India's National Education Policy 2020 does not once use the words 'sex', 'sexual', 'sexuality', 'reproductive', 'puberty' or 'menstruation' in its 66 pages [[nep-2020-full-text]].

Where sexuality education does exist, it tends to avoid the screen. UNESCO's 2021 global status report, drawing on a survey of countries in Asia-Pacific, sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America, found 'online media and technology' among the topics least included in secondary-school curricula [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. The place where teenagers actually learn about sex is the place the syllabus says least about.

Curiosity does not wait for permission. A question refused at home is not cancelled. It is redirected.

## What the evidence says about talking

The fear has been tested. The UN's International Technical Guidance on Sexuality Education, revised in 2018, rests mainly on two UNESCO-commissioned reviews: a 2008 review of 87 studies and a 2016 University of Oxford review of 22 systematic reviews and 77 randomised controlled trials. It states that sexuality education, in or out of school, does not increase sexual activity, sexual risk-taking or STI and HIV infection rates [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

The evidence points the other way. Curriculum-based programmes contribute to later first sex, less frequent sex, fewer partners and more use of condoms and contraception. Abstinence-only programmes were found ineffective at delaying first sex [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Most of these trials were run outside India, and the guidance itself says the evidence on infection rates is limited. But nothing in it supports the idea that information pushes teenagers into sex.

> Silence does not delay sex. It only decides who does the teaching.

## What the camera leaves out

Porn is scripted, edited entertainment made for adults. Treated as a lesson, it is missing four things.

**Asking.** On screen, almost nobody checks whether the other person wants this, or stops when someone hesitates.

**Protection.** Condoms, contraception and testing rarely appear. Off screen, many sexually transmitted infections have no symptoms, and only a test can tell [[who-sti]]. The basics are not common knowledge either: in NFHS-5 (2019-21), only 54.4% of young women aged 15-24 knew where to get a condom, against 87.3% of young men [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

**Real bodies.** Performers are cast for a look, and scenes shot over hours are cut down to minutes. Real bodies vary widely, and that is healthy.

**Everything around it.** Nervousness, laughter, changing your mind halfway, talking afterwards, worrying about pregnancy: none of it survives the edit.

## The consent script versus Section 63

Much mainstream porn runs on one consent script: reluctance is a phase, persistence is rewarded, silence means yes, and "no" turns into "yes" if he keeps going.

Indian law has a script too, and it is the reverse. Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines consent as an "unequivocal voluntary agreement", communicated by words, gestures or other communication, to the specific sexual act. It adds that a woman who does not physically resist is not, for that reason alone, to be treated as consenting [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. What the screen presents as seduction, the statute describes as the absence of consent. Below 18 there is no legal consent at all: sex with a girl under 18 is rape whatever she says, and the POCSO Act protects every child under 18, boy or girl [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

The porn script lands in a country where many already believe it. In NFHS-5, 12.2% of men aged 15-49, about one in eight, said a husband has the right to use force if his wife refuses sex. The share of men who rejected all four coercive responses to a wife's refusal fell from 77% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 72% in NFHS-5 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The survey does not ask about porn, and porn did not invent this belief. But a boy who has never seen a "no" respected on screen, and never heard one discussed at home, has nothing to set against it.

The law's own lines are worth knowing. In July 2015 the Supreme Court observed that it could not stop an adult from watching pornography in the privacy of their room [[hindu-sc-adult-porn-privacy-2015]]. Material showing a child is different: in September 2024 the court ruled that viewing, storing or possessing child sexual abuse material is an offence [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Talking about porn without shame

Start from the assumption that a teenager with a phone has already seen it. "Do you watch that filth?" ends the conversation. "A lot of what is online is acting. Has anything you have seen confused you?" begins one.

Say the four missing things out loud. Say what consent is: a clear, willing yes that can be taken back at any point. Say that nobody is owed sex, inside marriage or outside it.

Do not punish the question. A child punished for asking learns only to stop asking you. And if an adult or an older child has shown a child sexual material, treat it as a warning sign, not mischief: the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse counted exposure to pornography among the forms of child sexual abuse [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

In 2024 the Supreme Court itself recommended comprehensive sex education that gives young people a clear understanding of consent [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Until schools deliver it, the choice in most homes is not between talking and innocence. It is between your voice and the search bar.
porn-not-sex-education-consent.hg:
Imagine kijiye Lucknow ka ek 15 saal ka ladka. Uske paas phone hai, kamre ka darwaza band ho jaata hai, aur ek sawaal hai jo woh ghar mein kisi se nahi pooch sakta. Mummy-papa ne pyaar se tay kar liya hai ki "aisi baaton" ke liye woh abhi chhota hai. School ne woh chapter skip kar diya. Toh woh sawaal search bar mein type karta hai, aur kuch hi seconds mein ek video jawab de deta hai.

Kisi ne porn ko uska teacher nahi chuna tha. Uske aas-paas ke badon ne chuppi chuni, aur chuppi ne jo jagah khaali chhodi, woh porn ne bhar di.

## Woh chuppi jo kaam porn ko saunp deti hai

Chuppi ke peeche ki soch simple hai: teenagers se sex ki baat karoge toh woh jaakar kar baithenge. Isliye families channel badal deti hain, aur koi school reproduction wala chapter "self-study" ke liye chhod deta hai. India ki National Education Policy 2020 apne 66 pages mein ek baar bhi 'sex', 'sexual', 'sexuality', 'reproductive', 'puberty' ya 'menstruation' shabd use nahi karti [[nep-2020-full-text]].

Jahan sexuality education hai bhi, wahan woh screen ki baat se bachti hai. UNESCO ki 2021 ki global status report ne Asia-Pacific, sub-Saharan Africa aur Latin America ke countries ke ek survey ke aadhaar par paaya ki 'online media and technology' un topics mein tha jo secondary-school curricula mein sabse kam shamil the [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. Jis jagah teenagers asal mein sex ke baare mein seekhte hain, usi jagah ke baare mein syllabus sabse kam bolta hai.

Curiosity permission ka intezaar nahi karti. Ghar mein mana kiya gaya sawaal cancel nahi hota. Woh bas kahin aur chala jaata hai.

## Baat karne ke baare mein evidence kya kehta hai

Is darr ko test kiya ja chuka hai. UN ki International Technical Guidance on Sexuality Education, jo 2018 mein revise hui, mainly UNESCO ke karwaye do reviews par tiki hai: 2008 ka ek review jismein 87 studies thi, aur 2016 ka University of Oxford ka review jismein 22 systematic reviews aur 77 randomised controlled trials the. Guidance kehti hai ki sexuality education, school ke andar ho ya bahar, sexual activity, sexual risk-taking ya STI aur HIV infection rates nahi badhati [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

Evidence ulti disha mein jaata hai. Curriculum-based programmes se pehla sex der se hota hai, sex kam baar hota hai, partners kam hote hain, aur condom aur contraception ka use badhta hai. Sirf abstinence sikhane wale programmes pehle sex ko taalne mein bekaar paaye gaye [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Inmein se zyada tar trials India ke bahar hue the, aur guidance khud maanti hai ki infection rates par evidence limited hai. Par ismein kahin aisa kuch nahi hai jo kahe ki jaankari teenagers ko sex ki taraf dhakelti hai.

> Chuppi sex ko taalti nahi. Woh bas yeh tay karti hai ki sikhayega kaun.

## Camera kya chhod deta hai

Porn adults ke liye bana scripted, edited entertainment hai. Ise lesson maan liya jaaye, toh ismein chaar cheezein gayab hain.

**Poochna.** Screen par lagbhag koi check nahi karta ki saamne wala yeh chahta hai ya nahi, aur kisi ke hichkichane par koi rukta bhi nahi.

**Protection.** Condom, contraception aur testing shayad hi kabhi dikhte hain. Screen ke bahar, kai sexually transmitted infections ke koi symptoms nahi hote, aur sirf test se pata chalta hai [[who-sti]]. Basic baatein bhi sabko pata nahi hain: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 15-24 saal ki young women mein sirf 54.4% ko pata tha ki condom kahan milta hai, jabki young men mein 87.3% ko [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

**Asli bodies.** Performers ek khaas look ke liye chune jaate hain, aur ghanton mein shoot hue scenes kaat kar kuch minute ke kar diye jaate hain. Asli bodies bahut alag-alag hoti hain, aur yeh healthy hai.

**Aas-paas ka sab kuch.** Nervousness, hansi, beech mein mann badal jaana, baad ki baatcheet, pregnancy ki chinta: edit mein inmein se kuch nahi bachta.

## Consent ki script banaam Section 63

Bahut saara mainstream porn ek hi consent script par chalta hai: hichkichahat bas ek phase hai, peeche pade rehne ka inaam milta hai, chuppi ka matlab haan hai, aur agar woh lagaa rahe toh "na" bhi "haan" ban jaati hai.

Indian law ki bhi ek script hai, aur woh iski theek ulti hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 63 consent ko "unequivocal voluntary agreement" kehta hai, yaani saaf aur apni marzi ki haan, jo shabdon, isharon ya kisi aur tarah se us specific sexual act ke liye batayi gayi ho. Section yeh bhi kehta hai ki agar aurat physically resist nahi karti, toh sirf is wajah se use consent dene wali nahi maana jayega [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Jise screen seduction bana kar dikhati hai, use statute consent ka na hona kehta hai. 18 se kam umar mein legal consent hota hi nahi: 18 se kam ki ladki ke saath sex rape hai, chahe woh kuch bhi kahe, aur POCSO Act 18 se kam ke har bachche ko protect karta hai, ladka ho ya ladki [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Porn ki script ek aise desh mein pahunchti hai jahan bahut log pehle se ise sach maante hain. NFHS-5 mein 15-49 saal ke 12.2% men ne, yaani lagbhag har aath mein se ek ne, kaha ki agar biwi sex se mana kare toh pati ko zabardasti karne ka haq hai. Jo men biwi ke mana karne par chaaron coercive responses ko galat maante the, unka share NFHS-4 (2015-16) ke 77% se girkar NFHS-5 mein 72% reh gaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Survey porn ke baare mein nahi poochta, aur yeh soch porn ne paida nahi ki. Par jis ladke ne screen par kabhi kisi "na" ki izzat hote nahi dekhi, aur ghar mein kabhi is par baat hote nahi suni, uske paas is soch ke saamne rakhne ko kuch nahi hai.

Law ki apni lines jaan lena zaroori hai. July 2015 mein Supreme Court ne kaha tha ki woh kisi adult ko apne kamre ki privacy mein pornography dekhne se nahi rok sakta [[hindu-sc-adult-porn-privacy-2015]]. Jis material mein bachcha dikhaya gaya ho, woh alag cheez hai: September 2024 mein court ne faisla diya ki child sexual abuse material dekhna, store karna ya apne paas rakhna offence hai [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Bina sharm ke porn par baat kaise karein

Yeh maan kar chaliye ki jis teenager ke paas phone hai, woh porn dekh chuka hai. "Tum yeh gandagi dekhte ho?" se baat wahin khatam ho jaati hai. "Online jo dikhta hai usmein bahut kuch acting hoti hai. Kuch aisa dekha jisse confusion hua ho?" se baat shuru hoti hai.

Woh chaar gayab cheezein khul kar boliye. Bataiye ki consent kya hai: ek saaf, apni marzi ki haan, jo kisi bhi waqt wapas li ja sakti hai. Bataiye ki sex kisi ka haq nahi hai, shaadi ke andar bhi nahi aur bahar bhi nahi.

Sawaal poochne par saza mat dijiye. Jis bachche ko poochne par saza milti hai, woh bas itna seekhta hai ki aapse poochna band kar de. Aur agar kisi adult ya bade bachche ne kisi bachche ko sexual material dikhaya hai, toh ise shararat nahi, warning sign maaniye: government ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse ne pornography dikhaye jaane ko child sexual abuse ke forms mein gina tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

2024 mein Supreme Court ne khud comprehensive sex education recommend ki, jo young logon ko consent ki clear samajh de [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Jab tak schools yeh nahi dete, zyada tar gharon mein choice 'baat karna' aur 'masoomiyat' ke beech nahi hai. Choice aapki awaaz aur search bar ke beech hai.

rape-needs-force-myth-consent-laws.en:
Many people carry one picture of rape: a violent attack, a struggle, injuries afterwards. From that picture comes a rule that sounds like common sense: if he did not force her and she did not fight, it was not rape. Much of the world's law still agrees. In 2024, only 63 of the 131 countries with data, 48%, had rape laws based on lack of consent [[un-sdg-report-2025-goal5]]. India's penal code is, by its own text, on the consent side. Belief has changed more slowly than the statute.

## The picture of rape most people carry

The picture has a stranger in it, and usually a weapon. Police records describe something else: in 96.8% of rape cases registered in India in 2024, the accused was someone the woman knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A relative, a partner or an employer rarely needs a weapon. Fear, authority and shock do the work, and many frightened people go still and silent instead of fighting.

The questions that follow a complaint come from the old picture: did she scream, did she run, where are the injuries. In 1978 those questions decided a case in the highest court. The Supreme Court acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl inside a police station. It noted that "no marks of injury were found" on her, described the alleged intercourse as "a peaceful affair" and concluded that it was "not proved to amount to rape" [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

## Force-based and consent-based laws around the world

A force-based law defines rape by what the accused did: violence, or the threat of it. The prosecution has to show that force, so in practice the trial turns on how the woman resisted. A consent-based law defines rape by what was missing: her free agreement. The question moves from her body to his conduct.

By the UN's count, consent-based laws are the minority. Its 2026 report adds a second condition and finds that just 38% of 131 countries have consent-based rape laws that also explicitly criminalise marital rape [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]].

Life at home is a separate matter. Across 78 countries with data for 2025, 75.4% of married or partnered women aged 15-49 said they could refuse sex, and only 56.3% had full decision-making power over sex, contraception and their own health care [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]].

## Where India's law stands since 2013

After the 2012 Delhi gang rape case, Parliament rewrote the rape law. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 defined consent as "an unequivocal voluntary agreement": a woman communicates, by words, gestures or any other form of communication, that she is willing to take part in the specific sexual act. It added that a woman who does not physically resist shall not, for that reason alone, be regarded as consenting [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. That sentence reverses the reasoning of 1978. Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), in force since 1 July 2024, carries both parts forward [[indiacode-bns-2023]] [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]].

> Indian law does not ask how hard she fought. It asks whether she agreed.

The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes tells judges to write "rape", not "forcible rape" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

The consent rule has limits. Exception 2 to Section 63 says sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, are not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. That exception is under challenge. As of 19 November 2026 the Supreme Court had not ruled, and it said it would fix the final hearing for 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Inside marriage, the force idea is still said aloud: in NFHS-5, 12.2% of Indian men aged 15-49 said a husband has the right to use force to have sex if his wife refuses [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Section 63 is also written as an offence by a man against a woman, so non-consensual sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under the code [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Fear, deception, intoxication: consent the law does not accept

Section 63 lists situations in which a "yes", or silence, does not count. It is rape when her consent was obtained through fear of death or hurt; when intoxication or unsoundness of mind left her unable to understand what she was agreeing to; when she is unable to communicate consent; when the man posed as her husband; and when she is under 18, whatever she said [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. None of these needs a weapon, a bruise or a struggle.

Deception is narrower than many people assume. On lies, the rape section is specific: it names a man posing as the woman's husband.
