Other deceit, such as a promise of marriage he never meant to keep, or a false promise of a job or promotion, falls under Section 69, a separate offence punishable with up to 10 years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The POCSO Act treats everyone under 18 as a child, boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], and a child's agreement is no defence.

## What 'unequivocal' means in real life

Consider this situation. A 19-year-old student in Pune is in a friend's room. She says "not today" and turns away. He carries on. She goes still and says nothing more. Nobody shouts and there are no injuries. Under a force-based law, her case would turn on why she did not fight. Under Section 63, the question is whether she communicated that she was willing, and she communicated the opposite.

"Unequivocal" means clear: if he is guessing, he does not have it. "Voluntary" means free: a yes given to end pressure, sulking or threats is not free. "The specific sexual act" means this act, now: a yes to a kiss, or a yes last week, does not carry over.

The statute changed in 2013. The questions asked at home and at the police station have changed far less. If someone tells you they were assaulted, do not ask why they did not fight. If it happened to you and you froze, the law does not treat that as agreement. In an emergency call 112; if you are under 18, you can also call the Child Helpline on 1098. This is general information, not legal advice.
rape-needs-force-myth-consent-laws.hg:
Bahut se logon ke dimaag mein rape ki ek hi picture hai: ek violent attack, haathapai, aur baad mein chotein. Isi picture se ek rule nikalta hai jo common sense jaisa lagta hai: agar usne zabardasti nahi ki aur woh ladi nahi, toh yeh rape nahi tha. Duniya ke bahut se deshon ka law aaj bhi yahi maanta hai. 2024 mein jin 131 deshon ka data tha, unmein se sirf 63, yaani 48%, ke rape laws consent ki kami par based the [[un-sdg-report-2025-goal5]]. India ka penal code, apne text ke hisaab se, consent wali side par hai. Lekin logon ki soch law jitni tezi se nahi badli.

## Rape ki woh picture jo zyada tar logon ke dimaag mein hai

Is picture mein ek stranger hota hai, aur aksar ek hathiyaar. Police records kuch aur dikhate hain: 2024 mein India mein register hue rape cases mein se 96.8% mein accused koi aisa tha jise aurat jaanti thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Kisi relative, partner ya employer ko hathiyaar ki zaroorat kam hi padti hai. Dar, authority aur shock hi kaafi hote hain, aur bahut se log dar ke maare ladne ke bajaye sunn aur chup ho jaate hain.

Complaint ke baad jo sawaal poochhe jaate hain, woh isi purani picture se aate hain: woh chillayi kyun nahi, bhaagi kyun nahi, chotein kahan hain. 1978 mein desh ki sabse badi court mein ek case inhi sawaalon par tay hua. Supreme Court ne do policemen ko bari kar diya, jin par police station ke andar ek minor ladki ke rape ka aarop tha. Court ne note kiya ki ladki par "no marks of injury were found", kathit intercourse ko "a peaceful affair" kaha aur nateeja nikala ki yeh "not proved to amount to rape" tha [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

## Duniya bhar mein force-based aur consent-based laws

Force-based law rape ko is baat se define karta hai ki accused ne kya kiya: violence, ya uski dhamki. Prosecution ko woh force saabit karni padti hai, isliye practice mein poora trial is par tik jaata hai ki aurat ne kitna resist kiya. Consent-based law rape ko is baat se define karta hai ki kya missing tha: aurat ki apni marzi se di gayi haan. Sawaal uski body se hatkar aadmi ke behaviour par aa jaata hai.

UN ki ginti ke hisaab se consent-based laws minority mein hain. Uski 2026 ki report ek aur condition jodti hai aur batati hai ki 131 deshon mein se sirf 38% ke paas aise consent-based rape laws hain jo marital rape ko bhi saaf-saaf crime maante hain [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]].

Ghar ke andar ki zindagi ek alag maamla hai. 2025 ke data wale 78 deshon mein, 15-49 saal ki married ya partnered women mein se 75.4% ne kaha ki woh sex se mana kar sakti hain, aur sirf 56.3% ke paas sex, contraception aur apni health care, teenon par poora decision-making power tha [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]].

## 2013 ke baad India ka law kahan khada hai

2012 ke Delhi gang rape case ke baad Parliament ne rape law ko naye sire se likha. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne consent ko "an unequivocal voluntary agreement" kaha: aurat shabdon, gestures ya kisi bhi tarah ke communication se batati hai ki woh us specific sexual act mein hissa lene ko taiyaar hai. Act ne yeh bhi joda ki jo aurat physically resist nahi karti, use sirf isi wajah se consenting nahi maana jaayega [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Yeh ek line 1978 ki reasoning ko ulat deti hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 63, jo 1 July 2024 se laagu hai, dono baatein aage le jaata hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]] [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]].

> Indian law yeh nahi poochhta ki woh kitna ladi. Woh poochhta hai ki usne haan kaha tha ya nahi.

Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook judges ko "forcible rape" ki jagah sirf "rape" likhne ko kehti hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Lekin consent wale rule ki bhi hadein hain. Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar patni 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh pati ke uske saath sexual acts rape nahi hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Is exception ko court mein challenge kiya gaya hai. 19 November 2026 tak Supreme Court ne faisla nahi diya tha, aur usne kaha ki final hearing woh 9 ya 10 December 2026 ke liye fix karegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Shaadi ke andar force wali soch aaj bhi khule aam boli jaati hai: NFHS-5 mein 15-49 saal ke 12.2% Indian men ne kaha ki agar patni mana kare toh pati ko sex ke liye force use karne ka haq hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Section 63 aadmi ke haathon aurat ke khilaaf offence ke roop mein likha gaya hai, isliye kisi adult man ya transgender person ke saath non-consensual sex is code mein rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Dar, dhokha, nasha: woh consent jise law nahi maanta

Section 63 un situations ki list deta hai jinmein "haan", ya chuppi, count nahi hoti. Yeh rape hai jab uska consent maut ya chot ka dar dikha kar liya gaya ho; jab nashe ya unsoundness of mind ki wajah se woh samajh hi na paayi ho ki kis cheez ke liye haan keh rahi hai; jab woh consent communicate karne ki haalat mein na ho; jab aadmi uska pati ban kar aaya ho; aur jab woh 18 se kam umr ki ho, chahe usne kuch bhi kaha ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Inmein se kisi ke liye bhi hathiyaar, chot ya haathapai zaroori nahi.

Dhokhe ka daayra utna bada nahi jitna bahut se log samajhte hain. Jhooth ke maamle mein rape wala section specific hai: woh aadmi ka khud ko aurat ka pati batana naam leke likhta hai. Baaki dhokha, jaise shaadi ka woh vaada jise nibhane ka iraada kabhi tha hi nahi, ya job ya promotion ka jhootha vaada, Section 69 mein aata hai. Yeh alag offence hai, jismein 10 saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO Act 18 se kam umr ke har insaan ko child maanta hai, ladka ho ya ladki [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], aur child ki haan koi defence nahi hai.

## Asli zindagi mein 'unequivocal' ka matlab

Ek situation sochiye. Pune ki ek 19 saal ki student apne dost ke kamre mein hai. Woh kehti hai "aaj nahi" aur munh pher leti hai. Uska dost rukta nahi. Woh sunn ho jaati hai aur aage kuch nahi kehti. Koi chillata nahi, aur koi chot nahi lagti. Force-based law mein uska case is par tikta ki woh ladi kyun nahi. Section 63 mein sawaal yeh hai ki kya usne bataya ki woh taiyaar hai, aur usne toh ulta bataya tha.

"Unequivocal" ka matlab hai saaf: agar woh andaaza laga raha hai, toh uske paas haan nahi hai. "Voluntary" ka matlab hai apni marzi se: jo haan pressure, rootne ya dhamkiyon se peechha chhudane ke liye di gayi, woh apni marzi ki nahi hai. "The specific sexual act" ka matlab hai yahi act, abhi: kiss ke liye haan, ya pichhle hafte ki haan, aage carry nahi hoti.

Law 2013 mein badal gaya. Ghar par aur police station mein poochhe jaane wale sawaal utne nahi badle. Agar koi aapko bataye ki uske saath assault hua, toh yeh mat poochhiye ki woh ladi kyun nahi. Agar yeh aapke saath hua aur aap freeze ho gaye, toh law use haan nahi maanta. Emergency mein 112 par call kijiye; agar aap 18 se kam umr ke hain, toh Child Helpline 1098 par bhi call kar sakte hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

rape-not-modern-import-myth.en:
After almost every rape case that makes national news, someone on a TV panel, in a family WhatsApp group or at the dinner table names the cause: mobile phones, the internet, jeans, films, girls who go out. The idea behind the blame is that India was once safe and sexual violence arrived with modern life. India's own records say otherwise. The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) began counting rape in 1971 and recorded 2,487 cases that year [[ncrb-cii-2013-trends-1953-2013]], decades before anyone in India carried a smartphone.

## The usual suspects: phones, jeans, cinema

The suspect changes with the decade; the logic does not. Something new from outside, a gadget, a fashion, a film, is said to have corrupted men or made girls "invite" trouble. The fix that follows is nearly always about controlling girls: take her phone, check her clothes, bring her home early.

The Supreme Court has rejected the heart of this story. Its 2023 handbook for judges lists as false stereotypes the ideas that a woman's clothing, drinking or smoking invites sexual contact and that rapists are usually strangers, and notes that men very often assault women they know [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## What the records show from 1971

The 1971 figure does not measure how much rape there was. The legal definition, the population and the willingness to report were all very different, so the rise in recorded cases since then cannot be read simply as a rise in rape. But it shows the crime was there to be counted.

Court files show it too. In a judgment dated 15 September 1978, the Supreme Court acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl inside a police station in Maharashtra in 1972. It noted that no marks of injury were found on her and called the alleged intercourse "a peaceful affair" (AIR 1979 SC 185) [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Protests over that acquittal led Parliament to pass the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983, which made custodial rape a separate aggravated offence and made it a crime to reveal a rape victim's identity [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. In 1995 a Rajasthan trial court acquitted the dominant-caste men accused of the 1992 gang rape of a government social worker, reasoning partly that dominant-caste men would not rape an oppressed-caste woman [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Neither case involved a phone. Both involved power: a lock-up, a uniform, caste.

Then look at who the accused are. In 2012, police recorded the offender as known to the victim in 98.2% of rape cases, 24,470 of 24,915 [[ncrb-cii-2012-snapshots]]. In 2024 the share was 96.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Whatever else changed in Indian life between those years, the basic pattern did not: the accused is almost always someone with access.

## Abuse that needed no phone

Children tell the same story. In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 53.22% of 12,447 children surveyed in 13 states reported one or more forms of sexual abuse, and 5.69% reported sexual assault [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The sample was not random and the definition was broad, so this is not a national rate. But half the abusers were people the child knew or adults in a position of trust, and 72.1% of the children who had been sexually assaulted had told no one [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Worldwide, UNICEF estimates that more than 370 million girls and women alive today, about 1 in 8, were raped or sexually assaulted before 18, along with 240 million to 310 million boys and men [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. That count covers every generation alive, including people whose childhoods ended long before the internet.

Some abuse was even protected by law. When Parliament raised the age of consent to 18 in 2013, it left the marital exception at 15, so a husband's sex with a wife aged 15 to 17 was not legally rape until the Supreme Court's Independent Thought ruling of 11 October 2017 [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. That shield for child marriage was kept in place by Parliament, not brought in by phones or films.

## Why blaming modernity suits abusers

Blaming the phone turns everyone's eyes away from the uncle, the tutor, the husband and the man in uniform, the people the records keep naming. It turns prevention into surveillance of girls. And it tells a child abused at home, in a "respectable" family, that what happened to her cannot have happened here.

The same "culture" argument has blocked the education that helps children name abuse. In 2007, as several states banned or refused to implement a new school sex education curriculum, the Madhya Pradesh government said sex education had "no place in Indian culture" [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]]. That was the year of the government study above. Our investigation of those bans tests each argument made for them.

None of this means technology is harmless. In 2024 police recorded 18,615 cyber crimes against women, including 1,224 cases of cyber stalking or bullying and 370 of cyber blackmail or threats [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Phones have handed abusers new tools, and those crimes need laws, platforms and police that keep up. But a tool is not a cause.

## What has really changed

What is new is not rape but the willingness and the means to report it. NCRB itself warns that a rise in registered crime is not the same as a rise in crime, and that e-FIRs and women's help desks can push the numbers up [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. A 2012 study found that when states reserved a third of local council seats for women, recorded rapes rose 23%, driven mainly by more women reporting rather than more crime [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

The law has even learnt to use the device it is told to fear. Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, a rape survivor's statement may be recorded on video, including on a mobile phone (Section 176), and anyone can file an e-FIR, or a Zero FIR at any police station (Section 173) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

The silence is older than any gadget, and it is still loud. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 77% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Blaming the phone asks them to stay quiet a little longer. The record asks the opposite: look at who had access, and believe the person who tells you.
rape-not-modern-import-myth.hg:
Jab bhi koi rape case national news banta hai, lagbhag har baar koi TV panel par, family WhatsApp group mein ya dinner table par uski wajah bata deta hai: mobile phone, internet, jeans, filmein, bahar jaane wali ladkiyan. Is blame ke peeche soch yeh hai ki India pehle safe tha aur sexual violence modern zindagi ke saath aaya. India ke apne records kuch aur kehte hain. National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ne 1971 mein rape ki ginti shuru ki aur us saal 2,487 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2013-trends-1953-2013]], yaani India mein kisi ke haath mein smartphone aane se dashkon pehle.

## Wahi purane suspects: phone, jeans, cinema

Suspect har dashak ke saath badal jaata hai; logic wahi rehta hai. Bahar se aayi koi nayi cheez, koi gadget, koi fashion, koi film, mardon ko bigaadne ya ladkiyon ke "musibat bulaane" ki wajah bata di jaati hai. Iske baad jo ilaaj sujhaaya jaata hai, woh lagbhag hamesha ladkiyon par control ka hota hai: uska phone le lo, uske kapde check karo, use jaldi ghar bulao.

Supreme Court is kahani ki jad ko hi khaarij kar chuka hai. Judges ke liye uski 2023 handbook in baaton ko jhoothe stereotypes mein ginti hai ki aurat ke kapde, sharaab peena ya smoking sexual contact ko nyota dete hain, aur ki rapist aksar ajnabi hote hain. Handbook yeh bhi kehti hai ki mard bahut baar un aurton par hamla karte hain jinhe woh jaante hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## 1971 se records kya dikhate hain

1971 ka aankda yeh nahi naapta ki us waqt kitne rape hue. Rape ki legal definition, aabaadi aur report karne ka maahaul, sab kuch bahut alag tha, isliye tab se darj cases mein jo uchhaal aaya, use seedhe rape badhne ki tarah nahi padha ja sakta. Lekin yeh saabit karta hai ki crime tab bhi tha, aur ginne ke liye maujood tha.

Court files bhi yahi dikhati hain. 15 September 1978 ke judgment mein Supreme Court ne do policewalon ko bari kar diya, jin par 1972 mein Maharashtra ke ek police station ke andar ek minor ladki ke rape ka aarop tha. Court ne kaha ki ladki ke shareer par chot ke nishaan nahi mile, aur kathit intercourse ko "a peaceful affair" bataya (AIR 1979 SC 185) [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Is acquittal ke khilaaf protests ke baad Parliament ne Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 paas kiya, jisne custodial rape ko alag aggravated offence banaya aur rape victim ki pehchaan zaahir karna crime bana diya [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. 1995 mein Rajasthan ki ek trial court ne 1992 mein ek sarkari social worker ke gang rape ke aaropi dominant-caste mardon ko bari kar diya. Uske tark ka ek hissa yeh tha ki dominant-caste mard kisi oppressed-caste aurat ka rape nahi karenge [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Dono mein se kisi case mein phone nahi tha. Dono mein power thi: lock-up, vardi, caste.

Ab dekhiye accused kaun hote hain. 2012 mein police ne 98.2% rape cases mein offender ko victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala darj kiya, yaani 24,915 mein se 24,470 cases mein [[ncrb-cii-2012-snapshots]]. 2024 mein yeh hissa 96.8% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In saalon mein Indian zindagi mein aur jo bhi badla ho, buniyadi pattern nahi badla: accused lagbhag hamesha woh hota hai jiski victim tak pahunch hoti hai.

## Woh abuse jise phone ki zaroorat nahi thi

Bachche bhi yahi kahani sunaate hain. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein 13 states ke 12,447 bachchon ka survey hua, jinmein se 53.22% ne ek ya zyada tarah ka sexual abuse bataya, aur 5.69% ne sexual assault [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Sample random nahi tha aur definition kaafi chaudi thi, isliye yeh national rate nahi hai. Lekin aadhe abusers aise log the jinhe bachcha jaanta tha ya jo bharose ki position mein the, aur jin bachchon ka sexual assault hua tha unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Duniya bhar ke liye UNICEF ka anumaan hai ki aaj zinda 370 million se zyada ladkiyon aur aurton ka, yaani lagbhag 8 mein se 1 ka, 18 saal se pehle rape ya sexual assault hua, aur saath mein 240 million se 310 million ladkon aur mardon ka bhi [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]]. Is ginti mein aaj zinda har peedhi shaamil hai, woh log bhi jinka bachpan internet aane se bahut pehle khatam ho gaya tha.

Kuch abuse ko toh law ne hi bachaaya hua tha. Jab Parliament ne 2013 mein age of consent badhakar 18 ki, tab marital exception ko 15 par hi chhod diya. Isliye 15 se 17 saal ki patni ke saath pati ka sex legally rape nahi tha, jab tak 11 October 2017 ko Supreme Court ke Independent Thought faisle ne yeh gap band nahi kiya [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. Child marriage ko mili yeh dhaal Parliament ne bani rehne di thi; ise phone ya filmein nahi laaye the.

## Modernity ko blame karna abusers ke kaam kyun aata hai

Phone ko blame karne se sabki nazar us chacha, tutor, pati aur vardi wale aadmi se hat jaati hai, jinka naam records baar-baar lete hain. Prevention ladkiyon ki nigraani ban jaata hai. Aur ghar par, kisi "izzatdaar" parivar mein abuse jhel rahe bachche ko yeh sandesh milta hai ki uske saath jo hua, woh yahan ho hi nahi sakta.

Yahi "culture" wala tark us education ko bhi rokta aaya hai jo bachchon ko abuse ko naam dena sikhati hai. 2007 mein, jab kai states ne schools ka naya sex education curriculum ban kiya ya lagu karne se mana kar diya, tab Madhya Pradesh sarkar ne kaha ki sex education ki "no place in Indian culture", yaani Indian culture mein koi jagah nahi [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]]. Yeh wahi saal tha jab upar wali sarkari study aayi. Un bans par hamari investigation unke paksh mein diye gaye har tark ko parakhti hai.

Iska matlab yeh nahi ki technology bilkul bekasoor hai. 2024 mein police ne aurton ke khilaaf 18,615 cyber crimes darj kiye, jinmein cyber stalking ya bullying ke 1,224 cases aur cyber blackmail ya dhamki ke 370 cases shaamil the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Phone ne abusers ke haath mein naye tools diye hain, aur in crimes ke liye aise laws, platforms aur police chahiye jo saath chal sakein. Lekin tool wajah nahi hota.

## Asal mein kya badla hai

Naya rape nahi hai. Naya hai use report karne ki himmat aur saadhan. NCRB khud chetaavni deta hai ki darj crime ka badhna crime ke badhne jaisa nahi hai, aur e-FIR aur women help desks jaise qadam aankde badha sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. 2012 ki ek study ne paaya ki jab states ne local councils ki ek-tihaai seatein aurton ke liye reserve kin, toh darj rape 23% badhe, aur iski mukhya wajah zyada crime nahi, balki zyada aurton ka report karna tha [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

Law ne toh usi device ko use karna seekh liya hai jisse humein darne ko kaha jaata hai. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita ke tahat rape survivor ka statement video par record ho sakta hai, mobile phone par bhi (Section 176), aur koi bhi e-FIR kar sakta hai, ya kisi bhi police station mein Zero FIR (Section 173) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Khamoshi kisi bhi gadget se purani hai, aur aaj bhi gehri hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 77% aurton ne kabhi madad nahi maangi ya kisi ko nahi bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Phone ko blame karna unse thodi der aur chup rehne ko kehta hai. Record ulta kehta hai: dekhiye kiski pahunch thi, aur jo aapko bataye uska yakeen kariye.

rape-power-not-desire-explained.en:
Most Indians grow up hearing that rape is about desire: a man sees an attractive woman, loses control, and something "happens". The fixes follow from that story: cover her up, keep her home, blame her clothes. India's own penal code tells a different story. Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) sets at least 10 years in prison for rape, and lists 13 aggravated forms punishable with up to imprisonment for the rest of the offender's natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. That list is not a list of tempting moments. It is a map of power.

## The 'uncontrollable desire' myth

The desire story shifts blame from the man who acted to the woman who supposedly tempted him. Our story on the "she asked for it" myth takes that excuse apart.

The Supreme Court's 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes names the real pattern: "Rape and sexual violence have long been used as a tool of social control." [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]] Our case files on Hathras and on the 1992 Rajasthan gang rape show how caste power works the same way.

If rape were about attraction, the man with the most power over a woman would be no more dangerous than a stranger. Indian law assumes the opposite.

## What Section 64 says about power

The aggravated list covers rape by a police officer, a public servant, a member of the armed forces, jail or hospital staff, and "a relative, guardian or teacher of, or a person in a position of trust or authority towards the woman". It covers rape during communal violence, rape of a pregnant or disabled woman, and repeated rape of the same woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Each item describes control: a lock-up, a ward, a classroom, a home, a riot.

Evidence law agrees. In a prosecution for aggravated rape under Section 64(2), once intercourse is proved and the woman tells the court she did not consent, the court must presume that she did not consent [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Where the accused held the power, the law makes him disprove her account.

Look how rarely police use these clauses. In 2024 they registered rape cases under the aggravated categories for rape by police personnel (27 cases), other public servants (15), members of the armed forces (2), staff of jails, remand homes or other places of custody (3) and hospital staff (8) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A case enters these rows only when police invoke the clause. So 27 is not a measure of how often police officers rape. It is a measure of how often police wrote down that one of their own did.

## Custody, riots and the cases the record holds

In 1978 the Supreme Court acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl inside a police station in Maharashtra, overturning their convictions by the Bombay High Court (AIR 1979 SC 185) [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. The court noted that no marks of injury were found on the girl and concluded that the intercourse was "not proved to amount to rape" [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

Rape during communal violence is listed separately because in a riot a woman can be targeted for the community she belongs to. On 21 January 2008 a special court in Mumbai sentenced 11 men to life imprisonment for the gang rape of a pregnant woman and the murder of 14 of her relatives during the 2002 Gujarat riots. It also convicted a police officer of deliberately recording the FIR incorrectly. On 4 May 2017 the Bombay High Court upheld the 11 convictions and convicted five police personnel and two doctors whom the trial court had acquitted [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

Power did not stop at the verdict. On 15 August 2022 all 11 walked out of Godhra jail after the Gujarat government granted them remission under its 1992 policy. On 8 January 2024 the Supreme Court quashed the remission, holding that Gujarat had no power to grant it and that the court's own May 2022 order had been obtained by suppressing facts and fraud [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. The men were ordered back to jail.

Men and transgender people are protected even less: the BNS has no counterpart to IPC Section 377, so forced penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under it, and no specific offence replaced the old section [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Disabled women and the 'no one would want her' stereotype

The handbook also lists as a stereotype the belief that able-bodied men do not want sex with disabled women, so their complaints must be false. Its answer: "The presence of a disability does not mean that there is a lower likelihood of sexual violence," and women whose disabilities affect how they communicate are particularly vulnerable [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

This stereotype is the desire myth turned inside out. If rape were about attraction, disabled women would be safe. Instead the myth works for offenders twice: the women most exposed are often the least able to tell, and their complaints are the easiest to dismiss.

The law names that power. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 punishes anyone "in a position to dominate the will" of a disabled woman or child who uses it to exploit her sexually [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. Since a disabled survivor may struggle to reach a police station, police must record her complaint at her home or a place she chooses, with an interpreter or special educator, and videograph it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yet of 29,536 rape cases registered in 2024, police recorded only 144 under the aggravated clause for raping a disabled woman [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Prevention that starts with power, not dress codes

If rape is about power, prevention has to start where power goes unchecked: lock-ups and remand homes, hostels and hospital wards, coaching classes and workplaces, and homes where one adult's word is law. Dress codes and curfews put the burden on the person with the least power in the room.

Institutions need a safe way to complain about the people who run them. Families need to treat a complaint against a respected uncle as seriously as one against a stranger. And when police refuse to register an FIR for rape, the refusal is itself a crime under Section 199 of the BNS, punishable with 6 months to 2 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

This is general information, not legal advice.
rape-power-not-desire-explained.hg:
Zyada tar Indians yahi sunkar bade hote hain ki rape desire ka maamla hai: ek aadmi ne attractive aurat dekhi, control kho diya, aur kuch "ho gaya". Isi kahani se solutions bhi nikalte hain: ladki ko dhak do, ghar mein rakho, uske kapdon ko blame karo. Lekin India ka apna penal code kuch aur kahani batata hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 64 rape ke liye kam se kam 10 saal ki jail tay karti hai, aur rape ke 13 aggravated forms ginati hai jinki saza baaki poori zindagi ki jail tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh list behakne wale lamhon ki list nahi hai. Yeh power ka naksha hai.

## 'Uncontrollable desire' wala myth

Desire wali kahani blame us aadmi se hata deti hai jisne crime kiya, aur us aurat par daal deti hai jisne kathit taur par use "behkaya". "She asked for it" myth par hamari story is bahane ki poori pol kholti hai.

Supreme Court ki 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes asli pattern ka naam leti hai: "Rape and sexual violence have long been used as a tool of social control." [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]] Yaani rape aur sexual violence lambe samay se samaj ko control mein rakhne ka hathiyaar rahe hain. Hathras aur 1992 ke Rajasthan gang rape par hamari case files dikhati hain ki caste ki power bhi aise hi kaam karti hai.

Agar rape sirf attraction ka maamla hota, toh aurat par sabse zyada power rakhne wala aadmi kisi stranger se zyada khatarnaak nahi hota. Indian law bilkul ulta maanta hai.

## Section 64 power ke baare mein kya kehti hai

Aggravated list mein yeh shaamil hain: police officer, public servant, armed forces ka member, jail ya hospital staff, aur "a relative, guardian or teacher of, or a person in a position of trust or authority towards the woman". Ismein communal violence ke dauraan rape, pregnant ya disabled aurat ka rape, aur ek hi aurat ka baar-baar rape bhi aata hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Har item control ki kahani hai: lock-up, hospital ward, classroom, ghar, danga.

Evidence law bhi yahi maanta hai. Section 64(2) ke under aggravated rape ke case mein, agar intercourse saabit ho jaaye aur aurat court mein kahe ki uska consent nahi tha, toh court ko maanna hoga ki consent nahi tha [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Yaani jahan power accused ke haath mein thi, wahan aurat ki baat ko galat saabit karna accused ka kaam hai.

Ab dekhiye police in clauses ka kitna kam use karti hai. 2024 mein aggravated categories ke under yeh cases register hue: police personnel ke kiye rape ke 27 cases, doosre public servants ke 15, armed forces ke members ke 2, jail, remand home ya custody ki doosri jagahon ke staff ke 3, aur hospital staff ke 8 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Koi case in rows mein tabhi aata hai jab police yeh clause lagaye. Isliye 27 yeh nahi batata ki policewale kitni baar rape karte hain. Yeh batata hai ki police ne kitni baar likha ki uske apne kisi aadmi ne aisa kiya.

## Custody, dange aur record mein darj cases

1978 mein Supreme Court ne do policewalon ko bari kar diya, jin par Maharashtra ke ek police station ke andar ek minor ladki ke rape ka aarop tha. Bombay High Court ne unhe saza di thi, jise Supreme Court ne palat diya (AIR 1979 SC 185) [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Court ne note kiya ki ladki ke shareer par chot ke koi nishaan nahi mile, aur nateeja nikala ki intercourse "not proved to amount to rape" tha [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

Communal violence mein rape ko alag se isliye gina gaya hai kyunki dange mein aurat ko uski community ki wajah se target kiya ja sakta hai. 21 January 2008 ko Mumbai ki ek special court ne 11 aadmiyon ko umrqaid di. Crime tha 2002 ke Gujarat riots ke dauraan ek pregnant aurat ka gang rape aur uske 14 rishtedaaron ka qatl. Court ne ek police officer ko bhi convict kiya jisne jaan-boojhkar FIR galat darj ki thi. 4 May 2017 ko Bombay High Court ne 11 convictions ko barkaraar rakha, aur un paanch police personnel aur do doctors ko bhi convict kiya jinhe trial court ne bari kar diya tha [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

Power ka asar verdict ke baad bhi khatam nahi hua. 15 August 2022 ko Gujarat sarkar ne apni 1992 ki policy ke under remission diya, aur sabhi 11 Godhra jail se bahar aa gaye. 8 January 2024 ko Supreme Court ne remission cancel kar diya: Gujarat ko remission dene ka haq hi nahi tha, aur court ka apna May 2022 ka order facts chhupakar aur fraud se liya gaya tha [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Unhe wapas jail jaane ka order diya gaya.

Mard aur transgender log toh aur bhi kam protected hain: BNS mein IPC ki Section 377 jaisa kuch nahi rakha gaya, isliye kisi adult mard ya transgender insaan ke saath zabardasti penetrative sex is code mein rape nahi hai, aur purani section ki jagah koi khaas offence bhi nahi banaya gaya [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Disabled aurtein aur 'use kaun chahega' wala stereotype

Handbook ek aur stereotype ko galat batati hai: ki able-bodied mard disabled aurton ke saath sex nahi chahte, isliye unki complaints jhoothi hongi. Handbook ka jawab hai: "The presence of a disability does not mean that there is a lower likelihood of sexual violence", aur jin aurton ki disability baat-cheet par asar daalti hai, woh khaas taur par vulnerable hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Yeh stereotype desire wale myth ka hi ulta roop hai. Agar rape attraction ka maamla hota, toh disabled aurtein safe hotin. Par yeh myth offenders ko do tarah se bachata hai: jo aurtein sabse zyada khatre mein hain woh aksar sabse kam bata paati hain, aur unki complaint sabse aasaani se taal di jaati hai.

Law is power ko pehchaanta hai. Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 har us insaan ko saza deta hai jo kisi disabled aurat ya bachche ki marzi par haavi hone ki position mein ho ("in a position to dominate the will") aur iska use sexual exploitation ke liye kare [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. Disabled survivor ke liye police station tak pahunchna mushkil ho sakta hai, isliye police ko uski complaint uske ghar ya uski chuni jagah par, interpreter ya special educator ke saath record karni hoti hai, aur uski video recording bhi honi chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Phir bhi 2024 mein register hue 29,536 rape cases mein se sirf 144 disabled aurat ke rape wale aggravated clause mein record hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Prevention jo power se shuru ho, dress code se nahi

Agar rape power ka maamla hai, toh prevention wahan se shuru hona chahiye jahan power par koi lagaam nahi: lock-ups aur remand homes, hostels aur hospital wards, coaching classes aur offices, aur woh ghar jahan ek bade ki baat hi law hai. Dress codes aur curfews us insaan par bojh daalte hain jiske paas kamre mein sabse kam power hai.

Institutions mein ek safe raasta hona chahiye jisse unhe chalane walon ke khilaaf complaint ho sake. Families ko kisi "izzatdaar" chacha ya mama ke khilaaf complaint ko utni hi seriously lena chahiye jitna kisi stranger ke khilaaf. Aur agar police rape ki FIR register karne se mana kare, toh yeh mana karna khud BNS ki Section 199 ke under crime hai, jiski saza 6 mahine se 2 saal tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

sex-myths-written-into-indian-law.en:
Some myths travel by WhatsApp forward. Others travelled by Gazette notification. For years at a time, Indian law has stated as legal text that contraception belongs to married couples, that a husband cannot rape his 15-year-old wife, and that one kind of sex is "against the order of nature". It has also let doctors claim to read a woman's sexual history from her body. All four have since been removed. Two other myths are still in force. This is general information, not legal advice.

## When a belief becomes a clause

A belief in a living room can be argued with. A belief in a statute tells a police officer which complaints to register, a doctor what to examine and a judge what counts as evidence.

It also makes the belief respectable. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 12.2% of Indian men aged 15-49 said a husband has the right to use force if his wife refuses sex [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The penal code still does not call what they describe rape, as the last section shows.

The pattern below repeats. The clause enters as an assumption and leaves only when someone forces the question, usually years later.

## The married-only abortion clause, 1971-2021

The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 let a doctor presume that a pregnancy caused by contraceptive failure was a grave injury to a woman's mental health. But the clause spoke only of a method used by "any married woman or her husband" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. The myth inside it: contraception, and so sex, belongs to marriage.

Consider a 22-year-old unmarried woman in 2015 whose contraception has failed. The Act did not say she could not have an abortion. But the one clause written for her situation described somebody else, and her doctor could read that too.

It took Parliament 50 years to rewrite the phrase. The 2021 amendment made it "any woman or her partner" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. On 29 September 2022 the Supreme Court went further, holding that shutting unmarried or single women out of abortion between 20 and 24 weeks would violate Article 14 of the Constitution [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## The 15-year-old wife, 2013-2017

The second myth says marriage is itself consent, and a married girl is a woman. In 2013 Parliament rewrote the rape law and raised the age of consent to 18. It kept the marital exception for wives aged 15 and above [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. So from 2013 until 2017, sex with a 16-year-old was rape if she was unmarried and not rape if the man was her husband.

Parliament had been told. The Justice Verma Committee, which reported on 23 January 2013, recommended deleting the marital rape exception [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament kept it.

The contradiction ended in court. On 11 October 2017, in Independent Thought v. Union of India, the Supreme Court read the exception down so that sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

## 'Against the order of nature' and the two-finger test

The third myth says only one kind of sex is natural. Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code spoke of "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. In the Naz Foundation case, the Delhi High Court decriminalised consensual gay sex on 2 July 2009. The Supreme Court reversed that verdict on 11 December 2013, making it a crime again for nearly five years. On 6 September 2018, in Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, a five-judge bench unanimously read the section down [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

The fourth myth says a woman's body records her sexual past, and her past shows whether she consented. This one never had a section number. It had a place in medical training and in rape trials, as the "two-finger test".

The hymen cannot show whether someone has had sex. In April 2013 the Supreme Court held that the test violates a rape survivor's right to privacy, physical and mental integrity and dignity [[barandbench-lillu-2013]]. That same year Parliament wrote into the Evidence Act that a victim's character or previous sexual experience is irrelevant to consent [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Yet the Court had to return to the test. On 31 October 2022 it said the practice has "no scientific basis" and "re-victimizes and re-traumatizes" women, held that anyone who conducts it is guilty of misconduct, and ordered it removed from medical curricula [[theprint-sc-two-finger-test-2022]].

## The myths still on the books

Two remain, both in Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which replaced the Indian Penal Code on 1 July 2024.

The first: a husband cannot rape his wife. Exception 2 says sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

In an affidavit verified on 3 October 2024, the Union government told the Supreme Court that treating this as rape could be "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. As of 19 November 2026 the Court had not ruled. The bench said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Until then, a wife can turn to the Domestic Violence Act, 2005, which counts sexual abuse as domestic violence [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

The second: men cannot be raped. Section 63 defines rape as an act by "a man" against "a woman". The BNS also dropped Section 377 without a replacement, so forced penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under the code [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. On 10 November 2023 a parliamentary standing committee warned that this would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men and transgender persons unpunished, and recommended keeping the section. The government did not accept that [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Children are covered: the POCSO Act protects boys and girls under 18 alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

None of the four myths that fell did so on its own. Each needed someone to challenge it, years of waiting, and a bench or a Parliament willing to say the assumption was wrong. A section number proves that a belief was once written down. It does not prove the belief was true.
sex-myths-written-into-indian-law.hg:
Kuch myths WhatsApp forward se phailte hain. Kuch Gazette notification se phaile. Indian law ne saalon tak legal text mein yeh likha rakha ki contraception shaadishuda couples ki cheez hai, ki pati apni 15 saal ki wife ka rape nahi kar sakta, aur ki ek tarah ka sex "against the order of nature" hai, yaani kudrat ke khilaf. Isi law ne doctors ko yeh daava bhi karne diya ki woh aurat ke body se uski sexual history padh sakte hain. Yeh chaaron ab hataye ja chuke hain. Do aur myths aaj bhi lagu hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Jab belief ek clause ban jaata hai

Drawing room mein kahe gaye belief se behes ki ja sakti hai. Statute mein likha belief police officer ko batata hai ki kaun si complaint register karni hai, doctor ko batata hai ki kya examine karna hai, aur judge ko batata hai ki evidence kya maana jaayega.

Isse us belief ko izzat bhi mil jaati hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 15-49 saal ke 12.2% Indian mardon ne kaha ki wife sex se mana kare toh pati ko zabardasti karne ka haq hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Penal code aaj bhi us cheez ko rape nahi kehta jiska yeh mard zikr kar rahe hain, jaisa aakhiri section mein dikhega.

Neeche har case mein ek hi pattern dohraya jaata hai. Clause ek assumption ki tarah andar aata hai, aur tabhi bahar jaata hai jab koi zor dekar sawaal uthata hai, aksar kai saal baad.

## Sirf shaadishuda auraton wala abortion clause, 1971-2021

Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 doctor ko yeh maan lene deta tha ki contraceptive fail hone se hui pregnancy aurat ki mental health ke liye "grave injury" hai. Lekin clause sirf us method ki baat karta tha jo "any married woman or her husband" ne use kiya ho [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Iske andar chhupa myth: contraception, aur isliye sex, sirf shaadi ke andar hota hai.

2015 ki 22 saal ki ek unmarried aurat ko sochiye, jiska contraception fail ho gaya hai. Act ne yeh nahi kaha tha ki uska abortion nahi ho sakta. Lekin jo ek clause theek uski situation ke liye likha gaya tha, woh kisi aur ka zikr karta tha, aur uska doctor bhi yeh padh sakta tha.

Parliament ko yeh phrase dobara likhne mein 50 saal lage. 2021 ke amendment ne ise "any woman or her partner" kar diya [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 29 September 2022 ko Supreme Court isse aage gaya: usne kaha ki unmarried ya single auraton ko 20 se 24 weeks ke beech ke abortion se bahar rakhna Constitution ke Article 14 ka violation hoga [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## 15 saal ki wife, 2013-2017

Doosra myth kehta hai ki shaadi khud hi consent hai, aur shaadishuda ladki aurat hai. 2013 mein Parliament ne rape law dobara likha aur age of consent 18 kar di. Lekin 15 saal aur usse badi wives ke liye marital exception waise ka waisa rakha [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. Yaani 2013 se 2017 tak, 16 saal ki ladki ke saath sex rape tha agar woh unmarried thi, aur rape nahi tha agar woh aadmi uska pati tha.

Parliament ko bataya ja chuka tha. Justice Verma Committee ne, jisne 23 January 2013 ko apni report di, marital rape exception ko hatane ki recommendation ki thi [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament ne use rakha.

Yeh contradiction court mein khatam hua. 11 October 2017 ko, Independent Thought v. Union of India mein, Supreme Court ne exception ko read down kiya, taaki 18 saal se kam umar ki wife ke saath sex rape maana jaaye [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

## 'Against the order of nature' aur two-finger test

Teesra myth kehta hai ki sirf ek hi tarah ka sex natural hai. Indian Penal Code ki Section 377 "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" ki baat karti thi [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. Naz Foundation case mein Delhi High Court ne 2 July 2009 ko consensual gay sex ko decriminalise kiya. Supreme Court ne 11 December 2013 ko woh faisla palat diya, aur yeh lagbhag paanch saal ke liye phir se crime ban gaya. 6 September 2018 ko, Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India mein, paanch judges ki bench ne ek raay se section ko read down kiya [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Chautha myth kehta hai ki aurat ka body uska sexual past record karta hai, aur uska past batata hai ki usne consent diya tha ya nahi. Is myth ka kabhi koi section number nahi tha. Iski jagah medical training aur rape trials mein thi, "two-finger test" ke naam se.

Hymen yeh nahi bata sakta ki kisi ne sex kiya hai ya nahi. April 2013 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki yeh test rape survivor ke privacy, physical aur mental integrity, aur dignity ke haq ka violation hai [[barandbench-lillu-2013]]. Usi saal Parliament ne Evidence Act mein likha ki consent ke sawaal par victim ka character ya uska previous sexual experience irrelevant hai [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Phir bhi Court ko is test par dobara aana pada. 31 October 2022 ko usne kaha ki is practice ka "no scientific basis" hai aur yeh auraton ko "re-victimizes and re-traumatizes" karti hai, yaani unhe dobara victim banati hai aur dobara trauma deti hai. Court ne kaha ki jo bhi yeh test karega woh misconduct ka doshi hoga, aur ise medical curricula se hatane ka order diya [[theprint-sc-two-finger-test-2022]].

## Woh myths jo aaj bhi kitaab mein hain

Do bache hain, aur dono Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 63 mein hain. BNS ne 1 July 2024 ko Indian Penal Code ki jagah li.

Pehla: pati apni wife ka rape nahi kar sakta. Exception 2 kehta hai ki apni wife ke saath, agar woh 18 saal ya usse badi hai, mard ka sexual intercourse ya sexual acts rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

3 October 2024 ko verify hue affidavit mein Union government ne Supreme Court se kaha ki ise rape maanna "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" ho sakta hai, yaani zaroorat se zyada sakht [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. 19 November 2026 tak Court ne faisla nahi diya tha. Bench ne kaha ki woh final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko fix karegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Tab tak wife Domestic Violence Act, 2005 ka sahara le sakti hai, jo sexual abuse ko domestic violence maanta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Doosra: mardon ka rape nahi ho sakta. Section 63 rape ko aisa act batati hai jo "a man" kisi "a woman" ke khilaf karta hai. BNS ne Section 377 ko bhi bina kisi replacement ke hata diya, isliye kisi adult mard ya transgender insaan ke saath zabardasti kiya gaya penetrative sex is code ke under rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 10 November 2023 ko ek parliamentary standing committee ne warn kiya tha ki isse mardon aur transgender logon ke khilaf non-consensual sexual offences bina saza ke reh jaayenge, aur section ko rakhne ki recommendation ki thi. Government ne yeh nahi maana [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Bachche cover hain: POCSO Act 18 saal se kam umar ke ladkon aur ladkiyon, dono ko barabar protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Jo chaar myths gire, unmein se koi bhi apne aap nahi gira. Har ek ke liye kisi ko use challenge karna pada, saalon intezaar karna pada, aur ek aisi bench ya Parliament chahiye thi jo keh sake ki yeh assumption galat tha. Section number bas yeh saabit karta hai ki ek belief kabhi likh diya gaya tha. Yeh saabit nahi karta ki woh belief sach tha.

sex-worker-consent-rape-myth.en:
Ask why a rape complaint by a woman in sex work went nowhere, and the answer can be a shrug: what did she expect? The excuse has two halves. The first says she has already agreed, because she sells sex. The second says her word counts for less, because of who she is. Indian law rejects both in writing. The people who apply it, from police station to courtroom, do not always follow.

## The excuse: 'she has already agreed'

The first half treats consent as a contract signed once: agree a price, and everything after is settled. Indian law does not define consent that way. Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) calls it an "unequivocal voluntary agreement": by words, gestures or other communication, a woman shows she is willing to take part in "the specific sexual act". A woman who does not physically resist is not, for that reason alone, consenting [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Imagine a 26-year-old sex worker in Pune. She agrees to meet a client. In the room he demands something she refused, or a second man walks in whom she never agreed to meet. She says no, and they go ahead. Her earlier yes covered one act with one man; it does not turn this no into a yes. In law, what happens next is rape.

## What Section 63 says about every woman

Section 63 lists seven circumstances that make an act rape, including acts against a woman's will, acts without her consent, consent obtained through fear of death or hurt, and sex with a girl under 18, whatever she says [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The section speaks of "a woman". It does not say a respectable woman, a married woman or a woman with no past.

Nor does the punishment shrink. Rape carries at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to life, under Section 64 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Nothing in it lowers that because of how a survivor earns a living.

The Supreme Court's 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes tells judges to drop "prostitute" and say "sex worker" or "trafficked victim", depending on the context. Labels such as "harlot", "whore" and "woman of easy virtue" become simply "woman" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. For a woman in sex work, the court's own guidance now says its words should not mark her as a lesser witness.

## Character is not evidence

The second half lives in the courtroom, where a defence lawyer suggests that a woman with many partners must have agreed to this one too. Parliament closed that door in 2013, when Section 53A of the Indian Evidence Act made a victim's character or previous sexual experience irrelevant to the question of consent [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

The rule survives in the new evidence law. Under Section 48 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), her character or sexual past is irrelevant to consent in rape and related cases. Under Section 149, she may not be asked in cross-examination about her "general immoral character" or her sexual past to prove consent [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

In plain words: her work may explain why she was in that room. It cannot prove that she agreed to what happened there.

## Trafficked or working: the line that matters

Some women in the sex trade chose the work. Others were trafficked into it. In 2024, 5,839 trafficking victims were rescued in India; 2,347 of them, 40%, had been trafficked for sexual exploitation for prostitution, more than for forced labour (1,493) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These count recorded rescues, not everyone still trapped.

In a trafficking case, her "consent" does not count at all. Section 143 of the BNS punishes trafficking for sexual exploitation with 7 to 10 years, at least 10 if the victim is a child, and says the victim's consent is immaterial. Under Section 144, knowingly sexually exploiting a trafficked adult carries 3 to 7 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Whether she was trafficked decides how the state treats her: as a victim to rescue, or as an adult making her own choices. It does not decide whether she can be raped: either way, forced sex is rape. And a girl under 18 is not a "sex worker" at all: the handbook replaces "child prostitute" with "child who has been trafficked" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Sex with her is rape whatever she says [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and the POCSO Act protects every child under 18, boys as well as girls [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

There is one hole. Section 63 protects only women. An adult man or a transgender person in sex work who is forced has no rape offence under the BNS, which dropped the old Section 377 and put nothing in its place [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Sexual abuse of a transgender person carries only six months to two years [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

## Health, police and the right to say no

In 2024, HIV prevalence among female sex workers in India was 1.13%, against 0.20% among all adults [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. After any rape, HIV prevention medicine (PEP) should start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours, and is taken for 28 days [[who-pep]]. Every hospital, government or private, must give a rape survivor immediate free treatment and inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A hospital in-charge who refuses faces up to a year in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

A woman can report a rape at any police station, wherever it happened, and a woman officer must record it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. An officer who fails to register a rape FIR faces six months to two years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Rape by a police officer of a woman in his custody or at a police station is aggravated rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In such aggravated cases, once intercourse is proved and she testifies that she did not consent, the court must presume she did not [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. In 2024 police registered 27 cases of rape by police personnel [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

None of these protections asks what a woman does for a living. The gap is whether the officer at the desk, the doctor on duty and the judge on the bench believe that. This is general information, not legal advice.
sex-worker-consent-rape-myth.hg:
Sex work karne wali kisi aurat ki rape complaint kahin nahi pahunchi, aur aap wajah poochiye, toh jawab mein bas kandhe uchkaaye ja sakte hain: "Aur kya expect kar rahi thi?" Is excuse ke do hisse hain. Pehla: woh toh pehle hi haan keh chuki hai, kyunki woh paise lekar sex karti hai. Doosra: uski baat ka wazan kam hai, kyunki woh "aisi" aurat hai. Indian law likhkar dono baatein reject karta hai. Lekin police station se court tak, law lagu karne wale log hamesha uske hisaab se nahi chalte.

## Excuse number one: 'woh toh pehle hi maan gayi thi'

Yeh excuse consent ko ek baar sign hue contract ki tarah dekhta hai: price tay ho gaya, toh aage jo bhi ho, sab tay. Law consent ko aise define nahi karta. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 63 consent ko ek "unequivocal voluntary agreement" kehti hai, yaani saaf aur apni marzi se di gayi haan: aurat words, gestures ya kisi aur tarah se jatati hai ki woh "the specific sexual act", yaani us khaas sexual act mein shamil hona chahti hai. Agar aurat ne physically resist nahi kiya, toh sirf is wajah se use consenting nahi maana jaayega [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Imagine kijiye, Pune mein 26 saal ki ek sex worker hai. Woh ek client se milne ke liye maan jaati hai. Room mein woh aadmi kuch aisa demand karta hai jisse usne mana kiya tha, ya ek doosra aadmi aa jaata hai jisse milne ke liye usne kabhi haan nahi kahi thi. Woh mana karti hai, phir bhi woh nahi rukte. Uski pehle wali "haan" ek aadmi ke saath ek act ke liye thi; woh is "na" ko "haan" nahi bana deti. Law ki nazar mein iske baad jo hota hai, woh rape hai.

## Section 63 har aurat ke baare mein kya kehti hai

Section 63 mein saat circumstances hain jinmein koi act rape maana jaata hai, jaise: aurat ki marzi ke khilaf, uske consent ke bina, maut ya chot ka darr dikhakar liya gaya consent, aur 18 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex, woh chahe kuch bhi kahe [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section mein bas "aurat" likha hai. Yeh nahi likha ki "izzatdar" aurat, shaadishuda aurat, ya aisi aurat jiska koi "past" na ho.

Saza bhi chhoti nahi hoti. Section 64 ke under rape ki saza kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, jo life imprisonment tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Survivor kis kaam se kamaati hai, iski wajah se yeh saza kam ho jaaye, aisa section mein kuch nahi hai.

Supreme Court ki 2023 ki Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes judges se kehti hai ki "prostitute" chhodiye, aur context ke hisaab se "sex worker" ya "trafficked victim" kahiye. "Harlot", "whore" aur "woman of easy virtue" jaise labels ki jagah bas "woman" likhiye [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Sex worker ke liye iska matlab hai ki ab court ki apni guidance kehti hai: court ke words use kamtar witness ki tarah pesh na karein.

## Character evidence nahi hai

Excuse ka doosra hissa courtroom mein dikhta hai, jahan defence lawyer ishaara karta hai ki jis aurat ke kai partners rahe hon, usne is baar bhi haan kahi hogi. Parliament ne 2013 mein yeh darwaza band kar diya, jab Indian Evidence Act ki Section 53A mein likha gaya ki consent ke sawaal par victim ka character ya uska previous sexual experience irrelevant hai [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Naye evidence law mein bhi yeh rule bacha hai. Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) ki Section 48 ke under rape aur usse jude cases mein consent ke liye uska character ya sexual past irrelevant hai. Section 149 ke under cross-examination mein usse uske "general immoral character" ya sexual past ke baare mein sawaal poochkar consent prove nahi kiya ja sakta [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Seedhi baat: uska kaam yeh explain kar sakta hai ki woh us room mein kyun thi. Yeh prove nahi kar sakta ki wahan jo hua, uske liye usne haan kahi thi.

## Trafficked ya apni marzi se kaam: asli line kahan hai

Kuch aurton ne yeh kaam khud chuna. Kuch ko trafficking karke isme dhakela gaya. 2024 mein India mein 5,839 trafficking victims rescue kiye gaye; inmein se 2,347, yaani 40%, ki trafficking prostitution ke liye sexual exploitation ke maqsad se hui thi, jo forced labour (1,493) se bhi zyada hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh sirf record hue rescues hain, un sab ki ginti nahi jo abhi bhi phanse hain.

Trafficking case mein uske "consent" ka koi matlab hi nahi. BNS ki Section 143 sexual exploitation ke liye trafficking par 7 se 10 saal ki saza deti hai, bachche ki trafficking par kam se kam 10 saal, aur kehti hai ki victim ka consent immaterial hai. Section 144 ke under kisi trafficked adult ka jaan-boojhkar sexual exploitation karne par 3 se 7 saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Uski trafficking hui thi ya nahi, isse yeh tay hota hai ki state uske saath kaise pesh aaye: ek victim ki tarah jise rescue karna hai, ya ek adult ki tarah jo apne faisle khud le rahi hai. Isse yeh tay nahi hota ki uska rape ho sakta hai ya nahi: dono haalat mein zabardasti kiya gaya sex rape hai. Aur 18 saal se kam umar ki ladki "sex worker" hoti hi nahi: handbook "child prostitute" ki jagah "child who has been trafficked" kehti hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Uske saath sex rape hai, woh chahe kuch bhi kahe [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur POCSO Act 18 saal se kam umar ke har bachche ko protect karta hai, ladkon ko bhi aur ladkiyon ko bhi [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Yahan ek hole hai. Section 63 sirf aurton ko protect karti hai. Sex work karne wale kisi adult aadmi ya transgender insaan ke saath zabardasti ho, toh BNS mein uske liye rape ka koi offence nahi hai, kyunki BNS ne purani Section 377 hata di aur uski jagah kuch nahi rakha [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Transgender insaan ke sexual abuse ki saza sirf chhe mahine se do saal hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

## Health, police aur 'na' kehne ka haq

2024 mein India mein female sex workers mein HIV prevalence 1.13% thi, jabki sabhi adults mein 0.20% [[naco-sankalak-2025]]. Kisi bhi rape ke baad HIV se bachane wali dawa (PEP) jitni jaldi ho sake shuru honi chahiye, aur 72 ghante ke baad nahi; yeh 28 din tak li jaati hai [[who-pep]]. Har hospital ko, sarkari ho ya private, rape survivor ka turant free ilaaj karna hoga aur police ko inform karna hoga [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo hospital in-charge ilaaj se mana kare, use ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Aurat kisi bhi police station mein rape report kar sakti hai, ghatna chahe kahin bhi hui ho, aur uski baat ek woman officer hi record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo officer rape ki FIR register na kare, use chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Agar koi police officer apni custody mein kisi aurat ka ya police station mein rape kare, toh yeh aggravated rape hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aise aggravated cases mein, jab intercourse prove ho jaaye aur aurat gawahi de ki usne consent nahi diya tha, toh court ko maanna hoga ki consent nahi tha [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. 2024 mein police ne police personnel dwara rape ke 27 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

In mein se koi bhi protection yeh nahi poochta ki aurat kaam kya karti hai. Asli gap yeh hai ki desk par baitha officer, duty par doctor aur bench par baitha judge is baat ko maante hain ya nahi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

she-asked-for-it-provocation-myth.en:
"She was wearing a short dress." "She had been drinking." "What was she doing out at that hour?" These lines turn up in family WhatsApp groups, in comments under news of a rape and, as recently as 2022, in an Indian court order. Each one moves the question away from what a man did and towards what a woman wore. Police data from 2024 make the argument hard to sustain: among the children recorded as victims of penetrative sexual assault under POCSO that year, 831 were under the age of six [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Where the provocation story comes from

The 'she asked for it' story survives because it offers two comforts. The first is control: if rape is caused by clothes, drink or late nights, then a careful woman, or a careful family, can prevent it. The second is somewhere to put the blame that is not the man, and often not the man the family knows. Both comforts are false. Blame is also a heavy reason to stay silent, and silence is the norm: in NFHS-5, 77% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The Supreme Court has named the myth. Its 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes lists, among false beliefs, the idea that a woman's clothing, drinking or smoking invites sexual contact [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. As an example, it quotes a 2022 bail order from a sessions court in Kozhikode, Kerala, which said photographs showed the complainant "exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. That was a bail order, not a verdict, and we do not name the accused. The point is that a court wrote the myth into an official order.

## What the ages of victims say

If clothes, drinks or late nights caused rape, the victims would look like the myth: young women at parties. The 2024 records do not. Of 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault recorded under POCSO, 831 were under six and 3,438 were aged 6 to 12 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Young children rarely tell anyone, so these are minimums. Boys made up 892 of the 44,567 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and the provocation story never mentions them at all.

Among the 29,742 victims recorded under the rape head, which mostly covers adults, 19,489 were women aged 18 to 30 and 89 were over 60 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Many survivors are young, as the myth expects. But youth is also when women study, start work and fall in love, and the numbers track access, not outfits. In 96.8% of rape cases registered in 2024, the offender was someone the survivor knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A cousin, a neighbour or a tutor does not need a short dress or a late night. He needs only access and trust.

> A child under six did not choose an outfit. The myth has no answer for that number.

## What the law means by consent

The law does not ask what she wore. (This is general information, not legal advice.) Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines consent as an "unequivocal voluntary agreement" to the specific sexual act, communicated by words, gestures or other communication. It adds that a woman who does not physically resist is not, for that reason alone, consenting [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The same section says consent given when a woman was too intoxicated to understand what she was agreeing to, or when she cannot communicate consent, does not count, and no girl under 18 can consent [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A drink is never an invitation, and enough of it can make real consent impossible.

Her character is not on trial either. In 2013, Parliament added Section 53A to the Indian Evidence Act (since replaced by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023), making a victim's character or previous sexual experience irrelevant to the question of consent [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Our stories on dating myths and on the 1978 custodial rape acquittal explain how these rules were won and what they mean between partners.

## Why judges were told to drop 'provocative clothing'

Words in a judgment are not decoration. They tell police, lawyers and the next judge what counts. In 2021, in Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh, the Supreme Court set aside a bail condition that required a man accused of sexual assault to ask the complainant to tie a rakhi on him. It told courts to avoid stereotypical or patriarchal notions about women, and ordered gender-sensitisation training for every judge [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. A year later, the Kozhikode order still called a dress provocative.

So in 2023 the Supreme Court went down to single words. Its handbook's glossary tells judges to write "clothing" or "dress" instead of "provocative clothing", "rape" instead of "forcible rape", and "street sexual harassment" instead of "eve teasing" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. "Provocative" puts the cause in her wardrobe. "Forcible rape" suggests that some rape is not forced. "Eve teasing" makes harassment sound like a game.

## Answering the myth when you hear it

You will hear it again: at dinner, in a group chat, under a news post. Some short answers:

- "Look at what she was wearing." The 2024 data include 831 children under six [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Clothes are not the cause.
- "She was drunk." Then the question is whether she could consent at all, and the law says consent given by a woman too intoxicated to understand what she is agreeing to does not count [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. If drink matters, look at his glass: 71% of women whose husbands often get drunk reported spousal physical or sexual violence, against 23% of women whose husbands do not drink [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That is an association, not proof that alcohol causes violence, but it points at the drinker, not at her.
- "Why was she out so late?" Most accused are not strangers on a road: in 96.8% of rape cases registered in 2024, the offender was known to the survivor [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- "She led him on." Consent is a clear yes to a specific act. A flirt, a date or a past yes is not that yes.

And if it happened to you, it was not your fault. The only person who made a choice was the one who did not wait for a yes.
she-asked-for-it-provocation-myth.hg:
"Usne short dress pehni thi." "Usne drink kar rakhi thi." "Itni raat ko woh bahar kya kar rahi thi?" Yeh lines family WhatsApp groups mein dikhti hain, rape ki news ke neeche comments mein dikhti hain, aur 2022 mein toh ek Indian court order mein bhi dikhin. Har line sawaal ko is taraf mod deti hai ki ladki ne kya pehna tha, na ki aadmi ne kya kiya. 2024 ka police data is argument ko tikne nahi deta: us saal POCSO ke tahat penetrative sexual assault ke jo child victims darj hue, unmein 831 bachche chhe saal se bhi chhote the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 'She asked for it' wali kahani aati kahan se hai

Yeh kahani isliye tiki hai kyunki isse do tarah ka comfort milta hai. Pehla, control ka: agar rape kapdon, drink ya late nights ki wajah se hota hai, toh ek careful ladki ya careful family use rok sakti hai. Doosra, blame daalne ki ek jagah jo aadmi nahi hai, aur aksar woh aadmi bhi nahi jise family jaanti hai. Dono comforts jhoothe hain. Blame ka darr chup rehne ki badi wajah bhi hai, aur chup rehna hi normal hai: NFHS-5 mein physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 77% women ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Supreme Court is myth ka naam le chuka hai. Uski 2023 ki Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes jhoothi beliefs ki list mein yeh soch bhi rakhti hai ki ek aurat ke kapde, drinking ya smoking sexual contact ko invite karte hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Example ke taur par handbook Kerala ke Kozhikode ki ek sessions court ke 2022 ke bail order ko quote karti hai, jisme likha tha ki photographs mein complainant "exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Woh bail order tha, verdict nahi, aur hum accused ka naam nahi le rahe. Asli baat yeh hai ki ek court ne yeh myth ek official order mein likh diya.

## Victims ki umar kya batati hai

Agar rape kapdon, drinks ya late nights ki wajah se hota, toh victims bhi myth jaise dikhte: party mein gayi young ladkiyan. 2024 ke records aisa nahi dikhate. POCSO ke tahat darj penetrative sexual assault ke 44,567 child victims mein se 831 chhe saal se chhote the aur 3,438 ki umar 6 se 12 saal thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Chhote bachche aksar kisi ko bata hi nahi paate, isliye yeh minimum numbers hain. In 44,567 mein 892 ladke bhi the [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur provocation wali kahani mein unka zikr tak nahi aata.

Rape head ke tahat darj 29,742 victims mein, jo zyadatar adults hain, 19,489 women 18 se 30 saal ki thin aur 89 women 60 saal se upar ki [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Haan, kai survivors young hain, jaisa myth kehta hai. Lekin yahi woh umar hai jab ladkiyan padhti hain, kaam shuru karti hain, pyaar karti hain, aur numbers outfits ko nahi, access ko follow karte hain. 2024 mein darj 96.8% rape cases mein offender survivor ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Kisi cousin, padosi ya tutor ko short dress ya late night ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Use bas access aur bharosa chahiye.

> Chhe saal se chhote bachche ne koi outfit nahi chuna tha. Is number ka myth ke paas koi jawab nahi hai.

## Law consent kise maanta hai

Law yeh nahi poochta ki ladki ne kya pehna tha. (Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.) Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 63 consent ko kisi specific sexual act ke liye ek "unequivocal voluntary agreement" kehta hai, yaani saaf aur apni marzi ki haan, jo words, gestures ya kisi aur communication se jatayi jaaye. Section yeh bhi kehta hai ki agar aurat ne physically resist nahi kiya, toh sirf is wajah se use consenting nahi maana jaayega [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yahi section us haan ko consent nahi maanta jo aurat ne itne nashe mein di ho ki use samajh hi na aaye ki woh kis cheez ke liye haan keh rahi hai, ya aisi situation ko jisme woh consent communicate hi na kar sake, aur 18 se kam umar ki koi ladki consent de hi nahi sakti [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Drink kabhi invitation nahi hai, aur zyada nasha asli consent ko impossible bana sakta hai.

Uske character par bhi trial nahi chalta. 2013 mein Parliament ne Indian Evidence Act mein Section 53A joda (yeh Act ab Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 se replace ho chuka hai), jisse consent ke sawaal par victim ka character ya uska previous sexual experience irrelevant ho gaya [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Hamari dating myths wali story aur 1978 ke custodial rape acquittal wali story batati hain ki yeh rules kaise jeete gaye aur partners ke beech inka kya matlab hai.

## Judges ko 'provocative clothing' likhna band karne ko kyun kaha gaya

Judgment ke shabd sirf decoration nahi hote. Woh police, lawyers aur agle judge ko batate hain ki kis baat ka wazan hai. 2021 mein Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh case mein Supreme Court ne ek bail condition cancel kar di, jisme sexual assault ke accused se kaha gaya tha ki woh complainant se rakhi bandhwaaye. Court ne courts se kaha ki woh aurton ke baare mein stereotypical ya patriarchal soch se bachein, aur har judge ke liye gender-sensitisation training zaroori ki [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Phir bhi ek saal baad Kozhikode ka order ek dress ko provocative bata raha tha.

Isliye 2023 mein Supreme Court single words tak gaya. Uski handbook ki glossary judges se kehti hai ki "provocative clothing" ki jagah sirf "clothing" ya "dress" likhein, "forcible rape" ki jagah "rape", aur "eve teasing" ki jagah "street sexual harassment" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. "Provocative" shabd wajah ko uski almaari mein daal deta hai. "Forcible rape" se lagta hai jaise koi rape bina force ke bhi hota hai. Aur "eve teasing" harassment ko khel jaisa bana deta hai.

## Jab koi yeh myth dohraaye, toh kya kahein

Aap yeh baat phir sunenge: dinner par, group chat mein, kisi news post ke neeche. Kuch chhote jawab:

- "Dekho usne kya pehna tha." 2024 ke data mein chhe saal se chhote 831 bachche hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Kapde wajah nahi hain.
- "Usne drink ki thi." Toh sawaal yeh hai ki kya woh consent de bhi sakti thi, aur law kehta hai ki agar aurat itne nashe mein thi ki use samajh hi nahi aa raha tha ki woh kis cheez ke liye haan keh rahi hai, toh woh haan consent nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aur agar drink ki baat karni hai, toh aadmi ka glass dekhiye: jin women ke husbands aksar nashe mein rehte hain, unmein se 71% ne spousal physical ya sexual violence report ki, jabki jinke husbands drink nahi karte, unmein yeh 23% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh ek association hai, is baat ka saboot nahi ki sharaab hi violence ki wajah hai, lekin ungli peene wale ki taraf uthti hai, ladki ki taraf nahi.
- "Woh itni raat ko bahar kyun thi?" Zyadatar accused sadak ke strangers nahi hote: 2024 mein darj 96.8% rape cases mein offender survivor ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- "Usi ne toh lead kiya tha." Consent kisi specific act ke liye clear haan hai. Flirting, ek date ya pehle kabhi di gayi haan, woh haan nahi hai.

Aur agar yeh aapke saath hua hai, toh isme aapki koi galti nahi thi. Choice sirf us insaan ne ki jisne haan ka intezaar nahi kiya.

stranger-dark-lane-rape-myth.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old in Bhopal. She must be home by 7 pm. Her younger brother has no such rule. The rule comes from love, and from one picture of rape: a stranger, a dark lane, a girl alone. That picture is real, but it is rare. When India's national family health survey asked never-married women who had faced sexual violence who did it, only 5% named a stranger [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Where the 'dark lane' picture comes from

The stranger story survives because it is comfortable. It keeps the threat outside the family, makes rape something a girl can avoid with the right timing, and turns the rapist into a monster rather than an uncle, a tutor or a boyfriend.

The gap is old. In 2012, the year of the Delhi gang rape case, police data showed the offender was known to the victim in 98.2% of rape cases [[ncrb-cii-2012-snapshots]]. In 2023, the Supreme Court's handbook for judges listed the belief that rapists are usually strangers among the false stereotypes judges should stop relying on [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

> A curfew guards the gate. Most of the time, the danger is already inside.

## Who survivors and police records actually name

NFHS-5 (2019-21) asked women directly. Among never-married women who had faced sexual violence, the most common perpetrators were relatives other than a father or brother (39%), a current or former boyfriend (16%) and a family friend (12%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The group was small, so read the shares as rough; the order is clear. Among ever-married women who had faced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband and 14% a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Police records say the same. Of 29,536 rape cases registered in 2024, the offender was known to the survivor in 28,597, or 96.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Family friends, neighbours, employers and other known persons accounted for 12,584 of them, and family members for 2,134 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Our story on exactly who the 96.8% were breaks down each group; friends and partners, the largest, are also the subject of our story on dating myths. The known share topped 90% in almost every state; the lowest, Nagaland, was still 78.6% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Child-rape cases registered under POCSO show the same pattern [[ncrb-cii-2024]], as our story on why 'stranger danger' is the wrong lesson for children explains.

Even this flatters the stranger myth. Husbands are largely missing from rape data, because Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) says sex by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]; a challenge to that exception is pending in the Supreme Court. And violence by a husband rarely reaches anyone: only 11.3% of women who faced violence solely from their current husband ever sought help, against 23.6% of those abused only by a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Streets and buses still matter

None of this makes the street safe. In the second half of 2024 alone, police registered 1,469 cases of sexual harassment in public places or pathways, and over the full year 459 cases in public transport [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Those are only complaints that reached the police. In a Jagori study of 270 women domestic workers in Delhi-NCR, surveyed in 2024, 45% felt very unsafe in the city at night, a further 17% somewhat unsafe, and 24% had faced sexual harassment in the previous two years [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]]. In 2005, 12% of households told a national survey that unmarried girls were harassed in their neighbourhood; police records implied 0.06% [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

So harassment on the road is real and badly under-counted. But the man in the dark lane is not who most survivors name. WHO's 2023 global estimates show how large the danger from partners is: 24.7% of ever-married or partnered women aged 15 and older, about 682 million, have faced physical or sexual violence from a partner [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Separately, 8.2% of all women that age, about 263 million, have faced sexual violence from someone other than a partner since the age of 15 [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]], and "someone other than a partner" still includes relatives, friends and colleagues.

## What misplaced protection costs

A curfew takes a young woman's evenings, classes, late shifts and friendships, and teaches her brother that her movements are the family's business while his are not. It also fails at its own goal.
