A 7 pm rule does nothing about a cousin who visits at 4 pm, a tutor in the living room, or a boyfriend's messages at midnight.

It costs in silence, too. If the family script says danger lives outside, a girl abused by a relative has no words for it and little hope of being believed. In NFHS-5, 77% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. And if she is attacked after dark, the rule becomes an accusation: why was she out?

The state shares the instinct. By July 2026, Safe City projects in eight cities had received Rs 1,686.73 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund, the largest of the three schemes that together took 63% of all the money released [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Those projects aim to make public places safer [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. One Stop Centres for women facing violence received Rs 1,299.10 crore [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Safer streets are worth the money. The question is whether the first rupee and the first rule go where most of the harm is.

## Safety that starts with the people we know

Real protection looks less like a curfew and more like a conversation. Tell teenagers plainly that a relative, a teacher, a boyfriend or a husband can commit sexual violence, and that it is still a crime. Keep one rule for daughters and sons about where they go and how they treat others. Teach that a partner who checks your phone, cuts you off from friends or pushes for sex after a no is showing a warning sign, not love.

Be the person someone can tell. The Supreme Court's handbook also rejects the idea that a real survivor cries non-stop or never speaks to the accused again [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. If someone tells you about abuse by a person you both know, believe them first. Keep the street in the plan too: share your live location when travelling, and call 112 in an emergency, on the road or at home.
stranger-dark-lane-rape-myth.hg:
Imagine kijiye, Bhopal mein ek 19 saal ki ladki hai. Use shaam 7 baje tak ghar pahunchna hota hai. Uske chhote bhai ke liye aisa koi rule nahi hai. Yeh rule pyaar se bana hai, aur rape ki ek tasveer se bhi: ek stranger, ek andheri gali, ek akeli ladki. Aisa hota hai, lekin bahut kam. Jab India ke National Family Health Survey ne un never-married women se poochha jinhone sexual violence jheli thi ki yeh kisne kiya, toh sirf 5% ne kisi stranger ka naam liya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 'Dark lane' wali tasveer aati kahan se hai

Stranger wali kahani isliye tiki hui hai kyunki yeh comfortable hai. Isme khatra family ke bahar rehta hai. Lagta hai ki sahi time par ghar aa gaye toh bach gaye. Aur rapist ek monster lagta hai, koi chacha, tutor ya boyfriend nahi.

Yeh gap purana hai. 2012 mein, jis saal Delhi gang rape case hua, police data ke mutabik 98.2% rape cases mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2012-snapshots]]. 2023 mein Supreme Court ne judges ke liye ek handbook nikaali. Usme is soch ko ki rapists aam taur par strangers hote hain, un jhoothe stereotypes ki list mein rakha gaya jin par judges ko bharosa karna band karna chahiye [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

> Curfew darwaaze par pehra deta hai. Zyadatar baar khatra pehle se ghar ke andar hota hai.

## Survivors aur police records asal mein kiska naam lete hain

NFHS-5 (2019-21) ne women se seedhe poochha. Jin never-married women ne sexual violence jheli, unmein sabse common perpetrators the: father ya brother ke alawa koi aur relative (39%), current ya former boyfriend (16%) aur family friend (12%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh group chhota tha, isliye in shares ko rough maaniye; order saaf hai. Jin ever-married women ne sexual violence jheli, unmein se 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya aur 14% ne former husband ka [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Police records bhi yahi kehte hain. 2024 mein rape ke 29,536 cases darj hue. Inmein se 28,597 mein, yaani 96.8% mein, offender survivor ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 12,584 cases mein accused family friend, padosi, employer ya koi aur known person tha, aur 2,134 mein family member [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh 96.8% asal mein kaun the, yeh hamari alag story har group ko kholkar batati hai; sabse bada group, friends aur partners, hamari dating myths wali story ka topic bhi hai. Lagbhag har state mein known offenders ka share 90% se upar tha; sabse kam Nagaland mein tha, phir bhi 78.6% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. POCSO ke tahat darj child-rape cases mein bhi yahi pattern hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]], jaisa hamari story batati hai ki bachchon ke liye 'stranger danger' galat lesson kyun hai.

Aur yeh numbers bhi poori sachchai nahi dikhate. Husbands rape data se lagbhag gayab hain, kyunki Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar wife 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh aadmi ka apni wife ke saath sex rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]; is exception ke khilaaf challenge Supreme Court mein pending hai. Aur husband ki violence ki baat shayad hi kisi tak pahunchti hai: jin women ne sirf apne current husband se violence jheli, unmein se sirf 11.3% ne kabhi help maangi, jabki sirf former husband se abuse jhelne wali women mein yeh share 23.6% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Sadak aur bus ka khatra bhi sach hai

Iska matlab yeh nahi ki sadak safe hai. Sirf 2024 ke second half mein police ne public places ya raaston par sexual harassment ke 1,469 cases darj kiye, aur poore saal mein public transport mein 459 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh sirf woh complaints hain jo police tak pahunchin. Jagori ki ek study mein, jiska survey 2024 mein hua, Delhi-NCR ki 270 women domestic workers mein se 45% ko raat mein shehar bahut unsafe lagta tha, 17% ko thoda unsafe, aur 24% ne pichhle do saal mein sexual harassment jhela tha [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]]. 2005 mein ek national survey mein 12% households ne kaha ki unke mohalle mein unmarried ladkiyon ko pareshaan kiya jaata hai; police records se yeh figure sirf 0.06% banta tha [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

Toh sadak par harassment sach hai, aur uski ginti bahut kam hoti hai. Lekin zyadatar survivors dark lane wale aadmi ka naam nahi lete. WHO ke 2023 ke global estimates dikhate hain ki partner se khatra kitna bada hai: 15 saal aur usse upar ki ever-married ya partnered women mein se 24.7%, yaani kareeb 682 million, partner se physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki hain [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Iske alawa, isi umar ki sabhi women mein se 8.2%, yaani kareeb 263 million, ne 15 saal ki umar ke baad partner ke alawa kisi aur se sexual violence jheli hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]], aur is 'partner ke alawa kisi aur' mein bhi relatives, friends aur colleagues shaamil hain.

## Galat jagah pehre ki keemat

Curfew ek ladki se uski shaamein, classes, late shifts aur dostiyan chheen leta hai. Uske bhai ko sikhata hai ki behen kahan jaati hai, yeh poore ghar ka mamla hai, aur woh khud kahan jaata hai, yeh kisi ka mamla nahi. Aur yeh apna hi kaam nahi karta. Shaam 7 baje ka rule us cousin ko nahi rokta jo dopahar 4 baje aata hai, na drawing room mein baithe tutor ko, na aadhi raat ko aane wale boyfriend ke messages ko.

Iski keemat chuppi bhi hai. Agar family ki script yahi hai ki khatra bahar rehta hai, toh kisi relative ke haathon abuse jhelne wali ladki ke paas kehne ko shabd hi nahi hote, aur bharosa kiye jaane ki ummeed bhi kam hoti hai. NFHS-5 mein physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 77% women ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Aur agar andhere ke baad us par attack ho jaaye, toh wahi rule ilzaam ban jaata hai: woh bahar kyun thi?

Sarkar ki soch bhi kuch aisi hi hai. July 2026 tak aath shehron ke Safe City projects ko Nirbhaya Fund se Rs 1,686.73 crore mile. Yeh un teen schemes mein sabse badi rakam thi jinhe milakar release hue kul paise ka 63% mila [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. In projects ka maksad public places ko safe banana hai [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Violence jhel rahi women ke liye bane One Stop Centres ko Rs 1,299.10 crore mile [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Safe sadkon par paisa lagana sahi hai. Sawaal yeh hai ki pehla rupaya aur pehla rule wahan jaata hai ya nahi, jahan sabse zyada nuksaan ho raha hai.

## Safety ki shuruaat jaan-pehchaan walon se

Asli protection curfew se kam aur baatcheet se zyada hota hai. Teenagers ko saaf-saaf bataiye ki relative, teacher, boyfriend ya husband bhi sexual violence kar sakta hai, aur woh bhi crime hi hai. Betiyon aur beton ke liye ek hi rule rakhiye: kahan jaana hai, aur doosron ke saath kaisa behave karna hai. Sikhaiye ki jo partner aapka phone check kare, aapko friends se door kare, ya 'no' ke baad bhi sex ke liye pressure daale, woh pyaar nahi, warning sign dikha raha hai.

Aise insaan baniye jisse koi apni baat keh sake. Supreme Court ki handbook is soch ko bhi galat batati hai ki 'asli' survivor lagataar roti rehti hai ya accused se phir kabhi baat nahi karti [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Agar koi bataye ki aap dono ke kisi jaan-pehchaan wale ne uske saath galat kiya, toh pehle uski baat par bharosa kijiye. Sadak ko bhi plan mein rakhiye: travel karte waqt apni live location kisi bharosemand insaan ke saath share kijiye, aur emergency mein 112 par call kijiye, chahe khatra sadak par ho ya ghar mein.

supreme-court-cannot-create-offence.en:
Every time a gap in India's rape law makes news, the same comment appears: why doesn't the Supreme Court just fix it? A husband who forces sex on his adult wife cannot be charged with rape. An adult man raped by another man has no rape offence to turn to. Both gaps are real. But the courts' power over them is not the same, and that difference decides whom you should be pressing.

## The question everyone asks

Consider two adults who walk into the same police station in Jaipur on the same night: a woman forced into sex by her husband, and a man sexually assaulted by another man. Neither can file a rape case today. Her situation could change through a Supreme Court judgment. His needs a new law from Parliament. To see why, look at what courts have actually done, and what they have refused to do.

## Striking down: what courts can do

Courts can test a law against the Constitution and cut out, or narrow, the part that violates rights. In 2013 Parliament raised the age of consent to 18 but left the marital rape exception, then Exception 2 to Section 375 of the IPC, at 15, so a husband's sex with a wife aged 15 to 17 was not rape. On 11 October 2017, in Independent Thought v. Union of India, the Supreme Court read the exception down: sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

On 6 September 2018, in Navtej Singh Johar, a five-judge bench unanimously read down Section 377 of the IPC. Consensual sex between adults of the same sex stopped being a crime, while non-consensual acts stayed punishable [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Notice what both judgments did. Neither invented a crime. One removed a shield that protected husbands of girls from an offence that already existed. The other took consenting adults out of an offence's reach.

Courts can also fill a vacuum, for a while. In 1997, with no law against sexual harassment at work, the Supreme Court in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan laid down binding guidelines, to be treated as law until Parliament acted [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]]. Parliament took nearly 16 years: the POSH Act was published on 23 April 2013 [[pib-law-posh-act-gazette-2013]]. The guidelines told employers how to handle complaints. They did not make anything a crime.

## Creating a crime: what they cannot

Deciding what counts as a crime, and how long a person goes to prison for it, belongs to the legislature. A judge who invented an offence would be punishing people under a law nobody voted for.

The Supreme Court said so itself. On 14 October 2024 a bench led by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud refused a plea to make sexual offences against men and transgender persons crimes under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). It said it "cannot by recourse under article 142 direct that a particular act constitutes an offence" [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. Article 142 is the court's special power to pass any order needed for complete justice in a case. Even that does not stretch to writing a crime.

The Delhi High Court has pressed the government instead. On 28 August 2024, hearing a demand to restore punishment for non-consensual "unnatural" sex, it asked the Centre to decide within six months, remarking that "there can't be a vacuum to an offence" [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. In March 2026, with still no decision, it revived the case, said "the decision is nowhere in sight" and ordered the Centre to file an affidavit within four weeks [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]]. A court can ask, remind and demand an answer. It cannot supply the answer itself.

## The marital rape case and the gap for men

The two gaps sit on different sides of that line. Marital rape is an exception problem. Exception 2 to Section 63 of the BNS says sex by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The offence exists; the exception shields husbands from it. Narrowing an exception is what the court did in 2017.

That is why the question is in court. On 11 May 2022, ruling on the same exception in the old IPC, the Delhi High Court split: Justice Rajiv Shakdher held the exception unconstitutional, while Justice C. Hari Shankar upheld it [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]]. In October 2024 the Union government opposed striking it down, arguing that calling it rape could be "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" and that other laws already give remedies [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]]. The Supreme Court will decide both whether the exception is valid and whether a husband can be prosecuted while it stands [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. As of 19 November 2026 it had not ruled, and said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

The gap for men is a missing-offence problem. The BNS dropped Section 377 and put nothing in its place [[indiacode-bns-2023]], so there is no exception to cut. Protecting men would mean writing new words into the law, not striking old ones out. Parliament was warned: on 10 November 2023 its Standing Committee on Home Affairs said dropping Section 377 would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men, transgender persons and animals unpunished, and recommended keeping it. The government did not accept it [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]].

## How citizens push courts and Parliament

Both routes are open to ordinary people. Courts usually move when someone files. The Delhi case began as a public interest petition by a lawyer [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]], and the marital rape batch includes a petition filed as recently as 24 April 2025 [[clpr-aweksha-v-union-2025]].

When the Supreme Court turned away the 2024 plea on men, it left the petitioner free to make a representation to the government [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. Anyone can do the same: write to the Home Ministry and to your MP, and ask what happened to the committee's recommendation. The best time to close a gap is before a Bill becomes law, which is exactly when that committee spoke.

Whatever the Supreme Court finally decides, Parliament keeps the power to change the law. Judges can remove a shield. Only lawmakers can build a new offence. This is general information, not legal advice.
supreme-court-cannot-create-offence.hg:
Jab bhi India ke rape law ka koi gap news banta hai, story ke neeche ek hi comment aata hai: Supreme Court ise fix kyun nahi kar deta? Koi pati apni adult biwi ke saath zabardasti sex kare, toh us par rape ka charge nahi lagta. Kisi adult aadmi ka rape koi doosra aadmi kare, toh uske liye rape ka koi offence hi nahi hai. Dono gaps real hain. Lekin in par court ki power ek jaisi nahi hai, aur yahi fark decide karta hai ki aapko pressure kis par banana chahiye.

## Sawaal jo har koi poochta hai

Sochiye, ek hi raat Jaipur ke ek hi police station mein do adults pahunchte hain: ek aurat jiske pati ne uske saath zabardasti sex kiya, aur ek aadmi jis par kisi doosre aadmi ne sexual assault kiya. Aaj dono mein se koi bhi rape case file nahi kar sakta. Aurat ki situation Supreme Court ke ek judgment se badal sakti hai. Aadmi ke liye Parliament ko naya law banana hoga. Aisa kyun hai, yeh samajhne ke liye dekhiye ki courts ne ab tak kya kiya hai, aur kis cheez se saaf mana kiya hai.

## Strike down: courts kya kar sakte hain

Courts kisi bhi law ko Constitution ke against test kar sakte hain, aur jo hissa rights todta hai use kaat sakte hain ya chhota kar sakte hain. 2013 mein Parliament ne age of consent 18 kar di, lekin marital rape exception mein, jo tab IPC ki Section 375 ka Exception 2 tha, biwi ki umar 15 hi rehne di, yaani 15 se 17 saal ki biwi ke saath pati ka sex rape nahi maana jaata tha. 11 October 2017 ko Independent Thought v. Union of India mein Supreme Court ne exception ko read down kiya: 18 saal se kam umar ki biwi ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

6 September 2018 ko Navtej Singh Johar case mein paanch judges ki bench ne ek raay se IPC ki Section 377 ko read down kiya. Do adults ke beech consensual same-sex sex crime nahi raha, jabki non-consensual acts punishable bane rahe [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]].

Dhyaan dijiye dono judgments ne kya kiya. Kisi ne bhi naya crime invent nahi kiya. Ek ne woh shield hatayi jo minor ladkiyon ke patiyon ko pehle se maujood offence se bacha rahi thi. Doosre ne consenting adults ko offence ke daayre se bahar nikaala.

Courts kuch waqt ke liye vacuum bhi bhar sakte hain. 1997 mein workplace sexual harassment ke khilaf koi law nahi tha, tab Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan mein Supreme Court ne binding guidelines banayin, jinhe tab tak law maana jaana tha jab tak Parliament kuch na kare [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]]. Parliament ko lagbhag 16 saal lage: POSH Act 23 April 2013 ko publish hua [[pib-law-posh-act-gazette-2013]]. Guidelines ne employers ko bataya ki complaints kaise handle karein. Unhone kisi cheez ko crime nahi banaya.

## Naya crime banana: courts kya nahi kar sakte

Kya crime hai, aur uske liye kitne saal ki jail hogi, yeh decide karna legislature ka kaam hai. Agar koi judge khud offence invent kar de, toh logon ko aise law ke under saza milegi jiske liye kisi ne vote hi nahi diya.

Supreme Court ne yeh khud kaha hai. 14 October 2024 ko Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ki bench ne ek plea sunne se mana kar diya, jismein maang thi ki mardon aur transgender logon ke khilaf sexual offences ko Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) mein crime banaya jaaye. Court ne kaha ki woh "cannot by recourse under article 142 direct that a particular act constitutes an offence" [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. Article 142 court ki special power hai jisse woh kisi case mein complete justice ke liye zaroori koi bhi order de sakta hai. Woh power bhi naya crime likhne tak nahi jaati.

Delhi High Court ne iske bajaye government par dabaav banaya. 28 August 2024 ko, non-consensual "unnatural" sex ki saza wapas laane ki maang sunte hue, usne Centre se chhe mahine mein decide karne ko kaha, aur remark kiya ki "there can't be a vacuum to an offence" [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. March 2026 mein, lagbhag dedh saal tak koi decision na hone par, court ne case phir khola, kaha ki "the decision is nowhere in sight", aur Centre ko chaar hafte mein affidavit file karne ka order diya [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]]. Court pooch sakta hai, yaad dila sakta hai, jawab maang sakta hai. Lekin jawab khud nahi likh sakta.

## Marital rape case aur mardon wala gap

Yeh do gaps us line ke alag-alag taraf hain. Marital rape ek exception problem hai. BNS ki Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar biwi 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh pati ka uske saath sex rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Offence exist karta hai; exception bas patiyon ko usse bachata hai. Aur exception kaatna wahi kaam hai jo court 2017 mein kar chuka hai.

Isiliye yeh sawaal court mein hai. 11 May 2022 ko, purane IPC wale isi exception par, Delhi High Court ka verdict split ho gaya: Justice Rajiv Shakdher ne exception ko unconstitutional kaha, jabki Justice C. Hari Shankar ne use sahi thehraya [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]]. October 2024 mein Union government ne ise hataane ka virodh kiya, yeh kehkar ki ise rape kehna "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" ho sakta hai aur doosre laws pehle se remedy dete hain [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]]. Supreme Court do baatein decide karega: kya exception valid hai, aur kya exception ke rehte pati par prosecution chal sakta hai [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. 19 November 2026 tak court ne faisla nahi diya tha, aur kaha tha ki final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko rakhi jaayegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

Mardon wala gap ek missing-offence problem hai. BNS ne Section 377 hata di aur uski jagah kuch nahi rakha [[indiacode-bns-2023]], toh yahan koi exception hi nahi hai jise kaata jaaye. Mardon ko protect karne ke liye law mein naye words likhne honge, purane words hatane se kaam nahi chalega. Parliament ko warn kiya gaya tha: 10 November 2023 ko Home Affairs ki Standing Committee ne kaha ki Section 377 hatane se mardon, transgender logon aur animals ke khilaf non-consensual sexual offences bina saza ke reh jaayenge, aur ise rakhne ki recommendation di. Government ne yeh recommendation nahi maani [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]].

## Citizens courts aur Parliament par pressure kaise banayein

Dono raaste aam logon ke liye khule hain. Court aam taur par tab move karta hai jab koi case file karta hai. Delhi wala case ek lawyer ki public interest petition se shuru hua tha [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]], aur marital rape wale batch mein ek petition toh 24 April 2025 ko hi file hui hai [[clpr-aweksha-v-union-2025]].

Jab 2024 mein Supreme Court ne mardon wali plea lautayi, toh petitioner ko government ke saamne representation dene ki chhoot di [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. Yahi koi bhi kar sakta hai: Home Ministry aur apne MP ko likhiye, aur poochiye ki committee ki recommendation ka kya hua. Kisi gap ko band karne ka sabse achha waqt tab hai jab Bill abhi law nahi bana, aur committee ne theek usi waqt warning di thi.

Supreme Court aakhir mein jo bhi decide kare, law badalne ki power Parliament ke paas rehti hai. Judges shield hata sakte hain. Naya offence sirf lawmakers bana sakte hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

theres-a-law-for-that-myth.en:
Imagine a family WhatsApp group in Kanpur. Someone forwards a news report about a young bride's death and a dowry case against her in-laws. An uncle replies that dowry has been illegal for decades: "There's a law for that." The chat moves on to a wedding invitation.

He is right about the statute book. India has had a dowry law since 1961, a law against sex selection since 1994, a domestic violence law since 2005 and its current child marriage law since 2006. He assumes that a law, once passed, is at work. The 2024 records test that. Across India, 209 cases under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ended in conviction that year, against 625 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## The comfort of a law on paper

A law protects someone only when three things happen in a row: a case is registered, it is investigated, and a court decides it. "There's a law for that" skips all three.

We followed four laws through the National Crime Records Bureau's (NCRB) 2024 tables. Each stalls at a different point.

| Law | Police cases, 2024 | In court, 2024 |
|---|---|---|
| Domestic Violence Act, 2005 | 616 | 22 convictions; 3,912 pending |
| Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 | 12,343 | 17.4% conviction rate; 83,298 pending |
| Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 | 1,499 | 209 convictions, 625 acquittals |
| PC-PNDT Act, 1994 (sex selection) | 31 | Often court complaints, which police counts can miss |

The NCRB counts cases that reached the police, not what happens in homes [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And this article is general information, not legal advice.

## The Domestic Violence Act: a civil law in a criminal count

Police registered 616 cases under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act in 2024, 496 of them in Kerala [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In the provisional NFHS-6 survey of 2023-24, 22.3% of ever-married women aged 18 to 49 reported physical or sexual violence by a husband [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

The tiny number is partly a misreading. The 2005 Act is mainly a civil law: a woman asks a magistrate for a protection, residence or maintenance order. Its only crimes are breaching a protection order and a Protection Officer failing in his duty, each punishable with at most one year in prison or a Rs 20,000 fine [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. So 616 counts breaches that reached the police, not women the Act helped. Applications to magistrates are not in the crime data at all.

Breaches that did become criminal cases joined a queue. Courts had 4,017 such cases before them in 2024, completed 84 trials and convicted in 22; 3,912 cases, or 97.4%, were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The order protects; the punishment for ignoring it is small and slow.

> A statute is a promise. A registered case, an investigation and a verdict are the delivery.

## Dowry and child marriage: from FIR to verdict

The dowry law looks severe: giving, taking or abetting dowry carries at least five years in prison and a fine of at least Rs 15,000 or the value of the dowry, whichever is more [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Police registered 12,343 cases under it in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The first stall is registration. Uttar Pradesh (4,482), Bihar (3,780) and Karnataka (1,991) accounted for most of those cases, while West Bengal registered none and Maharashtra 12 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That reflects police practice, not an absence of dowry. The second stall is the courtroom: 17.4% of the cases decided in 2024 ended in conviction, and 83,298 were pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Child marriage stalls earlier still. In NFHS-6, 20.1% of women aged 20 to 24 said they were married before 18 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Police registered 1,499 cases in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The year before it was 6,038, of which Assam alone accounted for 5,267 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Registrations track police drives, not how many children were married.

The law itself is light. The maximum sentence is two years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs 1 lakh, with no mandatory minimum, a gap the Supreme Court said in October 2024 had led to ineffective enforcement [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. The 209 convictions and 625 acquittals of 2024 made a conviction rate of 25.0%, with 8,553 cases pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Sex selection: the cases police barely register

The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PC-PNDT) Act bans sex selection and the misuse of prenatal tests to find out a foetus's sex [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Police registered 31 cases under it in 2024, and 30 in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The design of the law explains part of the number. A court can take up a case only on a complaint from the district's Appropriate Authority, an officer it authorises, or a person or organisation that has given the authority at least 15 days' notice [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. So prosecutions tend to begin as court complaints by health officials, which police counts can miss. In practice the law moves mostly when an official acts, against an offence the family and the clinic both want kept quiet.

The result is easier to see than the enforcement: India's sex ratio at birth was 918 girls per 1,000 boys in 2022-24 [[srs-statistical-report-2024]]. Nature produces about 105 boys for every 100 girls [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]], so a ratio of 918 means girls are still missing at birth.

## Using the laws that do work

None of this makes the laws useless. It means knowing which part of each one a person can actually use.

For violence at home, the tool to reach for is the civil one. Ask a magistrate for a protection order, and report any breach to the police, because the breach is itself a crime [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. The Women Helpline and One Stop Centres are places to start; 985 of the 1,033 approved centres were operational in July 2026 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

For a child marriage, act before the wedding: call Child Helpline 1098 or 112 with the place and date. Someone married as a child can ask a district court to annul the marriage until two years after reaching adulthood [[indiacode-pcma-2006]].

For dowry, a demand alone is an offence, punishable with six months to two years in prison [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]], so keep messages, gift lists and bank transfers. For sex selection, the law presumes a pregnant woman was compelled by her husband or relatives, and does not punish a woman who was forced [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

So when someone says there's a law for that, ask the next question: how many cases did it register, and how many reached a verdict?
theres-a-law-for-that-myth.hg:
Imagine kijiye, Kanpur ka ek family WhatsApp group. Koi ek news report forward karta hai: ek nayi dulhan ki maut, aur sasuraal walon par dowry case. Ek uncle reply karte hain ki dowry toh dashakon se illegal hai: "Iske liye toh law hai." Chat aage badh jaati hai, kisi shaadi ke invitation par.

Statute book ke hisaab se woh sahi hain. India mein dowry law 1961 se hai, sex selection ke khilaf law 1994 se, domestic violence law 2005 se aur current child marriage law 2006 se. Woh yeh maan kar chal rahe hain ki law ek baar pass ho gaya toh kaam bhi kar raha hai. 2024 ke records is baat ko test karte hain. Us saal poore India mein Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ke tahat 209 cases conviction par khatm hue, aur 625 acquittal par [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Kaagaz par likhe law ka sukoon

Law kisi ko tabhi bachata hai jab teen cheezein ek ke baad ek hon: case darj ho, uski investigation ho, aur court us par faisla de. "Iske liye toh law hai" in teeno ko skip kar deta hai.

Humne National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ki 2024 ki tables mein chaar laws ko follow kiya. Har ek alag jagah atakta hai.

| Law | Police cases, 2024 | Court mein, 2024 |
|---|---|---|
| Domestic Violence Act, 2005 | 616 | 22 convictions; 3,912 pending |
| Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 | 12,343 | 17.4% conviction rate; 83,298 pending |
| Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 | 1,499 | 209 convictions, 625 acquittals |
| PC-PNDT Act, 1994 (sex selection) | 31 | Aksar court complaints, jo police ki ginti mein chhoot sakti hain |

NCRB sirf woh cases ginta hai jo police tak pahunche, woh nahi jo gharon ke andar hota hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur yeh article general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Domestic Violence Act: civil law, jise criminal ginti se naapa jaata hai

2024 mein police ne Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act ke tahat 616 cases darj kiye, jinmein se 496 Kerala ke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Doosri taraf, 2023-24 ke provisional NFHS-6 survey mein 18 se 49 saal ki 22.3% ever-married women ne bataya ki unhone husband ki physical ya sexual violence jheli hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Yeh chhota sa number kuch had tak galat padha jaata hai. 2005 ka Act mainly ek civil law hai: woman magistrate se protection, residence ya maintenance order maangti hai. Is Act mein sirf do crimes hain: protection order todna, aur Protection Officer ka apni duty na nibhana. Dono ki saza zyada se zyada ek saal ki jail ya Rs 20,000 ka fine hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Yaani 616 un breaches ki ginti hai jo police tak pahunche, un women ki nahi jinhe Act se madad mili. Magistrates ke paas di gayi applications crime data mein hain hi nahi.

Jo breaches criminal case bane, woh line mein lag gaye. 2024 mein courts ke saamne aise 4,017 cases the. 84 mein trial poora hua aur 22 mein conviction hui; saal ke end mein 3,912 cases, yaani 97.4%, pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Order protection deta hai; use todne ki saza chhoti hai aur der se milti hai.

> Statute ek vaada hai. Darj hua case, investigation aur verdict us vaade ki delivery hain.

## Dowry aur child marriage: FIR se verdict tak

Dowry law dekhne mein sakht hai: dowry dene, lene ya usme madad karne par kam se kam paanch saal ki jail hai, aur kam se kam Rs 15,000 ya dowry ki value ke barabar fine, jo bhi zyada ho [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. 2024 mein police ne iske tahat 12,343 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Pehli rukaavat registration hai. In cases mein se zyadatar Uttar Pradesh (4,482), Bihar (3,780) aur Karnataka (1,991) ke the, jabki West Bengal mein ek bhi case darj nahi hua aur Maharashtra mein 12 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh police ke kaam karne ka tareeka dikhata hai, yeh nahi ki wahan dowry nahi hai. Doosri rukaavat courtroom hai: 2024 mein decide hue cases mein se 17.4% conviction par khatm hue, aur saal ke end mein 83,298 pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Child marriage isse bhi pehle atak jaati hai. NFHS-6 mein 20 se 24 saal ki 20.1% women ne bataya ki unki shaadi 18 se pehle ho gayi thi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. 2024 mein police ne 1,499 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usse pichhle saal yeh number 6,038 tha, jismein se 5,267 akele Assam ke the [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Registrations police drives ke saath upar-neeche hote hain, is baat ke saath nahi ki kitne bachchon ki shaadi hui.

Law khud bhi halka hai. Maximum saza do saal ki rigorous imprisonment aur Rs 1 lakh ka fine hai, aur koi mandatory minimum nahi hai. October 2024 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki isi kami ki wajah se enforcement ineffective raha hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. 2024 ke 209 convictions aur 625 acquittals se conviction rate 25.0% bana, aur 8,553 cases pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Sex selection: woh cases jo police lagbhag darj hi nahi karti

Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PC-PNDT) Act sex selection par ban lagata hai, aur foetus ka sex jaanne ke liye prenatal tests ke misuse par bhi [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Police ne iske tahat 2024 mein 31 cases darj kiye, aur 2023 mein 30 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Is number ki kuch wajah law ke design mein hai. Court tabhi case le sakta hai jab complaint district ki Appropriate Authority kare, ya uska authorised officer, ya koi aisa insaan ya organisation jisne authority ko kam se kam 15 din ka notice diya ho [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Isliye prosecutions aksar health officials ki court complaints se shuru hote hain, jo police ki ginti mein chhoot sakti hain. Practically, law zyadatar tabhi hilta hai jab koi official action le, ek aise offence par jise family aur clinic dono chhupana chahte hain.

Enforcement ke muqable nateeja zyada aasaani se dikhta hai: 2022-24 mein India ka sex ratio at birth har 1,000 ladkon par 918 ladkiyan tha [[srs-statistical-report-2024]]. Natural taur par har 100 ladkiyon par lagbhag 105 ladke paida hote hain [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]], isliye 918 ka matlab hai ki birth ke waqt ladkiyan ab bhi gayab hain.

## Un laws ka istemaal jo kaam karte hain

Iska matlab yeh nahi ki yeh laws bekaar hain. Matlab yeh hai ki pata hona chahiye, har law ka kaun sa hissa sach mein istemaal ho sakta hai.

Ghar ki violence ke liye civil raasta pakadiye. Magistrate se protection order maangiye, aur order tode jaane par police ko report kijiye, kyunki order todna khud ek crime hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Shuruaat Women Helpline ya One Stop Centre se ho sakti hai; July 2026 mein 1,033 approved centres mein se 985 chal rahe the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

Child marriage ke case mein shaadi se pehle action lijiye: jagah aur date ke saath Child Helpline 1098 ya 112 par call kijiye. Jiski shaadi bachpan mein hui, woh adult hone ke do saal baad tak district court se shaadi annul karwane ki petition de sakta hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]].

Dowry mein sirf demand karna bhi offence hai, jiski saza chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]], isliye messages, gifts ki list aur bank transfers sambhaal kar rakhiye. Sex selection mein law yeh maan kar chalta hai ki pregnant woman ko husband ya relatives ne majboor kiya, aur jis woman ko force kiya gaya use saza nahi deta [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

Toh agli baar koi kahe ki iske liye toh law hai, toh agla sawaal poochhiye: us law ke tahat kitne cases darj hue, aur kitne verdict tak pahunche?

violence-against-women-trend-misread.en:
Two headlines can be written from the World Health Organization's own reports, and both would mislead. The first: "Violence against women rises to 840 million." The second: "Partner violence in India falls from 35% to 29.9%." One reads like a crisis spreading, the other like progress. WHO says neither comparison holds. Here is why, and how to read such numbers.

## Two headlines, one mistake

In March 2021, WHO estimated that about 736 million women, roughly 1 in 3, had been subjected to physical or sexual violence by a partner, or sexual violence by someone else, using data from 2000 to 2018 [[who-vaw-estimates-2021]]. Its next estimates, published in 2025, put the figure for 2023 at about 840 million women aged 15 and older, or 30.4% of all women that age [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

The mistake in both headlines is the same: treating two separate estimates as two points on one line.

Notice also the kind of number. 736 million and 840 million are counts. A count can grow simply because there are more women in the world. The share is what tells you how common violence is, and both rounds describe roughly one woman in three.

## Why WHO's rounds cannot be compared

WHO says it plainly: because of changes in methods and data, its 2023 estimates are not comparable with its 2018 and 2010 estimates, and differences between the rounds should not be read as a trend [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

These are modelled estimates: WHO pools surveys of different years and kinds and runs them through a statistical model. Change the surveys or the model, and the outputs move.

The surveys themselves differ. WHO notes that dedicated violence surveys draw more disclosure than short violence modules inside broader health surveys, the kind India's National Family Health Survey (NFHS) uses [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. It also says women in more gender-equal societies are more likely to disclose sexual violence, while in places with high stigma and few services, the true level of sexual violence by non-partners is likely much higher than the estimates show [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

So a figure can move because violence changed, because women told surveyors more or less, or because different surveys were used. A raw comparison between two rounds cannot tell these apart.

## India: 35%, then 29.9%

WHO's 2018 round put lifetime physical or sexual violence by a partner, among ever-married or partnered Indian women aged 15-49, at 35%, and violence in the past year at 18% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2021]]. The 2023 model gives 29.9% for lifetime and 22.4% for the past year [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Read carelessly, India improved on one measure and got worse on the other. Our story on India and its South Asian neighbours already warns against both readings. Here is the arithmetic behind that warning.

Look at the ranges WHO prints beside each estimate. The 2018 lifetime figure of 35% came with an uncertainty interval of 23% to 47% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2021]]. The 2023 figure of 29.9% has an interval of 24.4% to 36.4% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. The newer range sits entirely inside the older one. Even with identical methods, an estimate that could plausibly lie anywhere between 23% and 47% cannot show a change of about five points.

These are also model outputs, so they will not match India's own survey exactly [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. NFHS, comparing its own rounds, found ever-married women aged 18-49 who had faced spousal physical or sexual violence moving only from 31% in 2015-16 to 29% in 2019-21 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Our story on NFHS-6 examines why its much sharper reported fall has drawn doubts.

## The trend WHO does report: 0.2% a year

WHO does estimate a trend, using its own model across two decades of data, and the answer is bleak. Partner violence against women has declined by only about 0.2% a year on average over the past 20 years, and the "one in three" figure has stagnated [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]]. At that pace, WHO says, the global goal of ending violence against women and girls by 2030 is very unlikely to be met [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]].

That is the real headline. Not "exploding", not "improving": almost flat.

For the present, the past-year figure matters more than any lifetime total. A lifetime figure carries every older woman's past, so it moves slowly by design. A past-year figure is a snapshot. At least 316 million women worldwide faced partner violence in the 12 months before they were surveyed [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Now set India against the world. Globally, among ever-partnered women aged 15-49, 25.8% have faced partner violence in their lifetime and 13.7% in the past year, roughly half [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. In India the figures are 29.9% and 22.4% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Since past-year cases sit inside the lifetime total, most Indian women in that lifetime figure are not describing an old memory. For them, the violence is recent, or still going on.

## How to read the next big number

1. **Count or share?** A count can grow with the population. Compare shares.
2. **Same source, same method?** Two rounds of a model, or two different surveys, are not a trend unless their makers say so.
3. **Lifetime or past year?** Lifetime moves slowly. The past-year figure tells you about now.
4. **Who was counted?** The 840 million covers all women aged 15 and older, and sexual violence by non-partners as well as partner violence; India's 29.9% covers partner violence against ever-married or partnered women aged 15-49. Different groups, different questions.
5. **How wide is the range?** An estimate with a wide uncertainty interval cannot prove a small change.
6. **Who never told?** Every survey depends on disclosure, and where stigma is high, the true level is likely higher than the estimate.

The honest message from WHO's latest numbers is neither panic nor relief. It is that partner violence against women has barely moved in 20 years, and that in India, most partnered women who have ever faced it from a husband or partner faced it in the past 12 months.
violence-against-women-trend-misread.hg:
World Health Organization ki apni reports se do headlines likhi ja sakti hain, aur dono mislead karengi. Pehli: "Aurton ke khilaaf violence badh kar 840 million tak pahuncha." Doosri: "India mein partner violence 35% se gir kar 29.9% hua." Ek lagti hai jaise crisis phail raha hai, doosri jaise progress ho rahi hai. WHO kehta hai ki dono mein se koi bhi comparison tikta nahi. Yeh rahi wajah, aur aise numbers padhne ka tareeka.

## Do headlines, ek hi galti

March 2021 mein WHO ne estimate kiya ki lagbhag 736 million aurtein, yaani roughly 3 mein se 1, kisi partner ki physical ya sexual violence, ya kisi aur ki sexual violence jhel chuki thi; is estimate mein 2000 se 2018 tak ka data use hua [[who-vaw-estimates-2021]]. 2025 mein chhape agle estimates ne 2023 ke liye yeh figure lagbhag 840 million bataya: 15 saal aur usse badi umar ki aurtein, yaani us umar ki saari aurton ka 30.4% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Dono headlines mein galti ek hi hai: do alag estimates ko ek hi line ke do points maan lena.

Number kis type ka hai, yeh bhi dekhiye. 736 million aur 840 million counts hain. Count sirf isliye bhi badh sakta hai kyunki duniya mein aurtein pehle se zyada hain. Violence kitna common hai, yeh share batata hai, aur dono rounds lagbhag teen mein se ek aurat ki baat karte hain.

## WHO ke rounds compare kyun nahi ho sakte

WHO yeh saaf-saaf kehta hai: methods aur data badalne ki wajah se uske 2023 ke estimates 2018 aur 2010 ke estimates se comparable nahi hain, aur rounds ke beech ke farq ko trend ki tarah nahi padhna chahiye [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Yeh modelled estimates hain: WHO alag-alag saalon aur alag-alag type ke surveys ko ikattha karta hai, aur unhe ek statistical model se guzaarta hai. Surveys badliye ya model, output bhi hilega.

Surveys khud bhi ek jaise nahi hote. WHO note karta hai ki sirf violence par bane surveys mein aurtein zyada batati hain, jabki broader health surveys ke andar ke chhote violence modules mein kam; India ka National Family Health Survey (NFHS) isi doosri type ka module use karta hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. WHO yeh bhi kehta hai ki zyada gender-equal samaj mein aurtein sexual violence ke baare mein zyada batati hain, jabki jahan stigma zyada hai aur services kam, wahan non-partners ki sexual violence ka asli level estimates se kahin zyada hone ka chance hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Toh koi figure isliye hil sakta hai kyunki violence badla, kyunki aurton ne surveyors ko zyada ya kam bataya, ya kyunki alag surveys use hue. Do rounds ka seedha comparison in teeno mein farq nahi kar sakta.

## India: 35%, phir 29.9%

WHO ke 2018 round ne India mein 15-49 saal ki ever-married ya partnered aurton ke liye partner ki lifetime physical ya sexual violence 35% batayi thi, aur pichhle saal ki violence 18% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2021]]. 2023 ka model lifetime ke liye 29.9% aur pichhle saal ke liye 22.4% deta hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Bina dhyaan se padhein toh lagega ki India ek measure par sudhra aur doosre par bigda. India aur uske South Asian padosiyon par hamari story pehle hi dono readings ke khilaaf warning deti hai. Yeh rahi us warning ke peeche ki arithmetic.

Har estimate ke saath WHO jo range chhaapta hai, use dekhiye. 2018 ke 35% lifetime figure ka uncertainty interval 23% se 47% tha [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2021]]. 2023 ke 29.9% ka interval 24.4% se 36.4% hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Nayi range poori ki poori purani range ke andar baithti hai. Methods bilkul same hote, tab bhi jo estimate 23% se 47% ke beech kahin bhi ho sakta hai, woh lagbhag paanch points ka badlaav nahi dikha sakta.

Yeh bhi model ke outputs hain, isliye yeh India ke apne survey se bilkul match nahi karenge [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. NFHS ne apne hi rounds compare kiye, toh pati ki physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 18-49 saal ki ever-married aurton ka share 2015-16 ke 31% se 2019-21 mein sirf 29% par aaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. NFHS-6 par hamari story dekhti hai ki uski kahin tez reported girawat par sawaal kyun uthe hain.

## WHO jo trend batata hai: saal ka 0.2%

WHO trend ka estimate bhi karta hai, do dashakon ke data par apne model se, aur jawab bahut maayoos karne wala hai. Pichhle 20 saalon mein aurton ke khilaaf partner violence average mein saal ka sirf lagbhag 0.2% ghata hai, aur 'teen mein se ek' wala figure wahin atka hua hai [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]]. WHO kehta hai ki is raftaar se 2030 tak aurton aur ladkiyon ke khilaaf violence khatam karne ka global goal poora hone ki ummeed bahut kam hai [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]].

Asli headline yahi hai. Na "violence explode ho raha hai", na "sab sudhar raha hai": lagbhag flat.

Aaj ki tasveer samajhne ke liye pichhle saal wala figure kisi bhi lifetime total se zyada maayne rakhta hai. Lifetime figure mein har badi umar ki aurat ka past bhi shaamil hota hai, isliye woh design se hi dheere hilta hai. Pichhle saal wala figure ek snapshot hai. Survey se pehle ke 12 mahinon mein duniya bhar mein kam se kam 316 million aurton ne partner violence jhela [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Ab India ko duniya ke saamne rakhiye. Duniya bhar mein 15-49 saal ki ever-partnered aurton mein se 25.8% ne zindagi mein kabhi partner violence jhela hai, aur 13.7% ne pichhle saal, yaani lifetime figure ka lagbhag aadha [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. India mein yeh figures 29.9% aur 22.4% hain [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Kyunki pichhle saal ke cases lifetime total ke andar hi aate hain, us lifetime figure ki zyada tar Indian aurtein koi purani yaad nahi bata rahi. Unke liye violence haal hi ka hai, ya abhi bhi chal raha hai.

## Agla bada number kaise padhein

1. **Count hai ya share?** Count population ke saath badh sakta hai. Share compare kijiye.
2. **Same source, same method?** Ek model ke do rounds, ya do alag surveys, tab tak trend nahi hain jab tak unhe banane wale khud aisa na kahein.
3. **Lifetime ya pichhla saal?** Lifetime figure dheere hilta hai. Pichhle saal ka figure abhi ke baare mein batata hai.
4. **Kise gina gaya?** 840 million mein 15 saal aur usse badi umar ki saari aurtein hain, aur partner violence ke saath non-partners ki sexual violence bhi; India ka 29.9% sirf 15-49 saal ki ever-married ya partnered aurton ke khilaaf partner violence ko cover karta hai. Alag groups, alag sawaal.
5. **Range kitni chaudi hai?** Jis estimate ka uncertainty interval chauda ho, woh chhota badlaav saabit nahi kar sakta.
6. **Kisne kabhi bataya hi nahi?** Har survey is par tika hai ki aurtein batayein, aur jahan stigma zyada hai, wahan asli level estimate se zyada hone ka chance hai.

WHO ke latest numbers ka honest message na panic hai, na rahat. Message yeh hai ki aurton ke khilaaf partner violence 20 saal mein mushkil se hila hai, aur India mein jin partnered aurton ne kabhi pati ya partner ki violence jheli hai, unmein se zyada tar ne ise pichhle 12 mahinon mein jhela.

virginity-myth-child-marriage-honour-con.en:
Virginity sounds like a fact about the body. It is not. No examination can tell whether a woman has had sex, and India's highest court has said so in plain words. What the idea really measures is control: who decides when a girl marries, whom she marries, and whether she is believed when she reports rape. Follow the word 'purity' and it leads to three places at once: the examination room, the early wedding and the 'honour' killing.

## What the body can and cannot show

The hymen cannot show whether someone has had sex. In 2013 the Supreme Court held that the 'two-finger test' on rape survivors violates their right to privacy, physical and mental integrity and dignity [[barandbench-lillu-2013]]. On 31 October 2022, in State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai, it went further. The test, it said, 'has no scientific basis and neither proves nor disproves allegations of rape', and anyone who conducts it in breach of the court's directions 'shall be guilty of misconduct' [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. It told governments to review medical curricula so that the test is not prescribed.

The court had to return to the subject nine years after its first ruling, and it ordered the Health Ministry's 2014 guidelines circulated to every government and private hospital [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. A family that asks for proof of a daughter's virginity is asking for a test that does not exist. Our guide to the medical exam after rape explains what a survivor can refuse.

## 'Purity' as family property

If no test can measure purity, why does the idea survive? Because it was never about the body. It treats a daughter's sexuality as something her family owns and can lose. A rape becomes the family's disgrace. A love marriage becomes a theft.

The Supreme Court has rejected this logic in so many words. Its 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes tells judges [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]:

> 'Rape does not taint the honour of the survivor / victim or her family. The marriage of the rapist to the survivor / victim does not restore honour... Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape.'

Once purity is treated as property, three things follow. Families protect it by marrying girls early. They defend it by punishing the choices of adult daughters. And institutions test it when a woman reports a crime.

## Married early to stay 'safe'

Consider a hypothetical. A 16-year-old in a district town is seen talking to a classmate after tuition. Within weeks, relatives fix a match 'before anything happens'. Nobody in the family calls this violence. They call it protection.

That logic still reaches a fifth of India's young women. In NFHS-6 (2023-24), 20.1% of women aged 20-24 had been married before 18: 23.3% in rural areas and 11.4% in urban areas [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. The share has fallen from 47.4% in 2005-06, but the fall slowed after 2015-16 [[ceda-genderstats-underage-marriage-2021]].

An early marriage does not make a girl safe. UNICEF notes that girls who marry before 18 are more likely to face domestic violence and less likely to stay in school [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. Since 2017, sex with a wife under 18 has been rape in Indian law [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. In October 2024 the Supreme Court urged Parliament to consider outlawing child betrothals, saying that marriages fixed in childhood violate a child's 'free choice, autonomy, agency and childhood' [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

## When choosing a partner becomes dangerous

The same idea follows women into adulthood. When a daughter picks her own partner, especially from another caste, some families treat it as an attack on their 'honour'. In June 2026, hearing a bail plea in a 2025 killing, a Madras High Court judge observed that Tamil Nadu had seen 59 honour killings over the past ten years and blamed 'deep-rooted casteism' [[livelaw-madras-hc-honour-killings-2026]].

Police data barely sees this. NCRB recorded no honour killings in Tamil Nadu from 2020 to 2023, and one in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Nationally, the count has stayed between 18 and 38 a year since 2020, with 36 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. There is no separate offence of honour killing, and such murders are widely believed to be logged under other motives; 'love affairs' alone accounted for 1,391 murders in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The law is clear about whose decision a marriage is. In Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018), the Supreme Court held that the right to choose a life partner is a facet of individual liberty, and ordered preventive, remedial and punitive measures to protect couples [[barandbench-shakti-vahini-madras-pil-2021]]. Enforcement lags. In December 2025 the Delhi High Court was told that no fast-track courts for honour-killing cases had been set up in Delhi, more than seven years later [[barandbench-honour-killing-fast-track-2025]]. The Law Commission proposed a special law against such interference in August 2012 [[livelaw-honour-killing-amicus-2018]]; the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita of 2023 still has no separate offence of honour killing. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Letting go of the myth

Letting go of the virginity myth does not mean caring less about daughters. It means moving the worry from her 'purity' to the things that actually protect her: her schooling, her age at marriage, her right to say no and her right to choose.

The courts have done much of their part. The two-finger test is misconduct, sex with a wife under 18 is rape, and choosing a partner is a matter of individual liberty. What no judgment can change on its own is the belief that a girl's body belongs to her family's reputation. That belief changes at home: in what parents ask before a wedding, in how they react to a daughter's phone call, and in whether they stand with her when she chooses.
virginity-myth-child-marriage-honour-con.hg:
Virginity sunne mein body ki koi baat lagti hai. Par aisa nahi hai. Koi examination yeh nahi bata sakta ki kisi aurat ne sex kiya hai ya nahi, aur desh ki sabse badi court yeh saaf shabdon mein keh chuki hai. Asli mein yeh soch control ko naapti hai: ladki ki shaadi kab hogi, kisse hogi, aur rape report karne par uski baat maani jayegi ya nahi, yeh kaun decide karega. "Purity" shabd ke peeche chaliye, toh yeh ek saath teen jagah le jaata hai: examination room, jaldi ki shaadi, aur "honour" ke naam par murder.

## Body kya bata sakti hai, aur kya nahi

Hymen se yeh pata nahi chal sakta ki kisi ne sex kiya hai ya nahi. 2013 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki rape survivors par kiya jaane wala "two-finger test" unke privacy, physical aur mental integrity aur dignity ke right ke khilaf hai [[barandbench-lillu-2013]]. 31 October 2022 ko State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai case mein court aur aage gaya. Court ne kaha ki is test ka "no scientific basis" hai, yaani koi scientific aadhaar nahi, aur yeh rape ke allegation ko na sahi saabit karta hai na galat. Jo bhi court ke directions tod kar yeh test karega, woh "misconduct" ka doshi hoga [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. Court ne governments se yeh bhi kaha ki medical curriculum review karein, taaki yeh test kahin prescribe na ho.

Pehle faisle ke nau saal baad court ko is test par phir se bolna pada, aur usne order diya ki Health Ministry ki 2014 ki guidelines har government aur private hospital tak pahunchayi jaayein [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. Jo family beti ki virginity ka saboot maangti hai, woh aisa test maang rahi hai jo exist hi nahi karta. Rape ke baad medical exam mein survivor kin cheezon se mana kar sakti hai, yeh hamari guide mein hai.

## "Purity" family ki property

Agar koi test purity naap hi nahi sakta, toh yeh soch bachi kyun hai? Kyunki yeh kabhi body ke baare mein thi hi nahi. Yeh soch beti ki sexuality ko aisi cheez maanti hai jo family ki hai aur kho sakti hai. Phir rape family ki "badnaami" ban jaata hai, aur apni pasand ki shaadi "chori".

Supreme Court is soch ko saaf shabdon mein reject kar chuka hai. Apni 2023 ki "Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes" mein court judges se kehta hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]:

> "Rape does not taint the honour of the survivor / victim or her family. The marriage of the rapist to the survivor / victim does not restore honour... Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape." Yaani rape se survivor ya uski family ki izzat par daag nahi lagta, rapist se shaadi karwane se izzat wapas nahi aati, aur shaadi rape ki violence ka ilaaj nahi hai.

Jab purity ko property maan liya jaata hai, toh teen cheezein apne aap hoti hain. Families use bachane ke liye ladkiyon ki jaldi shaadi kar deti hain. Adult betiyon ki choices ko saza dekar uski "raksha" karti hain. Aur jab koi aurat crime report karti hai, toh institutions usi ko "test" karte hain.

## "Safe" rakhne ke liye jaldi shaadi

Ek hypothetical lijiye. Kisi chhote shehar mein 16 saal ki ek ladki tuition ke baad ek classmate se baat karti dikh jaati hai. Kuch hi hafton mein relatives uska rishta pakka kar dete hain, "kuch hone se pehle". Family mein koi ise violence nahi kehta. Sab ise protection kehte hain.

Yahi soch aaj bhi India ki har paanch mein se ek young woman tak pahunchti hai. NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein 20-24 saal ki 20.1% women ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho gayi thi: rural areas mein 23.3% aur urban areas mein 11.4% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. 2005-06 mein yeh 47.4% tha. Yaani girawat aayi hai, par 2015-16 ke baad uski speed dheemi pad gayi [[ceda-genderstats-underage-marriage-2021]].

Jaldi shaadi ladki ko safe nahi banati. UNICEF ke mutabik 18 se pehle byaahi gayi ladkiyon ke saath domestic violence ka risk zyada hota hai, aur unka school chhootne ka chance bhi zyada hota hai [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. 2017 se Indian law mein 18 se kam umar ki wife ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. October 2024 mein Supreme Court ne Parliament se kaha ki bachpan mein hone wali sagaai par rok lagane ke baare mein soche. Court ne kaha ki bachpan mein fix ki gayi shaadiyan bachche se uski "free choice, autonomy, agency and childhood" chheen leti hain, yaani apni pasand, azaadi, apne faisle khud lene ka haq aur bachpan [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

## Jab partner chunna khatarnaak ban jaata hai

Yahi soch bade hone ke baad bhi aurton ka peecha karti hai. Jab beti apna partner khud chunti hai, khaas kar doosri caste se, toh kuch families ise apni "izzat" par hamla maanti hain. June 2026 mein Madras High Court ke ek judge 2025 ki ek killing se judi bail plea sun rahe the. Unhone kaha ki pichhle das saal mein Tamil Nadu mein 59 honour killings hui, aur iske liye logon ke mann mein "deep-rooted casteism" ko zimmedar thehraya [[livelaw-madras-hc-honour-killings-2026]].

Police data mein yeh mushkil se dikhta hai. NCRB ne 2020 se 2023 tak Tamil Nadu mein ek bhi honour killing record nahi ki, aur 2024 mein sirf ek [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Poore desh mein 2020 se yeh ginti har saal 18 se 38 ke beech rahi, aur 2024 mein 36 thi [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. Law mein honour killing alag se koi offence nahi hai, aur maana jaata hai ki aisi kai murders doosre motives ke khaate mein darj hoti hain. Akele "love affairs" ke khaate mein 2024 mein 1,391 murders darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Law saaf hai ki shaadi ka faisla kiska hai. Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018) mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki life partner chunne ka right individual liberty ka hissa hai, aur couples ko bachane ke liye preventive, remedial aur punitive measures ka order diya [[barandbench-shakti-vahini-madras-pil-2021]]. Par implementation peeche hai. December 2025 mein Delhi High Court ko bataya gaya ki saat saal se zyada beet jaane ke baad bhi Delhi mein honour killing cases ke liye ek bhi fast-track court nahi bana [[barandbench-honour-killing-fast-track-2025]]. Law Commission ne August 2012 mein aise interference ke khilaf ek alag law ka suggestion diya tha [[livelaw-honour-killing-amicus-2018]]; par 2023 ki Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita mein bhi honour killing ka koi alag offence nahi hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Is myth ko chhodna

Virginity ke myth ko chhodne ka matlab betiyon ki fikar kam karna nahi hai. Iska matlab hai fikar ko uski "purity" se hata kar un cheezon par laana jo sach mein use bachati hain: uski padhai, shaadi ke waqt uski umar, uska na kehne ka haq, aur apni pasand chunne ka haq.

Courts apna kaafi kaam kar chuki hain. Two-finger test misconduct hai, 18 se kam umar ki wife ke saath sex rape hai, aur partner chunna individual liberty ka mamla hai. Par koi bhi faisla akele yeh soch nahi badal sakta ki ladki ki body family ki reputation ki cheez hai. Yeh soch ghar mein badalti hai: shaadi se pehle parents kya poochte hain, beti ke phone call par kaise react karte hain, aur jab woh apna faisla khud leti hai, toh uske saath khade hote hain ya nahi.

what-counts-as-rape-indian-law.en:
"It wasn't really rape." People say it about what was done to a friend, and survivors say it about themselves. Two beliefs sit behind the sentence: that rape means only one act, penile-vaginal intercourse, and that anything short of it is "just touching". Indian law has not said that since 3 February 2013 [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. Here are the common questions, answered from the text of the law. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Is it rape if there was no intercourse?

It can be. Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) does not stop at intercourse. It covers penetration of the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus by the penis, insertion of any object or body part, manipulation to cause penetration, and oral contact [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The 2013 wording says "to any extent", so the law has no category of an act that was "not complete enough" to count [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. And rape does not need a struggle. The act is rape when it is against a woman's will or without her consent, when consent came from fear of death or hurt, when it was given while she was intoxicated, when she cannot communicate consent, and with any girl under 18 whatever she says. Consent means an "unequivocal voluntary agreement", and a woman who does not physically resist is not, for that reason alone, consenting [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Imagine a 19-year-old college student. A man she knows forces a sexual act on her that is not intercourse. She tells a friend it "wasn't really rape, because we didn't have sex". If the act falls within Section 63 and she did not consent, the law calls it rape, whatever she has been taught to call it.

## What changed in 2013, and what did the BNS keep?

The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, deemed in force from 3 February 2013, widened the definition beyond penile-vaginal intercourse to the acts listed above [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. The same Act fixed the age of consent at 18 and created the offences of sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

The data moved at once. Police registered 24,923 rape cases in 2012 [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]] and 33,707 in 2013 [[ncrb-cii-2013-figures-at-a-glance]]. Part of that jump came from the wider definition and from more reporting, so any trend line that crosses 2013 has a break in it.

The BNS replaced the Indian Penal Code on 1 July 2024 [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]] and carried the 2013 definition into Section 63. It also kept two limits. Rape is still defined as an act by "a man" against "a woman". And Exception 2 still says sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, are not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]; a constitutional challenge to that exception is pending in the Supreme Court. For adult men, transgender people and wives aged 18 or over, "it wasn't rape" is true only because of how the section is drafted. Children under 18, boys and girls alike, are covered by the POCSO Act [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## If it wasn't rape, what is it?

Usually, a different crime. "Just touching" has a section number.

| BNS section | Offence | Prison term |
|---|---|---|
| 74 | Assault to outrage a woman's modesty | 1 to 5 years |
| 75 | Sexual harassment | up to 3 years |
| 76 | Assault to disrobe | 3 to 7 years |
| 77 | Voyeurism | 1 to 3 years; 3 to 7 on a repeat |
| 78 | Stalking | up to 3 years; up to 5 on a repeat |
| 79 | Words or gestures insulting a woman's modesty | up to 3 years |

These are the terms in the code [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and the charges are not rare. Police registered 48,303 cases of assault to outrage modesty in 2024, more than the 29,536 cases under the rape head. Rajasthan (8,276) and Odisha (7,299) recorded the most. Odisha also had the highest rate, 31.5 per lakh women against 7.1 for India [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These are FIRs, not incidents, and the NCRB warns against comparing states purely on crime figures.

With children, the "only touching" excuse fails faster. On 18 November 2021 the Supreme Court set aside a High Court ruling that had demanded "skin-to-skin" contact. It held that the important ingredient of sexual assault under POCSO "is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child" [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

## Why does the label matter?

Because the section on the FIR sets the ceiling. Rape carries at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and up to life under Section 64. Assault to outrage modesty carries 1 to 5 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The most a court can give under Section 74 is half the least it can give for rape.

So when a survivor, a relative or a police officer describes a Section 63 act as "molestation" or "misbehaviour", the case can begin under the lighter section. Courts do it too. In a child sexual assault case, a High Court reduced the charges from attempt to rape to lesser offences. The Supreme Court took up that order on its own, and on 10 February 2026 said efforts to sensitise judges "have not borne the fruit that was expected" [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

## What should you do if it happened to you?

You do not have to work out the section. Say what happened, in your own words; naming the offence is the job of the police and the court.

Start with a hospital. Every hospital, public or private, must treat a rape survivor immediately and free of cost [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. HIV prevention medicine (PEP) should start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours [[who-pep]]. Emergency contraception can be used up to 5 days after the assault, and sooner is better [[who-ec]].

You can report at any police station, wherever it happened. A woman officer must record a woman's complaint of rape or another sexual offence, and you must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Read which sections it lists. An officer who fails to record an FIR for rape or sexual assault faces six months to two years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

If you are under 18, the POCSO Act protects you whatever your gender; call 1098. In an emergency, call 112. Whatever section it turns out to be, it was not "nothing".
what-counts-as-rape-indian-law.hg:
"Woh asli rape thodi tha." Log yeh baat kisi dost ke saath hui ghatna ke baare mein kehte hain, aur survivors khud apne baare mein kehte hain. Is ek line ke peeche do beliefs hain: ki rape ka matlab sirf ek act hai, penile-vaginal intercourse, aur usse kam jo bhi ho woh "bas touching" hai. Indian law 3 February 2013 se aisa nahi kehta [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. Yeh rahe aam sawaal, aur unke jawab seedhe law ke text se. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Agar intercourse nahi hua, toh kya woh rape hai?

Ho sakta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 63 intercourse par nahi rukti. Ismein penis se vagina, mouth, urethra ya anus ka penetration, kisi bhi object ya body part ka insertion, penetration karwane ke liye manipulation, aur oral contact shamil hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

2013 ki wording mein "to any extent" likha hai, yaani kisi bhi hadd tak. Isliye law mein aisi koi category nahi hai ki act "poora nahi hua" toh gina nahi jaayega [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. Aur rape ke liye haatha-paai hona zaroori nahi. Act tab rape hai jab woh aurat ki marzi ke khilaf ho ya uske consent ke bina; jab consent maut ya chot ke darr se liya gaya ho; jab consent nashe ki haalat mein diya gaya ho; jab woh consent communicate hi na kar sake; aur 18 saal se kam umar ki kisi bhi ladki ke saath, woh chahe kuch bhi kahe. Consent ka matlab hai "unequivocal voluntary agreement", yaani saaf aur apni marzi se di gayi haan, aur jo aurat physically resist nahi karti, use sirf is wajah se consenting nahi maana jaata [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Imagine kijiye, 19 saal ki ek college student hai. Uski jaan-pehchaan ka ek aadmi us par zabardasti ek aisa sexual act karta hai jo intercourse nahi hai. Woh apni dost se kehti hai ki "asli rape nahi tha, kyunki sex toh hua hi nahi". Agar woh act Section 63 ke andar aata hai aur usne consent nahi diya tha, toh law use rape kehta hai, chahe use bachpan se kuch bhi kehna sikhaya gaya ho.

## 2013 mein kya badla, aur BNS ne kya rakha?

Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne, jo 3 February 2013 se lagu maana gaya, definition ko penile-vaginal intercourse se aage badhakar upar likhe acts tak phaila diya [[prs-cla-bill-2013-as-passed-ls]]. Isi Act ne age of consent 18 tay ki aur sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism aur stalking ke alag offences banaye [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

Data turant badla. Police ne 2012 mein rape ke 24,923 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2012-figures-at-a-glance]] aur 2013 mein 33,707 [[ncrb-cii-2013-figures-at-a-glance]]. Is uchhaal ka ek hissa wider definition aur zyada reporting se aaya, isliye jo bhi trend line 2013 ko cross karti hai, usmein ek break hai.

BNS ne 1 July 2024 ko Indian Penal Code ki jagah li [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]] aur 2013 wali definition ko Section 63 mein le aayi. Usne do limits bhi rakhin. Rape aaj bhi aisa act hai jo "a man" kisi "a woman" ke khilaf karta hai. Aur Exception 2 aaj bhi kehta hai ki apni wife ke saath, agar woh 18 saal ya usse badi hai, mard ke sexual acts rape nahi hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]; is exception ke khilaf constitutional challenge Supreme Court mein pending hai. Adult mardon, transgender logon aur 18 saal ya usse badi wives ke liye "woh rape nahi tha" sirf isliye sach hai ki section aise draft ki gayi hai. 18 saal se kam umar ke bachche, ladke aur ladkiyan dono, POCSO Act mein cover hain [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Agar woh rape nahi tha, toh kya tha?

Aksar, ek alag crime. "Bas touching" ka bhi ek section number hai.

| BNS section | Offence | Jail ki saza |
|---|---|---|
| 74 | Assault to outrage a woman's modesty | 1 se 5 saal |
| 75 | Sexual harassment | 3 saal tak |
| 76 | Assault to disrobe | 3 se 7 saal |
| 77 | Voyeurism | 1 se 3 saal; dobara karne par 3 se 7 |
| 78 | Stalking | 3 saal tak; dobara karne par 5 tak |
| 79 | Aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale words ya gestures | 3 saal tak |

Yeh saza code mein likhi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur yeh charges kam nahi lagte. Police ne 2024 mein assault to outrage modesty ke 48,303 cases register kiye, jo rape head ke 29,536 cases se zyada hain. Sabse zyada cases Rajasthan (8,276) aur Odisha (7,299) mein darj hue. Odisha ka rate bhi sabse upar tha: 31.5 per lakh women, jabki India ka 7.1 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh FIRs hain, ghatnaon ki ginti nahi, aur NCRB khud kehta hai ki states ko sirf crime figures ke aadhaar par compare na kiya jaaye.

Bachchon ke maamle mein "sirf touch kiya" wala bahana aur jaldi girta hai. 18 November 2021 ko Supreme Court ne ek High Court ka woh faisla radd kar diya jo "skin-to-skin" contact maangta tha. Court ne kaha ki POCSO ke under sexual assault ka important ingredient "is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child", yaani asli cheez sexual intent hai, skin-to-skin contact nahi [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

## Label se farq kyun padta hai?

Kyunki FIR par likhi section saza ki ceiling tay karti hai. Section 64 ke under rape ki saza kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, jo life imprisonment tak ja sakti hai. Assault to outrage modesty ki saza 1 se 5 saal hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 74 mein court zyada se zyada jitni saza de sakta hai, woh rape ki kam se kam saza ki aadhi hai.

Isliye jab koi survivor, rishtedaar ya police officer Section 63 wale act ko "chhed-chhaad" ya "badtameezi" keh deta hai, toh case halki section ke saath shuru ho sakta hai. Courts bhi aisa karte hain. Ek child sexual assault case mein ek High Court ne charges ko attempt to rape se ghatakar chhote offences kar diya. Supreme Court ne us order ko khud hi (suo motu) uthaya, aur 10 February 2026 ko kaha ki judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishein "have not borne the fruit that was expected", yaani unka woh nateeja nahi nikla jiski ummeed thi [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

## Agar aapke saath aisa hua hai, toh kya karein?

Section aapko khud tay nahi karni. Jo hua, apne shabdon mein bataiye; offence ka naam dena police aur court ka kaam hai.

Hospital se shuru kijiye. Har hospital ko, sarkari ho ya private, rape survivor ka turant aur free ilaaj karna hoga [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. HIV se bachane wali dawa (PEP) jitni jaldi ho sake shuru honi chahiye, aur 72 ghante ke baad nahi [[who-pep]]. Emergency contraception assault ke 5 din baad tak li ja sakti hai, aur jitni jaldi utna behtar [[who-ec]].

Aap kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakte hain, ghatna chahe kahin bhi hui ho. Aurat ki rape ya kisi aur sexual offence ki complaint ek woman officer ko record karni hogi, aur FIR ki free copy aapko milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Padhiye ki usmein kaun si sections likhi hain. Jo officer rape ya sexual assault ki FIR record nahi karta, use chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Agar aap 18 saal se kam hain, toh POCSO Act aapko protect karta hai, aapka gender chahe jo ho; 1098 par call kijiye. Emergency mein 112 par call kijiye. Aakhir mein section chahe jo bhi lage, jo hua woh "kuch nahi" nahi tha.

women-killed-by-family-not-strangers.en:
Picture a woman's murder the way crime shows teach us to: a stranger, an empty road, a late night. Now look at the count. Men and boys were 80% of the world's homicide victims in 2024, and only 11% of male victims were killed by a partner or relative. For women and girls the pattern flips: almost 60% of those killed died at the hands of a partner or family member [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. The person who kills a woman is usually not a stranger waiting on a dark road. More often than not, it is someone she calls family.

## The killer we picture

Families answer the fear of murder the way they answer the fear of rape: curfews, escorts, a brother sent along, "call when you reach". All of it guards the street. Killings by strangers are real, but most women and girls who are killed die at the hands of partners or relatives, and the stranger image pulls attention away from home.

Consider a hypothetical. A 24-year-old in Kanpur, married for three years, tells her parents twice that her husband's family keeps demanding money and that she is scared. Her parents tell her to adjust; every marriage has problems. Everyone around her worries about her travelling alone after dark. No one treats her fear of her own home as the emergency.

## Who actually kills women

About 50,000 women and girls worldwide were killed by an intimate partner or another family member in 2024: 60% of the roughly 83,000 women and girls killed intentionally that year, or 137 a day [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. Asia accounted for an estimated 17,400 of these killings, second only to Africa's 22,600, and in Asia 55% of the women killed died at the hands of a partner or relative [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]].

"Family" here means more than husbands. Outside Europe and the Americas, in the countries with data, women killed in the private sphere in 2023 were more often killed by other family members (59%) than by partners (41%) [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]]. In an Indian home, that can mean a father or brother angry over a marriage choice, or in-laws over dowry.

India publishes no single count of women killed by partners or relatives, a gap our investigation into India's missing femicide count examines. One category gives a sense of scale. UNODC found that dowry deaths alone made up 40% to 50% of all female homicides recorded in India each year from 1999 to 2016 [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]]. In 2024 police registered 5,737 dowry-death cases, about 16 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Under Section 80 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, a dowry death is a woman's death in abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage, when she faced dowry-linked cruelty by her husband or his relatives soon before she died [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. None of these is a stranger's crime.

## Killings that were reported before they happened

The second half of the myth is that these killings come from nowhere: he "snapped", it was a "crime of passion". Often there were warnings. In France (2019-2022), South Africa (2020-2021) and Colombia (2014-2017), between 22% and 37% of women killed by their partners had already reported physical, sexual or psychological violence by that partner. UNODC and UN Women read this as a sign that many such killings are preventable [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]]. We found no comparable data for India.

In India, warnings rarely reach anyone with the power to act. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), only 14.1% of women aged 18-49 who had faced physical or sexual violence ever sought help, and 77.2% never sought help or told anyone. Of those who did seek help, 60.9% turned to their own family and 6.3% to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The family is the first responder, and sometimes the family is the danger.
